T4-0001.ex: 그 회사의 경영자는 직원들의 의견을 잘 들어요.
T4-0001.x: The head of that company listens carefully to employees' opinions.
T4-0001.e: Literally 'person who runs and manages'; -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.

T4-0002.x: The management announced next year's plan to the employees.
T4-0002.e: Literally 'management lineup'; 진 was a battle formation, so it means a group of people.

T4-0003.ex: 그는 마흔 살에 회사 임원이 되었어요.
T4-0003.x: He became a company executive at forty.
T4-0003.t: Pronounced [이뭔] — the ㅁ carries over to the next vowel.

T4-0004.x: The company's senior staff gathered for a meeting.
T4-0004.e: Literally 'trunk part' — the core people holding up an organization.

T4-0005.m: deputy general manager (rank between 과장 and 부장)
T4-0005.x: Deputy Manager Kim went on a business trip today.
T4-0005.e: Literally 'next head' — the rank just below the 부장.
T4-0005.t: Add 님 when you address or mention a superior: 차장님, not just 차장.

T4-0006.x: The new CEO greeted the employees today.
T4-0006.e: Literally 'representative director' — the officially registered head of a Korean company.
T4-0006.t: Business cards often translate 대표이사 as CEO; in conversation people usually say 사장님 or 대표님.

T4-0007.ex: 이 회사의 창업자는 대학생 때 사업을 시작했어요.
T4-0007.x: This company's founder started the business as a college student.

T4-0008.m: to establish, to found, to set up
T4-0008.x: My grandfather founded this company in 1970.
T4-0008.e: Literally 'set up and make stand' — used for companies, schools and organizations.
T4-0008.t: Use 설립되다 for 'to be founded': 이 학교는 1950년에 설립되었어요.

T4-0009.ex: 우리 회사는 조직이 크지 않아서 분위기가 좋아요.
T4-0009.x: Our company isn't a big organization, so the atmosphere is nice.
T4-0009.e: Literally 'braid and weave' — people woven together into one structure.

T4-0010.ex: 정부 기관에서 일하려면 시험을 봐야 해요.
T4-0010.x: To work at a government agency, you have to take an exam.
T4-0010.e: Originally 'mechanism'; now the working bodies that keep society running.
T4-0010.t: 기관 is for official bodies: 정부 기관, 교육 기관, 의료 기관.

T4-0011.x: My father is a member of the Korean Chefs' Association.
T4-0011.e: Literally 'cooperative gathering' — members joined for a shared goal.

T4-0012.ex: 여러 나라가 연합을 만들어서 문제를 함께 해결했어요.
T4-0012.x: Several countries formed an alliance and solved the problem together.

T4-0013.ex: 저는 다음 달부터 서울 본사에서 일해요.
T4-0013.x: Starting next month, I'll work at the Seoul head office.
T4-0013.e: Literally 'root company' — the main office the branches grow from.

T4-0014.x: That company has a branch office in the US too.
T4-0014.e: Literally 'branch company' — a branch off the main trunk.
T4-0014.t: 지사 is a company's regional office; 지점 is a local branch of a bank or store.

T4-0015.ex: 이 은행 지점은 오후 4시에 문을 닫아요.
T4-0015.x: This bank branch closes at 4 p.m.

T4-0016.ex: 그는 대학을 졸업하고 벤처 기업을 시작했어요.
T4-0016.x: After graduating from college, he started a venture company.
T4-0016.e: From English 'venture'; usually in 벤처 기업, meaning a tech startup.

T4-0017.ex: 요즘 어떤 업종이 가장 인기가 많아요?
T4-0017.x: Which type of business is the most popular these days?
T4-0017.t: 업종 is a category of business; 직종 is a category of job.

T4-0018.m: industry, the business world, the trade
T4-0018.x: He worked in the game industry for ten years.
T4-0018.e: Literally 'business world'; -계 = field or world: 업계, 교육계, 연예계.

T4-0019.ex: 이 직종은 경력이 있는 사람을 원해요.
T4-0019.x: This line of work looks for people with experience.

T4-0020.x: He holds a high position in the company.
T4-0020.t: 직위 is your title, 직급 your rank level, 직책 your role and responsibilities.

T4-0021.x: When your rank goes up, your salary goes up too.

T4-0022.ex: 그는 새로운 직책을 맡아서 요즘 무척 바빠요.
T4-0022.x: He took on a new role, so he's very busy these days.

T4-0023.ex: 다음 주에 회사 인사 발표가 있어요.
T4-0023.x: The company's personnel announcement is next week.
T4-0023.e: Literally 'people affairs'; the everyday word for 'greeting' is written the same way.
T4-0023.t: 인사 also means 'greeting'; in 인사팀 or 인사 발표 it means personnel.

T4-0024.x: There will be a big personnel reshuffle at the end of the year.
T4-0024.e: Literally 'moving people around' within an organization.

T4-0025.x: I was assigned to the Busan branch.
T4-0025.e: Literally 'issuing an order' — the company's order placing you in a post.
T4-0025.t: Common patterns: 발령을 받다 (to be assigned) and 발령이 나다 (an assignment is made).

T4-0026.x: My husband is being transferred to Daegu.
T4-0026.t: Students change schools with 전학; workers change offices with 전근.

T4-0027.ex: 그는 일 년 동안 베트남 지사에 파견을 갔어요.
T4-0027.x: He was sent to the Vietnam branch for a year.

T4-0028.ex: 합격자는 다음 주 월요일에 발표할 거예요.
T4-0028.x: The successful candidates will be announced next Monday.
T4-0028.t: Pronounced [합껵짜] — tensing after ㅂ and ㄱ.

T4-0029.ex: 올해 우리 팀에 신입 사원이 두 명 들어왔어요.
T4-0029.x: Two new employees joined our team this year.
T4-0029.t: Often shortened to just 신입: 신입이 들어왔어요.

T4-0030.x: This time they're hiring experienced people, not new graduates.
T4-0030.e: Literally 'experience job' — the opposite of hiring 신입.
T4-0030.t: Pronounced [경녁찍] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T4-0031.x: The first three months are a probation period.
T4-0031.e: Literally 'practice and learn' on the job.
T4-0031.t: A different 수습 means 'bringing a situation under control', as in 사태를 수습하다.

T4-0032.m: non-regular job, temporary or contract position
T4-0032.ex: 비정규직 직원들은 월급이 적은 경우가 많아요.
T4-0032.x: Non-regular employees are often paid less.
T4-0032.e: Literally 'not-regular job' — the opposite of 정규직.
T4-0032.t: 정규직 means a permanent, full-time job with benefits; the gap between the two is a big social issue.

T4-0033.ex: 그 식당은 대학생 아르바이트생을 많이 고용해요.
T4-0033.x: That restaurant hires a lot of college students as part-timers.
T4-0033.t: 고용하다 sounds formal; in everyday speech people often say 뽑다 or 쓰다.

T4-0034.ex: 고용주는 직원에게 최저 임금 이상을 줘야 해요.
T4-0034.x: Employers must pay workers at least the minimum wage.

T4-0035.x: He opened a small shop with his severance pay.
T4-0035.t: In Korea, workers who stay a year or more are legally owed 퇴직금 when they leave.

T4-0036.x: He decided to resign because of health problems.
T4-0036.t: 사직 is formal; in conversation people say 회사를 그만두다.

T4-0037.x: He handed his resignation letter to his manager yesterday.
T4-0037.t: The fixed phrase is 사표를 내다 (to hand in one's resignation).

T4-0038.m: to change jobs, to move to another company
T4-0038.ex: 저는 작년에 연봉이 더 높은 회사로 이직했어요.
T4-0038.x: Last year I moved to a company with a higher salary.
T4-0038.t: 이직 means switching companies; 전근 means moving offices within the same company.

T4-0039.ex: 요즘 구직자들은 안정적인 회사를 더 좋아해요.
T4-0039.x: Job seekers these days prefer stable companies.
T4-0039.t: Opposite pair: 구인 (seeking workers) vs 구직 (seeking work); pronounced [구직짜].

T4-0040.m: unemployed person, someone who lost their job
T4-0040.x: As the economy got worse, the number of unemployed people rose.

T4-0041.x: Young people are having a harder and harder time finding jobs.
T4-0041.e: Literally 'job-getting difficulty'; -난 = shortage or crisis: 취업난, 주택난.
T4-0041.t: Pronounced [취엄난] — ㅂ becomes ㅁ before ㄴ.

T4-0042.x: This factory works around the clock in three shifts.
T4-0042.t: 교대 is also the short name for 교육대학교, a teachers' college.

T4-0043.ex: 저는 일주일에 두 번 재택근무를 해요.
T4-0043.x: I work from home twice a week.
T4-0043.t: Pronounced [재택끈무] — the ㄱ is tensed after ㄱ.

T4-0044.ex: 그녀는 건강 때문에 1년 동안 휴직을 했어요.
T4-0044.x: She took a one-year leave of absence for health reasons.
T4-0044.e: Literally 'resting from the job' — you keep the position while away.
T4-0044.t: 휴직 is a long leave where you keep your job; 휴가 is a short vacation.

T4-0045.ex: 남편이 육아 휴직을 하고 아이를 돌보고 있어요.
T4-0045.x: My husband is on parental leave, taking care of our child.

T4-0046.ex: 이번 금요일에 연차를 내고 여행을 가요.
T4-0046.x: I'm taking a day off this Friday and going on a trip.
T4-0046.e: Short for 연차 휴가, literally 'yearly leave'.
T4-0046.t: Say 연차를 내다 or 연차를 쓰다 to take a day off; 반차 is a half day.

T4-0047.x: This year's minimum wage went up from last year.

T4-0048.x: If you work on weekends, you get extra pay.
T4-0048.e: Came in via Japanese; its characters (hand + apply) don't explain the meaning.

T4-0049.ex: 올해는 회사 실적이 좋아서 성과급을 많이 받았어요.
T4-0049.x: The company did well this year, so I got a big performance bonus.

T4-0050.x: The company gives a bonus at the holidays.
T4-0050.t: In speech 보너스 is more common; 상여금 appears in contracts and the news.

T4-0051.x: The employees asked the company for a pay raise.
T4-0051.e: Literally 'pulling up'; the opposite is 인하 'pulling down'.
T4-0051.t: A different 인상 means 'impression', as in 첫인상 (first impression).

T4-0052.x: The company was struggling, so employees' pay was cut.
T4-0052.t: Common phrases: 예산 삭감 (budget cut) and 임금 삭감 (pay cut).

T4-0053.x: In the countryside, there aren't nearly enough workers.
T4-0053.e: Literally 'work power'; -력 = power or ability: 노동력, 경쟁력.
T4-0053.t: Pronounced [노동녁] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T4-0054.ex: 노조는 회사와 임금 문제를 협상하고 있어요.
T4-0054.x: The union is negotiating wages with the company.
T4-0054.e: Short for 노동조합: the first syllables of 'labor' and 'union'.

T4-0055.x: The employees decided to form a labor union.
T4-0055.e: Literally 'labor association' — workers combined into one group.

T4-0056.ex: 지하철 노조가 내일 파업을 한다고 해요.
T4-0056.x: They say the subway union is going on strike tomorrow.

T4-0057.ex: 많은 사람들이 광장에 모여서 시위를 했어요.
T4-0057.x: Many people gathered in the square and held a protest.
T4-0057.t: 시위하다 = to protest; 시위대 = the group of protesters.

T4-0058.ex: 그는 회사를 위해 큰 업적을 남겼어요.
T4-0058.x: He left behind great achievements for the company.
T4-0058.t: Pronounced [업쩍] — the ㅈ is tensed after ㅂ.

T4-0059.x: You need enough rest for your work efficiency to go up.
T4-0059.e: Literally 'ability rate' — how much you get done for your effort.
T4-0059.t: Pronounced [능뉼] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T4-0060.ex: 새 프로그램을 쓰니까 일의 효율이 높아졌어요.
T4-0060.x: Using the new program made our work more efficient.
T4-0060.t: 효율 often describes systems and resources; 능률 describes how well people work.

T4-0061.ex: 회사는 생산성을 높이려고 새 기계를 샀어요.
T4-0061.x: The company bought new machines to raise productivity.
T4-0061.e: Literally 'producing quality'; -성 = quality or nature: 생산성, 가능성.

T4-0062.ex: 다음 주까지 새 상품 기획안을 내 주세요.
T4-0062.x: Please submit the new product proposal by next week.

T4-0063.ex: 이 문서를 인쇄해서 회의 전에 나눠 주세요.
T4-0063.x: Please print this document and hand it out before the meeting.
T4-0063.t: 서류 means paper forms; 문서 also covers digital files.

T4-0064.x: Review the contract carefully before you sign it.

T4-0065.ex: 이 일은 부장님의 승인을 받아야 해요.
T4-0065.x: This needs the department head's approval.

T4-0066.x: I'll decide that after discussing it with the team.
T4-0066.t: 협의 is the process of talking it over; 합의 is the agreement you reach.

T4-0067.ex: 두 회사는 오랜 회의 끝에 합의를 했어요.
T4-0067.x: The two companies reached an agreement after a long meeting.
T4-0067.t: Pronounced [하븨], and usually [하비] in everyday speech.

T4-0068.m: signing, conclusion (of a contract or treaty)
T4-0068.x: The two companies signed the contract today.
T4-0068.t: Common collocation: 계약을 체결하다 (to sign a contract).

T4-0069.x: I'll write up today's meeting minutes.

T4-0070.ex: 오늘 회의의 첫 번째 안건은 예산 문제예요.
T4-0070.x: The first item on today's agenda is the budget.
T4-0070.e: Literally 'proposed matter' — something put on the table.

T4-0071.ex: 내일 손님들 앞에서 프레젠테이션을 해야 해서 긴장돼요.
T4-0071.x: I'm nervous because I have to give a presentation to clients tomorrow.
T4-0071.e: From English 'presentation'; in offices it's often shortened to PT, read 피티.

T4-0072.ex: 제 후임이 오면 일을 잘 가르쳐 줄게요.
T4-0072.x: When my successor comes, I'll teach them the job well.

T4-0073.x: The former department head moved to another branch.
T4-0073.t: A different 전임 means 'full-time', as in 전임 강사 (full-time lecturer).

T4-0074.x: I asked a senior colleague about things I didn't know.
T4-0074.e: Literally 'appointed first' — someone who started before you.
T4-0074.t: A different 선임 means 'appointment', as in 대표를 선임하다 (to appoint a CEO).

T4-0075.ex: 이 문제에 대해서 책임자와 이야기하고 싶어요.
T4-0075.x: I'd like to talk to the person in charge about this problem.

T4-0076.x: If there's a problem with the building, contact the manager.
T4-0076.e: Literally 'person who controls and keeps order'.
T4-0076.t: Pronounced [괄리자] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T4-0077.ex: 건강 관리를 위해서 매일 운동을 해요.
T4-0077.x: I exercise every day to take care of my health.
T4-0077.t: Pronounced [괄리]; 관리비 is the monthly maintenance fee in apartments.

T4-0078.m: to share (work, costs), to divide up
T4-0078.x: Our family shares the housework fairly.
T4-0078.e: Literally 'divide and carry' — everyone takes part of the load.

T4-0079.x: My team leader delegated this task to me.
T4-0079.e: Literally 'entrust a duty' — handing your job or power to someone else.
T4-0079.t: Common pattern: [person]에게 권한을 위임하다 — to delegate authority to someone.

T4-0080.x: I don't have permission to edit this document.
T4-0080.e: Literally 'power within limits' — the power you have inside a set scope.
T4-0080.t: Don't mix up 권한 (authority to act) with 권리 (a right you're entitled to).

T4-0081.x: Our new team leader has really outstanding leadership.
T4-0081.e: From English 'leadership'; Koreans often say 리더십이 있다 — to have leadership.

T4-0082.x: This project succeeded because the teamwork was good.

T4-0083.e: Literally 'inside the company'; mostly used before another noun.
T4-0083.t: Homonym warning: native 사내 means 'man, guy' — context makes it clear.

T4-0084.ex: 회사 워크숍 때문에 주말에 강원도에 가요.
T4-0084.x: I'm going to Gangwon-do this weekend for a company retreat.
T4-0084.e: From English 'workshop'; in Korean offices it often means an overnight team retreat, not just a class.
T4-0084.t: Often spelled 워크샵 in daily writing, but 워크숍 is the standard spelling.

T4-0085.ex: 신입 사원들은 한 달 동안 연수를 받아요.
T4-0085.x: New employees receive training for a month.
T4-0085.e: Literally 'study and cultivate' — training to polish your skills.
T4-0085.t: 어학연수 is a very common word: going abroad for language study.

T4-0086.x: A competitor released a similar product first.

T4-0087.ex: 우리 회사의 시장 점유율이 작년보다 높아졌습니다.
T4-0087.x: Our company's market share has risen compared to last year.
T4-0087.t: -율/-률 = rate: 점유율, 증가율, 합격률. Use 율 after a vowel or ㄴ.

T4-0088.x: This year's sales passed 10 billion won for the first time.
T4-0088.e: Literally 'selling-out amount' — the total money from sales.

T4-0089.ex: 광고주가 광고 내용을 바꿔 달라고 했어요.
T4-0089.x: The advertiser asked us to change the ad content.
T4-0089.e: Literally 'advertising owner' — -주 = owner: 광고주, 건물주, 주주.

T4-0090.x: This bag is a famous brand-name product.
T4-0090.e: From English 'brand'; 명품 브랜드 means a luxury brand.

T4-0091.ex: 옷에 붙어 있는 상표를 확인해 보세요.
T4-0091.x: Check the label attached to the clothes.

T4-0092.ex: 그 회사는 새 기술로 특허를 받았어요.
T4-0092.x: That company got a patent for its new technology.
T4-0092.e: Literally 'special permission' — the right to be the only one using an invention.
T4-0092.t: Pronounced [트커]: ㄱ + ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-0093.ex: 한국의 경제력은 지난 50년 동안 크게 성장했습니다.
T4-0093.x: Korea's economic power has grown greatly over the past 50 years.

T4-0094.ex: 요즘 경기가 안 좋아서 장사가 힘들어요.
T4-0094.x: Business is tough these days because the economy is bad.
T4-0094.e: Literally 'view of the atmosphere' — the general mood of the economy.
T4-0094.t: Homonym: 경기 (競技) also means a sports game; 경기가 좋다 is about the economy.

T4-0095.x: Back then the economy was booming, so there were lots of jobs.

T4-0096.ex: 불황 때문에 문을 닫는 가게가 많아요.
T4-0096.x: Lots of stores are closing because of the recession.
T4-0096.e: Literally 'not (a good) situation' — the opposite of 호황.

T4-0097.ex: 불경기라서 사람들이 돈을 잘 안 써요.
T4-0097.x: People don't spend much because times are hard.

T4-0098.ex: 경기 침체가 계속되면서 실업률이 올라가고 있습니다.
T4-0098.x: As the economic downturn continues, the unemployment rate is rising.

T4-0099.x: It's a market where producers and consumers meet directly.
T4-0099.e: -자 = person who does it: 생산자, 소비자, 투자자.

T4-0100.ex: 올해는 비가 많이 와서 쌀 생산량이 줄었어요.
T4-0100.x: Rice output dropped this year because it rained a lot.
T4-0100.t: Pronounced [생산냥]: here ㄹ after ㄴ becomes ㄴ.

T4-0101.x: The power supply was temporarily cut off.

T4-0102.x: In summer, demand for air conditioners rises sharply.
T4-0102.t: Don't confuse with 수요일 (Wednesday) — 수 there means 'water'.

T4-0103.x: If you cut down the distribution process, prices go down.
T4-0103.e: Literally 'flowing through' — goods moving from maker to shop.
T4-0103.t: 유통 기한 (sell-by date) is the version you'll see on every food package.

T4-0104.x: This store sells imported goods cheaply.

T4-0106.x: Our company went back into the black for the first time in three years.
T4-0106.e: Literally 'black letters' — profits were written in black ink, just like 'in the black'.
T4-0106.t: Pronounced [흑짜]: the ㅈ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T4-0107.x: I'm worried because the store keeps losing money.
T4-0107.e: Literally 'red letters' — losses were written in red ink, like English 'in the red'.
T4-0107.t: Pronounced [적짜]. Common: 적자가 나다 / 적자를 보다 — to lose money.

T4-0108.ex: 기업은 이윤을 남기기 위해 비용을 줄입니다.
T4-0108.x: Companies cut costs to make a profit.
T4-0108.e: Literally 'benefit that moistens' — gain that enriches the business.

T4-0109.x: The typhoon caused heavy losses for farms.
T4-0109.t: 손실 is formal and money-focused; 손해 is the everyday word, e.g. 손해를 보다.

T4-0110.x: I made a small profit investing in stocks.

T4-0111.ex: 이 사업은 수익성이 낮아서 그만두기로 했어요.
T4-0111.x: We decided to drop this business because its profitability was low.
T4-0111.e: -성 = quality of being: 수익성, 가능성, 안전성.
T4-0111.t: Pronounced [수익썽] — the ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T4-0112.x: Material prices went up, so production costs rose a lot.
T4-0112.e: Literally 'original price' — what it costs before any profit is added.
T4-0112.t: Pronounced [원까]. 원가 이하로 팔다 = to sell below cost.

T4-0113.x: Rising prices have increased the burden on household finances.
T4-0113.e: Literally 'house calculation' — a family's money matters.
T4-0113.t: Often pronounced [가게], so it can sound just like 가게 (store) — context tells them apart.

T4-0114.ex: 저는 매일 가계부를 써서 돈을 아껴요.
T4-0114.x: I save money by keeping a household budget every day.
T4-0114.t: The verb is 쓰다: 가계부를 쓰다 — to keep a budget book (apps count too).

T4-0115.ex: 혼자 살면 식비가 생각보다 많이 들어요.
T4-0115.x: When you live alone, food costs more than you'd think.

T4-0116.x: Having insurance lowers the burden of medical costs.

T4-0117.m: utility bills, public charges (taxes and fees)
T4-0117.x: I pay my utility bills automatically every month.
T4-0117.e: Literally 'public levy money' — electricity, water, gas bills and similar charges.

T4-0118.x: Income tax is automatically taken out of my salary.

T4-0119.t: Pronounced [부가쎄]. In Korea it's 10% and usually already in the menu price.

T4-0120.ex: 세금 문제 때문에 세무서에 가야 해요.
T4-0120.x: I have to go to the tax office about a tax issue.

T4-0121.x: I got a little tax back through the year-end settlement.
T4-0121.e: Literally 'year-end exact settling' — Korea's annual tax refund process for employees.
T4-0121.t: Every January, Korean workers submit receipts at work — like a simplified tax return.

T4-0122.x: That company has over one trillion won in assets.

T4-0123.e: Literally 'carry a debt'. Homonym: native 부채 means a hand fan.
T4-0123.t: In daily speech people say 빚; 부채 is the news and finance word.

T4-0124.x: When interest rates go up, loan interest goes up too.
T4-0124.e: Literally 'money benefit' — the price of borrowing money.
T4-0124.t: Pronounced [금니]: ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ.

T4-0125.x: I put half of my allowance into savings.

T4-0126.ex: 외국인 투자자들이 한국 주식을 많이 샀습니다.
T4-0126.x: Foreign investors bought a lot of Korean stocks.
T4-0126.e: -자 = person who does it: 투자자, 생산자, 소비자.

T4-0127.ex: 요즘 주식을 시작하는 젊은 사람이 많아요.
T4-0127.x: A lot of young people are getting into stocks these days.
T4-0127.e: Literally 'stump form' — the hanja for 'stump' came to mean 'share' in East Asian business.
T4-0127.t: Homonym: 주식 (主食) also means 'staple food,' as in 한국인의 주식은 쌀이에요.

T4-0128.x: The stock price rose as soon as the good news came out.

T4-0129.x: The company distributed profits to its shareholders.
T4-0129.e: Literally 'share owner' — -주 = owner, as in 광고주.

T4-0130.x: I opened an account at a securities company.
T4-0130.e: Literally 'proof certificate' — a paper proving your financial claim.

T4-0131.x: Bonds tend to be safer than stocks.
T4-0131.e: Literally 'debt certificate' — a paper saying someone owes you money.
T4-0131.t: Pronounced [채꿘]. A different 채권 (債權) means a legal claim to collect a debt.

T4-0132.x: Long ago, people used seashells as money.
T4-0132.e: Literally 'goods and silk' — things once used to pay before coins.
T4-0132.t: 화폐 is the formal or academic word; in daily life just say 돈.

T4-0133.x: If your credit is good, it's easy to get a loan.
T4-0133.e: Literally 'trust and use' — being trusted enough to be lent to.

T4-0134.m: lump-sum payment, paying in full at once
T4-0134.x: Please put it on my card as a single payment.
T4-0134.e: Literally 'one-time payment' — the opposite of paying in installments (할부).
T4-0134.t: At Korean stores the cashier often asks 일시불로 해 드릴까요? — pay in full or in installments?

T4-0135.m: to pay (for), to make a payment, to settle
T4-0135.x: I'll pay for the meal by card.
T4-0135.e: Literally 'decide and settle' — completing a transaction.
T4-0135.t: Don't confuse with 결재하다 (to approve a document) — same pronunciation, different word.

T4-0136.ex: 그는 대학 졸업 후 금융 회사에 취직했어요.
T4-0136.x: He got a job at a financial company after graduating from college.
T4-0136.e: Literally 'money melting' — money flowing and circulating.

T4-0137.x: The older you are, the more expensive insurance premiums get.
T4-0137.t: Pronounced [보험뇨]. 보험료 is what you pay; 보험금 is what you receive.

T4-0138.x: I received an insurance payout after a car accident.
T4-0138.e: Literally 'insurance money' — -금 = a sum of money: 보험금, 지원금, 장학금.
T4-0138.t: Easy to mix up: you pay 보험료 and you receive 보험금.

T4-0139.m: to cancel (a contract or subscription), to terminate
T4-0139.x: I canceled the phone plan I wasn't using.
T4-0139.e: Literally 'release and stop' — ending an ongoing contract.
T4-0139.t: Use 해지하다 for ongoing contracts (insurance, phone, bank); use 취소하다 for orders or reservations.

T4-0140.x: My grandfather receives a pension every month.
T4-0140.e: Literally 'yearly money' — paid regularly after retirement.

T4-0141.x: Office workers pay into the national pension from their salaries.
T4-0141.e: Literally 'citizens' yearly money' — Korea's public pension, like U.S. Social Security.

T4-0142.ex: 정부가 전기차를 사는 사람에게 보조금을 줍니다.
T4-0142.x: The government gives a subsidy to people who buy electric cars.

T4-0143.ex: 코로나 때 모든 가정에 지원금이 나왔어요.
T4-0143.x: During COVID, every household got relief payments.
T4-0143.t: Homonym alert: 지원하다 (志願) can also mean 'to apply,' as for a job.

T4-0144.x: The donations collected will be given to neighbors in need.

T4-0145.ex: 이 행사는 여러 기업의 후원으로 열렸어요.
T4-0145.x: This event was held with sponsorship from several companies.

T4-0146.x: The area around the subway station is a busy commercial district.
T4-0146.e: Literally 'commerce circle' — the area where shops draw customers.

T4-0147.x: I got a department store gift card as a birthday present.
T4-0147.e: Literally 'merchandise ticket'; -권 = ticket: 상품권, 입장권, 승차권.
T4-0147.t: Pronounced [상품꿘]. Very popular as a holiday gift in Korea.

T4-0148.x: They sell this book 10% below the list price.

T4-0149.ex: 이 식당은 음식이 맛있고 가격도 저렴해요.
T4-0149.x: This restaurant has tasty food and affordable prices.
T4-0149.t: 저렴하다 sounds more polite and positive than 싸다, which can imply poor quality.

T4-0150.ex: 집값 폭등으로 젊은 사람들이 집을 사기 어려워요.
T4-0150.x: Because housing prices skyrocketed, it's hard for young people to buy homes.

T4-0151.ex: 주가 폭락으로 많은 투자자들이 돈을 잃었습니다.
T4-0151.x: Many investors lost money due to the stock crash.
T4-0151.e: Literally 'violent fall' — the opposite of 폭등.
T4-0151.t: Pronounced [퐁낙]: double nasalization of ㄱ and ㄹ.

T4-0152.x: The sudden jump in fuel prices has increased the burden on drivers.

T4-0153.ex: 환율 급락 때문에 수출 기업들이 걱정하고 있습니다.
T4-0153.x: Export companies are worried because of the sharp drop in the exchange rate.
T4-0153.t: Pronounced [금낙]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ, then ㅂ becomes ㅁ.

T4-0154.x: This year the population growth rate hit 0% for the first time.

T4-0155.ex: 온라인 쇼핑 이용자가 계속 증가세를 보이고 있습니다.
T4-0155.x: Online shopping users continue to show an upward trend.
T4-0155.e: Literally 'increase momentum'; -세 = trend: 증가세, 감소세, 상승세.
T4-0155.t: Typical news phrase: 증가세를 보이다 — to show an upward trend.

T4-0156.ex: 환율 변동이 심해서 여행 경비를 계산하기 어려워요.
T4-0156.x: The exchange rate fluctuates so much that it's hard to budget for the trip.

T4-0157.ex: 요즘 경제가 불안정해서 사람들이 돈을 잘 안 써요.
T4-0157.x: The economy is unstable these days, so people aren't spending much money.
T4-0157.t: 불- negates Sino words (불안정, 불평등, 불공평), but becomes 부- before ㄷ or ㅈ, as in 부족.

T4-0158.x: That company finally went bankrupt last year.
T4-0158.t: 파산 신청 = filing for bankruptcy; it works for both people and companies.

T4-0159.m: default, failure to pay (bills or checks); business failure
T4-0159.ex: 경기가 나빠서 작은 회사들이 부도가 났어요.
T4-0159.x: The economy was bad, so small companies defaulted.
T4-0159.e: Literally 'not handed over': a bill or check that couldn't be paid.
T4-0159.t: Used with 나다: 부도가 나다 = a company defaults; 부도 수표 = a bounced check.

T4-0160.ex: 회사가 구조 조정을 해서 직원 백 명이 회사를 떠났어요.
T4-0160.x: The company restructured, so a hundred employees left.
T4-0160.e: Literally 'adjusting the structure'; often a polite word for cutting jobs.

T4-0161.m: takeover, acquisition; taking over (a business or duties)
T4-0161.ex: 큰 회사가 작은 게임 회사를 인수했어요.
T4-0161.x: A big company acquired a small game company.

T4-0162.ex: 두 은행이 합병해서 하나의 큰 은행이 되었습니다.
T4-0162.x: The two banks merged and became one large bank.
T4-0162.t: Pronounced [합뼝]: ㅂ makes the next consonant tense.

T4-0163.ex: 그는 젊은 나이에 성공한 기업가가 되었어요.
T4-0163.x: He became a successful entrepreneur at a young age.
T4-0163.e: -가 = professional or expert: 기업가, 작가, 전문가.
T4-0163.t: Pronounced [기업까]; a 기업가 founds or runs a business, while a 회사원 is an employee.

T4-0164.ex: 우리 부모님은 이십 년 동안 자영업을 하셨어요.
T4-0164.x: My parents ran their own business for twenty years.

T4-0165.x: The economy is bad, so self-employed people are struggling a lot.
T4-0165.e: -자 = person who does it: 자영업자, 운전자, 과학자.
T4-0165.t: Pronounced [자영업짜]: the ㅂ batchim makes 자 tense.

T4-0166.ex: 이 거리에는 문을 닫은 점포가 많아졌어요.
T4-0166.x: There are more closed stores on this street now.

T4-0167.ex: 이 옷은 온라인에서만 팔고 매장에서는 안 팔아요.
T4-0167.x: These clothes are sold only online, not in stores.
T4-0167.e: Literally 'selling place'. Homonym warning: 매장 can also mean 'burial'.

T4-0168.ex: 요즘은 동네에도 프랜차이즈 카페가 정말 많아요.
T4-0168.x: These days there are a lot of chain cafes even in neighborhoods.
T4-0168.e: From English 'franchise'. In everyday speech Koreans also say 체인점 for a chain store.

T4-0169.ex: 삼만 원 이상 사면 배송비가 무료예요.
T4-0169.x: Shipping is free if you spend 30,000 won or more.
T4-0169.e: -비 = cost or fee: 배송비, 교통비, 생활비.
T4-0169.t: 무료 배송 = free shipping; 배송 is for parcels, while 배달 is used for food delivery.

T4-0170.ex: 세일 기간에는 충동구매를 하지 않도록 조심하세요.
T4-0170.x: Be careful not to buy on impulse during sales.

T4-0171.ex: 신용 카드를 자주 쓰면 과소비를 하기 쉬워요.
T4-0171.x: If you use credit cards often, it's easy to overspend.
T4-0171.e: 과- = too much: 과소비, 과식, 과로.

T4-0172.ex: 제 언니는 알뜰해서 돈을 많이 모았어요.
T4-0172.x: My older sister is thrifty, so she has saved a lot of money.
T4-0172.e: Doubled form 알뜰살뜰 means 'very thrifty and careful with the household'.
T4-0172.t: A positive word for smart saving; 알뜰폰 = budget phone plan, 알뜰 시장 = flea market.

T4-0173.x: He is rich, but he lives very modestly.
T4-0173.t: 검소하다 describes a modest, simple lifestyle; 알뜰하다 is about managing money cleverly.

T4-0174.ex: 비싼 가방을 여러 개 사는 것은 사치예요.
T4-0174.x: Buying several expensive bags is an extravagance.

T4-0175.ex: 그런 사치스러운 생활은 오래 할 수 없어요.
T4-0175.x: You can't keep up such an extravagant lifestyle for long.

T4-0176.ex: 아직도 많은 아이들이 빈곤 속에서 살고 있습니다.
T4-0176.x: Many children are still living in poverty.
T4-0176.t: 빈곤 is formal and written; in conversation 가난 is more common.

T4-0177.m: gap between rich and poor, wealth gap
T4-0177.x: The gap between rich and poor is growing wider.

T4-0178.x: He was born into a wealthy family.
T4-0178.t: Rather formal; in speech people usually say 부자예요 or 돈이 많아요.

T4-0179.x: The government's financial situation is not good.

T4-0180.x: The budget for this trip is one million won.

T4-0181.ex: 요즘은 젊은 사람들도 재테크에 관심이 많아요.
T4-0181.x: These days even young people are very interested in growing their money.
T4-0181.e: Blend of 재 'wealth' + 테크 from English 'tech(nology)': the technique of growing money.
T4-0181.t: 재테크 covers savings, stocks and real estate; English has no single word for it.

T4-0182.e: 경제 comes from a phrase meaning 'govern the world, relieve the people'; -학 = field of study.

T4-0183.ex: 그 아이는 사회성이 좋아서 친구가 많아요.
T4-0183.x: That child has good social skills, so he has lots of friends.
T4-0183.e: -성 = quality or nature: 사회성, 가능성, 중요성.
T4-0183.t: 사회성이 좋다 / 사회성이 부족하다 = to have good / poor social skills.

T4-0184.m: member (of a group, family or society)
T4-0184.ex: 가족 구성원 모두가 집안일을 나누어서 해요.
T4-0184.x: Every member of the family shares the housework.
T4-0184.e: -원 = member or staff: 구성원, 회사원, 직원.

T4-0185.ex: 사회의 모든 계층이 이 정책의 영향을 받습니다.
T4-0185.x: Every class of society is affected by this policy.
T4-0185.t: 계층 is about income or social layers; 계급 suggests rigid ranks, like in the military or a caste system.

T4-0186.x: Rank is very important in the military.

T4-0187.ex: 옛날에는 신분에 따라 할 수 있는 일이 달랐어요.
T4-0187.x: In the old days, the work you could do depended on your social status.
T4-0187.t: 신분증 = ID card: 신분증 좀 보여 주세요 = Please show me your ID.

T4-0188.ex: 남녀 불평등 문제는 아직도 남아 있어요.
T4-0188.x: The problem of gender inequality still remains.

T4-0189.ex: 부모님은 우리 형제를 항상 공평하게 대해 주셨어요.
T4-0189.x: Our parents always treated us siblings fairly.
T4-0189.t: 공평하다 means everyone gets equal treatment; 공정하다 means the process or rules are just.

T4-0190.ex: 나만 매일 청소를 하는 건 불공평해요.
T4-0190.x: It's unfair that I'm the only one who cleans every day.

T4-0191.ex: 두 정당의 대립이 점점 심해지고 있습니다.
T4-0191.x: The confrontation between the two parties is getting worse.
T4-0191.t: 대립 is about opposing positions or sides; 갈등 is broader tension, emotional or social.

T4-0192.ex: 두 나라 사이에 국경 분쟁이 계속되고 있습니다.
T4-0192.x: A border dispute continues between the two countries.

T4-0193.ex: 부모님과 대화할 때 가끔 세대 차이를 느껴요.
T4-0193.x: I sometimes feel a generation gap when I talk with my parents.
T4-0193.t: 세대 차이를 느끼다 = to feel a generation gap; this is the most common pairing.

T4-0194.ex: 한국은 빠르게 고령화 사회가 되고 있습니다.
T4-0194.x: Korea is quickly becoming an aging society.
T4-0194.e: Literally 'society becoming high-aged'; -화 works like English '-ization'.

T4-0195.ex: 저출산 때문에 학교마다 학생 수가 줄고 있어요.
T4-0195.x: Because of the low birth rate, the number of students is falling at every school.
T4-0195.t: 저출산 고령화 is a fixed news phrase for Korea's population crisis.

T4-0196.ex: 한국의 출산율은 세계에서 가장 낮은 편이에요.
T4-0196.x: Korea's birth rate is among the lowest in the world.
T4-0196.e: -률/-율 = rate; it is written 율 after a vowel or ㄴ: 출산율, 비율, 합격률.

T4-0197.ex: 할아버지는 시골에서 행복한 노년을 보내고 계세요.
T4-0197.x: My grandfather is spending a happy old age in the countryside.

T4-0198.ex: 미성년자는 술과 담배를 살 수 없습니다.
T4-0198.x: Minors cannot buy alcohol or cigarettes.
T4-0198.e: Literally 'person who has not yet completed their years'.
T4-0198.t: In Korea, people under 19 count as 미성년자 for alcohol and tobacco.

T4-0199.ex: 한국에도 다문화 학생이 점점 늘고 있어요.
T4-0199.x: The number of multicultural students is growing in Korea, too.

T4-0200.ex: 우리 반에는 다문화 가정 아이들이 세 명 있어요.
T4-0200.x: There are three kids from multicultural families in our class.
T4-0200.e: In Korea, usually a family where one parent is Korean and the other is from abroad.

T4-0201.ex: 그 가족은 십 년 전에 캐나다로 이민을 갔어요.
T4-0201.x: That family emigrated to Canada ten years ago.
T4-0201.t: 이민을 가다 = to emigrate (leave); 이민을 오다 = to immigrate (come here).

T4-0202.ex: 미국에는 여러 나라에서 온 이민자가 많아요.
T4-0202.x: There are many immigrants from various countries in America.

T4-0203.ex: 전쟁 때문에 많은 사람들이 난민이 되었습니다.
T4-0203.x: Many people became refugees because of the war.

T4-0204.ex: 그 사람은 한국에서 태어났지만 국적은 미국이에요.
T4-0204.x: He was born in Korea, but his nationality is American.
T4-0204.t: Pronounced [국쩍]; a polite question is 국적이 어떻게 되세요?

T4-0205.ex: 정부는 내년에 사회 복지 예산을 늘리기로 했습니다.
T4-0205.x: The government decided to increase the social welfare budget next year.

T4-0206.ex: 연말에는 이웃과 나눔을 실천하는 사람들이 많아요.
T4-0206.x: At the end of the year, many people practice sharing with their neighbors.
T4-0206.e: Noun made from 나누다 'to divide, to share' + -ㅁ.

T4-0207.m: to be alienated, to be left out, to be marginalized
T4-0207.ex: 혼자 사는 노인들이 사회에서 소외되지 않도록 도와야 해요.
T4-0207.x: We should help elderly people who live alone so they aren't left out of society.

T4-0208.ex: 이 단체는 소외 계층 아이들에게 무료로 공부를 가르쳐요.
T4-0208.x: This organization teaches underprivileged children for free.
T4-0208.e: Literally 'social layers left on the outside'.

T4-0209.ex: 추운 겨울에는 노숙자들을 위한 쉼터가 꼭 필요해요.
T4-0209.x: In the cold winter, shelters for homeless people are really needed.
T4-0209.e: Literally 'person who sleeps out in the dew'.
T4-0209.t: 노숙인 is the newer, more respectful official term; 노숙자 is pronounced [노숙짜].

T4-0210.x: The police are chasing the criminal who ran away.

T4-0211.ex: 경찰은 사고를 내고 도망간 가해자를 찾고 있습니다.
T4-0211.x: The police are looking for the driver who caused the accident and fled.
T4-0211.e: Literally 'person who inflicts harm'; its opposite 피해자 is 'person who suffers harm'.
T4-0211.t: Used for anyone who causes harm, in accidents, bullying or crime, not only for criminals.

T4-0212.ex: 어떤 이유가 있어도 폭력은 절대 안 돼요.
T4-0212.x: Whatever the reason, violence is never okay.
T4-0212.t: Pronounced [퐁녁]: ㄱ before ㄹ turns into [ㅇ] and ㄹ into [ㄴ] (nasalization).

T4-0213.ex: 학교 폭력을 당하면 바로 선생님께 말씀드리세요.
T4-0213.x: If you experience school violence, tell a teacher right away.
T4-0213.e: Often shortened to 학폭 in news and everyday talk.

T4-0214.ex: 직장 내 괴롭힘은 법으로 금지되어 있어요.
T4-0214.x: Workplace harassment is prohibited by law.
T4-0214.e: Noun from 괴롭히다 'to bother, torment', built on 괴롭다 'painful, distressing'.
T4-0214.t: Pronounced [괴로핌]: ㅂ and ㅎ merge into [ㅍ].

T4-0215.m: ostracism, being left out, social exclusion
T4-0215.ex: 그 학생은 반 친구들에게 따돌림을 당했어요.
T4-0215.x: That student was ostracized by classmates.
T4-0215.e: Noun from 따돌리다 'to leave someone out, shun'.
T4-0215.t: Used with 당하다: 따돌림을 당하다 = to be ostracized.

T4-0216.ex: 그 아이는 반에서 왕따를 당해서 학교에 가기 싫어해요.
T4-0216.x: That kid is being ostracized in class, so he doesn't want to go to school.
T4-0216.e: Slang: 왕 'king, super' + 따 from 따돌림, so 'the most shunned one'.
T4-0216.t: Slangy but known to everyone; 왕따를 당하다 = to be ostracized.

T4-0217.ex: 정부는 자살을 예방하기 위해 상담 전화를 운영합니다.
T4-0217.x: The government runs a counseling hotline to prevent suicide.

T4-0218.x: Smartphone addiction is a big problem these days.
T4-0218.e: Literally 'hit by poison'; 중 here means 'to strike', as in hitting a target.
T4-0218.t: X 중독 = X addiction (게임 중독, 알코올 중독); 식중독 = food poisoning.

T4-0219.ex: 그 사람은 도박으로 돈을 모두 잃었어요.
T4-0219.x: He lost all his money gambling.

T4-0220.x: Buying or selling drugs is illegal.
T4-0220.t: In food names it means 'addictively good': 마약 김밥 is just very tasty gimbap.

T4-0221.ex: 음주 운전은 다른 사람의 생명도 위험하게 해요.
T4-0221.x: Drunk driving puts other people's lives in danger too.

T4-0222.ex: 그 사기꾼은 노인들을 속여서 돈을 받았어요.
T4-0222.x: That con artist tricked elderly people and took their money.
T4-0222.e: 사기 'fraud' + -꾼 'person who does it', often negative, as in 장사꾼, 노름꾼.
T4-0222.t: 사기를 당하다 = to be scammed; 사기를 치다 = to scam someone.

T4-0223.ex: 요즘 우리 동네에서 절도 사건이 자주 일어나요.
T4-0223.x: Thefts have been happening often in our neighborhood lately.
T4-0223.t: Formal or legal word, pronounced [절또]; in daily speech people say 도둑질 or 훔치다.

T4-0224.x: A robber broke into the neighborhood convenience store last night.
T4-0224.e: Literally 'stealing by force'. Homonym warning: 강도 also means 'strength, intensity'.
T4-0224.t: 강도 uses force or threats; 도둑 steals secretly. Use 강도가 들다 for a robbery at a place.

T4-0225.ex: 그 영화는 형사가 살인 사건을 해결하는 이야기예요.
T4-0225.x: That movie is about a detective solving a murder case.

T4-0226.x: The police safely rescued the kidnapped child.
T4-0226.t: 납치되다 = to be kidnapped; it is also used for planes: 비행기 납치 = hijacking.

T4-0227.x: A man who went hiking went missing in the mountains.
T4-0227.t: Pronounced [실쫑되다]; 실종 신고 = a missing-person report.

T4-0228.ex: 한국은 치안이 좋아서 밤에도 안전한 편이에요.
T4-0228.x: Korea has good public safety, so it's fairly safe even at night.

T4-0229.ex: 사회 규범을 지키는 것은 모두에게 중요해요.
T4-0229.x: Following social norms is important for everyone.

T4-0230.ex: 그 행동은 법적으로는 괜찮지만 도덕적으로는 문제가 있어요.
T4-0230.x: That behavior is legally okay, but it's morally problematic.
T4-0230.t: Pronounced [도덕쩍]; -적 words take 인 before nouns and 으로 as adverbs.

T4-0231.x: Professional ethics are very important for doctors.

T4-0232.x: I lied to my friend, so my conscience bothered me.
T4-0232.t: 양심에 찔리다 = to feel a pang of guilt; 양심이 없다 = to be shameless.

T4-0233.ex: 여론 조사 결과 국민의 60%가 이 정책에 찬성했습니다.
T4-0233.x: According to the poll, 60% of the public supported this policy.
T4-0233.t: 여론 조사 is for public or political polls; 설문 조사 is any questionnaire survey.

T4-0234.x: More than half of the respondents answered 'yes.'

T4-0235.ex: 전체 인구에서 노인이 차지하는 비중이 커지고 있어요.
T4-0235.x: The share of elderly people in the total population is growing.
T4-0235.e: Literally 'compared weight': how heavy one part is relative to the whole.
T4-0235.t: Usually paired with 차지하다: 비중을 차지하다 'to account for a share'.
rel: to take up, to account for

T4-0236.ex: 최근 결혼을 늦게 하는 추세가 계속되고 있어요.
T4-0236.x: Recently, the trend of marrying later has continued.
T4-0236.e: Literally 'the force things are moving toward'.
T4-0236.t: Common phrases: 증가 추세 'rising trend', 감소 추세 'falling trend'; for fashion fads use 유행.

T4-0237.ex: 정부는 국내 경제 동향을 매달 발표합니다.
T4-0237.x: The government announces domestic economic trends every month.

T4-0238.m: plan, measure, way (to solve a problem)
T4-0238.ex: 정부가 교통 문제를 해결할 방안을 찾고 있어요.
T4-0238.x: The government is looking for a way to solve traffic problems.
T4-0238.e: Literally 'method plan': a concrete way to deal with something.
T4-0238.t: Typical collocations: 방안을 마련하다 'to work out a plan', 방안을 찾다 'to look for a way'.

T4-0239.ex: 자동차 대신 자전거가 좋은 대안이 될 수 있어요.
T4-0239.x: Bikes can be a good alternative to cars.

T4-0240.forms: N에 영향을 미치다 · 미쳐요 · 미쳤어요 · 미칠 거예요
T4-0240.m: to influence, to have an effect on
T4-0240.ex: 스마트폰은 아이들의 생활에 큰 영향을 미쳐요.
T4-0240.x: Smartphones have a big influence on children's lives.
T4-0240.e: 영향 is literally 'shadow and echo'; 미치다 here means 'to reach'.
T4-0240.t: This 미치다 'to reach' differs from 미치다 'to go crazy'; in casual speech, 영향을 주다 is more common.

T4-0241.ex: 잠이 부족하면 건강에 악영향을 줄 수 있어요.
T4-0241.x: Lack of sleep can have a negative effect on your health.
T4-0241.t: Pronounced [아경향]: the ㄱ moves over to the next syllable.

T4-0242.m: to criticize, to blame, to condemn
T4-0242.ex: 많은 사람들이 그 정치인의 발언을 비난했어요.
T4-0242.x: Many people criticized the politician's remarks.
T4-0242.e: Literally 'calling something wrong and reproaching it'.
T4-0242.t: 비난 is an emotional attack on a person; 비판 is a reasoned critique of ideas or policies.

T4-0243.ex: 그 배우의 발언이 큰 논란이 되었어요.
T4-0243.x: The actor's comment became a big controversy.
T4-0243.t: Pronounced [놀란]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ. Common: 논란이 되다 'to become controversial'.

T4-0244.ex: 두 학자는 그 문제로 오랫동안 논쟁을 벌였어요.
T4-0244.x: The two scholars argued over that issue for a long time.
T4-0244.t: 논란 is public controversy around something; 논쟁 is an actual back-and-forth argument between sides.

T4-0245.ex: 이번 선거의 가장 큰 쟁점은 집값이에요.
T4-0245.x: The biggest issue in this election is housing prices.

T4-0246.ex: 그 문제에 대해 전문가들의 견해가 달라요.
T4-0246.x: Experts have different views on the issue.
T4-0246.e: Literally 'seeing and understanding': how you see something.
T4-0246.t: 견해 is more formal than 의견; common in 견해를 밝히다 'to state one's view'.

T4-0247.ex: 같은 일도 시각에 따라 다르게 보일 수 있어요.
T4-0247.x: The same thing can look different depending on your point of view.
T4-0247.e: Literally 'viewing angle'; a homonym 시각 means 'time, moment'.

T4-0248.ex: 요즘 젊은 사람들의 가장 큰 관심사는 취업이에요.
T4-0248.x: These days the biggest concern for young people is getting a job.

T4-0249.ex: 환경 문제가 요즘 큰 이슈가 되고 있어요.
T4-0249.x: Environmental problems have become a big issue lately.
T4-0249.e: From English 'issue', but it means a hot topic in the news, not a personal problem.
T4-0249.t: Don't use 이슈 for personal troubles like 'I have issues'; say 문제 instead.

T4-0250.ex: 학교에서 쓰레기 줄이기 캠페인을 하고 있어요.
T4-0250.x: The school is running a campaign to reduce trash.
T4-0250.e: From English 'campaign'; mostly for public-awareness drives, while election campaigns are usually 선거 운동.

T4-0251.x: Citizens gathered to stand in solidarity with the victims.
T4-0251.e: Literally 'linked by a belt'; don't confuse with 연대 'era, decade', as in 1990년대.

T4-0252.ex: 공익을 위해 개인의 자유를 제한할 수도 있어요.
T4-0252.x: Personal freedom may sometimes be limited for the public good.

T4-0253.ex: 지나친 이기주의는 사회 문제를 만들 수 있어요.
T4-0253.x: Too much selfishness can create social problems.
T4-0253.t: In everyday speech the adjective 이기적이다 'to be selfish' is much more common.

T4-0254.x: Individualism is growing stronger in cities.
T4-0254.t: 개인주의 is neutral (valuing the individual), while 이기주의 is negative (selfishness).

T4-0255.ex: 혼자 사는 1인 가구가 해마다 늘고 있어요.
T4-0255.x: The number of single-person households is rising every year.
T4-0255.e: Literally 'one-person household'; 가구 'household' is a homonym of 가구 'furniture'.
T4-0255.t: Read 1인 as 일인, pronounced [이린] because the ㄹ links to the next syllable.

T4-0256.x: These days nuclear families are far more common than extended families.
T4-0256.e: Literally 'core family', modeled on English 'nuclear family'.
T4-0256.t: Pronounced [핵까족]: the ㄱ after ㄱ is tensed.

T4-0257.ex: 옛날에는 할아버지, 할머니와 함께 사는 대가족이 많았어요.
T4-0257.x: In the past, many large families lived together with the grandparents.
T4-0257.e: Literally 'big family': several generations living under one roof.

T4-0258.m: single life, being unmarried; single person
T4-0258.ex: 그는 결혼하지 않고 평생 독신으로 살았어요.
T4-0258.x: He never married and lived single all his life.
T4-0258.t: 독신 suggests a long-term or lifelong single life; 미혼 just means 'not married yet'.

T4-0259.ex: 요즘 비혼을 선택하는 젊은이들이 늘고 있어요.
T4-0259.x: More young people are choosing not to marry these days.
T4-0259.e: Literally 'not-marriage': a newer word framing singlehood as a choice.
T4-0259.t: 비혼 implies a deliberate choice, unlike 미혼 'not married yet'.

T4-0260.ex: 회사에서 성차별을 겪으면 신고할 수 있어요.
T4-0260.x: If you experience gender discrimination at work, you can report it.

T4-0261.ex: 양성평등을 위해 여러 가지 제도가 만들어졌어요.
T4-0261.x: Various systems have been created to promote gender equality.

T4-0262.x: Several news outlets reported on the incident.
T4-0262.e: 언론 'the press' + -사 'company'; -사 = company: 방송사, 신문사, 여행사.
T4-0262.t: Pronounced [얼론사]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T4-0263.ex: 그 방송사는 뉴스와 드라마를 모두 만들어요.
T4-0263.x: That broadcaster makes both news and dramas.

T4-0264.x: My uncle works as a reporter at a newspaper.

T4-0265.ex: 대통령이 오늘 오후에 기자 회견을 열었어요.
T4-0265.x: The president held a press conference this afternoon.
T4-0265.t: Say 기자 회견을 열다 'to hold a press conference'; it is often written as one word, 기자회견.

T4-0266.ex: 워싱턴 특파원이 현지 소식을 전해 드리겠습니다.
T4-0266.x: Our Washington correspondent will bring you the local news.

T4-0267.ex: 저녁 뉴스 앵커가 오늘의 주요 소식을 전했어요.
T4-0267.x: The evening news anchor delivered today's top stories.
T4-0267.e: From English 'anchor', but only the newscaster sense; a ship's anchor is 닻.

T4-0268.ex: 그 프로그램 진행자는 말을 정말 재미있게 해요.
T4-0268.x: That show's host talks in a really fun way.
T4-0268.e: 진행 'running, progress' + -자 'person': the one who runs the show.

T4-0269.ex: 축구 경기는 해설을 들으면서 보면 더 재미있어요.
T4-0269.x: Soccer games are more fun when you listen to the commentary.
T4-0269.t: 해설 adds expert interpretation; 설명 is any ordinary explanation.

T4-0270.ex: 정당은 그 사건에 대해 공식 논평을 냈어요.
T4-0270.x: The party issued an official comment on the incident.

T4-0271.ex: 오늘 신문 사설은 교육 문제를 다루었어요.
T4-0271.x: Today's newspaper editorial dealt with education issues.
T4-0271.e: Literally 'the company's opinion'; a homonym 사설 means 'private', as in 사설 학원.
T4-0271.t: A 사설 gives the newspaper's own position; a 칼럼 is one writer's personal opinion.

T4-0272.ex: 저는 매주 그 교수님의 칼럼을 읽어요.
T4-0272.x: I read that professor's column every week.
T4-0272.e: From English 'column', newspaper sense only; a pillar is 기둥.

T4-0273.ex: 오늘 신문 헤드라인을 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
T4-0273.x: I was shocked when I saw today's newspaper headline.
T4-0273.e: From English 'headline'; Korean also says 제목 'title' or 머리기사 'top story'.

T4-0274.x: Breaking news about an earthquake just came on TV.

T4-0275.ex: 그 기자는 그 사건을 특종으로 보도했어요.
T4-0275.x: The reporter broke the story as an exclusive.
T4-0275.e: Literally 'special kind' of news that only one outlet has.

T4-0276.ex: 기자들이 사고 현장에서 취재를 하고 있어요.
T4-0276.x: Reporters are covering the story at the accident scene.
T4-0276.t: 취재 is collecting the information; 보도 is publishing or airing it.

T4-0277.x: You need to watch out for fake news on the internet.
T4-0277.e: Native 가짜 'fake' + 뉴스 from English 'news'; the opposite of 가짜 is 진짜 'real'.

T4-0278.ex: 젊은 사람들은 주로 인터넷 매체로 뉴스를 봐요.
T4-0278.x: Young people mostly get their news through online media.

T4-0279.ex: 대중 매체는 사람들의 생각에 큰 영향을 줘요.
T4-0279.x: The mass media has a big influence on how people think.
T4-0279.t: Often written as one word, 대중매체.

T4-0280.x: We need education on using the media wisely.

T4-0281.ex: 저는 소셜 미디어에 사진을 자주 올려요.
T4-0281.x: I often post photos on social media.
T4-0281.t: In everyday speech Koreans usually say SNS [에스엔에스] rather than 소셜 미디어.

T4-0282.ex: 그 채널이 좋아서 구독 버튼을 눌렀어요.
T4-0282.x: I liked the channel, so I hit the subscribe button.
T4-0282.e: Literally 'buy to read': first used for newspapers, now for channels too.

T4-0283.ex: 그 유튜버는 구독자가 백만 명이 넘어요.
T4-0283.x: That YouTuber has over a million subscribers.

T4-0284.x: That post got a lot of comments.
T4-0284.e: Literally 'thing put up to show', like a notice on a board.
T4-0284.t: In casual speech people often just say 글 or 게시글 for an online post.

T4-0285.m: to post, to put up (a notice)
T4-0285.x: We posted the exam schedule on the school website.
T4-0285.t: 게시하다 is formal; for your own social media posts, people usually say 올리다.

T4-0286.ex: 그 가수는 악플 때문에 많이 힘들어했어요.
T4-0286.x: The singer had a really hard time because of hateful comments.
T4-0286.e: Short for 악성 리플: 악 'evil' + 플 from English 'reply'.

T4-0287.x: The minister's remark drew criticism from the public.
T4-0287.t: A formal word, often used for public figures' remarks; pronounced [바런].

T4-0288.ex: 시민 단체가 정부를 비판하는 성명을 발표했어요.
T4-0288.x: A civic group released a statement criticizing the government.
T4-0288.e: Literally 'clearly voiced'; a homonym 성명 means 'full name'.
T4-0288.t: Common phrase: 성명을 발표하다 'to issue a statement'.

T4-0289.ex: 회사는 아직 공식 입장을 밝히지 않았어요.
T4-0289.x: The company hasn't announced its official position yet.
T4-0289.e: Literally 'public form'; the same word also means 'formula' in math.

T4-0290.x: The government officially announced the news.
T4-0290.e: 공식 'official' + -적 '-al'; -적 turns nouns into describing words: 사회적, 경제적.
T4-0290.t: Use 공식적인 before a noun and 공식적으로 as an adverb meaning 'officially'.

T4-0291.forms: 주목을 받다 · 받아요 · 받았어요 · 받을 거예요
T4-0291.m: to attract attention, to be in the spotlight
T4-0291.ex: 그 영화는 해외에서도 큰 주목을 받았어요.
T4-0291.x: The movie got a lot of attention overseas too.
T4-0291.e: 주목 is literally 'pouring your eyes' onto something.

T4-0292.forms: 관심을 끌어요 · 끌었어요 · 끌 거예요 · 관심을 끄는 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T4-0292.m: to attract interest, to draw attention
T4-0292.ex: 새로운 스마트폰이 소비자들의 관심을 끌고 있어요.
T4-0292.x: The new smartphone is drawing consumers' interest.
T4-0292.e: 끌다 means 'to pull': pulling people's interest toward you.
T4-0292.t: 관심을 끌다 focuses on the thing doing the attracting; 관심을 받다 focuses on receiving the attention.

T4-0293.m: to be revealed, to come to light, to be found out
T4-0293.x: The investigation revealed the cause of the accident.
T4-0293.e: 밝히다 'to make bright, to reveal' + -어지다 'become': brought into the light.
T4-0293.t: Pronounced [발켜지다]: ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-0294.m: to be reported, to be conveyed; to be handed down
T4-0294.ex: 그 배우가 다음 달에 결혼하는 것으로 전해졌습니다.
T4-0294.x: The actor is reported to be getting married next month.
T4-0294.e: 전하다 'to pass on' + -어지다 'become': to get passed on.
T4-0294.t: News reports often end with ~것으로 전해졌습니다 'it is reported that…'.

T4-0295.m: to be revealed, to come out, to show
T4-0295.ex: 시간이 지나면서 그 사건의 진실이 드러났어요.
T4-0295.x: As time passed, the truth about the incident came out.
T4-0295.t: 드러나다 means something comes out by itself; 드러내다 means someone reveals it.

T4-0296.ex: 한 직원의 폭로로 회사의 비밀이 알려졌어요.
T4-0296.x: The company's secret became known through an employee's revelation.

T4-0297.ex: 그는 가족의 명예를 지키기 위해 노력했어요.
T4-0297.x: He worked hard to protect his family's honor.
T4-0297.e: Literally 'name and praise': a good name.
T4-0297.t: 명예 훼손 'defamation' appears often in news about malicious online comments.

T4-0298.ex: 다른 사람의 사진을 쓸 때는 저작권을 확인하세요.
T4-0298.x: Check the copyright when you use other people's photos.
T4-0298.t: Pronounced [저작꿘]: the ㄱ of 권 is tensed.

T4-0299.ex: 남의 글을 그대로 베끼는 것은 표절이에요.
T4-0299.x: Copying someone else's writing word for word is plagiarism.
T4-0299.e: Literally 'rob and steal': taking someone's work as your own.

T4-0300.x: In that country, the government censors the internet.
T4-0300.e: Literally 'inspect and review' before something may be published.
T4-0300.t: Pronounced [거멸]: the ㅁ moves over to the next syllable.

T4-0301.ex: 이 프로그램은 매주 토요일 밤에 생방송으로 진행돼요.
T4-0301.x: This show airs live every Saturday night.

T4-0302.x: That show isn't live; it's prerecorded.
T4-0302.e: Literally 'recording pictures'; audio recording is 녹음.
T4-0302.t: Pronounced [노콰]: ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-0303.ex: 어제 못 본 드라마를 재방송으로 봤어요.
T4-0303.x: I watched the drama I missed yesterday as a rerun.
T4-0303.e: 재- 'again' + 방송 'broadcast'; 재- = again: 재사용, 재시험.

T4-0304.ex: 그 프로듀서는 인기 예능 프로그램을 많이 만들었어요.
T4-0304.x: That producer has made many popular variety shows.
T4-0304.t: For TV producers Koreans almost always say PD [피디].

T4-0305.x: The production team thanked the viewers.

T4-0306.m: cast member, performer, guest (on a show)
T4-0306.ex: 오늘 방송에는 유명한 출연자들이 많이 나와요.
T4-0306.x: Many famous guests are appearing on today's show.

T4-0307.ex: 아버지는 매일 저녁 시사 프로그램을 보세요.
T4-0307.x: My father watches a current affairs show every evening.

T4-0308.ex: 이 드라마는 여러 기업의 협찬을 받았어요.
T4-0308.x: This drama received sponsorship from several companies.
T4-0308.t: 협찬 usually means a company provides products or money in exchange for exposure on a show.

T4-0309.ex: 그 드라마는 다음 달부터 방영될 예정이에요.
T4-0309.x: That drama is scheduled to air starting next month.

T4-0310.ex: 라디오 진행자가 청취자의 사연을 읽어 줬어요.
T4-0310.x: The radio host read a listener's story.
T4-0310.t: Radio has 청취자, TV has 시청자, and newspapers have 독자.

T4-0311.m: contribution (of an article), contributed piece, op-ed
T4-0311.ex: 그 교수는 신문에 환경에 관한 글을 기고했어요.
T4-0311.x: The professor contributed an article on the environment to the newspaper.
T4-0311.e: Literally 'sending a manuscript' to a publication.

T4-0312.ex: 보고서에 다른 사람의 글을 인용할 때는 출처를 써야 해요.
T4-0312.x: When you quote others' writing in a report, you must cite the source.
T4-0312.t: Pronounced [이뇽]: the ㄴ moves over to the next syllable.

T4-0313.ex: 기사를 쓸 때는 출처를 꼭 밝혀야 해요.
T4-0313.x: When you write an article, you must always cite your sources.
T4-0313.e: Literally 'the place it came out of.'
T4-0313.t: 출처를 밝히다 'to reveal or cite the source' is the key collocation.

T4-0314.ex: 그 기사는 사실을 왜곡했다는 비판을 받았어요.
T4-0314.x: That article was criticized for distorting the facts.

T4-0315.x: It is important for the news to maintain objectivity.
T4-0315.e: Literally 'a guest's view'; -성 = '-ness/-ity': 객관성, 공정성, 신뢰성.
T4-0315.t: Pronounced [객꽌썽] — both 관 and 성 are tensed.

T4-0316.x: Broadcasters must keep their reporting fair.

T4-0317.x: These survey results are highly reliable.
T4-0317.e: Literally 'the quality of being trusted and relied on.'
T4-0317.t: Pronounced [실뢰썽] — ㄴ before ㄹ turns into ㄹ.

T4-0318.ex: 경찰 관계자는 사고 원인을 조사 중이라고 밝혔습니다.
T4-0318.x: A police official said they are investigating the cause of the accident.
T4-0318.e: -자 = person: literally 'a person with a connection' to the matter.
T4-0318.t: The sign 관계자 외 출입 금지 on doors means 'Authorized personnel only.'

T4-0319.x: The health authorities announced new rules.
T4-0319.t: Usually follows a field: 보건 당국 (health), 교육 당국 (education), 금융 당국 (financial).

T4-0320.ex: 회사 측은 아직 공식 입장을 밝히지 않았어요.
T4-0320.x: The company's side has not yet given an official position.
T4-0320.t: Comes after a group name with a space: 회사 측, 경찰 측, 피해자 측 — formal; casual speech uses 쪽.

T4-0321.ex: 정부 대변인은 오늘 오후 기자 회견을 열었습니다.
T4-0321.x: The government spokesperson held a press conference this afternoon.
T4-0321.e: Literally 'a person who speaks on someone's behalf.'

T4-0322.x: The police decided to release the criminal's face.
T4-0322.t: Useful collocations: 정보 공개 'disclosure of information', 공개 사과 'public apology', 공개되다 'to be released'.

T4-0323.x: The meeting was held behind closed doors.

T4-0324.x: That person donated a large sum anonymously.

T4-0325.x: You have to sign up for this site with your real name.
T4-0325.e: Literally 'real name'; don't confuse with the homonym 실명 'loss of sight.'

T4-0326.x: The incident became known thanks to a viewer's tip.

T4-0327.x: The informant did not reveal their name.
T4-0327.e: Literally 'a person who offers a report.'

T4-0328.ex: 이번 사고로 사망자가 세 명 발생했습니다.
T4-0328.x: Three people died in this accident.
T4-0328.t: 사망 is formal news language; in conversation say 죽다, or honorific 돌아가시다 for elders.

T4-0329.x: The injured were taken to a nearby hospital.

T4-0330.ex: 많은 사람들이 희생자의 가족을 위해 기도했어요.
T4-0330.x: Many people prayed for the victims' families.
T4-0330.e: 희생 'sacrifice' originally meant an animal offered in a ritual; + -자 'person.'
T4-0330.t: 희생자 usually implies loss of life; 피해자 is any victim of harm, like fraud or crime.

T4-0331.ex: 경찰이 그 사고의 목격자를 찾고 있어요.
T4-0331.x: The police are looking for witnesses to the accident.
T4-0331.e: Literally 'a person whose eyes were struck' by the event.
T4-0331.t: 목격자 is someone who saw the event; 증인 is someone who testifies in court.

T4-0332.m: to witness, to see with one's own eyes
T4-0332.x: I witnessed a car accident on the street yesterday.
T4-0332.t: Used mostly for accidents, crimes or striking events; for ordinary seeing, just use 보다.

T4-0333.ex: 기자가 사고 현장에서 소식을 전하고 있습니다.
T4-0333.x: A reporter is bringing us the news from the scene of the accident.
T4-0333.e: Literally 'the present place' — where it is actually happening.
T4-0333.t: Also means 'on site' or 'in the field': 현장 학습 is a field trip, 현장 경험 is hands-on experience.

T4-0334.x: The rescue team arrived and saved the people safely.

T4-0335.ex: 소방차 여러 대가 불이 난 건물 앞에 모였어요.
T4-0335.x: Several fire trucks gathered in front of the burning building.

T4-0336.ex: 소방관들이 두 시간 만에 불을 진화했습니다.
T4-0336.x: Firefighters put out the fire in two hours.
T4-0336.e: Literally 'subduing the fire'; don't confuse with the homonym 진화 'evolution.'
T4-0336.t: 진화 is news language (화재가 진화됐다); in everyday speech say 불을 끄다.

T4-0337.ex: 오래된 다리가 붕괴되어 많은 사람이 다쳤습니다.
T4-0337.x: An old bridge collapsed, and many people were injured.
T4-0337.t: The native verb is 무너지다; 붕괴 also works for systems, as in 경제 붕괴 'economic collapse'.

T4-0338.x: A big explosion happened at the factory last night.
T4-0338.t: Also figurative: 인기 폭발 'explosive popularity', 화가 폭발하다 'to explode with anger'.

T4-0339.x: I saw the news that a plane crashed into a mountain.

T4-0340.ex: 배가 침몰하기 전에 승객들이 모두 구조됐어요.
T4-0340.x: All the passengers were rescued before the ship sank.

T4-0341.ex: 태풍 경보가 내려져서 학교가 문을 닫았어요.
T4-0341.x: A typhoon warning was issued, so schools closed.
T4-0341.t: For weather, 주의보 (advisory) is milder and 경보 (warning) is more serious.

T4-0342.ex: 홍수 피해를 복구하는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
T4-0342.x: It took a month to repair the flood damage.
T4-0342.t: 복구 is for damaged places, systems or data (데이터 복구); recovering health is 회복.

T4-0343.x: I gave my parents health supplements as a gift.
T4-0343.t: In Korea, 건강식품 often means supplements like red ginseng (홍삼), a very popular holiday gift.

T4-0344.x: Getting enough sleep improves your immunity.
T4-0344.t: Pronounced [며녕녁] — nasalization; 면역력이 떨어지다 means 'your immunity goes down'.

T4-0345.ex: 한 번 걸린 병에는 면역이 생기기도 해요.
T4-0345.x: You sometimes become immune to a disease you've had once.

T4-0346.x: I'm the type of person who feels the cold a lot.
T4-0346.e: Literally 'body nature'; body types are central to traditional Korean medicine.
T4-0346.t: Common pattern '~는 체질이다' = 'I'm the type who…', e.g. 살이 안 찌는 체질.

T4-0347.x: Vegetables have lots of nutrients that are good for your body.

T4-0348.ex: 운동한 후에는 단백질을 먹는 게 좋아요.
T4-0348.x: It's good to eat protein after working out.
T4-0348.t: Pronounced [단백찔] — 질 is tensed after ㄱ.

T4-0349.ex: 밥과 빵에는 탄수화물이 많이 들어 있어요.
T4-0349.x: Rice and bread contain a lot of carbohydrates.
T4-0349.e: Literally 'carbon-water compound' — a direct translation of 'carbohydrate.'

T4-0350.x: Greasy food has a lot of fat.
T4-0350.t: Homonym alert: another 지방 means 'region, provinces', as in 지방 도시 'provincial city'.

T4-0351.x: These snacks are way too high in calories.
T4-0351.e: From English 'calorie'; note the double ㄹ sound: [칼로리].

T4-0352.x: The number of calories you need per day differs from person to person.
T4-0352.t: 열량 is the formal term on food labels; 칼로리 is the everyday word.

T4-0353.x: My grandmother has an herbal tonic made for me every winter.
T4-0353.e: Literally 'supplementing medicine' — a tonic to build up strength.
T4-0353.t: Herbal medicine is 'made up' with 짓다: 보약을 짓다, 한약을 짓다.

T4-0354.x: Herbal medicine tastes bitter, so it's hard to take.

T4-0355.ex: 요즘 한방 치료를 받는 외국인도 많아요.
T4-0355.x: These days many foreigners also get traditional Korean medical treatment.
T4-0355.e: Literally 'Korean methods/prescriptions'; don't confuse with native 한 방 'one hit, one shot.'

T4-0356.x: My back hurt, so I got acupuncture at a Korean medicine clinic.
T4-0356.e: Homonym warning: native 침 means 'saliva, spit.'
T4-0356.t: You 'receive' acupuncture with 맞다: 침을 맞다, just like 주사를 맞다 'to get a shot'.

T4-0357.x: My head hurt so much that I took a painkiller.
T4-0357.e: Literally 'pain-suppressing drug'; -제 = drug/agent: 진통제, 소화제, 해열제, 수면제.

T4-0358.ex: 점심을 너무 많이 먹어서 소화제를 먹었어요.
T4-0358.x: I ate too much lunch, so I took a digestive aid.
T4-0358.t: Koreans reach for 소화제 when they 체하다 — that heavy, 'blocked' feeling after eating.

T4-0359.x: My child had a fever, so I gave them a fever reducer.
T4-0359.t: Pronounced [해열쩨] — 제 is tensed after ㄹ.

T4-0360.x: Please take sleeping pills only after talking with a doctor.

T4-0361.ex: 의사 선생님이 항생제를 사흘 동안 먹으라고 하셨어요.
T4-0361.x: The doctor told me to take antibiotics for three days.
T4-0361.e: Literally 'anti-life drug' — a direct translation of 'antibiotic' (fights living germs).

T4-0362.ex: 이 약은 하루 세 번 식후에 복용하세요.
T4-0362.x: Take this medicine three times a day after meals.
T4-0362.t: 복용 is formal (labels, doctors); in everyday speech say 약을 먹다.

T4-0363.x: The nurse gave the shot with a new syringe.

T4-0364.x: I had a bad case of body aches, so I got an IV at the hospital.
T4-0364.e: From 'Ringer's (solution)', named after Sydney Ringer; English just says 'IV.'

T4-0365.x: The patient received a blood transfusion during surgery.

T4-0366.ex: 대학생 때 헌혈을 여러 번 했어요.
T4-0366.x: I donated blood several times when I was in college.

T4-0367.ex: 짠 음식을 많이 먹으면 혈관 건강에 안 좋아요.
T4-0367.x: Eating a lot of salty food is bad for your blood vessels.

T4-0368.ex: 한국에서는 혈액형으로 성격을 이야기하는 사람이 많아요.
T4-0368.x: In Korea, many people talk about personality based on blood type.
T4-0368.t: Pronounced [혀래켱]; 혈액형이 뭐예요? is a popular, if unscientific, personality icebreaker.

T4-0369.ex: 단 음식을 먹으면 혈당이 빨리 올라가요.
T4-0369.x: Eating sweet food makes your blood sugar rise quickly.

T4-0370.ex: 아버지는 고혈압 때문에 매일 약을 드세요.
T4-0370.x: My father takes medicine every day for high blood pressure.
T4-0370.e: Literally 'high blood pressure' — a word-for-word match with English.

T4-0371.x: I have low blood pressure, so it's hard to get up in the morning.

T4-0372.ex: 당뇨병이 있으면 단 음식을 조심해야 해요.
T4-0372.x: If you have diabetes, you need to be careful with sweets.
T4-0372.t: Often shortened to 당뇨: 당뇨가 있어요 'I have diabetes'; pronounced [당뇨뼝].

T4-0373.x: The test results showed a small tumor.
T4-0373.t: 양성 종양 is a benign tumor; 악성 종양 is a malignant one.

T4-0374.ex: 담배를 많이 피우면 심장병에 걸리기 쉬워요.
T4-0374.x: If you smoke a lot, you're more likely to get heart disease.

T4-0375.x: My grandfather collapsed from a stroke.
T4-0375.t: Often misspelled 뇌졸증; the correct ending is 중, not 증 'symptom'.

T4-0376.x: My grandmother has dementia, so the family is worried.
T4-0376.e: Literally 'foolish and dull', which is why some people push for a gentler name.
T4-0376.t: 치매 is a disease (치매에 걸리다); everyday forgetfulness is 건망증.

T4-0377.x: As you get older, your knee joints get weaker.
T4-0377.e: Literally 'gate and node' — the hinge points where bones meet.

T4-0378.ex: 어머니는 관절염 때문에 계단을 오르기 힘들어하세요.
T4-0378.x: My mother has a hard time climbing stairs because of arthritis.
T4-0378.t: Pronounced [관절렴] — an ㄴ sound is added before 염 and becomes ㄹ.

T4-0379.x: I fell and fractured my arm.
T4-0379.t: Pronounced [골쩔]; in conversation people usually say 뼈가 부러졌어요.

T4-0380.x: I fell on the stairs and sprained my ankle.
T4-0380.t: For a lighter twist, Koreans say 삐끗하다: 허리를 삐끗했어요 'I tweaked my back'.

T4-0381.ex: 아침에 얼굴에 붓기가 있어서 찬물로 세수했어요.
T4-0381.x: My face was puffy in the morning, so I washed it with cold water.
T4-0381.e: Speakers link it to 붓다 'to swell', but the dictionary spelling is 부기.
T4-0381.t: 붓기가 빠지다 means 'the swelling goes down'.

T4-0382.forms: 멍들어요 · 멍들었어요 · 멍들 거예요 · 멍든 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T4-0382.x: I fell, and my knee got a dark bruise.
T4-0382.t: Also figurative: 마음이 멍들다 'to be hurt deep inside'.

T4-0383.ex: 다행히 큰 부상은 없고 가벼운 타박상만 입었어요.
T4-0383.x: Luckily there was no serious injury, just minor bruises.

T4-0384.ex: 뜨거운 물에 손을 데어서 화상을 입었어요.
T4-0384.x: I burned my hand with hot water.
T4-0384.e: Literally 'fire wound'; a homonym 화상 means 'video', as in 화상 회의.
T4-0384.t: The everyday native verb is 데다: 손을 데었어요 'I burned my hand'.

T4-0385.ex: 어렸을 때 다친 흉터가 아직 남아 있어요.
T4-0385.x: I still have a scar from an injury when I was little.
T4-0385.e: 흉 'scar, blemish' + 터 'site' — the spot a wound leaves behind.

T4-0386.x: The bleeding was bad, so I went straight to the hospital.

T4-0387.x: If you have back pain, don't overdo it.
T4-0387.t: 통증 is physical, medical pain; 고통 also covers emotional suffering.

T4-0388.ex: 그는 오랫동안 병 때문에 고통을 받았어요.
T4-0388.x: He suffered from illness for a long time.

T4-0389.ex: 사랑하는 사람과 헤어지는 것은 정말 고통스러워요.
T4-0389.x: Breaking up with someone you love is truly painful.
T4-0389.e: 고통 'suffering' + -스럽다 'full of'; -스럽다 builds adjectives: 자랑스럽다, 걱정스럽다.

T4-0390.m: to ache, to throb; to poke, to pick
T4-0390.x: My knees ache when it rains.
T4-0390.e: Its basic sense is 'to poke or jab' — the ache feels like being jabbed.
T4-0390.t: A classic complaint: 온몸이 쑤셔요 'My whole body aches', often with flu or before rain.
rel: to have a stiff, sharp ache

T4-0391.m: to feel a stiff, stabbing pain, to have a crick (neck, shoulder, side)
T4-0391.ex: 자고 일어났더니 목이 결려서 고개를 못 돌리겠어요.
T4-0391.x: I woke up with a crick in my neck and can't turn my head.
T4-0391.e: Used for a sharp, stiff pain that hurts when you move or breathe — think 'a crick'.

T4-0392.m: to go numb, to tingle (pins and needles); to ache (heart, figurative)
T4-0392.x: I sat for a long time, and now my legs have fallen asleep.
T4-0392.e: Also figurative: 가슴이 저리다 means 'my heart aches' with sadness.
T4-0392.t: Don't confuse it with 절이다 'to salt, pickle' — both are pronounced [저리다].

T4-0393.x: My eyes really sting because of the smoke.
T4-0393.e: Also 햇볕이 따갑다 'the sun is scorching'.
T4-0393.t: Use 따갑다 for a surface sting (eyes, throat, skin); 쓰리다 for a burning ache, like an empty stomach.

T4-0394.m: to throb, to ache with a pulsing pain
T4-0394.x: The knee I fell on yesterday throbbed all night.
T4-0394.e: 욱신 imitates a throbbing ache; -거리다 means 'keep doing it', as in 욱신욱신.

T4-0395.x: When I'm on a boat for a long time, I feel queasy.
T4-0395.e: Almost always with 속 'insides': 속이 메스껍다 = to feel sick to your stomach.

T4-0396.m: to feel queasy, to churn (stomach); to pound, flutter (heart)
T4-0396.x: I read a book on the bus, and now my stomach is churning.
T4-0396.e: 울렁 pictures a rolling, wavy motion — your stomach rocking like waves; 울렁울렁.
T4-0396.t: Also used for a nervous or excited heart: 가슴이 울렁거리다.

T4-0397.ex: 갑자기 일어나면 어지러움을 느낄 수 있어요.
T4-0397.x: If you stand up suddenly, you may feel dizzy.
T4-0397.e: Noun made from 어지럽다 'dizzy' (ㅂ irregular): 어지러우- + -ㅁ.
T4-0397.t: In everyday speech people usually just say 어지러워요 'I'm dizzy' instead of the noun.

T4-0398.ex: 더운 날씨에 오래 서 있다가 현기증이 났어요.
T4-0398.x: I got dizzy after standing for a long time in the hot weather.
T4-0398.e: Literally 'dazed-energy symptom'. -증 = symptom or condition: 불면증, 우울증.
T4-0398.t: Pronounced [현기쯩]; the usual verb is 나다: 현기증이 나다.

T4-0399.ex: 발표 전에 너무 긴장해서 식은땀이 났어요.
T4-0399.x: I was so nervous before the presentation that I broke out in a cold sweat.
T4-0399.e: 식은 'cooled' (from 식다) + 땀 'sweat' = a cold sweat.

T4-0400.x: My child suffered from a high fever all last night.

T4-0401.ex: 감기에 걸려서 기침할 때마다 가래가 나와요.
T4-0401.x: I have a cold, so phlegm comes up every time I cough.
T4-0401.e: Homonym warning: 가래 is also a farm spade and a stick of rice cake (가래떡).
T4-0401.t: 'Phlegm comes up' is 가래가 나오다; 'to spit out phlegm' is 가래를 뱉다.

T4-0402.ex: 천식이 있어서 찬 공기를 마시면 기침이 나요.
T4-0402.x: I have asthma, so I cough when I breathe cold air.

T4-0403.ex: 봄만 되면 비염 때문에 콧물이 계속 나요.
T4-0403.x: Every spring my nose won't stop running because of my allergies.
T4-0403.e: Literally 'nose inflammation'. -염 = inflammation: 위염, 장염, 폐렴.
T4-0403.t: Koreans use 비염 casually for hay fever; the full term is 알레르기성 비염.

T4-0404.x: My grandmother's cold got worse, and she was hospitalized with pneumonia.
T4-0404.t: Spelled 폐렴 with ㄹ, unlike 위염 or 장염 — just memorize it; pronounced [페렴].

T4-0405.x: I ate spoiled food and came down with a stomach bug.
T4-0405.t: Pronounced [장념] — an ㄴ sound is inserted before 여.

T4-0406.ex: 요즘 스트레스 때문에 위염이 생긴 것 같아요.
T4-0406.x: I think I've developed gastritis from stress lately.

T4-0407.ex: 전염병을 막으려면 손을 자주 씻어야 합니다.
T4-0407.x: To prevent infectious diseases, you should wash your hands often.
T4-0407.e: Literally 'passed-on staining disease' — it spreads like dye.

T4-0408.ex: 오늘 확진자가 백 명 넘게 나왔습니다.
T4-0408.x: More than 100 confirmed cases were reported today.
T4-0408.e: Literally 'person with a certain diagnosis'. -자 = person: 환자, 운전자.
T4-0408.t: An everyday word since COVID-19; the news says 확진자가 나오다 or 확진자가 발생하다.

T4-0409.ex: 확진자는 일주일 동안 집에서 격리를 해야 했어요.
T4-0409.x: Confirmed cases had to isolate at home for a week.

T4-0410.x: I went to the clinic to get a flu shot.
T4-0410.e: From 'vaccine'; the v sound becomes ㅂ in Korean.
T4-0410.t: You 'get' a vaccine with 맞다: 백신을 맞다, not 받다.

T4-0411.ex: 아이들은 정해진 시기에 예방 접종을 받아야 해요.
T4-0411.x: Children need to get their vaccinations at set times.
T4-0411.e: Literally 'prevent beforehand' plus 'graft a seed' — planting immunity in advance.
T4-0411.t: Say 예방 접종을 하다/받다; with 주사 it's 예방 주사를 맞다.

T4-0412.ex: 미세먼지가 심한 날에는 마스크를 꼭 써요.
T4-0412.x: On days with bad fine dust, I always wear a mask.
T4-0412.e: From English 'mask'; in Korean it usually means a face mask.
T4-0412.t: Put a mask on with 쓰다 (or 끼다) and take it off with 벗다.

T4-0413.ex: 정부는 전염병을 막기 위해 방역을 강화했습니다.
T4-0413.x: The government tightened disease-control measures to stop the epidemic.

T4-0414.ex: 식당은 위생 관리를 철저히 해야 합니다.
T4-0414.x: Restaurants must keep strict hygiene standards.

T4-0415.x: Hospitals must always be kept clean.

T4-0416.ex: 가게 입구에 손 소독제가 놓여 있어요.
T4-0416.x: There's hand sanitizer at the store entrance.
T4-0416.e: Literally 'poison-removing agent'. -제 = medicine or agent: 해열제, 진통제.

T4-0417.ex: 손에는 눈에 보이지 않는 병균이 많아요.
T4-0417.x: There are lots of invisible germs on your hands.
T4-0417.t: 세균 is the general word for bacteria; 병균 stresses germs that cause disease.

T4-0418.ex: 우리 몸은 수많은 세포로 이루어져 있어요.
T4-0418.x: Our bodies are made up of countless cells.

T4-0419.ex: 키는 유전의 영향을 많이 받는다고 해요.
T4-0419.x: They say height is strongly influenced by genetics.
T4-0419.e: Literally 'left behind and passed on'. Homonym: 유전 'oil field'.
T4-0419.t: For diseases, use 유전되다: 이 병은 유전돼요 'This disease is hereditary.'

T4-0420.ex: 이 병은 유전자 검사로 미리 알 수 있어요.
T4-0420.x: This disease can be detected early with a genetic test.
T4-0420.e: Literally 'heredity unit'; -자 here means a tiny unit, as in 원자 'atom'.

T4-0421.ex: 의료진 덕분에 환자가 빨리 회복할 수 있었어요.
T4-0421.x: Thanks to the medical staff, the patient was able to recover quickly.
T4-0421.e: Literally 'medical-treatment lineup'. -진 = a team or lineup: 취재진, 코치진.

T4-0422.ex: 정확한 진단을 위해 전문의에게 진료를 받으세요.
T4-0422.x: See a specialist for an accurate diagnosis.
T4-0422.t: Pronounced [전무늬]; specialists name their field, e.g. 피부과 전문의 'dermatologist'.

T4-0423.ex: 주치의 선생님이 수술 결과를 설명해 주셨어요.
T4-0423.x: My attending doctor explained the results of the surgery.

T4-0424.m: caring for a sick person, nursing care
T4-0424.ex: 어머니가 아버지의 간병을 혼자 하고 계세요.
T4-0424.x: My mother is taking care of my sick father by herself.
T4-0424.t: 간호 is professional nursing; 간병 is hands-on daily care, often by family or a hired caregiver.

T4-0425.ex: 가족이 모두 바빠서 간병인을 따로 구했어요.
T4-0425.x: Everyone in our family was busy, so we hired a caregiver.
T4-0425.e: Literally 'person who watches over illness'. -인 = person: 외국인, 직장인.

T4-0426.ex: 사고 환자는 지금 중환자실에서 치료를 받고 있습니다.
T4-0426.x: The accident victim is now being treated in the ICU.

T4-0427.ex: 다친 사람에게 먼저 응급 처치를 했어요.
T4-0427.x: I gave first aid to the injured person first.
T4-0427.e: Literally 'responding to an emergency' plus 'handling it'.

T4-0428.ex: 쓰러진 사람에게 심폐 소생술을 해서 생명을 구했어요.
T4-0428.x: They saved a collapsed person's life by performing CPR.
T4-0428.e: Literally 'heart-lung revival technique'. -술 = skill, technique: 기술, 수술.

T4-0429.ex: 수술 전에 마취를 해서 하나도 안 아팠어요.
T4-0429.x: They gave me anesthesia before the surgery, so it didn't hurt at all.

T4-0430.ex: 보험이 있어서 진료비가 많이 나오지 않았어요.
T4-0430.x: I have insurance, so the medical bill wasn't much.
T4-0430.t: Pronounced [질료비] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T4-0431.ex: 회사에서 일 년에 한 번 검진을 받아요.
T4-0431.x: I get a checkup through my company once a year.

T4-0432.x: I go to the dentist for a regular checkup every six months.

T4-0433.x: I got an X-ray to see if my arm was broken.
T4-0433.e: From English 'X-ray'; the letter X is said 엑스.
T4-0433.t: You 'take' an X-ray with 찍다: 엑스레이를 찍다.

T4-0434.ex: 임신 중에 초음파로 아기를 처음 봤어요.
T4-0434.x: During my pregnancy, I saw the baby for the first time on an ultrasound.
T4-0434.e: Literally 'beyond-sound wave' — sound too high to hear.

T4-0435.ex: 내일 위 내시경을 해서 오늘 밤부터 굶어야 해요.
T4-0435.x: I'm having a gastroscopy tomorrow, so I have to fast from tonight.
T4-0435.t: 수면 내시경, endoscopy under light sedation, is very common in Korean checkups.

T4-0436.ex: 혈액 검사 결과는 일주일 후에 나와요.
T4-0436.x: The blood test results come out in a week.
T4-0436.t: Pronounced [혀랙 검사]; in casual speech people say 피 검사.

T4-0437.ex: 검사를 위해 소변을 이 컵에 받아 주세요.
T4-0437.x: Please collect your urine in this cup for the test.
T4-0437.t: 소변 is neutral and medical; 오줌 is the casual word.

T4-0438.x: The hospital told me to get a stool test.
T4-0438.e: Literally 'big excretion' — the word for poop.
T4-0438.t: 대변 is medical and polite; 똥 is the casual word.

T4-0439.x: When I checked with a thermometer, my temperature was 38 degrees.
T4-0439.e: Literally 'body-warmth meter'. -계 = measuring device: 온도계, 시계.

T4-0440.ex: 다리 수술 후에 몇 달 동안 재활 치료를 받았어요.
T4-0440.x: After leg surgery, I did rehab therapy for several months.

T4-0441.ex: 꾸준히 치료를 받으면 이 병은 완치될 수 있어요.
T4-0441.x: With steady treatment, this disease can be completely cured.

T4-0442.m: to improve, to take a turn for the better (health, situation)
T4-0442.ex: 약을 바꾼 후로 증상이 많이 호전됐어요.
T4-0442.x: Since I changed medication, my symptoms have improved a lot.
T4-0442.t: Formal; in conversation people usually say 좋아지다 instead.

T4-0443.ex: 치료를 미루면 병이 악화될 수 있어요.
T4-0443.x: If you put off treatment, the illness can get worse.
T4-0443.t: Pronounced [아콰] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-0444.ex: 허리 통증이 재발해서 다시 병원에 갔어요.
T4-0444.x: My back pain came back, so I went to the hospital again.

T4-0445.ex: 만성 피로를 줄이려면 잠을 충분히 자야 해요.
T4-0445.x: To reduce chronic fatigue, you need to get enough sleep.
T4-0445.e: Literally 'slow nature'. -성 = nature, quality: 급성, 가능성.

T4-0446.x: Last night I went to the ER with acute gastroenteritis.

T4-0447.ex: 감기 증세가 있으면 집에서 푹 쉬세요.
T4-0447.x: If you have cold symptoms, get plenty of rest at home.
T4-0447.t: 증상 is a specific symptom; 증세 is the overall state of an illness, but they often overlap.

T4-0448.ex: 요즘은 정신과 상담을 받는 사람이 많아졌어요.
T4-0448.x: These days more people get counseling at psychiatric clinics.
T4-0448.e: Literally 'mind department'. -과 = medical department: 내과, 안과, 치과.
T4-0448.t: Pronounced [정신꽈]; many clinics now use the official name 정신건강의학과.

T4-0449.x: Talking with the school counselor put my mind at ease.
T4-0449.e: Literally 'consultation professional'. -사 = qualified professional: 변호사, 회계사.

T4-0450.ex: 시험을 앞두고 불안감 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
T4-0450.x: Ahead of the exam, I couldn't sleep because of anxiety.
T4-0450.t: Pronounced [부란감]; the usual verb is 느끼다: 불안감을 느끼다.

T4-0451.x: Getting enough sleep is very important for your health.
T4-0451.e: Both syllables mean 'sleep'. Homonym: 수면 'water surface'.
T4-0451.t: 수면 is formal or medical; in everyday speech say 잠.

T4-0452.ex: 요즘은 아무리 자도 피로감이 계속 남아 있어요.
T4-0452.x: These days, no matter how much I sleep, the tiredness doesn't go away.

T4-0453.x: My father collapsed from overwork and was hospitalized.
T4-0453.e: Literally 'excessive labor'. 과- = over-, too much: 과식, 과음.
T4-0453.t: 과로사 means 'death from overwork,' a serious social issue in Korea.

T4-0454.ex: 더운 날 물도 안 마시고 운동하다가 탈진했어요.
T4-0454.x: I exercised on a hot day without drinking water and got completely exhausted.
T4-0454.e: Literally 'stripped and used up' — every bit of energy is gone.

T4-0455.ex: 나이가 들수록 근력 운동을 꾸준히 해야 해요.
T4-0455.x: The older you get, the more you need to do strength training regularly.
T4-0455.e: Literally 'muscle power'. -력 = power, ability: 체력, 능력.
T4-0455.t: Pronounced [글력] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T4-0456.ex: 살을 빼려면 유산소 운동을 매일 30분씩 하세요.
T4-0456.x: To lose weight, do 30 minutes of cardio every day.

T4-0457.x: The doctor told me to quit drinking for my health.
T4-0457.e: Literally 'forbid alcohol'. 금- = banning: 금연, 금지.
T4-0457.t: Homonym: in formal writing 금주 can also mean 'this week.'

T4-0458.ex: 어제 과음해서 오늘 머리가 너무 아파요.
T4-0458.x: I drank too much yesterday, so my head really hurts today.

T4-0459.ex: 저녁에 과식하면 밤에 잠을 잘 못 자요.
T4-0459.x: If I overeat at dinner, I can't sleep well at night.

T4-0460.ex: 우리 아이는 편식이 심해서 채소를 안 먹어요.
T4-0460.x: My child is a really picky eater and won't eat vegetables.
T4-0460.t: Parents often say 편식하지 말고 골고루 먹어 'Don't be picky — eat a bit of everything.'

T4-0461.x: UV rays are a major cause of skin aging.

T4-0462.ex: 한국인의 평균 수명은 계속 늘어나고 있습니다.
T4-0462.x: Koreans' average life expectancy keeps rising.
T4-0462.e: Literally 'even and equal' plus 'span of life'.

T4-0463.ex: 할아버지는 장수의 비결이 규칙적인 생활이라고 하세요.
T4-0463.x: My grandfather says the secret to a long life is a regular routine.
T4-0463.e: Literally 'long life'. Homonym: 장수 also means 'merchant' or 'general'.
T4-0463.t: To wish an elder a long life, say 오래오래 건강하세요.

T4-0464.x: My older sister gave birth to a healthy son last week.

T4-0465.ex: 아내가 임신 중이라서 요즘 같이 술을 안 마셔요.
T4-0465.x: My wife is pregnant, so these days we don't drink.
T4-0465.t: 임신하다 = to get pregnant; 임신 중이다 = to be pregnant; 임신 몇 개월이에요? asks how far along.

T4-0466.ex: 지하철에는 임산부를 위한 자리가 따로 있어요.
T4-0466.x: The subway has seats set aside for pregnant women.
T4-0466.t: Seoul subways have pink 임산부 배려석 seats reserved for pregnant women.

T4-0467.x: I went to the OB-GYN today to check whether I was pregnant.

T4-0468.ex: 신생아는 하루에 열여섯 시간 넘게 잔다고 해요.
T4-0468.x: They say newborns sleep more than sixteen hours a day.

T4-0469.m: cosmetic surgery, plastic surgery; molding, shaping
T4-0469.x: These days, a lot of men get cosmetic surgery too.

T4-0470.ex: 그 배우는 성형 수술을 받았다는 소문이 있어요.
T4-0470.x: There's a rumor that the actor had plastic surgery.
T4-0470.t: Surgery is something you receive: 성형 수술을 받다 means 'to get plastic surgery'.

T4-0471.x: My eyesight got worse, so I started wearing glasses.
T4-0471.t: Use 좋다/나쁘다 with it: 시력이 좋아요 'I have good eyesight'.

T4-0472.ex: 나이가 들면 청력이 약해질 수 있어요.
T4-0472.x: Your hearing can get weaker as you get older.
T4-0472.t: Pronounced [청녁] — the ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T4-0473.x: In Korea, parents are extremely passionate about education.
T4-0473.t: Pronounced [교융녈] — an ㄴ is added before 열, then ㄱ nasalizes.

T4-0474.x: The Ministry of Education announced a new admissions system.

T4-0475.ex: 정부는 공교육을 강화하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
T4-0475.x: The government is working to strengthen public education.

T4-0476.ex: 많은 학생들이 방과 후에 학원에서 사교육을 받아요.
T4-0476.x: Many students get private tutoring at cram schools after school.
T4-0476.t: It means tutoring and cram schools outside regular school, not attending a private school.

T4-0477.x: Tutoring costs put a heavy burden on parents.

T4-0478.x: Elementary school kids are playing happily on the playground.

T4-0479.x: I learned English for the first time when I was in middle school.

T4-0480.x: Korean high school students study until late at night.

T4-0481.m: exam taker, test candidate (esp. for the college entrance exam)
T4-0481.ex: 수능 날 아침에 수험생들이 시험장으로 들어가고 있어요.
T4-0481.x: On the morning of the CSAT, test takers are heading into the exam halls.
T4-0481.t: Usually means high school seniors preparing for the 수능, though it works for any big exam.

T4-0482.m: studying a year to retake the college entrance exam
T4-0482.ex: 원하는 대학에 떨어져서 재수를 하기로 했어요.
T4-0482.x: I didn't get into the college I wanted, so I decided to retake the exam next year.
T4-0482.t: Don't confuse it with 재수 'luck': 재수 없다 means 'unlucky' or, rudely, 'obnoxious'.

T4-0483.m: student retaking the college entrance exam (after a year of study)
T4-0483.ex: 재수생은 일 년 동안 학원에서 수능을 준비해요.
T4-0483.x: Repeat students spend a year preparing for the CSAT at cram schools.

T4-0484.x: The CSAT is usually taken every November.
T4-0484.e: Short for 대학수학능력시험, 'College Scholastic Ability Test'.
T4-0484.t: Exams are 'seen' in Korean: 수능을 보다 means 'to take the CSAT'.

T4-0485.x: That school's entrance exam is really hard.
T4-0485.t: Pronounced [이팍씨험] — ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T4-0486.x: I passed the written driver's license test on the first try.

T4-0487.x: My score on this practice test went up from last time.

T4-0488.m: early admission (non-CSAT college admission); any time, frequently
T4-0488.ex: 저는 이번 수시에서 원하는 대학에 합격했어요.
