T4-0488.x: I got into the college I wanted through early admission this time.
T4-0488.e: Literally 'following the time'; short for 수시 모집, admissions held through the fall.
T4-0488.t: As an adverb, 수시로 means 'frequently, at any time': 수시로 확인하세요.

T4-0489.m: regular admission (CSAT-based); fixed time, on time
T4-0489.ex: 수시에 떨어지면 정시로 다시 지원할 수 있어요.
T4-0489.x: If you fail early admission, you can apply again through regular admission.
T4-0489.e: Literally 'fixed time'; short for 정시 모집, admissions after CSAT scores come out.

T4-0490.ex: 올해는 지원자가 작년보다 두 배나 많아요.
T4-0490.x: This year there are twice as many applicants as last year.
T4-0490.e: -자 = person who does it: 지원자, 연구자, 학습자.

T4-0491.x: The pass rate for this exam is around 30 percent.
T4-0491.t: Pronounced [합꼉뉼]; the suffix is 율 after a vowel or ㄴ (비율), 률 elsewhere.

T4-0492.ex: 그 회사는 학력보다 경험을 더 중요하게 생각해요.
T4-0492.x: That company values experience more than educational background.
T4-0492.e: Literally 'study history' — your record of schooling.
T4-0492.t: Pronounced [항녁]; a homonym 학력 means 'academic ability', so context decides.

T4-0493.m: academic pedigree (prestige of one's school); academic elitism
T4-0493.ex: 한국 사회에서는 아직도 학벌을 중요하게 여겨요.
T4-0493.x: Korean society still places a lot of weight on which school you went to.
T4-0493.t: 학력 is how far you studied; 학벌 is how prestigious your school was.

T4-0494.x: He graduated from a top university and joined a major company.
T4-0494.e: Literally 'famous-gate university'; short for 명문 대학.

T4-0495.x: I studied nursing at a junior college.

T4-0496.m: undergraduate (studies); school, faculty (division of a university)
T4-0496.x: I majored in economics as an undergraduate.

T4-0497.x: Grad students work late in the lab.

T4-0498.m: master's degree; holder of a master's
T4-0498.x: She got her master's degree in the U.S.

T4-0499.x: My uncle has a Ph.D. in physics.
T4-0499.t: Also used playfully for an expert: 컴퓨터 박사 means 'computer whiz'.

T4-0500.ex: 학사 학위가 있어야 이 일에 지원할 수 있어요.
T4-0500.x: You need a bachelor's degree to apply for this job.

T4-0501.ex: 졸업생들이 학교에 와서 후배들에게 조언을 해 줬어요.
T4-0501.x: Graduates came to the school and gave advice to younger students.

T4-0502.ex: 이 도서관은 재학생만 이용할 수 있어요.
T4-0502.x: Only current students can use this library.

T4-0503.x: In March, the campus fills up with freshmen.
T4-0503.t: Korean school years start in March, so that's when 신입생 arrive.

T4-0504.ex: 그는 다른 대학교로 편입을 준비하고 있어요.
T4-0504.x: He's preparing to transfer to another university.
T4-0504.e: Literally 'arranged into' — joining a school partway through.
T4-0504.t: 편입 is for colleges; for elementary through high school, use 전학.

T4-0505.ex: 아버지 회사 때문에 서울로 전학을 갔어요.
T4-0505.x: I transferred to a school in Seoul because of my dad's job.
T4-0505.t: Common patterns are 전학을 가다 (move away) and 전학을 오다 (arrive as a transfer).

T4-0506.x: He dropped out of school because of health problems.
T4-0506.t: 자퇴 is your own choice; 퇴학 means being expelled.

T4-0507.m: returning to school (after a leave of absence)
T4-0507.x: After finishing military service, I'll go back to school next year.
T4-0507.t: Pronounced [보칵]; very common for Korean men after military service.

T4-0508.ex: 그는 일과 학업을 함께 하느라 바빠요.
T4-0508.x: He's busy juggling work and school.

T4-0509.x: I got my report card and showed it to my parents.

T4-0510.x: I emailed my professor a question.
T4-0510.t: Always add -님 when talking to or about your professor, and use 께 instead of 에게.

T4-0511.ex: 교직원 식당은 학생들도 이용할 수 있어요.
T4-0511.x: Students can also use the faculty and staff cafeteria.

T4-0512.x: The principal gave a speech at the graduation ceremony.
T4-0512.t: Usually said as 교장 선생님, with honorific verb endings.

T4-0513.x: The vice principal gave the students a warning.

T4-0514.ex: 과제에 대해 궁금한 점은 조교에게 물어보세요.
T4-0514.x: Ask the TA if you have questions about the assignment.

T4-0515.x: He lived his whole life as a respected educator.
T4-0515.e: -자 = person who does it: 교육자, 연구자, 학습자.

T4-0516.ex: 주입식 교육은 학생들의 창의력을 키우기 어려워요.
T4-0516.x: Rote education makes it hard for students to develop creativity.
T4-0516.e: Literally 'pour-in style' — stuffing facts into students.
T4-0516.t: Almost always appears as 주입식 교육 'rote education', usually in criticism.

T4-0517.ex: 학생 수준에 맞는 맞춤형 수업을 제공해요.
T4-0517.x: We offer customized lessons that fit each student's level.
T4-0517.t: Pronounced [맏춤형]; works before many nouns: 맞춤형 서비스, 맞춤형 교육.

T4-0518.ex: 이 내용은 고등학교 교과에 포함되어 있어요.
T4-0518.x: This content is included in the high school curriculum.

T4-0519.ex: 이번 학기에 다섯 과목을 수강하고 있어요.
T4-0519.x: I'm taking five classes this semester.

T4-0520.m: course registration, signing up for classes
T4-0520.ex: 수강 신청 날에는 인기 과목이 몇 분 만에 마감돼요.
T4-0520.x: On registration day, popular classes fill up in a few minutes.
T4-0520.t: Students jokingly call the scramble for seats 수강 신청 전쟁, 'the registration war'.

T4-0521.x: The teacher called our names while looking at the roll.

T4-0522.x: I have to turn in my paper by Friday.
T4-0522.e: From English 'report'; at Korean colleges it means a term paper or written assignment.

T4-0523.x: I crammed for the exam the night before.
T4-0523.e: From 벼락 'lightning' + 치다 'to strike': studying at lightning speed.
T4-0523.t: Common patterns are 벼락치기하다 and 벼락치기로 공부하다.

T4-0524.ex: 시험 중에 커닝을 하다가 선생님께 걸렸어요.
T4-0524.x: I got caught by the teacher while cheating on the test.
T4-0524.e: From English 'cunning' — but in Korean it means cheating on an exam.
T4-0524.t: Don't use 'cunning' in English for this; Americans say 'cheating'.

T4-0525.x: Anyone caught cheating during the exam gets a zero.

T4-0526.x: The teacher graded exam papers until late at night.

T4-0527.ex: 이 앱은 초급 학습자에게 특히 도움이 돼요.
T4-0527.x: This app is especially helpful for beginner learners.
T4-0527.e: -자 = person who does it: 학습자, 연구자, 교육자.

T4-0528.t: Pronounced [도칵]; 독학으로 배우다 means 'to teach yourself'.

T4-0529.ex: 철학은 아주 오래된 학문 중 하나예요.
T4-0529.x: Philosophy is one of the oldest academic disciplines.

T4-0530.ex: 이 논문은 학문적으로 큰 가치가 있어요.
T4-0530.x: This paper has great academic value.
T4-0530.e: -적 turns a noun into '-ic/-al': 학문적, 과학적, 경제적.

T4-0531.ex: 그는 한국 역사를 연구하는 유명한 학자예요.
T4-0531.x: He's a well-known scholar who studies Korean history.

T4-0532.ex: 그 연구 결과는 학계에서 큰 관심을 받았어요.
T4-0532.x: The research findings drew a lot of attention in academia.

T4-0533.ex: 다음 달에 일본에서 열리는 학회에 참석해요.
T4-0533.x: Next month I'm attending a conference in Japan.

T4-0534.x: The professor is in his office right now.
T4-0534.t: A professor's office is also called 연구실, not 사무실.

T4-0535.ex: 많은 연구자들이 이 문제를 해결하려고 노력하고 있어요.
T4-0535.x: Many researchers are trying to solve this problem.
T4-0535.e: -자 = person who does it: 연구자, 학습자, 교육자.

T4-0536.m: field trip, study visit, tour (for learning)
T4-0536.x: The kids went on a field trip to a TV station.

T4-0537.x: In my junior year of high school, we went on a school trip to Gyeongju.
T4-0537.e: Literally 'study travel' — this 수학 is not the 'math' 수학.
T4-0537.t: Pronounced [수항녀행] — an ㄴ is added before 여.

T4-0538.x: The student council is preparing the school festival.

T4-0539.ex: 학생증을 보여 주면 할인을 받을 수 있어요.
T4-0539.x: You can get a discount if you show your student ID.

T4-0540.x: You can't smoke on school grounds.
T4-0540.t: Mostly used with 에서 or before nouns: 교내 식당, 교내 대회.

T4-0541.m: going to school, arriving at school
T4-0541.ex: 아이들은 매일 아침 여덟 시에 등교해요.
T4-0541.x: The kids go to school at eight every morning.
T4-0541.t: 등교하다 and 하교하다 mirror 출근하다 and 퇴근하다 for workers.

T4-0542.m: leaving school (for the day), going home from school
T4-0542.ex: 하교 시간이 되면 학교 앞이 복잡해져요.
T4-0542.x: When school lets out, the area in front of the school gets crowded.

T4-0543.m: going on to the next level of school (e.g. college)
T4-0543.x: He's thinking about going on to grad school.

T4-0544.x: High school students worry a lot about their future path.
T4-0544.t: Pronounced [질로] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T4-0545.ex: 요즘 한국 학교에서는 체벌이 금지되어 있어요.
T4-0545.x: Corporal punishment is banned in Korean schools these days.

T4-0546.x: At school, character education matters as much as grades.
T4-0546.t: Koreans often judge someone with 인성이 좋다/나쁘다 'a good/bad person at heart'.

T4-0547.ex: 요즘 학교에서는 학생들의 창의성을 키우는 교육이 중요해요.
T4-0547.x: These days, education that develops students' creativity is important in schools.
T4-0547.e: Literally 'the quality of creating ideas'; -성 = '-ness, -ity': 가능성, 중요성.
T4-0547.t: Pronounced [창의썽] or [창이썽]; the -성 suffix is usually tensed to [썽].

T4-0548.ex: 독서는 아이들의 사고력을 기르는 데 도움이 됩니다.
T4-0548.x: Reading helps develop children's thinking skills.
T4-0548.e: Literally 'power of thinking'; -력 = ability, power: 기억력, 집중력, 이해력.
T4-0548.t: Don't confuse 사고 (思考, thinking) with its homonym 사고 (事故, accident).

T4-0549.ex: 그 학생은 이해력이 좋아서 설명을 금방 알아들어요.
T4-0549.x: That student has good comprehension, so he understands explanations right away.

T4-0550.ex: 글을 많이 쓰면 표현력이 좋아질 거예요.
T4-0550.x: If you write a lot, your ability to express yourself will improve.
T4-0550.t: Pronounced [표현녁]: ㄴ+ㄹ makes the ㄹ sound like ㄴ.

T4-0551.ex: 최근 청소년들의 문해력이 떨어졌다는 기사가 많습니다.
T4-0551.x: There have been many articles recently saying teenagers' literacy has declined.
T4-0551.t: A popular news buzzword; it means understanding what you read, not just being able to read.

T4-0552.ex: 잠을 충분히 못 자면 집중력이 떨어져요.
T4-0552.x: If you don't get enough sleep, your concentration drops.
T4-0552.e: Literally 'power to gather into the center'.

T4-0553.ex: 할머니는 연세가 많으신데도 기억력이 정말 좋으세요.
T4-0553.x: Even though my grandmother is quite old, her memory is really good.
T4-0553.t: Pronounced [기엉녁]: ㄱ becomes ㅇ and ㄹ becomes ㄴ.

T4-0554.x: In urgent situations, quick judgment is needed.

T4-0555.ex: 저는 방학 동안 서울에서 어학연수를 했어요.
T4-0555.x: I did a language study program in Seoul during the break.
T4-0555.t: Most common in compounds: 어학연수 (language program abroad), 어학원 (language institute), 어학 점수 (test score).

T4-0556.x: That person speaks Korean really fluently.
T4-0556.t: Usually as an adverb: 한국어를 유창하게 하다 'to speak Korean fluently'.

T4-0557.ex: 원어민 선생님과 매주 회화 수업을 해요.
T4-0557.x: I have a conversation class with a native-speaker teacher every week.
T4-0557.t: 원어민처럼 말하다 means 'to speak like a native'.

T4-0558.ex: 제 모국어는 영어지만 한국어도 조금 할 수 있어요.
T4-0558.x: My native language is English, but I can speak a little Korean too.

T4-0559.ex: 바빠서 요즘은 문화생활을 즐길 시간이 없어요.
T4-0559.x: I'm so busy that I have no time to enjoy cultural activities these days.
T4-0559.t: Koreans use it for going to movies, concerts or exhibitions: 문화생활을 하다/즐기다.

T4-0560.ex: 이 영화는 재미와 예술성을 모두 갖추었어요.
T4-0560.x: This movie has both entertainment value and artistic quality.

T4-0561.ex: 그 건물은 예술적인 가치가 아주 높습니다.
T4-0561.x: That building has very high artistic value.
T4-0561.e: -적 turns a noun into '-ic/-al': 예술적, 경제적, 문화적.
T4-0561.t: Use 예술적인 before a noun and 예술적으로 as an adverb.

T4-0562.ex: 그 영화는 흥행은 못 했지만 작품성은 인정받았어요.
T4-0562.x: That movie wasn't a box-office hit, but its artistic merit was recognized.
T4-0562.t: Often contrasted with 흥행 or 대중성: 작품성은 좋은데 흥행은 실패했다.

T4-0563.x: This novel is a classic that has been loved for a long time.

T4-0564.ex: 많은 사람들이 그 그림을 화가의 최고 걸작으로 꼽아요.
T4-0564.x: Many people consider that painting the artist's greatest masterpiece.
T4-0564.t: Pronounced [걸짝]; casually 걸작이다 can also mean something is hilarious.

T4-0565.ex: 이 영화는 그 감독의 대표작 중 하나예요.
T4-0565.x: This film is one of that director's best-known works.

T4-0566.ex: 좋아하는 작가의 신작이 다음 달에 나와요.
T4-0566.x: My favorite author's new work comes out next month.

T4-0567.ex: 이 드라마는 인기 웹툰을 원작으로 만들었어요.
T4-0567.x: This drama was made based on a popular webtoon.
T4-0567.t: Useful pattern: A를 원작으로 하다 'to be based on A'.

T4-0568.ex: 그는 요즘 새 소설 창작에 집중하고 있어요.
T4-0568.x: He is focusing on writing a new novel these days.

T4-0569.ex: 그 가수는 자기 노래의 작곡도 직접 해요.
T4-0569.x: That singer composes their own songs too.

T4-0570.x: Mozart was a famous 18th-century Austrian composer.

T4-0571.ex: 이 노래는 멤버들이 직접 작사를 했어요.
T4-0571.x: The members wrote the lyrics for this song themselves.
T4-0571.t: Watch out: 작사가 can be 'lyricist' or 작사 plus subject particle 가.

T4-0572.ex: 그 작사가는 아이돌 노래 가사를 많이 썼어요.
T4-0572.x: That lyricist wrote the lyrics for many idol songs.

T4-0573.ex: 이 곡은 선율이 아름다워서 자주 들어요.
T4-0573.x: This piece has a beautiful melody, so I listen to it often.
T4-0573.e: Literally 'circling tones'; a more literary word than 멜로디.
T4-0573.t: Pronounced [서뉼]; the ㄴ links over, and 률 becomes 율 after a ㄴ batchim.

T4-0574.ex: 그 노래는 멜로디가 쉬워서 금방 따라 부를 수 있어요.
T4-0574.x: That song has an easy melody, so you can sing along right away.

T4-0575.ex: 아이들이 음악 리듬에 맞춰 춤을 추고 있어요.
T4-0575.x: The children are dancing to the rhythm of the music.
T4-0575.e: From English 'rhythm'; Korean adds a vowel: 리-듬.
T4-0575.t: Common pattern: 리듬에 맞춰 'in time with the rhythm'; also 생활 리듬 'daily rhythm'.

T4-0576.ex: 노래할 때 박자를 잘 맞추는 것이 중요해요.
T4-0576.x: When singing, it's important to keep the beat well.
T4-0576.e: Literally 'clap'; 박수 'applause' shares the same 박.
T4-0576.t: Pronounced [박짜]; collocations: 박자를 맞추다 (keep time), 박자를 놓치다 (miss the beat).

T4-0577.ex: 저는 악보를 볼 줄 몰라서 귀로 듣고 연주해요.
T4-0577.x: I can't read sheet music, so I play by ear.
T4-0577.t: 'To read sheet music' is 악보를 보다 or 악보를 읽다.

T4-0578.ex: 주말에 오케스트라 공연을 보러 갈 거예요.
T4-0578.x: I'm going to see an orchestra performance this weekend.
T4-0578.e: From English 'orchestra'; each consonant cluster gets its own ㅡ vowel.

T4-0579.x: Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 is famous around the world.
T4-0579.e: Literally 'piece where sounds mingle and resound'.

T4-0580.ex: 오늘 공연은 유명한 지휘자가 지휘를 맡았어요.
T4-0580.x: A famous conductor led today's performance.
T4-0580.e: Literally 'point and wave', like a conductor's baton.
T4-0580.t: Also used outside music: 경찰의 지휘 아래 'under police command'.

T4-0581.x: When the conductor raised his hand, the performance began.
T4-0581.e: -자 = person who does it: 지휘자, 연주자, 수상자.

T4-0582.ex: 그 피아노 연주자는 어릴 때부터 상을 많이 받았어요.
T4-0582.x: That pianist has won many prizes since childhood.
T4-0582.t: Use 연주하다 for instruments; 악기를 치다/불다 is the everyday verb for specific instruments.

T4-0583.ex: 다음 주에 동생의 피아노 연주회가 있어요.
T4-0583.x: My younger sibling has a piano recital next week.
T4-0583.t: 연주회 is for instrumental or classical music; pop concerts are usually 콘서트.

T4-0584.ex: 졸업식에서 학생들이 다 같이 합창을 했어요.
T4-0584.x: The students all sang together in a chorus at the graduation ceremony.

T4-0585.x: I was in the choir when I was in college.

T4-0586.x: My friend majored in vocal music at a music college.
T4-0586.e: Literally 'voice music', as opposed to 기악 'instrumental music'.

T4-0587.ex: 외국인 친구와 함께 국악 공연을 보러 갔어요.
T4-0587.x: I went to see a traditional Korean music performance with a foreign friend.

T4-0588.ex: 판소리는 한 명의 소리꾼과 북 치는 사람이 함께 공연해요.
T4-0588.x: Pansori is performed by one singer together with a drummer.
T4-0588.e: 판 'open stage, scene' plus 소리 'sound, song'; a UNESCO-listed storytelling art.

T4-0589.ex: 축제에서 사물놀이 공연을 보고 신이 났어요.
T4-0589.x: I got excited watching the samulnori performance at the festival.
T4-0589.e: Literally 'playing four things': 꽹과리, 징, 장구, 북.

T4-0590.ex: 안동에 가면 하회 탈춤을 꼭 보세요.
T4-0590.x: If you go to Andong, be sure to see the Hahoe mask dance.
T4-0590.e: 탈 'mask' plus 춤 'dance'; performances often satirized nobles.
T4-0590.t: Don't confuse 탈 'mask' with 탈 'trouble, illness' as in 배탈.

T4-0591.ex: 가야금은 줄이 열두 개인 한국의 전통 악기예요.
T4-0591.x: The gayageum is a traditional Korean instrument with twelve strings.
T4-0591.e: Named after the ancient Gaya kingdom, where it is said to have been created.
T4-0591.t: You 'play' it with 타다 or 연주하다: 가야금을 타다.

T4-0592.x: Arirang is the most famous folk song in Korea.

T4-0593.x: Even the foreign tourists sang along to Arirang.
T4-0593.e: Name of Korea's best-known folk song; there are many regional versions. Origin of the word is uncertain.

T4-0594.ex: 한국 대중음악은 전 세계에서 인기가 많아요.
T4-0594.x: Korean pop music is very popular around the world.

T4-0595.ex: 제 동생은 아이돌이 되고 싶어서 춤을 연습해요.
T4-0595.x: My younger sibling wants to become an idol, so they practice dancing.
T4-0595.e: From English 'idol'; in Korea it means a trained K-pop singer, usually in a group.

T4-0596.ex: 그 가수는 3년 만에 새 음반을 냈어요.
T4-0596.x: That singer released a new album for the first time in three years.
T4-0596.t: Usually with 내다 or 발매하다: 음반을 내다 'to release an album'.

T4-0597.ex: 이번 앨범에는 모두 열 곡이 들어 있어요.
T4-0597.x: There are ten songs in total on this album.
T4-0597.e: From English 'album'; used for both music albums and photo albums.

T4-0598.x: These days I listen to music tracks by streaming.
T4-0598.e: Literally 'sound source'; now mostly means a digital or streaming track.

T4-0599.ex: 그녀는 어릴 때부터 한국 무용을 배웠어요.
T4-0599.x: She has learned Korean dance since she was little.
T4-0599.t: 무용 is formal or artistic dance; everyday dancing is 춤: 춤을 추다.

T4-0600.ex: 그 무용가는 해외 공연으로 이름을 알렸어요.
T4-0600.x: That dancer made a name for herself through performances abroad.

T4-0601.ex: 연말에는 가족과 함께 발레 공연을 보러 가요.
T4-0601.x: At the end of the year, I go to see a ballet performance with my family.
T4-0601.e: From French 'ballet'; the final 't' is silent, as in English.

T4-0602.ex: 그는 연극배우로 시작해서 지금은 영화에도 나와요.
T4-0602.x: He started as a stage actor and now appears in movies too.

T4-0603.ex: 배우들은 촬영 전에 대본을 여러 번 읽어요.
T4-0603.x: The actors read the script several times before filming.
T4-0603.t: Collocation: 대본을 외우다 'to memorize the script'; 대본 리딩 is a script read-through.

T4-0604.ex: 그 배우는 이번 영화에서 악당 배역을 맡았어요.
T4-0604.x: That actor took on the role of the villain in this movie.
T4-0604.t: Usually with 맡다: 배역을 맡다 'to take a role'.

T4-0605.ex: 그 배우가 처음으로 주연을 맡은 영화예요.
T4-0605.x: This is the first movie in which that actor played the lead role.
T4-0605.t: 주연 is the actor's position; 주인공 is the character in the story.

T4-0606.x: He was a supporting actor, but his acting was really impressive.

T4-0607.x: Bong Joon-ho is a world-famous Korean film director.
T4-0607.t: 감독 alone also means a sports team's head coach.

T4-0608.x: This drama was filmed in Busan.
T4-0608.t: Signs saying 촬영 금지 mean 'No photography'.

T4-0609.ex: 그 영화는 다음 주 수요일에 개봉합니다.
T4-0609.t: Also on packaging: 개봉 후 냉장 보관 'refrigerate after opening'.

T4-0610.x: This movie theater also shows independent films.
T4-0610.t: 개봉 is the first release date; 상영 is the ongoing showing: 상영 중.

T4-0611.ex: 그 영화는 관객 천만 명을 넘으며 크게 흥행했어요.
T4-0611.x: That movie was a huge hit, drawing more than ten million viewers.
T4-0611.e: Originally 'running a show for profit'; now mostly means being a hit.
T4-0611.t: 흥행에 성공하다/실패하다 means to be a box-office hit or flop.

T4-0612.ex: 개봉 전에 기자들을 위한 시사회가 열렸습니다.
T4-0612.x: A press screening was held before the release.

T4-0613.ex: 매년 가을 부산에서 국제 영화제가 열려요.
T4-0613.x: An international film festival is held in Busan every fall.

T4-0614.m: winning a prize, receiving an award
T4-0614.ex: 그 영화는 칸 영화제에서 큰 상을 수상했습니다.
T4-0614.x: That movie won a major award at the Cannes Film Festival.
T4-0614.t: Homonym warning: 수상 also means 'prime minister' and 'on the water', as in 수상 스키.

T4-0615.x: This year's Nobel Prize in Literature winner has been announced.

T4-0616.ex: 연말이 되면 방송사마다 큰 시상식을 해요.
T4-0616.x: When the year ends, every TV network holds a big awards ceremony.
T4-0616.e: Literally 'prize-giving ceremony'; 시상 is giving, 수상 is receiving.

T4-0617.ex: 그 배우는 올해 여우주연상 후보에 올랐어요.
T4-0617.x: That actress was nominated for Best Actress this year.
T4-0617.t: 후보에 오르다 means 'to be nominated'; in elections, 후보 means 'candidate'.

T4-0618.ex: 이 박물관에는 귀한 미술품이 많이 있어요.
T4-0618.x: This museum has many valuable works of art.

T4-0619.ex: 이 전시회에서는 조선 시대 회화를 볼 수 있어요.
T4-0619.x: At this exhibition, you can see paintings from the Joseon era.
T4-0619.t: Homonym warning: 회화 (會話) means 'conversation', as in 영어 회화.

T4-0620.ex: 공원 입구에 큰 돌 조각이 서 있어요.
T4-0620.x: A large stone sculpture stands at the park entrance.
T4-0620.t: Homonym warning: native 조각 means 'piece, fragment', as in 케이크 한 조각.

T4-0621.x: Rodin is a French sculptor famous for 'The Thinker'.

T4-0622.ex: 인사동에는 작은 갤러리가 많아서 구경하기 좋아요.
T4-0622.x: Insadong has lots of small galleries, so it's a nice place to look around.
T4-0622.e: From English 'gallery'; also used for golf spectators and phone photo apps.

T4-0623.ex: 전시장 안에서는 음식을 드시면 안 됩니다.
T4-0623.x: You may not eat inside the exhibition hall.

T4-0624.x: This painting is in the collection of the National Museum of Korea.
T4-0624.t: Homonym warning: 소장 (所長) also means 'head of an office or institute'.
rel: to own, to have in one's collection

T4-0625.x: My grandfather practices calligraphy every morning.
T4-0625.e: Literally 'writing art' — the art of brush writing.

T4-0626.x: Icheon is a city famous for its pottery.

T4-0627.ex: 저는 요즘 가죽 공예를 배우고 있어요.
T4-0627.x: These days I'm learning leather craft.
T4-0627.e: Literally 'work art' — art made by hand.

T4-0628.x: He majored in architecture in college.
T4-0628.t: 건축하다 means to build a building; 건설 is used for large projects like roads, bridges and dams.

T4-0629.x: A famous architect designed this art museum.
T4-0629.e: -가 = professional or expert: 건축가, 작가, 화가.

T4-0630.ex: 이 성당은 백 년이 넘은 건축물이에요.
T4-0630.x: This cathedral is a building over a hundred years old.
T4-0630.t: Pronounced [건충물] — the ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㅁ (nasalization).

T4-0631.x: The design of this bag is really pretty.

T4-0632.m: short work; short story, short film
T4-0632.ex: 이 작가는 주로 단편 소설을 써요.
T4-0632.x: This author mostly writes short stories.
T4-0632.t: Usually used before a noun: 단편 소설 (short story), 단편 영화 (short film).

T4-0633.ex: 그 작가의 첫 장편 소설이 큰 인기를 얻었어요.
T4-0633.x: The author's first novel became very popular.

T4-0634.x: I bought a book of poems by my favorite poet at the bookstore.
T4-0634.t: Don't confuse it with the other 시집 in 시집가다, 'a woman gets married (joins her husband's family)'.

T4-0635.ex: 그 작가는 여행에 대한 수필을 자주 써요.
T4-0635.x: That writer often writes essays about travel.
T4-0635.e: Literally 'following the brush' — writing freely as thoughts come.
T4-0635.t: 수필 is a personal, literary essay; a school paper is usually called 보고서 or 리포트.

T4-0636.ex: 제 꿈은 유명한 만화가가 되는 거예요.
T4-0636.x: My dream is to become a famous cartoonist.

T4-0637.ex: 저는 출근할 때 휴대폰으로 웹툰을 봐요.
T4-0637.x: I read webtoons on my phone on my way to work.
T4-0637.e: Korean-made blend of English 'web' + 'cartoon', now used in English too.
T4-0637.t: Many popular K-dramas are adapted from 웹툰, so fans often say 원작 웹툰 'the original webtoon'.

T4-0638.x: This drama has too many characters.
T4-0638.e: Literally 'people who step onto the stage'.

T4-0639.x: The ending of that movie was so sad.

T4-0640.ex: 그 영화는 마지막에 큰 반전이 있어요.
T4-0640.x: That movie has a big twist at the end.
T4-0640.t: 반전이 있다 = to have a twist; 반전 매력 = surprising charm, a popular casual expression.

T4-0641.x: The story reaches its climax in the last scene.
T4-0641.t: Common pattern: 절정에 이르다 'reach a peak'; also for seasons, like 단풍이 절정이에요 'fall colors are at their peak'.

T4-0642.ex: 신문에 새 소설에 대한 비평이 실렸어요.
T4-0642.x: A review of the new novel appeared in the newspaper.
T4-0642.t: 비평 judges a work's strengths and weaknesses; 비판 points out faults or wrongdoing.

T4-0644.ex: 그는 신문에 영화 평론을 쓰고 있어요.
T4-0644.x: He writes film reviews for a newspaper.
T4-0644.t: Pronounced [평논] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T4-0645.ex: 영화 평론가들이 그 감독의 새 영화를 칭찬했어요.
T4-0645.x: Film critics praised the director's new movie.

T4-0646.x: I have to write a book report for vacation homework.
T4-0646.t: Pronounced [도쿠감] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-0647.x: That book was published last year.
T4-0647.e: Literally 'putting out from the printing block'.

T4-0648.x: My older sister works as an editor at a publishing company.

T4-0649.ex: 그 작가의 새 소설이 다음 달에 출간돼요.
T4-0649.x: The author's new novel comes out next month.
T4-0649.t: 출간 focuses on a particular book coming out; 출판 also covers the publishing business in general.

T4-0650.ex: 그 소설은 몇 달 동안 베스트셀러였어요.
T4-0650.x: That novel was a bestseller for several months.

T4-0651.x: The author of this book is a famous scientist.
T4-0651.e: -자 = person who does it: 저자, 과학자, 운전자.
T4-0651.t: 저자 is the author of a specific book; 작가 is a writer or artist by profession.

T4-0652.ex: 그 교수님은 저서가 열 권이 넘어요.
T4-0652.x: That professor has written more than ten books.

T4-0653.ex: 그 소설은 유명한 번역가가 영어로 번역했어요.
T4-0653.x: A famous translator translated that novel into English.
T4-0653.t: 번역가 translates written text; someone who interprets speech aloud is a 통역사.

T4-0654.x: Hanok houses are a precious part of Korea's cultural heritage.

T4-0655.m: World Heritage Site, world cultural heritage
T4-0655.x: Bulguksa Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
T4-0655.e: Literally 'world cultural heritage' — sites on UNESCO's protected list.

T4-0656.m: intangible cultural heritage, intangible cultural asset
T4-0656.x: Pansori is an important intangible cultural asset.
T4-0656.e: Literally 'shapeless cultural asset' — skills and performing arts rather than objects.
T4-0656.t: Since 2024 the official term is 무형유산, but 무형 문화재 is still widely used.

T4-0657.x: On Lunar New Year, we play traditional folk games with the family.
T4-0657.e: Sino 민속 'folk custom' plus native 놀이 'game, play'.
T4-0657.t: Pronounced [민송노리] — the ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㄴ (nasalization).

T4-0658.m: yunnori (traditional board game played with four sticks)
T4-0658.x: I played yunnori with my family on Lunar New Year.
T4-0658.e: 윷 (the four throwing sticks) + 놀이 'game' — a classic Lunar New Year game.
T4-0658.t: Pronounced [윤노리] — the final ㅊ sounds like ㄷ, then becomes ㄴ before ㄴ.

T4-0659.x: The children are playing jegichagi in the yard.
T4-0659.e: 제기 (a shuttlecock with paper tassels) + 차기 'kicking', from 차다 'to kick'.

T4-0660.ex: 추석 밤에 여자들이 손을 잡고 강강술래를 했어요.
T4-0660.x: On Chuseok night, the women held hands and danced ganggangsullae.
T4-0660.e: The name's origin is uncertain; a moonlit circle dance with call-and-response singing at Chuseok.

T4-0661.m: Dano (festival on the 5th day of the 5th lunar month)
T4-0661.ex: 옛날에는 단오에 그네를 타고 씨름을 했어요.
T4-0661.x: In the old days, people rode swings and wrestled on Dano.
T4-0661.e: Held on the 5th day of the 5th lunar month; women washed their hair in iris water.

T4-0662.m: Daeboreum (first full moon of the lunar year)
T4-0662.x: On Daeboreum, people eat five-grain rice and seasoned greens.
T4-0662.e: 정월 = first lunar month; 대보름 = 'great full moon', on the 15th day.
T4-0662.t: People crack nuts like peanuts and walnuts (부럼) that morning, a custom said to keep skin healthy all year.

T4-0663.x: There's a custom of eating red bean porridge on the winter solstice.
T4-0663.e: Literally 'winter's extreme' — the longest night of the year.
T4-0663.t: Homonym: another 동지 means 'comrade'; context makes it clear.

T4-0664.ex: 추석 아침에 가족들이 모여서 차례를 지내요.
T4-0664.x: On Chuseok morning, the family gathers to hold the ancestral rite.
T4-0664.t: Homonym: 차례 also means 'turn, order' (제 차례예요 'It's my turn'); for the rite say 차례를 지내다.

T4-0665.x: On Chuseok, we go to our hometown and visit our ancestors' graves.
T4-0665.e: Literally 'checking on the grave' — tidying it and paying respects.
T4-0665.t: Families often trim the grass on graves, called 벌초, in the weeks before Chuseok.

T4-0666.m: Korean Wave (popularity of Korean culture abroad)
T4-0666.ex: 한류 덕분에 한국어를 배우는 사람이 많아졌어요.
T4-0666.x: Thanks to the Korean Wave, more people are learning Korean.
T4-0666.t: Pronounced [할류] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T4-0667.ex: 이 영화는 작품성과 대중성을 모두 갖췄어요.
T4-0667.x: This movie has both artistic quality and mass appeal.

T4-0668.ex: 그 영화는 상업성이 너무 강하다는 비판을 받았어요.
T4-0668.x: That movie was criticized for being too commercial.

T4-0669.ex: 방학 동안 고전 소설을 몇 권 읽었어요.
T4-0669.x: I read a few classic novels over vacation.
T4-0669.t: Classical music is technically 고전 음악, but people almost always say 클래식.

T4-0670.ex: 이 그림은 자연의 아름다움을 잘 보여 줘요.
T4-0670.x: This painting shows the beauty of nature well.
T4-0670.e: Noun form of 아름답다 'beautiful'; the ㅂ changes to 우 before -음.

T4-0671.x: That singer's songs are full of emotion.
T4-0671.e: Literally 'feeling nature' — the emotional side, as opposed to reason.
T4-0671.t: Trendy use: 감성 카페 means a cafe with a cozy, Instagram-worthy vibe.

T4-0672.x: The painter was inspired by the sea.
T4-0672.t: Use 영감을 받다/얻다 'to get inspiration'; another word 영감 means 'old man' (casual).

T4-0673.x: Children have richer imaginations than adults.
T4-0673.e: -력 = power or ability: 상상력, 기술력, 노력.
T4-0673.t: Pronounced [상상녁] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T4-0674.x: This painting was made with a new technique.

T4-0675.x: I like music of many genres.
T4-0675.e: From French 'genre' — the Korean form sounds quite different, so learn it by ear.

T4-0676.x: This method has been scientifically proven.
T4-0676.e: -적 = '-ic, -al', turning nouns into descriptions: 과학적, 혁신적, 이론적.
T4-0676.t: Use -적인 before nouns (과학적인 방법) and -적으로 as an adverb (과학적으로 설명하다).

T4-0677.m: cutting edge, state of the art, high tech
T4-0677.e: Literally 'pointed tip' — the very front of progress.
T4-0677.t: Usually used before a noun: 첨단 기술, 첨단 산업, 첨단 장비.

T4-0678.ex: 회사는 신기술 개발에 많은 돈을 투자해요.
T4-0678.x: The company invests a lot of money in developing new technology.

T4-0679.ex: 한국 기업들은 뛰어난 기술력을 가지고 있어요.
T4-0679.x: Korean companies have outstanding technological capabilities.

T4-0680.x: That company succeeded through constant innovation.
T4-0680.t: Pronounced [혁씬] — the ㅅ becomes tense after ㄱ.

T4-0681.ex: 그 회사는 혁신적인 제품을 많이 만들어요.
T4-0681.x: That company makes many innovative products.

T4-0682.e: Literally 'one who brings things to light'.

T4-0683.ex: 그 회사는 신제품의 특허권을 가지고 있어요.
T4-0683.x: That company holds the patent for the new product.
T4-0683.t: Pronounced [트커꿘] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-0684.ex: 이 기계가 움직이는 원리를 설명해 주세요.
T4-0684.x: Please explain the principle behind how this machine works.
T4-0684.t: 원리 is how something works; 원칙 is a rule or principle you follow.

T4-0685.x: Newton discovered the law of gravity.
T4-0685.t: 법칙 is a law of nature or science; laws made by a government are 법 or 법률.

T4-0686.x: The scientists confirmed the hypothesis through experiments.
T4-0686.e: Literally 'temporary theory' — one not yet proven.
T4-0686.t: Common pattern: 가설을 세우다 'to form a hypothesis'.

T4-0687.x: It's possible in theory, but difficult in reality.

T4-0688.x: The students are doing an experiment in the lab.
T4-0688.t: Often pronounced [시럼실] — ㅎ between sounds is nearly silent.

T4-0689.ex: 오늘 밤에 망원경으로 별을 관측할 거예요.
T4-0689.x: Tonight I'm going to observe the stars with a telescope.
T4-0689.t: 관측 is scientific observation of nature (stars, weather); 관찰 is close watching of anything.

T4-0690.x: The nurse measured my blood pressure.

T4-0691.ex: 물 분자는 수소와 산소로 이루어져 있어요.
T4-0691.x: A water molecule is made of hydrogen and oxygen.
T4-0691.t: In math, 분자 is the numerator of a fraction and 분모 is the denominator.

T4-0692.ex: 모든 물질은 아주 작은 원자로 이루어져 있어요.
T4-0692.x: All matter is made of very tiny atoms.

T4-0693.x: An atom is made of a nucleus and electrons.
T4-0693.t: 전자 also means 'electronic' (전자 제품); a different 전자 means 'the former' (vs. 후자 'the latter').

T4-0694.x: I want to study physics in college.
T4-0694.e: Literally 'study of the logic of things'.

T4-0695.ex: 화학 시간에 여러 가지 실험을 했어요.
T4-0695.x: We did various experiments in chemistry class.

T4-0696.ex: 제 동생은 대학에서 생물학을 전공하고 있어요.
T4-0696.x: My younger sibling is majoring in biology in college.

T4-0697.x: Astronomy is the field that studies stars and space.

T4-0698.x: He majored in engineering and became an engineer.
T4-0698.t: An engineering school is commonly called 공대, short for 공과 대학.

T4-0699.ex: 이 화장품에는 어떤 성분이 들어 있어요?
T4-0699.x: What ingredients are in this cosmetic product?
T4-0699.t: 성분 is what something contains (medicine, cosmetics, labels); cooking ingredients are 재료.

T4-0700.x: Plants take in sunlight and make oxygen.
T4-0700.e: Literally 'acid element' — oxygen was once thought to be in all acids.
T4-0700.t: Homonym: another 산소 means 'grave' (polite), as in 산소에 가다 'to visit a grave'.

T4-0701.x: Hydrogen cars are good for the environment.
T4-0701.e: Literally 'water element' — it helps make up water.

T4-0702.x: Cars give off a lot of carbon dioxide.
T4-0702.e: Literally 'carbon with two oxygens' — the chemical name for CO2.

T4-0703.ex: 이 컵은 금속으로 만들어서 아주 단단해요.
T4-0703.x: This cup is made of metal, so it's very sturdy.

T4-0704.ex: 철은 물에 오래 닿으면 녹이 슬어요.
T4-0704.x: Iron rusts if it touches water for a long time.
T4-0704.e: Homonym warning: native 철 means 'season', as in 제철 'in season'.
T4-0704.t: 철이 들다 is a different, native 철: it means 'to grow up, to mature'.

T4-0705.x: When water freezes, it becomes ice, which is a solid.

T4-0706.ex: 비행기 안에는 액체를 조금만 가지고 탈 수 있어요.
T4-0706.x: You can only bring a small amount of liquid onto a plane.

T4-0707.x: When you boil water in a pot, it turns into a gas.
T4-0707.t: In news, a different 기체 means an aircraft's body, e.g. 기체 결함 'aircraft defect'.

T4-0708.ex: 젖은 손으로 만지면 전류가 흘러서 위험해요.
T4-0708.x: If you touch it with wet hands, current can flow through you, which is dangerous.
T4-0708.t: Pronounced [절류]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T4-0709.ex: 여름에는 에어컨 때문에 전력 사용량이 크게 늘어요.
T4-0709.x: In summer, electricity use rises sharply because of air conditioners.
T4-0709.t: Pronounced [절력]; don't mix it up with 전력 'all-out effort', as in 전력을 다하다.

T4-0710.ex: 정전이 되자 병원에서 바로 발전기를 돌렸어요.
T4-0710.x: When the power went out, the hospital started its generator right away.
T4-0710.t: Don't confuse 발전 'power generation' with 발전 'development', as in 경제 발전.

T4-0711.x: Korea is a country that exports a lot of semiconductors.
T4-0711.e: Literally 'half-conducting body': it conducts electricity only partly.

T4-0712.x: I installed the software I need on my new computer.

T4-0713.ex: 하드웨어가 오래돼서 새 게임이 잘 안 돌아가요.
T4-0713.x: My hardware is old, so new games don't run well.
T4-0713.e: From English 'hardware'; only the computer sense, never tools.

T4-0714.x: These days even elementary school kids learn programming at school.

T4-0715.x: I take a coding class every weekend.
T4-0715.t: 코딩 is the everyday word, especially for kids' classes; 프로그래밍 sounds a bit more technical.

T4-0716.ex: 유튜브 알고리즘이 제가 좋아할 만한 영상을 추천해 줘요.
T4-0716.x: YouTube's algorithm recommends videos I'm likely to enjoy.
T4-0716.e: From English 'algorithm'; note the ending 즘, not 듬.
T4-0716.t: 알고리즘에 뜨다 means 'to show up in your recommended feed'.

T4-0717.x: Mobile data is expensive abroad, so be careful.
T4-0717.t: In daily talk it often means your phone plan's data: 데이터가 다 떨어졌어요 'I'm out of data'.

T4-0718.ex: 회사들은 빅데이터를 분석해서 고객의 취향을 알아내요.
T4-0718.x: Companies analyze big data to figure out customers' tastes.

T4-0719.ex: 네트워크에 문제가 생겨서 인터넷이 안 돼요.
T4-0719.x: There's a network problem, so the internet isn't working.
T4-0719.e: From English 'network'; also used for people networks, like 인적 네트워크.

T4-0720.ex: 요즘은 무선 이어폰을 쓰는 사람이 많아요.
T4-0720.x: These days lots of people use wireless earbuds.

T4-0721.ex: 회사에서는 유선 인터넷이 훨씬 더 빨라요.
T4-0721.x: At the office, wired internet is much faster.
T4-0721.t: 유선 전화 means a landline, and 유선으로 연락하다 means to contact someone by phone.

T4-0722.ex: 이 카페에서는 와이파이를 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
T4-0722.x: You can use the Wi-Fi for free at this café.
T4-0722.t: To ask for the password, say 와이파이 비밀번호가 뭐예요?

T4-0723.m: to connect (to), to access, to log on
T4-0723.ex: 사람이 너무 많아서 사이트에 접속하기가 어려워요.
T4-0723.x: There are too many people, so it's hard to get onto the site.
T4-0723.t: Use 에 for the place you connect to: 인터넷에 접속하다, 사이트에 접속하다.

T4-0724.x: There were too many applicants, so the server went down.
T4-0724.e: From English 'server'; only the computer sense, not a waiter.

T4-0725.ex: 사진을 클라우드에 저장하면 휴대폰을 잃어버려도 괜찮아요.
T4-0725.x: If you save your photos to the cloud, it's okay even if you lose your phone.
T4-0725.e: From English 'cloud'; only the computing sense, a real cloud is 구름.

T4-0726.x: I got hacked, so I changed all my passwords.
T4-0726.t: Use it with 당하다: 해킹을 당하다 'to get hacked'.

T4-0727.x: A hacker secretly broke into the bank's system.

T4-0728.x: For security, change your password often.

T4-0729.ex: 개인 정보 유출 사고가 또 일어났습니다.
T4-0729.x: Another personal data leak has occurred.
T4-0729.t: Common collocations: 정보 유출 'data leak', 기름 유출 'oil spill'.

T4-0730.m: to be leaked, to leak out
T4-0730.x: The company's customer information was leaked online.

T4-0731.ex: 하루에도 스팸 문자가 몇 개씩 와요.
T4-0731.x: I get several spam texts every day.
T4-0731.e: From English 'spam'; the canned meat is also hugely popular in Korea as a holiday gift set.

T4-0732.x: To log in, first enter your ID and password.
T4-0732.t: Add 하다 for the verb, 로그인하다; Koreans say 아이디 where Americans say 'username'.

T4-0733.ex: 앱을 최신 버전으로 업데이트하니까 오류가 없어졌어요.
T4-0733.x: After I updated the app to the latest version, the error went away.

T4-0734.ex: 어제 찍은 여행 사진을 블로그에 업로드했어요.
T4-0734.x: I uploaded the travel photos I took yesterday to my blog.
T4-0734.t: In casual speech, 올리다 is more common: 사진을 올렸어요.

T4-0735.ex: 이 앱은 무료로 다운로드할 수 있어요.
T4-0735.x: You can download this app for free.
T4-0735.t: Casually shortened to 다운: 다운받다; the native alternative is 내려받다.

T4-0736.ex: 자세한 내용은 홈페이지에서 파일을 내려받아 확인하세요.
T4-0736.x: For details, download the file from the website and check it.
T4-0736.e: 내리다 'to bring down' + 받다 'to receive': a native replacement for 다운로드.
T4-0736.t: Common in official notices and news; in conversation people mostly say 다운받다.

T4-0737.ex: 이 앱의 사용자가 천만 명을 넘었어요.
T4-0737.x: This app's users have passed ten million.
T4-0737.e: -자 = person who does it: 사용자, 운전자, 과학자.
T4-0737.t: In labor contexts, 사용자 also means 'employer', as opposed to 근로자 'worker'.

T4-0738.ex: 요즘은 고객 센터에 전화하는 대신 챗봇에게 물어봐요.
T4-0738.x: These days I ask a chatbot instead of calling customer service.

T4-0739.ex: 자율 주행 자동차가 곧 도로를 달릴 거예요.
T4-0739.x: Self-driving cars will soon be on the roads.

T4-0740.ex: 전기차는 기름 대신 전기를 충전해서 달려요.
T4-0740.x: Electric cars run on charged electricity instead of gas.

T4-0741.x: I took photos of the sea from the sky with a drone.
T4-0741.t: To fly a drone is 드론을 날리다, not 드론을 타다.

T4-0742.ex: 가상 현실 안경을 쓰면 진짜 바다에 있는 것 같아요.
T4-0742.x: When you put on VR goggles, it feels like you're really at the beach.
T4-0742.t: In everyday talk people usually just say VR, pronounced [브이알].

T4-0743.ex: 요즘은 디지털 카메라보다 휴대폰으로 사진을 더 많이 찍어요.
T4-0743.x: These days people take more photos with phones than with digital cameras.

T4-0744.e: From English 'analog'; 아날로그 감성 means a cozy, retro, low-tech vibe.

T4-0745.x: As the factory became automated, many jobs disappeared.
T4-0745.t: Add 되다 for 'to be automated': 자동화되다.

T4-0746.x: I watch movies or draw pictures on my tablet.
T4-0746.e: From English 'tablet'; also called 태블릿 PC.

T4-0747.ex: 해상도가 높은 모니터로 보니까 화면이 아주 선명해요.
T4-0747.x: Looking at it on a high-resolution monitor, the screen is really sharp.

T4-0748.x: My phone was low on storage, so I deleted some photos.
T4-0748.t: Pronounced [용냥]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T4-0749.x: There isn't enough memory, so the app keeps shutting down.
T4-0749.e: From English 'memory'; only the computer sense, a person's memory is 기억.

T4-0750.m: to work, to operate, to run (of a machine)
T4-0750.x: The elevator wasn't working, so I took the stairs.
T4-0750.t: For machines, use 작동하다 or 되다, never 일하다: 에어컨이 안 돼요.

T4-0751.x: The fire alarm went off because of a sensor malfunction.

T4-0752.x: The laptop repair cost more than I expected.
T4-0752.e: -비 = cost or fee: 수리비, 교통비, 식비.
T4-0752.t: Costs 'come out' in Korean: 수리비가 10만 원 나왔어요.

T4-0753.ex: 이 부품은 해외에서 주문해야 해서 오래 걸려요.
T4-0753.x: This part has to be ordered from overseas, so it takes a long time.

T4-0754.ex: 등산할 때는 안전 장비를 꼭 챙기세요.
T4-0754.x: When you go hiking, be sure to bring safety gear.
T4-0754.t: Gamers use it too: 장비를 맞추다 means 'to gear up'.

T4-0755.ex: 이 기계는 조작이 간단해서 누구나 쓸 수 있어요.
T4-0755.x: This machine is simple to operate, so anyone can use it.
T4-0755.t: A homonym 조작 means 'fabrication', as in 사진 조작 'doctored photo', so context matters.

T4-0756.ex: 사용하지 않을 때는 전원을 꺼 주세요.
T4-0756.x: Please turn off the power when you're not using it.
T4-0756.t: Watch for the homonym 전원 'all members', as in 전원 참석 'everyone attends'.

T4-0757.x: I can't find where the remote is.
T4-0757.e: From English 'remote control', clipped to 리모컨: Konglish, Americans just say 'remote'.

T4-0758.ex: 사람이 지나가면 센서가 반응해서 불이 켜져요.
T4-0758.x: When someone walks by, the sensor reacts and the light turns on.

T4-0759.x: The moon is the only satellite Earth has.
T4-0759.e: Literally 'guarding star': a body that circles a planet.
T4-0759.t: 위성 also shortens 인공위성 in compounds: 위성 사진, 위성 방송.

T4-0760.ex: 인공위성 덕분에 날씨를 정확하게 알 수 있어요.
T4-0760.x: Thanks to satellites, we can know the weather accurately.

T4-0761.ex: 우주선이 여섯 달 만에 무사히 지구로 돌아왔습니다.
T4-0761.x: The spacecraft returned safely to Earth after six months.

T4-0762.ex: 로켓이 큰 소리를 내며 하늘로 올라갔어요.
T4-0762.x: The rocket roared up into the sky.

T4-0763.x: The rocket launch was postponed because of the weather.

T4-0764.ex: 과학자들이 화성 탐사를 위해 로봇을 보냈어요.
T4-0764.x: Scientists sent a robot to explore Mars.

T4-0765.ex: 시골에서는 밤하늘의 은하수를 볼 수 있어요.
T4-0765.x: In the countryside, you can see the Milky Way in the night sky.
T4-0765.t: In the folktale 견우와 직녀, the two lovers are separated by the 은하수.

T4-0766.x: The biggest planet in the solar system is Jupiter.

T4-0767.x: The moon's gravity is much weaker than Earth's.
T4-0767.t: Pronounced [중녁]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T4-0768.x: The satellite is orbiting the Earth.
T4-0768.t: 궤도에 오르다 also means 'to get on track', e.g. a business finally running smoothly.

T4-0769.x: Looking at the moon through a telescope was really amazing.

T4-0770.ex: 현미경으로 보니까 작은 세포가 잘 보였어요.
T4-0770.x: Under the microscope, the tiny cells were clearly visible.

T4-0771.x: Scientists succeeded in cloning a sheep.
T4-0771.t: 불법 복제 means piracy, like illegally copied software or movies.

T4-0772.x: This technology will be commercialized within five years.

T4-0773.x: The spread of smartphones has changed our lives a lot.
T4-0773.t: A homonym 보급 means 'supplying' food or gear, as in the army: 식량 보급.

T4-0774.m: to become widespread, to be widely distributed
T4-0774.ex: 인터넷이 보급되면서 정보를 쉽게 찾을 수 있게 됐어요.
T4-0774.x: As the internet spread, it became easy to find information.

T4-0775.ex: 전기차가 대중화되려면 충전소가 더 많아야 해요.
T4-0775.x: For electric cars to go mainstream, there need to be more charging stations.

T4-0776.ex: 지구 온난화 때문에 여름이 점점 더워지고 있어요.
T4-0776.x: Summers are getting hotter and hotter because of global warming.

T4-0777.ex: 기후 변화로 농사짓기가 점점 어려워지고 있습니다.
T4-0777.x: Farming is getting harder and harder because of climate change.
T4-0777.t: 기후 is long-term climate; 날씨 is the weather today.

T4-0778.ex: 폭염 주의보가 내려졌으니 낮에는 외출을 피하세요.
T4-0778.x: A heat advisory has been issued, so avoid going out during the day.
T4-0778.t: Pronounced [포겸]: the batchim ㄱ carries over to the next syllable.

T4-0779.x: A cold snap hit suddenly, and the water pipes froze.

T4-0780.ex: 밤새 내린 폭설로 비행기가 모두 취소됐어요.
T4-0780.x: All the flights were canceled because of the heavy snow that fell overnight.

T4-0781.ex: 어젯밤 폭우 때문에 도로가 물에 잠겼어요.
T4-0781.x: Last night's heavy rain flooded the roads.
T4-0781.t: Pronounced [포구]: the ㄱ batchim slides onto the next vowel.

T4-0782.x: A landslide caused by the heavy rain blocked the road.
T4-0782.t: Use it with 나다 or 일어나다: 산사태가 나다 = a landslide happens.

T4-0783.ex: 지진 후에 쓰나미가 해안 마을을 덮쳤어요.
T4-0783.x: After the earthquake, a tsunami struck the coastal village.
T4-0783.e: From Japanese 'tsunami'; the official Korean term is 지진해일.

T4-0784.x: This island was formed when a volcano erupted.

T4-0785.m: ecology, the way living things exist in their environment
T4-0785.ex: 오염 때문에 강의 생태가 많이 바뀌었어요.
T4-0785.x: The river's ecology has changed a lot because of pollution.
T4-0785.t: You'll most often meet it in 생태계 (ecosystem): 생태계를 보호하다 = to protect the ecosystem.

T4-0786.x: There are still many unknown creatures in the ocean.
T4-0786.t: As a school subject, students say 생물 for biology, though the official course name is 생명과학.

T4-0787.ex: 숲을 보호하면 생물 다양성을 지킬 수 있어요.
T4-0787.e: Literally 'the many-kinds quality of living things'.

T4-0788.ex: 이 새는 멸종 위기 동물이라서 보호를 받아요.
T4-0788.x: This bird is an endangered animal, so it is protected.
T4-0788.e: Literally 'the crisis of a species being wiped out'.
T4-0788.t: Common patterns: 멸종 위기 동물 = endangered animal; 멸종 위기에 처하다 = to face extinction.

T4-0789.ex: 개발 때문에 동물들의 서식지가 줄어들고 있어요.
T4-0789.x: Animal habitats are shrinking because of development.
T4-0789.t: Pronounced [서식찌]: ㅈ becomes tense after the ㄱ batchim.

T4-0790.m: to inhabit, to live (of animals and plants)
T4-0790.x: Many kinds of fish live in this river.
T4-0790.t: Used for wildlife in formal or scientific writing; for people, just say 살다.

T4-0791.m: natural monument (a legally protected species, plant or site)
T4-0791.x: The Jindo dog is a natural monument protected by the Korean government.
T4-0791.e: Literally 'natural thing to remember'; a legal status for protected animals, plants and places.
T4-0791.t: Pronounced [처년기념물]: the ㄴ batchim of 천 links to 연.

T4-0792.ex: 지난봄에 난 산불로 넓은 산림이 사라졌어요.
T4-0792.x: A large area of forest was lost in the wildfire last spring.
T4-0792.t: Pronounced [살림], the same sound as 살림 (housekeeping); context tells them apart.

T4-0793.x: On Arbor Day, I planted trees with my family.
T4-0793.e: Literally 'tree-planting day'; no longer a public holiday since 2006.
T4-0793.t: Pronounced [싱모길]: nasalization turns ㄱ into ㅇ before ㅁ.

T4-0794.ex: 사막에서는 낮과 밤의 기온 차이가 커요.
T4-0794.x: In the desert, the temperature difference between day and night is large.

T4-0795.ex: 숲이 사라지면서 사막화가 빠르게 진행되고 있어요.
T4-0795.x: As forests disappear, desertification is progressing quickly.

T4-0796.x: Glaciers are melting because of global warming.

T4-0797.x: Polar bears are in danger because the Arctic ice is shrinking.
T4-0797.t: Pronounced [북끅]: ㄱ becomes tense after the ㄱ batchim.

T4-0798.ex: 아주 추운 남극에도 펭귄이 많이 살아요.
T4-0798.x: Many penguins live even in freezing Antarctica.

T4-0799.ex: 빙하가 녹아서 해수면이 계속 높아지고 있어요.
T4-0799.x: Sea levels keep rising as glaciers melt.
T4-0799.t: In the news you'll hear 해수면 상승 = sea-level rise.

T4-0800.ex: 오존층이 파괴되면 자외선이 더 많이 들어와요.
T4-0800.x: If the ozone layer is destroyed, more UV rays get in.

T4-0801.x: UV rays are strong in summer, so put on sunscreen.
T4-0801.t: Sunscreen is also called 자외선 차단제, literally 'UV blocker'.

T4-0802.x: The air has been polluted by factory smoke.
T4-0802.e: Literally 'great air'; don't confuse it with 대기 'waiting', a different word.
T4-0802.t: In news, 대기 오염 (air pollution) and 대기 질 (air quality) are the most common collocations.

T4-0803.ex: 이 강은 수질이 좋아서 물고기가 많아요.
T4-0803.x: This river has good water quality, so there are lots of fish.

T4-0804.ex: 농약을 많이 쓰면 토양이 오염될 수 있어요.
T4-0804.x: Using a lot of pesticide can pollute the soil.
T4-0804.t: 토양 is formal or scientific; in everyday speech, say 흙.

T4-0805.x: City noise is also a kind of pollution.
T4-0805.e: Literally 'public harm'; a different 공해 means 'international waters'.
T4-0805.t: Noise and light count too: 소음 공해 = noise pollution, 빛 공해 = light pollution.

T4-0806.ex: 자동차 배기가스는 대기 오염의 큰 원인이에요.
T4-0806.x: Car exhaust is a major cause of air pollution.
T4-0806.e: Literally 'expelled-air gas'; 가스 is from English 'gas'.

T4-0807.x: Trash can be put out from 8 p.m.
T4-0807.t: Two common uses: 탄소 배출 = carbon emissions, and 쓰레기 배출 = putting out the trash.

T4-0808.ex: 정부는 탄소 배출량을 줄이려고 노력하고 있어요.
T4-0808.x: The government is trying to reduce carbon emissions.

T4-0809.x: When greenhouse gases increase, the Earth's temperature rises.
T4-0809.e: 온실 'greenhouse', literally 'warm room', plus 가스 from English 'gas'.

T4-0810.ex: 화석 연료를 많이 쓰면 공기가 나빠져요.
T4-0810.x: Using a lot of fossil fuels makes the air worse.
T4-0810.t: 연료 is pronounced [열료]: ㄴ turns into ㄹ next to ㄹ.

T4-0811.x: When oil prices rise, gas prices go up too.
T4-0811.e: Literally 'stone oil', the same idea as Latin 'petroleum'.
T4-0811.t: For gas at the pump or cooking oil, people say 기름; 석유 is the raw resource.

T4-0812.x: In the old days, people heated their homes with coal.

T4-0813.x: These days many buses run on natural gas.

T4-0814.ex: 원자력은 전기를 많이 만들지만 위험할 수도 있어요.
T4-0814.x: Nuclear power produces a lot of electricity, but it can be dangerous.

T4-0815.ex: 그 나라는 원자력 발전소를 더 짓지 않기로 했어요.
T4-0815.x: That country decided not to build any more nuclear power plants.
T4-0815.t: News usually shortens it to 원전.

T4-0816.ex: 핵 문제는 여러 나라가 함께 해결해야 해요.
T4-0816.x: Nuclear issues have to be solved by many countries together.
T4-0816.e: Basic meaning 'core'; it became the word for 'nuclear'.

T4-0817.ex: 사고 후에 그 지역의 방사능 수치가 높아졌어요.
T4-0817.x: After the accident, radiation levels in the area went up.
T4-0817.t: 방사능 is radioactivity; the rays themselves are 방사선, as in an X-ray.

T4-0818.ex: 대체 에너지 개발이 점점 중요해지고 있어요.
T4-0818.x: Developing alternative energy is becoming more and more important.

T4-0819.ex: 정부는 신재생 에너지 사용을 늘리려고 해요.
T4-0819.x: The government wants to increase the use of renewable energy.
T4-0819.e: 신 'new' plus 재생 'renewable', covering both new and renewable sources.

T4-0820.x: This building heats water with solar heat.
T4-0820.t: Pronounced [태양녈] (ㄴ insertion); 태양열 uses heat, 태양광 turns sunlight into electricity.

T4-0821.x: We installed solar panels on the roof of our house.
T4-0821.e: Literally 'sun light'; in energy talk it means solar electricity.

T4-0822.ex: 바람이 많이 부는 제주도에는 풍력 발전기가 많아요.
T4-0822.x: Windy Jeju Island has a lot of wind turbines.
T4-0822.t: Pronounced [풍녁]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after the ㅇ batchim.

T4-0823.ex: 이 댐에서는 수력으로 많은 전기를 만들어요.
T4-0823.x: This dam produces a lot of electricity with water power.

T4-0824.ex: 여름에는 절전을 위해 에어컨 온도를 높이세요.
T4-0824.x: In summer, raise the air conditioner temperature to save electricity.
T4-0824.t: On devices you'll see 절전 모드 = power-saving or sleep mode.

T4-0825.ex: 이 나라는 천연자원이 풍부해서 수출을 많이 해요.
T4-0825.x: This country is rich in natural resources, so it exports a lot.

T4-0826.x: When oil runs out, we'll need other energy.
T4-0826.t: Usually used as 고갈되다 with resources, water or even energy: 체력이 고갈됐어요.

T4-0827.ex: 공장에서 나온 폐기물을 강에 버리면 안 돼요.
T4-0827.x: You must not dump factory waste into the river.
T4-0827.t: In everyday speech 폐 is usually pronounced [페].

T4-0828.x: We are running out of places to bury trash.

T4-0829.ex: 쓰레기를 소각할 때 나쁜 가스가 나올 수 있어요.
T4-0829.x: Harmful gases can be released when trash is burned.

T4-0830.m: sorting trash for disposal, separate collection
T4-0830.ex: 한국에서는 쓰레기를 꼭 분리 배출해야 해요.
T4-0830.x: In Korea, you must sort your trash before putting it out.
T4-0830.e: Literally 'separate and put out'; Korea's strict trash-sorting system.
T4-0830.t: Pronounced [불리 배출]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T4-0831.ex: 종량제 봉투는 편의점에서 살 수 있어요.
T4-0831.x: You can buy official trash bags at a convenience store.
T4-0831.e: Literally 'pay-by-amount system'; you pay by buying official trash bags.
T4-0831.t: Pronounced [종냥제]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after the ㅇ batchim.

T4-0832.x: In our apartment complex, we put out recyclables on Wednesdays.
T4-0832.e: Literally 'goods to be used alive again'.

T4-0833.x: Glass bottles can be washed and reused.
T4-0833.e: 재- = again, re-: 재사용, 재활용, 재시험.
T4-0833.t: 재사용 means using the same item again; 재활용 means turning it into something new.

T4-0834.ex: 카페에서 일회용 컵 사용을 줄이고 있어요.
T4-0834.x: Cafes are cutting down on disposable cups.
T4-0834.t: Mostly used before a noun: 일회용 컵, 일회용 젓가락, 일회용 마스크.

T4-0835.ex: 요즘 마트에서는 비닐봉지를 무료로 주지 않아요.
T4-0835.x: These days supermarkets don't give out free plastic bags.
T4-0835.t: Konglish alert: 비닐 means plastic film or bags, not just vinyl; 플라스틱 is for hard plastic.

T4-0836.ex: 텀블러를 가져가면 커피를 싸게 살 수 있어요.
T4-0836.x: If you bring a tumbler, you can get coffee for less.
T4-0836.e: From English 'tumbler'; in Korea it means a reusable, usually insulated, travel cup.

T4-0837.x: The river water got dirty because of factory wastewater.

T4-0838.x: You shouldn't pour oil down the drain.

T4-0839.ex: 나무와 식물은 공기를 정화하는 역할을 해요.
T4-0839.x: Trees and plants help purify the air.

T4-0840.ex: 사무실에 정수기가 있어서 물을 사지 않아요.
T4-0840.x: There's a water purifier in the office, so I don't buy water.
T4-0840.t: Many Korean homes rent a 정수기 monthly, with regular filter service included.

T4-0841.ex: 도시에 녹지가 많으면 사람들이 더 건강해져요.
T4-0841.x: When a city has lots of green space, people become healthier.
T4-0841.t: Pronounced [녹찌]: ㅈ becomes tense after the ㄱ batchim.

T4-0842.x: The rural population has dropped a lot due to urbanization.

T4-0843.ex: 난개발 때문에 산과 숲이 많이 사라졌어요.
T4-0843.x: Many mountains and forests have disappeared because of reckless development.

T4-0844.x: The damage to nature from the wildfire is serious.
T4-0844.t: It also covers reputation: 명예 훼손 = defamation.

T4-0845.m: to be damaged, to be destroyed
T4-0845.x: Old trees were damaged because of the construction.
T4-0845.e: Literally 'broken and harmed'; -되다 makes it passive.
T4-0845.t: To say someone damaged it, use 훼손하다.

T4-0846.ex: 자연 보전을 위해 쓰레기를 줄여야 해요.
T4-0846.x: We need to reduce trash to conserve nature.
T4-0846.t: Often confused with 보존: 보전 keeps something healthy and intact, 보존 keeps it unchanged, like artifacts.

T4-0847.ex: 이 지역은 자연환경이 아름다워서 관광객이 많아요.
T4-0847.x: This area has a beautiful natural environment, so there are many tourists.

T4-0848.x: The government announced it will achieve carbon neutrality by 2050.
T4-0848.e: 탄소 'carbon' plus 중립 'neutrality', literally 'standing in the middle'.
T4-0848.t: 중립 is pronounced [중닙]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after the ㅇ batchim.

T4-0849.x: The plane couldn't take off because of bad weather.
T4-0849.e: Literally 'air appearance'; 기상 'getting up' is a different word.
T4-0849.t: 기상 is formal and used in news; in conversation, just say 날씨.

T4-0850.m: Korea Meteorological Administration, the weather service
T4-0850.x: According to the weather service, it's going to rain tomorrow.

T4-0851.x: There was more rainfall this summer than last year.

T4-0852.m: daily temperature range (gap between day and night)
T4-0852.x: The temperature swings a lot between day and night these days, so watch out for colds.
T4-0852.t: Forecasts in spring and fall love 일교차가 크다; it's a hint to dress in layers.

T4-0853.x: Air pressure drops as you climb a high mountain.

T4-0854.ex: 고기압의 영향으로 내일은 전국이 대체로 맑겠습니다.
T4-0854.x: Thanks to high pressure, skies will be mostly clear nationwide tomorrow.

T4-0855.ex: 저기압이 다가오면서 오늘 밤부터 비가 내리겠습니다.
T4-0855.x: Rain is expected from tonight as a low-pressure system approaches.
T4-0855.t: Casual slang: 저기압이다 means someone is in a gloomy or bad mood.

T4-0856.x: The monsoon rain kept falling for a week.
T4-0856.e: 장마 'rainy season' plus 비 'rain'; the added ㅅ makes 비 sound tense [삐].

T4-0857.x: A fine-dust advisory was issued this afternoon.
T4-0857.t: 주의보 (advisory) is one step below 경보 (warning); alerts are 내려지다 (issued) and 해제되다 (lifted).

T4-0858.ex: 오늘은 미세먼지 농도가 높아서 마스크를 써야 해요.
T4-0858.x: Fine-dust levels are high today, so you should wear a mask.

T4-0859.m: tropical night (a night that stays above 25°C)
T4-0859.ex: 열대야 때문에 밤새 잠을 잘 못 잤어요.
T4-0859.x: I couldn't sleep well all night because of the tropical night.
T4-0859.e: Literally 'tropical-zone night'—a summer night that never cools down.
T4-0859.t: Pronounced [열때야] — ㄷ becomes tense after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

T4-0860.m: sweltering heat, hot and humid weather
T4-0860.x: This year the sweltering heat started early, in June.
T4-0860.e: Built like 무덥다 'to be hot and humid'; 더위 means 'heat'.

T4-0861.m: spring cold snap (a cold spell when flowers start to bloom)
T4-0861.ex: 꽃샘추위 때문에 다시 두꺼운 코트를 입었어요.
T4-0861.x: Because of the spring cold snap, I put my thick coat back on.
T4-0861.e: Literally 'flower-jealousy cold'—as if winter is jealous of the blooming flowers.
T4-0861.t: News uses it every March: 꽃샘추위가 찾아오다 'a spring cold snap arrives'.

T4-0862.ex: 일기 예보를 보니까 내일은 하루 종일 맑음이에요.
T4-0862.x: According to the weather forecast, tomorrow will be clear all day.
T4-0862.e: Noun form of 맑다 'to be clear' plus -음, used as a forecast label.
T4-0862.t: Pronounced [말금] — in ㄺ, the ㄱ moves over to the next syllable.

T4-0863.ex: 주말 날씨는 흐림이고 오후에 비가 올 수도 있어요.
T4-0863.x: The weekend weather will be cloudy, and it might rain in the afternoon.
T4-0863.e: Noun form of 흐리다 'to be cloudy', used as a forecast label.

T4-0864.ex: 그 계약은 법적으로 아무 문제가 없어요.
T4-0864.x: That contract has no legal problems at all.
T4-0864.e: -적 turns nouns into '-al' words: 법적, 정치적, 합법적.
T4-0864.t: Pronounced [법쩍]; use 법적 before a noun (법적 문제) and 법적으로 as an adverb.

T4-0865.ex: 법원은 그 회사에 벌금을 내라고 했어요.
T4-0865.x: The court ordered the company to pay a fine.
T4-0865.t: Pronounced [버붠] — the ㅂ links to the next syllable.

T4-0866.ex: 검찰은 그 사건을 다시 조사하기로 했습니다.
T4-0866.x: The prosecution decided to investigate the case again.

T4-0867.ex: 검사가 법정에서 새로운 증거를 보여 줬어요.
T4-0867.x: The prosecutor showed new evidence in court.
T4-0867.e: Homonym warning: 검사 also means 'test, inspection', as in 건강 검사.
T4-0867.t: Address a prosecutor as 검사님; 변호사 (lawyer) and 판사 (judge) end in -사 too.

T4-0868.x: The police are investigating the case.
T4-0868.t: 수사 is a criminal investigation by police or prosecutors; 조사 is any examination, survey, or research.

T4-0869.x: The police arrested the thief right at the scene.
T4-0869.t: The passive is 체포되다: 범인이 체포됐어요 'The criminal was arrested.'

T4-0870.ex: 그 정치인은 조사를 받은 후 결국 구속되었습니다.
T4-0870.x: After being questioned, that politician was eventually taken into custody.
T4-0870.t: In the news 구속 means being held in custody; in daily life it means restricting freedom (자유를 구속하다).

T4-0871.ex: 경찰은 어제 용의자의 얼굴을 언론에 공개했어요.
T4-0871.x: Yesterday the police released the suspect's face to the media.
T4-0871.e: Literally 'person under suspicion'; -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.

T4-0872.x: The defendant admitted his wrongdoing in court.
T4-0872.e: Literally 'the one accused'; 피- marks the receiving side.
T4-0872.t: In criminal trials the accused is formally 피고인; plain 피고 is the defendant in a civil suit.

T4-0873.x: The plaintiff filed a lawsuit against the company.
T4-0873.e: Literally 'original accuser'; homonym 원고 also means 'manuscript'.

T4-0874.x: He was defrauded, so he filed a complaint against the other person.
T4-0874.t: 고소 is filed by the victim; 고발 is filed by a third party. Note 고소하다 also means 'nutty, savory'.

T4-0875.m: accusation, report to the authorities; exposé
T4-0875.ex: 시민 단체가 그 회사를 경찰에 고발했어요.
T4-0875.x: A civic group reported the company to the police.

T4-0876.x: He filed a lawsuit against the company.
T4-0876.t: Common pairs: 소송을 걸다 or 소송을 제기하다 'to file a suit', 소송에서 이기다 'to win a suit'.

T4-0877.ex: 법원은 다음 주에 최종 판결을 내릴 예정입니다.
T4-0877.x: The court is scheduled to deliver its final ruling next week.
T4-0877.t: Use 판결을 내리다 'to hand down a ruling' and 판결이 나오다 'a ruling comes out'.

T4-0878.x: The judge sentenced him to three years in prison.
T4-0878.t: Also used outside court: 암 선고를 받다 'to be told you have cancer'.

T4-0880.ex: 그는 오랜 재판 끝에 무죄 판결을 받았어요.
T4-0880.x: After a long trial, he was found not guilty.
T4-0880.e: Literally 'no crime'; 무- = without: 무료, 무죄.

T4-0881.m: penalty, penal rule; forfeit (in a game)
T4-0881.ex: 게임에서 진 사람은 벌칙으로 노래를 불러야 해요.
T4-0881.x: Whoever loses the game has to sing a song as a penalty.
T4-0881.t: In daily life 벌칙 often means a fun penalty for losing a game, like singing or a forehead flick.

T4-0882.x: He was sentenced to two years in prison by the court.
T4-0882.t: Pattern: 징역 + time + 을 선고받다 'to be sentenced to X in prison'.

T4-0883.x: He spent ten years in prison when he was young.
T4-0883.t: 감옥 is the everyday or literary word; the official term is 교도소.

T4-0884.x: That criminal is in prison now.

T4-0885.x: He was released from prison after three years.
T4-0885.t: Pronounced [석빵] — ㅂ becomes tense after ㄱ.

T4-0886.ex: 허가 없이 건물을 짓는 것은 위법입니다.
T4-0886.x: Constructing a building without a permit is illegal.
T4-0886.t: 위법 is a formal legal term; in everyday speech 불법 is far more common.

T4-0887.x: Parking your car here is illegal.
T4-0887.t: Common compounds: 불법 주차 'illegal parking', 불법 다운로드 'illegal downloading'.

T4-0888.ex: 이 나라에서는 길에서 술을 마시는 것이 합법이에요.
T4-0888.x: In this country, drinking alcohol on the street is legal.
T4-0888.t: Pronounced [합뻡] — ㅂ becomes tense after ㅂ.

T4-0889.x: They earned money by legal means.

T4-0890.ex: 그 회사는 불법적으로 개인 정보를 모았어요.
T4-0890.x: That company collected personal information illegally.

T4-0891.ex: 운전할 때는 교통 법규를 꼭 지켜야 해요.
T4-0891.x: When you drive, you must obey the traffic laws.
T4-0891.t: Most common in 교통 법규 'traffic laws', paired with 지키다 'obey' or 위반하다 'violate'.

T4-0892.x: Read the clauses of the contract carefully.

T4-0893.x: The constitution guarantees the freedom of all citizens.
T4-0893.t: Pronounced [헌뻡]; 제헌절 (July 17) marks the adoption of Korea's constitution in 1948.

T4-0894.x: A new bill was passed in the National Assembly yesterday.
T4-0894.t: Collocations: 법안을 발의하다 'to propose a bill', 법안이 통과되다 'a bill passes'.

T4-0895.m: enactment, establishment (of a law or rule)
T4-0895.ex: 정부는 새로운 법의 제정을 추진하고 있습니다.
T4-0895.x: The government is pushing for the enactment of a new law.

T4-0896.ex: 법이 개정되어서 다음 달부터 규칙이 바뀝니다.
T4-0896.x: The law was revised, so the rules change starting next month.

T4-0897.ex: 새 제도의 시행으로 많은 것이 바뀌었어요.
T4-0897.x: Many things changed with the implementation of the new system.

T4-0898.m: to take effect, to be implemented, to be enforced
T4-0898.x: This law takes effect starting next January.
T4-0898.e: Passive of 시행하다 'to implement'; literally 'be applied and carried out'.
T4-0898.t: Typical news pattern: (date)부터 시행되다 'to take effect from (date)'.

T4-0899.x: The government decided to abolish that system.
T4-0899.t: Homonym: 폐지 (a different word) also means 'waste paper', as in 폐지 줍기.

T4-0900.x: Wearing seat belts in the back seat of cars became mandatory.

T4-0901.ex: 정부는 플라스틱 사용에 대한 규제를 강화했어요.
T4-0901.x: The government tightened regulations on plastic use.
T4-0901.t: Pair with 완화 and 강화: 규제를 완화하다 'ease regulations', 규제를 강화하다 'tighten regulations'.

T4-0902.x: The government decided to ease real estate regulations.

T4-0903.x: The police stepped up their crackdown on drunk driving.

T4-0904.ex: 오늘 밤 이 도로에서 음주 운전 단속이 있어요.
T4-0904.x: There is a drunk-driving checkpoint on this road tonight.
T4-0904.e: Literally 'gather and bind'—keeping things tightly under control.
T4-0904.t: 단속에 걸리다 'to get caught in a crackdown' is very common.

T4-0905.x: Last week I paid a fine for a parking violation.
T4-0905.t: 과태료 is an administrative fine (parking, late filing); 벌금 is a criminal fine set by a court.

T4-0906.x: I got 15 penalty points for running a red light.
T4-0906.t: Pronounced [벌쩜]; used for driver's licenses and also for school demerits.

T4-0907.ex: 세관 신고서를 비행기 안에서 미리 작성했어요.
T4-0907.x: I filled out the customs declaration form on the plane in advance.

T4-0908.m: civil complaint, petition or request to a government office
T4-0908.ex: 주민들이 소음 문제로 구청에 민원을 넣었어요.
T4-0908.x: Residents filed a complaint with the district office about the noise.
T4-0908.t: 민원을 넣다 or 민원을 제기하다 'to file a complaint'; the person filing it is a 민원인.

T4-0909.m: civil service office, public service counter
T4-0909.x: To get your documents issued, go to the civil service office on the first floor.
T4-0909.e: 민원 'civil request' plus -실 'room': 민원실, 사무실, 교실.

T4-0910.ex: 이 동네는 행정 서비스가 아주 빨라요.
T4-0910.x: Administrative services in this neighborhood are very fast.

T4-0911.x: Government offices are not open on weekends.

T4-0912.ex: 서울 시장이 새로운 교통 정책을 발표했어요.
T4-0912.x: The mayor of Seoul announced a new transportation policy.
T4-0912.e: Literally 'city head'; homonym 시장 also means 'market'.

T4-0913.ex: 많은 지자체가 지역 축제를 열고 있어요.
T4-0913.x: Many local governments are holding regional festivals.
T4-0913.e: Short for 지방 자치 단체 'local self-governing body'.

T4-0914.ex: 한국에서 지방 자치 제도는 1995년에 본격적으로 시작되었습니다.
T4-0914.x: In Korea, the local self-government system began in earnest in 1995.

T4-0915.x: The Minister of Education held a press conference.
T4-0915.e: Literally 'chief official'—like a U.S. cabinet secretary.
T4-0915.t: A different word 장관 means 'magnificent sight', as in 장관을 이루다.

T4-0916.ex: 국회에서 예산을 두고 긴 토론이 이어졌습니다.
T4-0916.x: A long debate over the budget continued in the National Assembly.
T4-0916.t: Pronounced [구쾨] — ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes aspirated ㅋ.

T4-0917.m: member of the National Assembly, lawmaker
T4-0917.x: He was elected to the National Assembly in the last election.
T4-0917.t: Pronounced [구쾨의원]; address a lawmaker as 의원님.

T4-0918.ex: 그 의원은 새 법안에 강하게 반대했어요.
T4-0918.x: That legislator strongly opposed the new bill.
T4-0918.e: Literally 'discussion member'; homonym 의원 also means 'small clinic'.
T4-0918.t: Address as 의원님; 시의원 is a city council member.

T4-0919.ex: 두 정당은 새 정책에 대해 서로 다른 의견을 가지고 있어요.
T4-0919.x: The two parties have different opinions about the new policy.
T4-0919.e: Literally 'political group'; don't confuse with 정당하다 'to be fair, just'.

T4-0920.ex: 여당은 이번 선거에서 많은 의석을 잃었습니다.
T4-0920.x: The ruling party lost many seats in this election.
T4-0920.e: Literally 'the party siding with' the government.
T4-0920.t: Remember the pair: 여당 'ruling party' vs. 야당 'opposition party'.

T4-0921.x: The opposition party strongly opposed the government's plan.
T4-0921.e: Literally 'party out in the field', meaning out of power.

T4-0922.ex: 다음 대선에서 누구에게 투표할지 아직 모르겠어요.
T4-0922.x: I still don't know who to vote for in the next presidential election.
T4-0922.t: News loves short forms: 총선 (parliamentary), 지방 선거 (local).

T4-0923.x: Voter turnout was quite high in this general election.
T4-0923.e: Short for 총선거 'general election'; in Korea it elects the National Assembly.

T4-0924.x: Last night the candidates appeared in a televised debate.
T4-0924.e: Literally 'person waiting to fill' a post; -자 = person.

T4-0925.ex: 유권자들은 후보자의 공약을 꼼꼼히 살펴봐야 해요.
T4-0925.x: Voters should look carefully at the candidates' campaign promises.
T4-0925.e: Literally 'person who has the right' to vote.
T4-0925.t: Pronounced [유꿘자] — the ㄱ in 권 is tensed.

T4-0926.x: Voter turnout in this election exceeded 70 percent.
T4-0926.t: Write -율 after a vowel or ㄴ, -률 after other consonants: 투표율 but 합격률.

T4-0927.x: In Korea, you have the right to vote from age 18.

T4-0928.m: being elected, winning (an election or contest)
T4-0928.x: He was elected mayor by a wide margin.
T4-0928.t: 당선되다 is for elections and contests; for lotteries use 당첨되다.

T4-0929.ex: 그 후보는 공약을 모두 지키겠다고 말했어요.
T4-0929.x: That candidate said he would keep all his campaign promises.

T4-0930.ex: 많은 사람들이 정치인의 말을 잘 믿지 않아요.
T4-0930.x: Many people don't really trust what politicians say.

T4-0931.x: That decision was made for political reasons.

T4-0932.x: Elections are the most important part of democracy.
T4-0932.t: Commonly pronounced [민주주이]; the possessive 민주주의의 is said [민주주이에].

T4-0933.x: Korea achieved democratization in the 1980s through great effort.
T4-0933.t: 민주화 운동 usually refers to Korea's pro-democracy movement, such as Gwangju 1980 and June 1987.

T4-0934.ex: 그 나라 국민들은 오랫동안 독재에 맞서 싸웠어요.
T4-0934.x: The people of that country fought against dictatorship for a long time.
T4-0934.t: Pronounced [독째] — ㅈ becomes tense after ㄱ.

T4-0935.ex: 새 정권이 들어선 후 많은 정책이 바뀌었어요.
T4-0935.x: Many policies changed after the new administration took power.
T4-0935.t: Pronounced [정꿘]; 정권 교체 means 'a change of government'.

T4-0936.ex: 두 나라는 외교 관계를 다시 시작했어요.
T4-0936.x: The two countries resumed diplomatic relations.

T4-0937.ex: 제 꿈은 외교관이 되어서 해외에서 일하는 거예요.
T4-0937.x: My dream is to become a diplomat and work abroad.
T4-0937.e: Literally 'outside-exchange official': an official who handles dealings with other countries.

T4-0938.ex: 정부는 올해 국방 예산을 크게 늘렸습니다.
T4-0938.x: The government greatly increased the defense budget this year.
T4-0938.t: Pronounced [국빵] — the ㅂ after ㄱ becomes tense.

T4-0939.ex: 한국 남자들은 대부분 군대에 가야 해요.
T4-0939.x: Most Korean men have to go to the military.
T4-0939.t: '군대에 가다' (go to the military) is the everyday way to say someone is doing military service.

T4-0940.ex: 동생이 다음 달에 입대해서 가족들이 걱정하고 있어요.
T4-0940.x: My younger brother enlists next month, so my family is worried.

T4-0941.ex: 형은 작년에 제대하고 다시 대학교에 다니고 있어요.
T4-0941.x: My older brother was discharged last year and is back in college.
T4-0941.t: In official settings 전역 is preferred, but 제대 is very common in everyday speech.

T4-0942.ex: 한국에서는 건강한 남성이라면 병역의 의무가 있습니다.
T4-0942.x: In Korea, healthy men have a duty to do military service.
T4-0942.t: Usually heard in set phrases like 병역의 의무 (duty of military service) and 병역 면제 (exemption).

T4-0943.x: The school sent an official letter to the parents.

T4-0944.x: Forging an official document leads to severe punishment.

T4-0945.x: I have to submit a certificate of enrollment to the company.
T4-0945.e: Literally 'a document that makes something clearly proven'.
T4-0945.t: Collocation: 증명서를 발급받다 = to get a certificate issued.

T4-0946.m: certified copy (of a register), resident registration copy
T4-0946.x: I got a copy of my resident registration from the community center.
T4-0946.e: Literally 'a copied-out version of the original' record.
T4-0946.t: Koreans say 등본을 떼다 for getting one issued, literally 'to tear off' a copy.

T4-0947.m: resident registration card, national ID card
T4-0947.ex: 은행에서 계좌를 만들 때 주민등록증이 필요해요.
T4-0947.x: You need your national ID card to open a bank account.
T4-0947.t: Pronounced [주민등녹쯩]; in conversation people often shorten it to 주민증.

T4-0948.ex: 이사하면 새 주소로 주민 등록을 옮겨야 해요.
T4-0948.x: When you move, you have to transfer your resident registration to the new address.
T4-0948.e: Literally 'registering the people who live here'.
T4-0948.t: Pronounced [주민등녹] — ㄹ after the ㅇ of 등 becomes [ㄴ].

T4-0949.m: immigration, entry and departure (of a country)
T4-0949.ex: 비자 문제로 출입국 관리 사무소에 다녀왔어요.
T4-0949.x: I went to the immigration office about a visa problem.
T4-0949.e: Literally 'going out of and into the country'.

T4-0950.ex: 집을 살 때는 인감 증명서가 필요합니다.
T4-0950.x: When you buy a house, you need a seal certificate.
T4-0950.e: A seal registered with the government so others can check that it's genuine.
T4-0950.t: Koreans traditionally use a registered stamp (인감 도장) instead of a signature for big contracts.

T4-0951.ex: 본인이 못 오면 대리인이 서류를 받을 수 있어요.
T4-0951.x: If you can't come yourself, a representative can pick up the documents.
T4-0951.e: Literally 'a person who manages things in your place'.

T4-0952.x: The deadline for the application is this Friday.
T4-0952.t: Pronounced [마가밀]; 마감하다 means 'to close' applications or a shop for the day.

T4-0953.x: A job posting went up on the company website.

T4-0954.ex: 이번 달 전기 요금 고지서가 집으로 왔어요.
T4-0954.x: This month's electricity bill came to the house.
T4-0954.e: Literally 'a document that lets you know' what you owe.

T4-0955.ex: 카드 값을 연체하면 신용 점수가 떨어져요.
T4-0955.x: If you're late on your card payments, your credit score drops.
T4-0955.e: Literally 'delayed and stuck': a payment that hasn't moved on time.

T4-0956.x: I returned the book late, so I paid a late fee.

T4-0957.x: I bought cosmetics at the airport duty-free shop.

T4-0958.x: A guardian's consent is required before surgery.
T4-0958.e: -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.
T4-0958.t: In Korean hospitals, the family member caring for a patient is called the 보호자.

T4-0959.ex: 아버지가 돌아가신 후 형제들이 재산을 상속했어요.
T4-0959.x: After their father passed away, the siblings inherited the property.
T4-0959.e: Wealth that continues from one generation to the next.

T4-0960.ex: 할아버지가 남기신 유산으로 작은 집을 샀어요.
T4-0960.x: We bought a small house with the inheritance my grandfather left.
T4-0960.e: Literally 'property left behind'. Homonym warning: another 유산 means miscarriage.

T4-0961.ex: 할머니는 가족들에게 사이좋게 지내라는 유언을 남기셨어요.
T4-0961.x: Grandma's last words to the family were to get along with each other.
T4-0961.t: Collocation: 유언을 남기다 = to leave a will or last words.

T4-0962.x: Ownership of this building belongs to City Hall.

T4-0963.x: The first floor of this building is leased out as shops.
T4-0963.e: Literally 'lend for rent'. The owner does 임대; the tenant does 임차.
T4-0963.t: A sign saying '임대' on an empty shop means 'for rent'.

T4-0964.ex: 가게 임대료가 너무 올라서 장사가 힘들어요.
T4-0964.x: The store's rent went up so much that business is hard.

T4-0965.ex: 집을 계약할 때 계약금으로 천만 원을 냈어요.
T4-0965.x: When I signed for the house, I paid ten million won as a down payment.
T4-0965.e: -금 = money for a purpose: 계약금, 보상금, 장학금.

T4-0966.m: penalty for breaking a contract, cancellation fee
T4-0966.x: I canceled my phone contract early, so I had to pay a penalty.
T4-0966.t: Collocation: 위약금을 물다 or 위약금을 내다 = to pay a penalty.

T4-0967.x: I went to a neighborhood real estate office and looked into studio apartments.
T4-0967.t: In everyday speech people simply say 부동산 for a real estate office.

T4-0968.ex: 공인 중개사가 계약서 내용을 자세히 설명해 줬어요.
T4-0968.x: The realtor explained the contract in detail.

T4-0969.ex: 피해자는 회사를 상대로 손해 배상을 청구했습니다.
T4-0969.x: The victim filed a claim for damages against the company.
T4-0969.t: Collocation: 손해 배상을 청구하다 = to claim damages.

T4-0970.ex: 택배 회사가 깨진 물건을 배상해 주기로 했어요.
T4-0970.x: The delivery company agreed to compensate for the broken item.
T4-0970.t: 배상 is paid for wrongdoing or damage you caused; 보상 is for a loss without fault.

T4-0971.ex: 열심히 노력한 만큼 좋은 보상을 받았어요.
T4-0971.x: I got a good reward for all the effort I put in.

T4-0972.ex: 공사 때문에 이사한 주민들은 보상금을 받았어요.
T4-0972.x: Residents who moved because of the construction received compensation.

T4-0973.ex: 그 유명한 변호사가 이 사건의 변호를 맡았어요.
T4-0973.x: That famous lawyer took on the defense in this case.

T4-0974.ex: 그는 사고를 직접 본 증인으로 법정에 나왔어요.
T4-0974.x: He appeared in court as a witness who saw the accident firsthand.

T4-0975.ex: 목격자의 증언 덕분에 범인을 잡을 수 있었어요.
T4-0975.x: Thanks to the eyewitness's testimony, they were able to catch the criminal.

T4-0976.ex: 경찰은 아직 확실한 증거를 찾지 못했어요.
T4-0976.x: The police still haven't found any solid evidence.

T4-0977.ex: 제가 그날 집에 있었다는 걸 증명할 수 있어요.
T4-0977.x: I can prove that I was at home that day.

T4-0978.m: statement (to police or in court), account
T4-0978.ex: 두 사람의 진술이 서로 달라서 조사가 길어졌어요.
T4-0978.x: The two people's statements didn't match, so the investigation dragged on.

T4-0979.ex: 화가 나도 감정적으로 말하지 않으려고 노력해요.
T4-0979.x: Even when I'm angry, I try not to speak emotionally.
T4-0979.e: -적 turns a noun into '-al/-ic': 감정적, 경제적, 문화적.
T4-0979.t: Use 감정적인 before nouns and 감정적으로 as an adverb; 감정적이다 works as a predicate.

T4-0980.ex: 우승이 확정되자 선수들은 감격의 눈물을 흘렸어요.
T4-0980.x: When the championship was confirmed, the players shed tears of emotion.
T4-0980.t: 감격 is stronger and more overwhelming than 감동; often in 감격의 눈물 (tears of joy).

T4-0981.ex: 10년 만에 가족을 다시 만나서 정말 감격스러웠어요.
T4-0981.x: It was truly overwhelming to see my family again after ten years.
T4-0981.e: 감격 + -스럽다 'full of': full of stirred-up feelings.

T4-0982.x: The tourists marveled at the beautiful scenery.
T4-0982.e: Literally 'feel and sigh' — the 'wow' you let out at something amazing.

T4-0983.m: overwhelmed (with emotion), full to bursting; too much to handle
T4-0983.ex: 아이가 태어난 날 가슴이 벅차서 말이 안 나왔어요.
T4-0983.x: The day my child was born, my heart was so full I couldn't speak.
T4-0983.e: Two uses: 가슴이 벅차다 (heart bursting with joy) and 일이 벅차다 (work is too much).
T4-0983.t: Usually with 가슴: 가슴 벅찬 순간 (a heart-swelling moment).

T4-0984.m: touched, moved (feeling a lump in your chest)
T4-0984.x: I was moved when I read my parents' letter.
T4-0984.e: Sound-symbolic: like a soft lump welling up in your chest.
T4-0984.t: Usually with 가슴 or 마음: 가슴이 뭉클하다.

T4-0985.m: touched, moved (to the point of tears)
T4-0985.ex: 영화 마지막 장면을 보고 코끝이 찡했어요.
T4-0985.x: The last scene of the movie got me choked up.
T4-0985.e: Sound-symbolic: the sharp tingle in your nose just before tears come.
T4-0985.t: Common phrases: 코끝이 찡하다 (tingle at the tip of the nose) and 가슴이 찡하다.

T4-0986.ex: 할머니는 손자들이 노는 모습을 흐뭇하게 바라보셨어요.
T4-0986.x: Grandma watched her grandchildren play with a contented smile.
T4-0986.t: Often used for the warm feeling of watching someone you care about, as in 흐뭇한 미소.

T4-0987.x: The boss was very pleased with the results this time.
T4-0987.t: Pronounced [흡조카다]; for someone else's feelings, use 흡족해하다.

T4-0988.x: All my exams are over, so I feel so much lighter.
T4-0988.t: Also used for traveling light: 짐이 없어서 홀가분해요 (No luggage, so I feel free).

T4-0989.m: relieved, refreshed (after getting something off your chest)
T4-0989.ex: 친구한테 고민을 다 털어놓으니까 속이 후련해요.
T4-0989.x: I told my friend all my worries, and now I feel relieved.
T4-0989.t: Typical phrases: 속이 후련하다, 속 시원하다 — both mean the frustration inside is finally released.

T4-0990.m: refreshed, clean-feeling; (of taste) clean and light
T4-0990.ex: 샤워를 하고 나니까 몸이 정말 개운해요.
T4-0990.x: After taking a shower, my body feels really refreshed.
T4-0990.t: Also describes soups: 국물이 개운하다 means the broth tastes clean and not greasy.

T4-0991.m: reassured, secure; reliable; (of a meal) filling
T4-0991.ex: 힘들 때 옆에 친구가 있어서 든든해요.
T4-0991.x: I feel reassured having my friend by my side during hard times.
T4-0991.t: After a big meal Koreans say 배가 든든해요 (I'm nicely full).

T4-0992.ex: 새 학기를 앞두고 기대와 설렘으로 잠을 못 잤어요.
T4-0992.x: Before the new semester, I couldn't sleep from anticipation and excitement.
T4-0992.e: Noun from 설레다 (to flutter). Spelled 설렘, not 설레임.
T4-0992.t: Pronounced [설렘] — the ㄹㄹ is a long 'l' sound, not an 'r'.

T4-0993.ex: 아이의 웃음은 우리 가족에게 큰 기쁨이에요.
T4-0993.x: Our child's laughter is a great joy to our family.

T4-0994.ex: 요리하는 즐거움을 알게 된 후 매일 집에서 밥을 해요.
T4-0994.x: Ever since I discovered the joy of cooking, I make meals at home every day.
T4-0994.e: Noun from 즐겁다 (to be fun); the ㅂ becomes 우.
T4-0994.t: 기쁨 is joy from good news; 즐거움 is the fun of an activity, like 여행의 즐거움.

T4-0995.ex: 그 노래를 들으면 이별의 슬픔이 느껴져요.
T4-0995.x: When I listen to that song, I can feel the sorrow of parting.

T4-0996.ex: 혼자 외국에서 살 때 외로움을 많이 느꼈어요.
T4-0996.x: I felt very lonely when I lived abroad by myself.
T4-0996.e: Noun from 외롭다 (to be lonely); the ㅂ becomes 우.
T4-0996.t: Collocation: 외로움을 타다 = to be prone to loneliness, to get lonely easily.

T4-0997.x: My longing for my hometown grew bigger and bigger.
T4-0997.e: Noun from 그립다 (to miss); same root as 그리워하다.

T4-0998.m: sorrow, feeling of being wronged or left out
T4-0998.ex: 아플 때 혼자 있으니까 서러움이 밀려왔어요.
T4-0998.x: When I was sick and all alone, a wave of self-pity washed over me.
T4-0998.e: Noun from 서럽다 (to feel sorrowful); the ㅂ becomes 우.

T4-0999.m: sorrowful, sad (feeling hurt, neglected, or wronged)
T4-0999.ex: 아무도 내 말을 믿어 주지 않아서 너무 서러웠어요.
T4-0999.x: Nobody believed me, and it hurt so much.
T4-0999.t: 서럽다 is sadness mixed with feeling unfairly treated or uncared for, unlike plain 슬프다.

T4-1000.ex: 그는 실수 때문에 오랫동안 괴로움에 시달렸어요.
T4-1000.x: He was tormented for a long time because of his mistake.
T4-1000.e: Noun from 괴롭다 (to be painful); the ㅂ becomes 우.

T4-1001.x: After the breakup, I was in so much pain for a while.
T4-1001.e: Related to 괴롭히다 (to bully, torment someone).

T4-1002.forms: 괴로워해요 · 괴로워했어요 · 괴로워할 거예요 · 괴로워하지 마세요
T4-1002.m: to suffer, to be distressed, to agonize
T4-1002.ex: 친구가 시험에 떨어져서 많이 괴로워하고 있어요.
T4-1002.x: My friend failed the exam and is really struggling.
T4-1002.t: Use 괴롭다 for your own feelings, but 괴로워하다 to describe someone else's.

T4-1003.ex: 시간이 지나면 이별의 아픔도 조금씩 잊혀요.
T4-1003.x: As time passes, even the pain of a breakup slowly fades.

T4-1004.ex: 반려견이 죽은 후 큰 상실감을 느꼈어요.
T4-1004.x: After my dog died, I felt a deep sense of loss.
T4-1004.e: -감 = a feeling or sense: 상실감, 우울감, 자신감.

T4-1005.x: Now that my roommate has moved out, the room feels empty.
T4-1005.t: Also used when something usual is missing: 시계가 없으니까 손목이 허전해요.

T4-1006.m: drained, deflated, dejected (after effort comes to nothing)
T4-1006.ex: 열심히 준비한 행사가 취소되어서 정말 허탈했어요.
