T4-1006.x: The event I'd worked so hard on was canceled, and I felt completely deflated.
T4-1006.e: Literally 'emptied out', as if all your strength has slipped away.

T4-1007.ex: 한 골 차이로 지니까 너무 허무했어요.
T4-1007.x: Losing by just one goal felt so pointless.

T4-1008.ex: 돈은 많이 벌었지만 마음은 늘 공허했어요.
T4-1008.x: I made a lot of money, but my heart always felt empty.
T4-1008.e: Two 'empty' syllables doubled for a deep, hollow emptiness.
T4-1008.t: More literary than 허전하다; also describes words, as in 공허한 약속 (empty promises).

T4-1009.m: at a loss, hopeless, bleak (not knowing what to do)
T4-1009.ex: 직장을 잃고 앞으로 어떻게 살아야 할지 막막했어요.
T4-1009.x: After losing my job, I had no idea how I was going to get by.
T4-1009.e: Literally 'vast and vast', like standing in an endless desert with no path.

T4-1010.x: The situation was hopeless, but we didn't give up.

T4-1011.x: Don't get discouraged just because you failed a few times.
T4-1011.e: Literally 'bent and snapped', like a branch breaking.
T4-1011.t: 좌절 is being crushed by failure, not everyday annoyance; for that, use 짜증.

T4-1012.x: I failed the interview, but I didn't get too discouraged.
T4-1012.e: Literally 'your gallbladder drops'; the gallbladder was thought to be the seat of courage.

T4-1013.ex: 선생님께 혼난 후로 동생이 의기소침해 있어요.
T4-1013.x: My younger sibling has been down ever since getting scolded by the teacher.
T4-1013.e: Literally 'your will and spirit melt away and sink'.
T4-1013.t: Often used as 의기소침해 있다 (to be in low spirits) or 의기소침해지다 (to become dejected).

T4-1014.ex: 겨울에는 햇빛이 부족해서 우울감을 느끼는 사람이 많아요.
T4-1014.x: In winter, many people feel down because there's not enough sunlight.

T4-1015.ex: 시험 결과를 듣고 그는 하루 종일 침울해 보였어요.
T4-1015.x: After hearing his test results, he looked gloomy all day.
T4-1015.e: Literally 'sunk in gloom' — a heavy, dark mood.

T4-1016.m: blue, down, gloomy, lonely and sad
T4-1016.ex: 비 오는 날에는 왠지 기분이 울적해요.
T4-1016.x: On rainy days, I feel down for some reason.
T4-1016.t: Pronounced [울쩌카다]: ㄱ + ㅎ becomes an aspirated ㅋ.

T4-1017.ex: 고향을 떠나는 날 마음이 정말 착잡했어요.
T4-1017.x: On the day I left my hometown, I had really mixed feelings.
T4-1017.e: Literally 'tangled and mixed' — emotions all jumbled together.

T4-1018.ex: 친구가 내 생일을 잊어버려서 좀 씁쓸했어요.
T4-1018.x: My friend forgot my birthday, so I felt a bit bitter.
T4-1018.e: Built from 쓰다 'bitter' — a taste word that also describes a disappointed feeling.

T4-1019.m: pitiful, heartbreaking to watch, feeling sorry for
T4-1019.x: I feel so sorry for my younger sibling, who works until late at night.
T4-1019.t: Used for people you care about who are struggling; it sounds warmer and less condescending than 불쌍하다.

T4-1020.ex: 길에서 떨고 있는 강아지가 너무 가엾었어요.
T4-1020.x: The puppy shivering on the street was so pitiful.
T4-1020.t: 가엽다 is also standard; it is ㅂ irregular: 가여워요, 가여운.

T4-1021.ex: 그 영화 속 아이가 너무 불쌍해서 울었어요.
T4-1021.x: The child in that movie was so pitiful that I cried.
T4-1021.t: Saying it directly to someone (너 불쌍해) can sound condescending; 안됐다 is gentler.

T4-1022.x: I don't need pity; I need help.
T4-1022.e: Literally 'same feeling' — feeling what another person feels.
T4-1022.t: Common pattern: 동정을 받다 'to receive pity' vs. 동정심 'a sense of compassion'.

T4-1023.ex: 그는 가난한 사람들에게 깊은 연민을 느꼈어요.
T4-1023.x: He felt deep compassion for poor people.
T4-1023.e: Two syllables that both mean 'pity', doubled for emphasis.

T4-1024.ex: 아이를 찾았다는 소식에 모두 안도의 한숨을 쉬었어요.
T4-1024.x: At the news that the child was found, everyone sighed with relief.
T4-1024.e: Literally 'at peace within one's walls' — safe at last.
T4-1024.t: Set phrase: 안도의 한숨을 쉬다 'to breathe a sigh of relief'.

T4-1025.x: Be sure to call when you arrive so Mom can stop worrying.
T4-1025.t: 안심하세요 'Don't worry, rest assured' is a very common reassuring phrase.

T4-1026.m: to be relieved, to feel reassured
T4-1026.ex: 선생님 말씀을 들으니까 이제 좀 안심돼요.
T4-1026.x: Now that I've heard what the doctor said, I feel a bit relieved.
T4-1026.e: 안심 'peace of mind' + 되다 'to become' — relief that comes over you.
T4-1026.t: 안심되다 is relief caused by something; 안심하다 is often used as a command: 안심하세요.

T4-1027.ex: 발표 순서를 기다리는 동안 마음이 조마조마했어요.
T4-1027.x: While waiting for my turn to present, I was on edge.
T4-1027.e: A doubled mimetic word that imitates a fluttering, anxious heart.

T4-1028.ex: 너무 조급하게 생각하지 말고 천천히 하세요.
T4-1028.x: Don't be so impatient; take it slowly.
T4-1028.t: Common phrase: 마음이 조급하다 'to feel impatient'; pronounced [조그파다].

T4-1029.ex: 실패에 대한 두려움 때문에 시작하지 못했어요.
T4-1029.x: I couldn't start because of my fear of failure.
T4-1029.e: Noun form of 두렵다 'to be afraid' (두려우- + -ㅁ).

T4-1030.ex: 저는 공포 영화를 혼자 못 봐요.
T4-1030.x: I can't watch horror movies alone.
T4-1030.e: Two syllables that both mean 'fear', doubled for intensity.

T4-1031.m: to be scared, to be frightened
T4-1031.ex: 혼자 밤길을 걷는 게 좀 겁나요.
T4-1031.x: I'm a little scared to walk alone at night.
T4-1031.e: 겁 'fear' + 나다 'to arise' — fear comes up in you.
T4-1031.t: Pronounced [검나다] — nasalization. In casual speech 겁나 also means 'super': 겁나 맛있어.

T4-1032.forms: 겁먹어요 · 겁먹었어요 · 겁먹을 거예요 · 겁먹지 마세요
T4-1032.m: to get scared, to be intimidated
T4-1032.ex: 큰 개를 보고 아이가 겁먹어서 울었어요.
T4-1032.x: The child got scared when he saw the big dog and cried.
T4-1032.e: 겁 'fear' + 먹다 'to eat' — literally 'to eat fear'.
T4-1032.t: Pronounced [검먹따]; 겁먹지 마 'Don't be scared' is a common reassurance.

T4-1033.ex: 그 사람의 차가운 웃음이 정말 섬뜩했어요.
T4-1033.x: That person's cold smile was really chilling.

T4-1034.x: Hearing the scary story sent a chill down my spine.
T4-1034.e: From the mimetic 오싹 — the sudden shiver.
T4-1034.t: Works for both cold and fear; 오싹오싹 intensifies it.

T4-1035.ex: 그 가수의 노래를 듣고 소름이 돋았어요.
T4-1035.x: I got goosebumps listening to that singer.
T4-1035.t: 소름 돋다 works for awe or fear; 소름 끼치다 is mostly for fear or disgust.

T4-1036.m: to give one the creeps, to send chills down one's spine
T4-1036.ex: 그 사건 이야기를 들으니까 소름이 끼쳐요.
T4-1036.x: Hearing about that incident gives me the creeps.

T4-1037.ex: 그 소식은 많은 사람들에게 놀라움을 주었어요.
T4-1037.x: That news came as a surprise to many people.

T4-1038.ex: 그렇게 쉬운 문제를 틀리다니 정말 어이없어요.
T4-1038.x: I can't believe I got such an easy question wrong. It's ridiculous.
T4-1038.e: 어이 + 없다 'to lack'; 어이 alone is not used, so learn it as a unit.
T4-1038.t: Pronounced [어이업따]; as a modifier, use 어이없는, not 어이없은.

T4-1039.m: to be dumbfounded, to be speechless; to be amazing, to be incredible
T4-1039.ex: 이 집 김치찌개는 정말 기가 막혀요.
T4-1039.x: The kimchi stew at this place is absolutely amazing.
T4-1039.e: Literally 'one's energy is blocked' — so shocked you can't breathe.
T4-1039.t: Context decides the sense: shock at something bad, or praise for something amazingly good, like food.

T4-1040.ex: 그런 어처구니없는 실수를 하다니 믿을 수가 없어요.
T4-1040.x: I can't believe he made such an absurd mistake.
T4-1040.e: Origin of 어처구니 is uncertain; the popular 'millstone handle' story is unproven.

T4-1041.x: I was suddenly asked a hard question, so I felt flustered.

T4-1042.m: awkward, embarrassing, in a difficult position
T4-1042.ex: 두 친구가 동시에 부탁해서 정말 난처했어요.
T4-1042.x: Two friends asked me for favors at the same time, so I was in a real bind.
T4-1042.t: Common pattern: 난처한 입장에 처하다 'to be put in an awkward position'.

T4-1043.m: embarrassing, awkward (to see or do); embarrassed
T4-1043.x: I fell in front of people, and it was so embarrassing.
T4-1043.e: Covers both your own embarrassment and secondhand embarrassment watching others.

T4-1044.x: Getting so many compliments makes me a little shy.
T4-1044.t: Used for mild, pleasant shyness, like being praised or on camera; it has no sense of guilt.

T4-1045.ex: 인사를 했는데 대답이 없어서 멋쩍게 웃었어요.
T4-1045.x: I said hello but got no answer, so I gave an awkward smile.
T4-1045.e: The suffix -쩍다 'seeming' also appears in 미심쩍다 'doubtful'.

T4-1046.ex: 그는 사람들 앞에서 혼나서 수치심을 느꼈어요.
T4-1046.x: He felt ashamed after being scolded in front of people.
T4-1046.e: Literally 'shame-disgrace heart'. -심 = a feeling or mindset: 수치심, 경계심, 동정심.

T4-1047.ex: 거짓말을 한 후에 계속 죄책감이 들었어요.
T4-1047.x: After I lied, I kept feeling guilty.
T4-1047.e: Literally 'feeling of blame for wrongdoing'. -감 = a feeling: 죄책감, 기대감, 호감.
T4-1047.t: Use 죄책감이 들다 or 죄책감을 느끼다 'to feel guilty'.

T4-1048.ex: 그 아이는 부끄러움이 많아서 말을 잘 안 해요.
T4-1048.x: That child is very shy, so she doesn't talk much.

T4-1049.m: venting one's anger, taking it out on someone
T4-1049.ex: 회사에서 힘들었다고 가족한테 화풀이하면 안 돼요.
T4-1049.x: You shouldn't take it out on your family just because work was hard.
T4-1049.t: Pattern: N한테 화풀이하다 'to take it out on N'.

T4-1050.m: resentful, bitter, mortified (at losing or being wronged)
T4-1050.x: We gave up a goal in the last minute, and it was so infuriating.

T4-1051.ex: 일이 잘못되어도 저는 아무도 원망하지 않아요.
T4-1051.x: Even if things go wrong, I don't blame anyone.
T4-1051.e: Literally 'resentful longing' — wishing things had been otherwise.
T4-1051.t: Often used toward people close to you or fate: 하늘을 원망하다 'to curse the heavens'.

T4-1052.e: Two 'hate' syllables combined; much stronger than everyday 미움.

T4-1053.ex: 그는 거짓말 때문에 친구들에게 미움을 받았어요.
T4-1053.x: He was disliked by his friends because of his lies.

T4-1054.ex: 인터넷의 혐오 표현은 큰 사회 문제입니다.
T4-1054.x: Hate speech online is a big social problem.
T4-1054.t: Common compounds: 혐오 표현 'hate speech', 혐오 시설 'unwanted facility (NIMBY)'.

T4-1055.ex: 직원의 무례한 태도 때문에 기분이 불쾌했어요.
T4-1055.x: I was offended by the employee's rude attitude.

T4-1056.ex: 그의 농담은 많은 사람들에게 불쾌감을 주었어요.

T4-1057.m: upset, displeased, in a bad mood
T4-1057.ex: 아버지는 제 대답을 듣고 언짢은 표정을 지으셨어요.
T4-1057.x: My father made a displeased face when he heard my answer.
T4-1057.t: Pronounced [언짠타]; ㄶ before ㄷ makes an aspirated ㅌ.

T4-1058.x: My grandmother disapproved of my short hair.
T4-1058.e: 못 'not' + 마땅하다 'proper, suitable' — something doesn't seem right to you.
T4-1058.t: Pronounced [몬마땅하다]; for a third person's feeling, use 못마땅해하다.

T4-1059.m: to be annoying, to bother, to get on one's nerves
T4-1059.ex: 옆 사람의 휴대폰 소리가 계속 귀에 거슬렸어요.
T4-1059.x: The sound of the person's phone next to me kept bothering me.
T4-1059.t: Usually paired with a sense: 귀에 거슬리다 (sound), 눈에 거슬리다 (sight), 비위에 거슬리다 (attitude).

T4-1060.x: When I'm tired, I snap at people without realizing it.
T4-1060.t: Set phrases: 신경질을 내다 'to snap', 신경질이 나다 'to get irritated'.

T4-1061.ex: 요즘 일이 많아서 그런지 그가 좀 신경질적이에요.
T4-1061.x: Maybe because he has a lot of work these days, he's a bit irritable.
T4-1061.e: -적 = '-ic, -al', turning a noun into a descriptor: 신경질적, 낙관적, 희망적.

T4-1062.ex: 광고 전화가 자꾸 와서 정말 성가셔요.
T4-1062.x: Spam calls keep coming, and it's really annoying.

T4-1063.ex: 매일 같은 음식을 먹으니까 이제 지겨워요.
T4-1063.x: I eat the same food every day, so I'm sick of it now.
T4-1063.t: 지루하다 is 'boring'; 지겹다 is stronger, 'so repetitive I'm sick of it'.

T4-1064.ex: 저는 무엇이든 금방 싫증을 내는 편이에요.
T4-1064.x: I tend to get bored of anything quickly.
T4-1064.t: Pronounced [실쯩]; use 싫증이 나다 'to grow tired of' or 싫증을 내다 'to show boredom'.

T4-1065.m: to be fed up with, to be sick of; to be appalled
T4-1065.ex: 이 노래는 아무리 들어도 질리지 않아요.
T4-1065.x: No matter how much I listen to this song, I never get tired of it.

T4-1066.x: I had nothing to do, so the weekend was boring.

T4-1067.m: bored, idle, with nothing to do
T4-1067.ex: 병원에 입원해 있는 동안 너무 무료했어요.
T4-1067.x: While I was in the hospital, I was so bored.
T4-1067.t: Homonym warning: 무료 입장 means 'free admission', not 'boring admission'.

T4-1068.x: I gave my younger brother a present, but his reaction was lukewarm.
T4-1068.t: Often describes a reaction or attitude: 반응이 시큰둥하다 'the response is lukewarm'.

T4-1069.x: She accepted the sad news calmly.
T4-1069.e: Literally 'mild and mild' — like a light, plain flavor.

T4-1070.x: Even after lying, he kept a straight face.
T4-1070.t: Often slightly negative: acting calm when you shouldn't be, as in 태연하게 거짓말하다.

T4-1071.ex: 새 정책에 대한 시민들의 반응은 냉담했습니다.
T4-1071.x: Citizens' reaction to the new policy was cold.
T4-1071.e: Literally 'cold and bland' — showing no warmth or interest.

T4-1072.ex: 바쁘다고 부모님께 너무 무심했던 것 같아요.
T4-1072.x: I think I've been too neglectful of my parents because I was busy.
T4-1072.e: Literally 'without heart' — not paying attention to others' feelings.

T4-1073.x: My father is gruff, but he has a warm heart.
T4-1073.e: A classic stereotype of reserved Korean fathers and men from the Gyeongsang region.
T4-1073.t: Pronounced [무뚝뚜카다]; usually describes personality, not one moment.

T4-1074.x: The clerk answered curtly, so I felt bad.
T4-1074.t: Usually describes a way of speaking: 퉁명스럽게 말하다 'to speak curtly'.

T4-1075.ex: 그 선생님은 학생들에게 친근하게 대해 주세요.
T4-1075.x: That teacher treats students in a friendly way.

T4-1076.ex: 그 배우는 이웃집 사람처럼 친근감이 느껴져요.
T4-1076.x: That actor feels as familiar as the person next door.

T4-1077.ex: 처음 만났을 때부터 그 사람에게 호감이 있었어요.
T4-1077.x: I've liked that person since we first met.
T4-1077.t: 호감이 가다 'to be drawn to'; 호감형 means 'a likable type', often said of faces.

T4-1078.ex: 강요하면 오히려 반감만 생길 수 있어요.
T4-1078.x: If you force it, you might only create resentment instead.

T4-1079.x: At first, I had an aversion to spicy food.
T4-1079.t: Common pattern: N에 거부감이 들다 'to feel resistant to N'.

T4-1080.x: The cat was wary of the stranger.

T4-1081.ex: 경찰은 그 남자를 범인으로 의심하고 있어요.
T4-1081.x: The police suspect that man of being the criminal.

T4-1082.x: I doubt whether what that person said is true.

T4-1083.ex: 우리 형은 어려울 때 언제나 믿음직한 사람이에요.
T4-1083.x: My older brother is always someone I can count on in hard times.
T4-1083.e: 믿음 'trust' (from 믿다) + -직하다 'rather, fairly' — worthy of trust.

T4-1084.x: My son became more dependable after coming back from the military.
T4-1084.e: 믿음직하다 with -스럽다 'seeming'; the meaning is almost the same.

T4-1085.ex: 새 학기를 앞두고 기대감이 커지고 있어요.
T4-1085.x: With the new semester ahead, my excitement is growing.

T4-1086.x: The doctor said the situation looks hopeful.
T4-1086.t: Pronounced [히망적] — ㅢ after a consonant sounds like ㅣ.

T4-1087.ex: 아직 경기 결과를 낙관하기는 조금 이릅니다.
T4-1087.x: It's still a little early to be optimistic about the game's outcome.

T4-1088.x: He always thinks optimistically about the future.
T4-1088.t: 낙관적 is about predictions or outlook; 낙천적 describes a cheerful personality.

T4-1089.ex: 한 번 실패했다고 너무 비관하지 마세요.
T4-1089.x: Don't despair just because you failed once.

T4-1090.ex: 전문가들은 경제 전망을 비관적으로 보고 있습니다.
T4-1090.x: Experts are taking a pessimistic view of the economic outlook.

T4-1091.ex: 그는 제 질문에 고개를 끄덕여 긍정했어요.
T4-1091.x: He nodded to say yes to my question.
T4-1091.e: Literally 'affirm and settle' — saying yes to something.
T4-1091.t: For a 'positive' attitude, Koreans use 긍정적: 긍정적인 사람 'a positive person'.

T4-1092.ex: 그 배우는 기자들 앞에서 소문을 강하게 부정했어요.
T4-1092.x: The actor strongly denied the rumor in front of reporters.
T4-1092.t: A different word, also spelled 부정, means 'injustice, cheating', as in 부정행위 'cheating on a test'.

T4-1093.ex: 저는 우리 회사에서 일하는 것에 자부심을 느껴요.
T4-1093.x: I take pride in working at our company.
T4-1093.e: Literally 'a heart that carries itself' — standing tall about what you do.

T4-1094.ex: 칭찬을 많이 받은 아이는 자존감이 높아요.
T4-1094.x: Children who get a lot of praise have high self-esteem.
T4-1094.t: 자존감 is healthy self-esteem; 자존심 is pride that can get hurt, as in 자존심이 상하다.

T4-1095.ex: 그는 형에 대해 열등감을 가지고 있어요.
T4-1095.x: He has an inferiority complex about his older brother.
T4-1095.e: Literally 'the feeling of being lower in rank'.
T4-1095.t: Pronounced [열뜽감] — ㄷ becomes tense after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

T4-1096.m: sense of alienation, feeling left out
T4-1096.ex: 새 학교에서 친구가 없어서 소외감을 느꼈어요.
T4-1096.x: I had no friends at my new school, so I felt left out.
T4-1096.e: Literally 'the feeling of being kept distant and outside'.

T4-1097.ex: 마라톤을 끝까지 뛰고 나니 큰 성취감을 느꼈어요.
T4-1097.x: After running the whole marathon, I felt a great sense of accomplishment.
T4-1097.t: 보람 is close but focuses on the work feeling worthwhile; 성취감 focuses on reaching a goal.

T4-1098.ex: 이 일을 하면서 큰 만족감을 얻어요.
T4-1098.x: I get a lot of satisfaction from doing this work.
T4-1098.e: Literally 'the feeling of being full and having enough'.

T4-1099.ex: 가족과 함께 있을 때 행복감을 느껴요.
T4-1099.x: I feel happy when I'm with my family.
T4-1099.e: Literally 'the feeling of good fortune and blessing'.

T4-1100.ex: 졸업식 날 선생님께 고마움을 전하고 싶어요.
T4-1100.x: I want to express my gratitude to my teacher on graduation day.
T4-1100.e: Noun from 고맙다 'thankful': ㅂ becomes 우, then -ㅁ is added.
T4-1100.t: Common patterns: 고마움을 전하다 or 고마움을 표현하다 'to express gratitude'.

T4-1101.m: regret, disappointment; a sense that something is missing
T4-1101.x: The trip was so short that I'm left wishing it had been longer.
T4-1101.e: Noun from 아쉽다 'regrettable, wanting': ㅂ becomes 우, then -ㅁ is added.
T4-1101.t: 아쉬움 is a mild 'too bad, I wish there were more', not the heavy guilt of 후회.

T4-1102.m: hurt feelings, disappointment (at being neglected); sadness at parting
T4-1102.ex: 친구가 내 생일을 잊어버려서 섭섭함을 느꼈어요.
T4-1102.x: My friend forgot my birthday, so I felt hurt.
T4-1102.e: Noun from 섭섭하다 'hurt, sad to part' + -ㅁ.
T4-1102.t: Pronounced [섭써팜] — ㅂ + ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T4-1103.m: hurt feelings, feeling let down (by someone close)
T4-1103.ex: 아들이 연락을 안 해서 엄마는 서운함을 느꼈어요.
T4-1103.x: The mother felt hurt because her son didn't keep in touch.
T4-1103.e: Noun from 서운하다 'hurt, let down' + -ㅁ; a near-synonym of 섭섭함.
T4-1103.t: Used when someone close falls short of your expectations; 서운해요 is a gentle way to say 'I'm a bit hurt.'

T4-1104.x: I got scolded even though I did nothing wrong, so I felt wronged.
T4-1104.e: Literally 'pressed-down gloom' — the frustration of unfair blame you can't fix.
T4-1104.t: 억울해요! is what Koreans say when blamed or punished for something they didn't do.

T4-1105.ex: 경기가 끝나자 팬들은 흥분해서 소리를 질렀어요.
T4-1105.x: When the game ended, the fans got excited and shouted.
T4-1105.t: 흥분하지 마세요 means 'calm down' — 흥분 often means getting worked up or angry, not just happy.

T4-1106.ex: 그 가수가 무대에 나오자 관객들이 열광했어요.
T4-1106.x: When the singer came on stage, the audience went wild.

T4-1107.ex: 그 선생님은 가르치는 일에 열정이 많아요.
T4-1107.x: That teacher is very passionate about teaching.

T4-1108.e: -적 turns a noun into '-ic/-ive': 열정 'passion' → 'passionate'; also 적극적, 사교적.

T4-1109.x: The students' eagerness to study is remarkable.
T4-1109.t: Pronounced [여리] — 의 after a consonant is usually said like 이.

T4-1110.ex: 요즘 너무 피곤해서 아무것도 할 의욕이 없어요.
T4-1110.x: I'm so tired these days that I have no motivation to do anything.
T4-1110.t: 의욕이 없다 'to have no motivation' is a very common way to describe feeling burned out.

T4-1111.ex: 새 팀장님은 일을 아주 의욕적으로 시작했어요.
T4-1111.x: The new team leader started the job with a lot of drive.

T4-1112.ex: 이번 시험에 꼭 합격하겠다는 각오로 공부하고 있어요.
T4-1112.x: I'm studying with the resolve to pass this exam no matter what.
T4-1112.e: Literally 'awaken and realize' — facing clearly what is coming.
T4-1112.t: 각오하다 also means bracing for something bad: 각오해! 'You'd better be ready!'

T4-1113.x: I resolved to exercise hard in the new year.
T4-1113.e: Related to 다지다 'to pack down, firm up' — making your intention solid.

T4-1114.e: Literally 'the power to decide and cut off' other options.
T4-1114.t: Pronounced [결딴녁] — tensing after ㄹ, and ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㄴ.

T4-1115.x: He hesitated for a long time over whether to confess his feelings.
T4-1115.t: Often used with -(으)ㄹ까 말까: 갈까 말까 망설이다 'to go back and forth about going'.

T4-1116.ex: 그 아이는 대답을 못 하고 머뭇거렸어요.
T4-1116.x: The child faltered and couldn't answer.
T4-1116.t: 머뭇거리다 is hesitation you can see in actions or speech; 망설이다 is more about inner indecision.

T4-1117.ex: 궁금한 것이 있으면 주저하지 말고 물어보세요.
T4-1117.x: If you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask.
T4-1117.e: Both syllables mean 'hesitate' — doubled for emphasis.
T4-1117.t: A bit more formal than 망설이다; 주저하지 마세요 'don't hesitate' is common in written messages.

T4-1118.x: That person has a gentle and kind nature.
T4-1118.e: Literally 'nature and quality' of a person.

T4-1119.ex: 그 선생님은 인품이 훌륭해서 모두가 존경해요.
T4-1119.x: That teacher has such fine character that everyone respects him.

T4-1120.m: character, personality; dignity as a person
T4-1120.x: You should respect other people's dignity.
T4-1120.e: Literally 'a person's standing' — your worth as a human being.
T4-1120.t: 인격 means moral character or dignity; for 'outgoing personality' use 성격 instead.

T4-1121.m: one's character, the kind of person one is
T4-1121.x: With people, character matters more than looks.
T4-1121.e: From 되다 'to become' — literally 'how a person has turned out'.

T4-1122.ex: 그는 어릴 때부터 예술가 기질이 있었어요.
T4-1122.x: He's had an artistic temperament since he was young.
T4-1122.e: Literally 'spirit and substance' — the temperament you are born with.
T4-1122.t: Often 'N 기질': 리더 기질, 예술가 기질 — a natural tendency to be like N.

T4-1123.x: When people get angry, their true nature shows.

T4-1124.x: Grandma is always lenient with her grandchildren.
T4-1124.e: Literally 'wide and big' — a big-hearted attitude.

T4-1125.x: That person has a gentle voice that's nice to listen to.

T4-1126.ex: 우리 아빠는 정말 자상하고 따뜻한 분이세요.
T4-1126.x: My dad is a really caring and warm person.
T4-1126.e: Literally 'careful and detailed' — attentive to every little need.

T4-1127.x: My boyfriend has a warm, affectionate personality.

T4-1128.ex: 그 친구는 배려심이 깊어서 인기가 많아요.
T4-1128.x: That friend is very considerate, so she's popular.
T4-1128.e: -심 = a heart or mind for something: 배려심, 이해심, 자부심.
T4-1128.t: 배려심이 깊다 or 배려심이 있다 'considerate' is a very common compliment.

T4-1129.ex: 우리 부모님은 이해심이 많으셔서 대화가 잘 통해요.
T4-1129.x: My parents are very understanding, so we communicate well.

T4-1130.e: 참을, the modifier of 참다 'to endure', + 성 'quality': the quality of enduring.

T4-1131.x: Learning a foreign language takes patience.

T4-1132.ex: 그는 끈기가 있어서 쉽게 포기하지 않아요.
T4-1132.x: He's tenacious, so he doesn't give up easily.
T4-1132.e: Literally 'sticky energy' — related to 끈끈하다 'sticky'; you stick with things.

T4-1133.ex: 그 기자는 대답을 들을 때까지 끈질기게 질문했어요.
T4-1133.x: The reporter kept asking persistently until he got an answer.
T4-1133.e: Probably related to 끈기 'stickiness' + 질기다 'tough, chewy' — hard to break.
T4-1133.t: Can be positive (tenacious) or negative (relentless), depending on context.

T4-1134.ex: 그는 집요하게 전화를 걸어서 결국 답을 받았어요.
T4-1134.x: He kept calling relentlessly and finally got an answer.
T4-1134.t: Usually more negative than 끈질기다, suggesting someone who just won't let it go.

T4-1135.ex: 우리 할아버지는 좀 고지식하셔서 규칙을 꼭 지키세요.
T4-1135.x: My grandfather is a bit rigid, so he always follows the rules.
T4-1135.e: Despite the look, probably unrelated to 지식 'knowledge'; it's a native word.
T4-1135.t: Not a harsh insult, but implies sticking to rules or principles without any flexibility.

T4-1136.ex: 일을 할 때는 융통성이 있어야 해요.
T4-1136.x: You need to be flexible when you work.
T4-1136.e: Literally 'the quality of blending and flowing through' — adapting to circumstances.
T4-1136.t: Pronounced [융통썽]; 융통성이 없다 'inflexible' is the most common pattern.

T4-1137.x: If you do yoga regularly, your body becomes flexible.

T4-1138.ex: 우리 부장님은 깐깐해서 작은 실수도 그냥 넘기지 않아요.
T4-1138.x: Our manager is so exacting that he doesn't let even small mistakes slide.
T4-1138.t: 깐깐하다 suggests strict and hard to please; 꼼꼼하다 is the positive 'meticulous'.

T4-1139.ex: 그 사람은 처음엔 까칠해 보였지만 사실 착해요.
T4-1139.x: He seemed prickly at first, but he's actually nice.
T4-1139.e: Originally 'rough, dry' skin — extended to a prickly personality.

T4-1140.ex: 그 배우는 유명하지만 성격이 아주 소탈해요.
T4-1140.x: That actor is famous, but he's very down-to-earth.
T4-1140.e: Literally 'loose and shed' — free of formality and airs.

T4-1141.ex: 그녀는 성격이 털털해서 누구와도 잘 어울려요.
T4-1141.x: She's easygoing, so she gets along with everyone.

T4-1142.ex: 새로 온 직원이 싹싹해서 모두 좋아해요.
T4-1142.x: The new employee is so friendly and polite that everyone likes her.
T4-1142.t: Praises someone, often younger, who greets people cheerfully and is quick to help; pronounced [싹싸카다].

T4-1143.m: sociability, knack for getting along with people
T4-1143.ex: 동생은 붙임성이 좋아서 친구를 쉽게 사귀어요.
T4-1143.x: My younger sibling is very sociable and makes friends easily.
T4-1143.e: 붙임 'attaching' (from 붙이다) + 성 'quality' — sticking easily to people.
T4-1143.t: Pronounced [부침썽]; the usual pattern is 붙임성이 좋다 or 붙임성이 있다.

T4-1144.x: He has an outgoing personality, so he likes get-togethers.

T4-1145.ex: 사교성이 좋은 사람은 어디서나 친구를 쉽게 만들어요.
T4-1145.x: People with good social skills make friends easily anywhere.
T4-1145.e: -성 = a quality or trait: 사교성, 융통성, 적극성.

T4-1146.ex: 우리 딸은 성격이 활달해서 친구가 많아요.
T4-1146.x: My daughter has a lively personality, so she has lots of friends.
T4-1146.e: Literally 'lively and getting through' — energetic and free-spirited.

T4-1147.x: She always greets people with a cheerful smile.

T4-1148.ex: 그는 낙천적이라서 걱정을 별로 안 해요.
T4-1148.x: He's optimistic, so he doesn't worry much.
T4-1148.e: Literally 'enjoying heaven' — content with whatever fate brings.
T4-1148.t: 낙천적 describes a personality; 낙관적 describes a view of a situation, as in 낙관적인 전망.

T4-1149.ex: 우리 회사는 진취적인 인재를 찾고 있어요.
T4-1149.x: Our company is looking for enterprising people.
T4-1149.e: Literally 'advancing and taking' — going after new opportunities.

T4-1150.ex: 회의에서 자기 의견을 말하는 적극성이 필요해요.
T4-1150.x: You need the initiative to share your opinions in meetings.
T4-1150.e: Literally 'piling up to the extreme' — going all in.

T4-1151.ex: 수업 시간에 너무 수동적인 태도는 좋지 않아요.
T4-1151.x: Being too passive in class isn't a good attitude.
T4-1151.e: Literally 'receiving movement' — being moved by others.

T4-1152.ex: 시키는 일만 하지 말고 능동적으로 일하세요.
T4-1152.x: Don't just do what you're told — work proactively.
T4-1152.e: Literally 'able to move' on your own.
T4-1152.t: Grammar terms use the same pair: 능동태 'active voice', 수동태 'passive voice'.

T4-1153.x: My older sister has lived independently since college.
T4-1153.t: Pronounced [동닙쩍] — nasalization: ㄱ + ㄹ becomes ㅇ + ㄴ.

T4-1154.x: He's still too dependent on his parents.

T4-1155.ex: 세일이라서 충동적으로 비싼 옷을 사 버렸어요.
T4-1155.x: It was on sale, so I impulsively bought expensive clothes.
T4-1155.t: 충동구매 'impulse buying' is a very common collocation.

T4-1156.ex: 우리는 주말에 즉흥적으로 바다에 가기로 했어요.
T4-1156.x: We spontaneously decided to go to the beach on the weekend.
T4-1156.e: Literally 'immediate mood' — acting on the feeling of the moment.
T4-1156.t: Pronounced [즈킁적]; more neutral than 충동적 and often positive, like a spontaneous trip.

T4-1157.ex: 그는 계획적인 사람이라서 매일 일정을 정리해요.
T4-1157.x: He's a methodical person, so he organizes his schedule every day.
T4-1157.t: Can also mean 'premeditated' in a bad sense: 계획적인 범죄 'a premeditated crime'.

T4-1158.e: Literally 'body-system' — organized as one whole structure.

T4-1159.m: meticulous, thorough; (of plans) carefully worked out
T4-1159.ex: 그는 여행 계획을 아주 치밀하게 세웠어요.
T4-1159.x: He planned the trip very meticulously.
T4-1159.e: Literally 'fine and dense' — leaving no gaps.

T4-1160.forms: 덜렁대요 · 덜렁댔어요 · 덜렁댈 거예요 · 덜렁대지 마세요
T4-1160.m: to be careless, to be scatterbrained
T4-1160.x: I'm scatterbrained, so I often lose things.
T4-1160.e: Mimetic 덜렁 'loosely, carelessly' + -대다 'keep doing'; a scatterbrain is 덜렁이.
T4-1160.t: Describes a habit more than a single act; 덜렁거리다 means the same.

T4-1161.forms: 덤벙대요 · 덤벙댔어요 · 덤벙댈 거예요 · 덤벙대지 마세요
T4-1161.m: to act rashly, to be careless and hasty
T4-1161.x: Don't rush — read the question slowly.
T4-1161.t: 덤벙대다 stresses rushing in without thinking; 덜렁대다 stresses forgetfulness.

T4-1162.x: The child is very distracted in class.

T4-1163.x: I'm sorry for speaking so thoughtlessly.
T4-1163.e: Literally 'light and hasty' — not weighing your words.
T4-1163.t: Common in apologies: 제가 경솔했습니다 'I was thoughtless.'

T4-1164.m: big-hearted, broad-minded; unfazed by small things
T4-1164.ex: 그는 대범해서 작은 실수에는 신경 쓰지 않아요.
T4-1164.x: He's easygoing about things, so he doesn't worry about small mistakes.
T4-1164.e: Literally 'big and broad' — not bothered by little things.

T4-1165.ex: 그녀는 대담하게 사장님께 자기 의견을 말했어요.
T4-1165.x: She boldly told the boss her opinion.
T4-1165.e: Literally 'big gallbladder' — traditionally the gallbladder was seen as the seat of courage.
T4-1165.t: Don't confuse it with the noun 대담 'a dialogue, interview', which is written with different hanja.

T4-1166.x: The company boldly invested in a new market.

T4-1167.ex: 친구를 두고 혼자 도망가는 건 비겁해요.
T4-1167.x: Running away alone and leaving your friend behind is cowardly.
T4-1167.t: Also means 'dirty, unfair': 비겁한 방법 'a dirty trick'.

T4-1168.x: In an interview, state your thoughts confidently.
T4-1168.e: Literally 'hall-hall' — grand and imposing like a great hall.

T4-1169.x: My little brother is in elementary school, but he's very mature.
T4-1169.t: Usually praises children or young people who behave calmly and maturely; pronounced [의저타다].

T4-1170.x: That child is mature for her age.

T4-1171.ex: 동생은 아직도 철없는 행동을 자주 해요.
T4-1171.x: My younger sibling still often acts immaturely.
T4-1171.e: 철 means good sense or maturity; 없다 means 'lacking.'
T4-1171.t: Pronounced [처럽따] — the ㄹ links over to the next syllable.

T4-1172.forms: 철이 들어요 · 철이 들었어요 · 철이 든 사람 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1172.m: to grow up, to mature, to come to one's senses
T4-1172.ex: 군대에 다녀온 후에 아들이 철이 들었어요.
T4-1172.x: My son grew up after he came back from the military.
T4-1172.e: Literally 'good sense comes in' — 들다 means to enter.

T4-1173.x: Please stop making such childish jokes now.
T4-1173.t: A different 유치하다 means 'to attract' (investment, events), as in 올림픽을 유치하다.

T4-1174.x: I really love children's pure hearts.

T4-1175.x: The people in the country village were simple, honest and kind.
T4-1175.e: Literally 'pure and plain,' like uncarved wood.
T4-1175.t: Pronounced [순바카다] — ㄱ plus ㅎ becomes a strong [ㅋ].

T4-1176.x: The child smiled brightly with an innocent face.
T4-1176.e: Literally 'heaven-given true nature' — untouched by the world.

T4-1177.ex: 그 친구는 가끔 엉뚱한 질문을 해요.
T4-1177.x: That friend sometimes asks off-the-wall questions.
T4-1177.t: Can be playful and positive: 엉뚱한 상상 means quirky, creative imagination.

T4-1178.x: The weather has been really fickle lately.
T4-1178.t: Common collocations: 변덕이 심하다 (to be very fickle) and 변덕을 부리다 (to act on a whim).

T4-1179.x: Spring weather in Korea is really changeable.

T4-1180.ex: 제 동생은 과자를 혼자 다 먹는 욕심쟁이예요.
T4-1180.x: My little brother is a greedy guy who eats all the snacks by himself.
T4-1180.e: 'Desire-heart' plus -쟁이, 'person who habitually is so': 겁쟁이, 거짓말쟁이.

T4-1181.x: That person is way too stingy with money.
T4-1181.e: Both syllables mean tight-fisted: 'stingy and miserly.'
T4-1181.t: Also used for praise: 칭찬에 인색하다 means 'slow to praise others.'

T4-1182.x: My uncle is a famous cheapskate in the neighborhood.
T4-1182.e: Not related to 구두 'dress shoes'; the origin is uncertain.

T4-1183.ex: 그 식당은 인심이 후해서 손님이 많아요.
T4-1183.x: That restaurant is generous with its portions, so it has lots of customers.
T4-1183.e: Literally 'thick' — generosity pictured as an ample, thick portion.
T4-1183.t: Common collocations: 인심이 후하다 and 점수를 후하게 주다 (to grade generously).

T4-1184.forms: 베풀어요 · 베풀었어요 · 베풀 거예요 · 베푸세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1184.m: to give, to bestow, to show (kindness); to throw (a party)
T4-1184.ex: 그분은 어려운 이웃에게 항상 사랑을 베풀어요.
T4-1184.x: That person always shows love to neighbors in need.
T4-1184.t: Takes abstract objects like 친절, 은혜, 사랑, or 잔치 (to throw a feast).

T4-1185.x: Even after lying, he smiled shamelessly.
T4-1185.t: 뻔뻔스럽다 means the same thing and is equally common.

T4-1186.ex: 염치가 있으면 그런 부탁은 못 해요.
T4-1186.x: If you had any sense of shame, you couldn't ask a favor like that.

T4-1187.x: I hate to impose, but please help me just one more time.
T4-1187.t: 염치없지만 is a humble opener meaning 'I'm embarrassed to ask, but…'.

T4-1188.x: The junior acted cocky toward his senior.
T4-1188.t: Usually said of someone younger or junior acting above their place.

T4-1189.ex: 어른 앞에서 그렇게 말하면 버릇없어 보여요.
T4-1189.x: Talking like that in front of elders looks rude.
T4-1189.t: Pronounced [버르덥따] — the final ㅅ turns into [ㄷ] before linking.

T4-1190.ex: 그런 질문은 좀 무례한 것 같아요.
T4-1190.x: I think that kind of question is a bit rude.

T4-1191.x: Even after he succeeded, he wasn't arrogant.
T4-1191.t: 오만 alone can also mean 50,000; context tells you which.

T4-1192.ex: 교만한 사람은 다른 사람의 말을 잘 듣지 않아요.
T4-1192.x: Arrogant people don't listen well to others.
T4-1192.t: More literary than 거만하다; common in proverbs, sermons and moral lessons.

T4-1193.ex: 그는 친구들 앞에서 허세를 부리는 걸 좋아해요.
T4-1193.x: He likes to put on a show in front of his friends.
T4-1193.e: Literally 'empty power' — a show of strength with nothing behind it.
T4-1193.t: Collocation: 허세를 부리다 means to put on airs or show off.

T4-1194.ex: 비싼 가방을 사는 것은 허영심 때문일 수도 있어요.
T4-1194.x: Buying an expensive bag might be because of vanity.

T4-1195.ex: 삼촌은 늘 허풍이 심해서 아무도 안 믿어요.
T4-1195.x: My uncle always exaggerates so much that nobody believes him.
T4-1195.e: Literally 'empty wind' — just like 'hot air' in English.
T4-1195.t: Collocation: 허풍을 떨다 means to talk big or brag.

T4-1196.m: to show off, to flaunt, to display
T4-1196.x: He showed off his new car to his friends.

T4-1197.x: Humility is a very important virtue in Korea.
T4-1197.t: Answering praise with 아니에요 is a common, expected show of 겸손 in Korea.

T4-1198.x: I think honesty is the best policy.

T4-1199.x: Everyone was moved by his candid story.

T4-1200.x: If your words and actions differ, that's hypocrisy.

T4-1201.x: That politician's behavior is so hypocritical.
T4-1201.e: -적 = '-ic, -al,' turning nouns into descriptive words: 위선적, 가식적, 이타적.
T4-1201.t: -적 words describe nouns with 인: 위선적인 사람 (a hypocritical person).

T4-1202.ex: 그 사람의 웃음에는 가식이 전혀 없어요.
T4-1202.x: There's no pretense at all in that person's smile.

T4-1203.ex: 가식적인 칭찬은 별로 듣고 싶지 않아요.
T4-1203.x: I don't really want to hear fake compliments.
T4-1203.t: Pronounced [가식쩍]; a common criticism of celebrities who seem fake.

T4-1204.ex: 동화 속 여우는 늘 교활한 동물로 나와요.
T4-1204.x: In fairy tales, the fox always appears as a cunning animal.

T4-1205.m: shrewd, calculating, quick to look out for oneself
T4-1205.x: He shrewdly looked out only for his own interests.
T4-1205.e: Ends in 빠르다 'fast' — quick to grab an advantage.

T4-1206.m: tact, social awareness, sense for others' feelings; someone's mood or reaction
T4-1206.ex: 그 친구는 눈치가 없어서 자주 실수해요.
T4-1206.x: That friend has no social awareness, so he often makes blunders.
T4-1206.e: Probably built on 눈 'eye' — reading the room with your eyes.
T4-1206.t: A key cultural idea: quietly sensing what others think or want without being told.

T4-1207.forms: 눈치가 빨라요 · 눈치가 빨랐어요 · 눈치 빠른 사람 (르 irregular)
T4-1207.m: to be quick to pick up on things, to be perceptive
T4-1207.ex: 그녀는 눈치가 빨라서 금방 분위기를 알아챘어요.
T4-1207.x: She's perceptive, so she read the atmosphere right away.

T4-1208.forms: 눈치를 봐요 · 눈치를 봤어요 · 눈치 보지 마세요
T4-1208.m: to watch someone's mood, to walk on eggshells, to worry about others' reactions
T4-1208.ex: 신입 사원이라서 아직 상사 눈치를 많이 봐요.
T4-1208.x: I'm a new employee, so I still worry a lot about my boss's reactions.
T4-1208.t: 눈치 보지 마세요 is a kind way to say 'Don't worry about what others think.'

T4-1209.m: to notice, to sense, to catch on
T4-1209.ex: 엄마는 제가 거짓말한 걸 바로 눈치챘어요.
T4-1209.x: My mom caught on right away that I had lied.
T4-1209.e: 눈치 'social sense' plus 채다 'to catch on.'
T4-1209.t: Written as one word, unlike the phrase 눈치를 보다.

T4-1211.x: That child was bright from a young age.
T4-1211.e: Literally 'keen ears and bright eyes' — sharp senses, sharp mind.

T4-1212.x: He solved the difficult problem wisely.
T4-1212.e: 슬기 'wisdom' plus -롭다 'full of'; a native match for 지혜롭다.
T4-1212.t: Seen in the drama title 슬기로운 의사생활, known in English as 'Hospital Playlist.'

T4-1213.ex: 할머니는 삶의 지혜를 많이 알고 계세요.
T4-1213.x: My grandmother knows a lot of life wisdom.

T4-1214.x: A wise person stays calm even when angry.

T4-1215.ex: 그는 어리숙해 보여도 사실 아주 똑똑해요.
T4-1215.x: He may look naive, but he's actually very smart.
T4-1215.t: 어수룩하다 is an equally standard variant with the same meaning.

T4-1216.ex: 열쇠를 집에 두고 오다니 정말 멍청했어요.
T4-1216.x: Leaving my keys at home was really dumb.
T4-1216.t: Blunt and rude toward others; safest when talking about yourself or joking with close friends.

T4-1217.ex: 그는 다른 사람의 감정에 좀 둔감해요.
T4-1217.x: He's a bit insensitive to other people's feelings.

T4-1218.x: He is a diligent and conscientious employee at the company.
T4-1218.t: More formal than 부지런하다; common in writing, résumés and speeches.

T4-1219.x: On weekends I want to laze around at home.
T4-1219.t: Collocation: 게으름을 피우다 means to laze around or slack off.

T4-1220.x: After exams ended, my daily life got a bit lazy.

T4-1221.ex: 약속을 안 지키는 것은 무책임한 행동이에요.
T4-1221.x: Not keeping your promises is irresponsible behavior.

T4-1222.x: He is always faithful to his work.
T4-1222.t: A homonym 충실하다 means 'solid, substantial,' as in 내용이 충실하다.

T4-1223.ex: 부모님의 헌신 덕분에 대학에서 공부할 수 있었어요.
T4-1223.x: Thanks to my parents' devotion, I was able to study in college.
T4-1223.e: Literally 'offering one's body,' that is, giving oneself.

T4-1224.x: The nurses cared for the sick patients with devotion.

T4-1225.m: sacrifice; loss of life (in an accident or disaster)
T4-1225.ex: 많은 사람들의 희생으로 나라를 지킬 수 있었어요.
T4-1225.x: The country could be defended thanks to the sacrifice of many people.
T4-1225.e: Originally an animal offered in ancient rituals.
T4-1225.t: Pronounced [히생] — ㅢ after a consonant sounds like [ㅣ].

T4-1226.ex: 소방관들의 희생정신은 정말 존경스러운 것 같아요.
T4-1226.x: I think firefighters' spirit of self-sacrifice is truly admirable.

T4-1227.ex: 이 게임은 협동심이 없으면 이길 수 없어요.
T4-1227.x: You can't win this game without team spirit.

T4-1228.ex: 그 모임은 새 회원에게 좀 배타적이에요.
T4-1228.x: That group is a bit closed off to new members.
T4-1228.t: Also a legal term: 배타적 경제 수역 means 'exclusive economic zone.'

T4-1229.ex: 그는 늘 남을 먼저 생각하는 이타적인 사람이에요.
T4-1229.x: He's an altruistic person who always thinks of others first.
T4-1229.e: Literally 'benefiting others'; the opposite, 이기적, is 'benefiting oneself.'

T4-1230.x: It's hard to work with self-centered people.

T4-1231.x: Grandpa is so stubborn that he won't go to the hospital.
T4-1231.t: In everyday speech, 고집이 세다 is the most common way to say 'stubborn.'

T4-1232.m: stubborn, inflexible, set in one's ways
T4-1232.ex: 아버지는 완고해서 생각을 잘 안 바꾸세요.
T4-1232.x: My father is set in his ways, so he rarely changes his mind.

T4-1233.ex: 그는 우유부단해서 메뉴 하나도 잘 못 골라요.
T4-1233.x: He's so indecisive he can't even pick one item off a menu.
T4-1233.e: Literally 'soft and gentle, unable to cut' — too soft to make a decision.
T4-1233.t: Nothing to do with 우유 'milk' — it's a four-character idiom.

T4-1234.x: He doesn't talk much, but he's a very warm person.

T4-1235.ex: 제 친구는 수다스러워서 같이 있으면 재미있어요.
T4-1235.x: My friend is chatty, so it's fun to be with her.
T4-1235.t: 수다를 떨다 means to chat or gossip; it's usually friendly, not negative.

T4-1236.x: He's been talking a lot less lately.
T4-1236.e: Native 말 'words' plus 수 'number' — literally 'word count.'
T4-1236.t: Pronounced [말쑤]; usually in 말수가 적다 (quiet) or 말수가 많다 (talkative).

T4-1237.forms: 입이 무거워요 · 입이 무거웠어요 · 입이 무거운 사람 (ㅂ irregular)
T4-1237.m: to be tight-lipped, to be able to keep a secret
T4-1237.ex: 민수는 입이 무거워서 비밀을 말해도 돼요.
T4-1237.x: Minsu can keep a secret, so it's okay to tell him.
T4-1237.e: Literally 'one's mouth is heavy' — hard to open.

T4-1238.forms: 입이 가벼워요 · 입이 가벼웠어요 · 입이 가벼운 사람 (ㅂ irregular)
T4-1238.m: to be a blabbermouth, to be unable to keep a secret
T4-1238.x: That person can't keep a secret, so be careful.
T4-1238.e: Literally 'one's mouth is light' — it opens too easily.

T4-1239.forms: 눈이 높아요 · 눈이 높았어요 · 눈이 높은 사람
T4-1239.m: to have high standards, to be picky
T4-1239.ex: 언니는 눈이 높아서 아직 남자 친구가 없어요.
T4-1239.x: My older sister has high standards, so she still doesn't have a boyfriend.

T4-1240.forms: 발이 넓어요 · 발이 넓었어요 · 발이 넓은 사람
T4-1240.m: to know a lot of people, to be well-connected
T4-1240.ex: 우리 아빠는 발이 넓어서 아는 사람이 많아요.
T4-1240.x: My dad is well-connected, so he knows a lot of people.
T4-1240.e: Literally 'one's feet are wide' — feet that reach many places.

T4-1241.forms: 손이 커요 · 손이 컸어요 · 손이 큰 사람 (ㅡ drops)
T4-1241.m: to be generous (esp. with food or spending), to do things on a big scale
T4-1241.ex: 할머니는 손이 커서 음식을 항상 많이 만드세요.
T4-1241.x: Grandma is generous, so she always makes lots of food.
T4-1241.t: Not about actual hand size; often said of someone who cooks huge portions.

T4-1242.forms: 귀가 얇아요 · 귀가 얇았어요 · 귀가 얇은 사람
T4-1242.m: to be gullible, to be easily swayed
T4-1242.ex: 저는 귀가 얇아서 광고를 보면 바로 사요.
T4-1242.x: I'm easily swayed, so I buy things as soon as I see an ad.
T4-1242.e: Literally 'one's ears are thin' — everything gets through.

T4-1243.forms: 속이 좁아요 · 속이 좁았어요 · 속이 좁은 사람
T4-1243.m: to be petty, to be narrow-minded
T4-1243.ex: 그런 작은 일로 화내다니 속이 좁네요.
T4-1243.x: Getting angry over such a small thing is petty.
T4-1243.e: Literally 'one's insides are narrow' — little room for others.

T4-1244.ex: 그 사람은 뒤끝이 없어서 금방 화가 풀려요.
T4-1244.x: He doesn't hold grudges, so his anger fades quickly.
T4-1244.e: 뒤 'after' plus 끝 'end' — what's left after something is over.
T4-1244.t: 뒤끝이 있다 means someone holds grudges; 뒤끝이 없다 means they get over things fast.

T4-1245.ex: 가령 내일 비가 오면 소풍은 어떻게 해요?
T4-1245.x: Say it rains tomorrow — what do we do about the picnic?
T4-1245.t: Formal and written; in conversation, 예를 들어 or 만약 is more common.

T4-1246.m: as much as possible, if at all possible
T4-1246.x: Please come to the meeting as early as possible.
T4-1246.e: Literally 'as far as one can reach.'

T4-1247.m: as it is, already (and on top of that)
T4-1247.x: I'm busy as it is, and now my computer's broken too.
T4-1247.e: Probably related to 가득 'full' — already full of trouble.
T4-1247.t: Almost always followed by -(으)ㄴ데/-는데 and then a complaint.

T4-1248.t: Pronounced [각깍]; 각각의 works before nouns, as in 각각의 의견.

T4-1249.forms: 간간이 + verb (비가 간간이 내리다); ≈ 가끔, 때때로
T4-1249.m: now and then, occasionally; here and there
T4-1249.x: Now and then, I can hear birds singing outside the window.
T4-1249.e: Literally 'interval after interval' plus adverb ending -이: things happening with gaps in between.

T4-1250.forms: 간혹 + verb (간혹 있다); written ≈ spoken 가끔
T4-1250.m: occasionally, once in a while, now and then
T4-1250.x: Mistakes like this do happen once in a while.
T4-1250.e: Literally 'in between, perhaps': something that turns up now and then.
T4-1250.t: Common in the pattern 간혹 ~기도 하다, 'sometimes it also happens that ~'.

T4-1251.forms: 감히 + verb (감히 말하다); 감히 어디서! = How dare you!
T4-1251.m: dare to, venture to; how dare
T4-1251.ex: 저는 감히 선생님께 반대 의견을 말할 수 없었어요.
T4-1251.x: I didn't dare to voice a different opinion to my teacher.
T4-1251.e: Sino syllable 'dare, be bold' plus adverb ending -히.
T4-1251.t: 감히 말씀드리면 is a humble way to say 'if I may be so bold'; 감히! alone scolds someone.

T4-1252.forms: 거듭 + verb (거듭 강조하다); 거듭되다 = to be repeated
T4-1252.m: repeatedly, again and again, over and over
T4-1252.x: He apologized over and over for his mistake.
T4-1252.e: Same root as 거듭되다 'to be repeated' and 거듭나다 'to be reborn'.

T4-1253.forms: 거꾸로 + verb (거꾸로 입다/들다); 거꾸로 말하면 = conversely
T4-1253.m: upside down, backwards, inside out; the other way around
T4-1253.ex: 동생이 옷을 거꾸로 입고 학교에 갔어요.
T4-1253.x: My little brother went to school with his clothes on backwards.
T4-1253.e: Related to the verb 거꾸러지다 'to fall headlong'.

T4-1254.m: at the slightest provocation, at every turn, too readily
T4-1254.x: My older brother gets angry at the drop of a hat.
T4-1254.e: Built from the old verb 걸핏하다 plus -면 'if': 'whenever the slightest thing happens'.
T4-1254.t: Pronounced [걸피타면]; used with annoying habits, much like the casual synonym 툭하면.
rel: at the drop of a hat

T4-1255.forms: 고작 + small amount (고작 천 원); 고작이다 = that's all
T4-1255.m: only, merely, at most, a mere
T4-1255.ex: 하루 종일 일하고 고작 만 원을 받았어요.
T4-1255.x: I worked all day and got a mere 10,000 won.
T4-1255.t: Carries disappointment: the amount is smaller than it should be.

T4-1256.m: right after, immediately following, shortly after
T4-1256.ex: 개회식이 끝나고 곧이어 첫 경기가 시작되었습니다.
T4-1256.x: The opening ceremony ended, and the first game started right after.
T4-1256.t: Pronounced [고디어]: no palatalization here, because 이어 is a full word, not a suffix.

T4-1257.x: Come straight home when class is over.

T4-1258.forms: 골똘히 생각하다 (almost always with thinking verbs)
T4-1258.ex: 그는 창밖을 보며 골똘히 생각에 잠겼어요.
T4-1258.x: He looked out the window, lost deep in thought.
T4-1258.e: From 골똘하다 'to be absorbed in one thing'.

T4-1259.forms: 공연히 + verb (공연히 걱정하다); spoken form 괜히
T4-1259.m: for no reason, needlessly, in vain
T4-1259.ex: 공연히 걱정만 하지 말고 직접 물어보세요.
T4-1259.x: Don't just worry for nothing; ask directly.
T4-1259.e: Literally 'emptily so': doing something with no real purpose.

T4-1260.forms: 괜히 + verb (괜히 왔다); 괜히 ~았/었어요 = I shouldn't have
T4-1260.m: for no reason, needlessly; (I) shouldn't have
T4-1260.x: I washed my car for nothing, and now it's raining.
T4-1260.t: 괜히 + past tense expresses regret: 괜히 말했어요 = 'I shouldn't have said it.'

T4-1261.forms: 구태여 + question or negative (구태여 ~할 필요 없다)
T4-1261.m: deliberately, go out of one's way to, bother to
T4-1261.x: There's no need to bother going all the way there.
T4-1261.e: A more formal, written cousin of 굳이.

T4-1262.forms: 굳이 + question or negative (굳이 그럴 필요 없어요)
T4-1262.m: insist on, bother to, go out of one's way to
T4-1262.ex: 굳이 비싼 걸 살 필요는 없어요.
T4-1262.x: There's no need to insist on buying the expensive one.
T4-1262.e: From 굳다 'to harden': stubbornly sticking to something.
T4-1262.t: Pronounced [구지] — palatalization; a top spelling mistake is writing 구지.

T4-1263.m: even so, at least, fortunately; even that little
T4-1263.ex: 다쳤지만 그나마 크게 다치지 않아서 다행이에요.
T4-1263.x: I got hurt, but at least it wasn't serious.
T4-1263.e: 그 'that' + -나마 'even if only': taking comfort in the little there is.

T4-1264.x: It's not all that cold today.
T4-1264.t: Used only with negatives, like 별로 but a bit more written in tone.

T4-1265.m: that much, to that extent, as much
T4-1265.x: The more you exercise, the healthier you get.
T4-1265.e: 그 'that' + 만큼 'as much as': literally 'as much as that'.

T4-1266.e: 그 'that' + -야 emphasis + 말로 'in words': 'that, in the truest words'.
T4-1266.t: Adds strong emphasis, like 'nothing short of': 그야말로 최고예요 'It's truly the best.'

T4-1267.x: Cases like this are extremely rare.
T4-1267.e: Sino syllable 'extreme, pole' plus adverb ending -히.
T4-1267.t: Pronounced [그키] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-1268.forms: 기껏 + verb (기껏 만들었는데...); 기껏해야 = at most
T4-1268.m: with great effort (only to be wasted); at most, merely
T4-1268.x: I went to all the trouble of cooking, and nobody ate.
T4-1268.t: 기껏 ~았/었는데 means effort went to waste: 'I bothered to ~, but...'.

T4-1269.m: at most, at best, no more than
T4-1269.ex: 이 일은 기껏해야 한 시간이면 끝나요.
T4-1269.x: This job will take an hour at most.
T4-1269.e: 기껏 'at most' + 해야 'even if one does': even at the very limit.

T4-1270.m: at all costs, determinedly; in the end, finally
T4-1270.ex: 그는 반대를 무릅쓰고 기어이 유학을 떠났어요.
T4-1270.x: Despite the opposition, he insisted on going to study abroad.
T4-1270.e: Literally 'aiming at (the goal)' plus -이: refusing to stop until it's done.

T4-1271.forms: 기왕 ~(으)ㄴ/는 김에; 기왕이면 = if you're going to anyway
T4-1271.m: since (it's already so), as long as; already
T4-1271.x: Since we've come all this way, let's see the museum too.
T4-1271.e: Literally 'already gone by': accepting what's done and making the best of it.

T4-1272.forms: 꼼짝 못 하다 / 꼼짝 않다 / 꼼짝 마! (Freeze!)
T4-1272.m: (not) budge an inch, (not) move at all
T4-1272.ex: 너무 아파서 하루 종일 꼼짝도 못 했어요.
T4-1272.x: I was so sick I couldn't move all day.
T4-1272.e: A mimetic word for a tiny movement; related to 꼼지락거리다 'to wriggle'.
T4-1272.t: Almost always negative: 꼼짝 못 하다, 꼼짝도 안 하다, or the command 꼼짝 마!

T4-1273.x: To succeed, you have to keep working hard without stopping.
T4-1273.e: 끊임 'a break' (from 끊다 'to cut') + 없이 'without': 'without a break'.
T4-1273.t: Pronounced [끄니멉씨]; ㄶ drops its ㅎ before a vowel.

T4-1274.m: day by day, every day, daily
T4-1274.x: Your Korean is improving day by day.

T4-1275.forms: 날로 + change verb (날로 심해지다); 날로 먹다 = eat raw / get for free
T4-1275.ex: 도시의 교통 문제가 날로 심각해지고 있습니다.
T4-1275.x: The city's traffic problems are growing more serious by the day.
T4-1275.e: 날 'day' + -로. Homonym warning: 날 also means 'raw', so 날로 먹다 = eat raw.
T4-1275.t: Slang 날로 먹다 means 'to get something without any effort'.

T4-1276.m: one by one, in every detail, thoroughly
T4-1276.x: The police revealed every detail of the truth behind the case.
T4-1276.e: 낱 'a single piece' doubled + -이: 'piece by piece'.

T4-1277.forms: time + 내내 (여름 내내, 일 년 내내); 내내 + verb
T4-1277.m: all along, throughout, the whole time
T4-1277.x: I did nothing but play games at home the whole vacation.

T4-1278.forms: 내심 + feeling verb (내심 기대하다); noun: 내심을 드러내다
T4-1278.m: inwardly, secretly (at heart); one's true feelings
T4-1278.x: I acted like it was nothing, but inwardly I was happy.

T4-1279.x: There will be many guests, so prepare plenty of food.
T4-1279.t: Pronounced [넝너키] — nasalization, then ㄱ+ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

T4-1280.ex: 이 식당의 인기 메뉴는 단연 불고기예요.
T4-1280.x: The most popular dish at this restaurant is by far the bulgogi.
T4-1280.e: Literally 'cut-off so': decisive, with no room for doubt.
T4-1280.t: Pronounced [다년]; pairs with 최고, 으뜸, or 1위 to mean 'the clear winner'.

T4-1281.x: I only wanted to help, that's all.
T4-1281.e: Both syllables mean 'only', doubled for emphasis.
T4-1281.t: Usually ends with 뿐이다; homonym 단지 also means 'housing complex' (아파트 단지).

T4-1282.m: for the time being, for a while
T4-1282.ex: 공사 때문에 당분간 이 길을 이용할 수 없습니다.
T4-1282.x: This road will be closed for the time being due to construction.

T4-1283.forms: 대개 + verb (대개 ~는 편이다); noun: 대개의 경우
T4-1283.x: I usually rest at home on weekends.
T4-1283.e: Literally 'the big outline': speaking in general terms.

T4-1284.x: Thank you very much for your help.
T4-1284.t: 대단히 감사합니다 and 대단히 죄송합니다 are standard formal phrases.

T4-1285.forms: 대략 + number (대략 백 명); noun: 대략적인 내용
T4-1285.ex: 서울에서 부산까지 기차로 대략 세 시간 걸려요.
T4-1285.x: It takes roughly three hours from Seoul to Busan by train.
T4-1285.e: Literally 'the big outline': the rough picture without details.

T4-1286.forms: 대폭 + change verb (대폭 늘리다/줄이다); noun: 대폭 할인
T4-1286.m: drastically, sharply, by a large margin
T4-1286.ex: 정부는 내년 예산을 대폭 늘리기로 했습니다.
T4-1286.x: The government decided to sharply increase next year's budget.
T4-1286.e: Literally 'big width': a change of large scale.
T4-1286.t: A news favorite with 인상, 인하, 증가, 감소; the opposite is 소폭 'slightly'.

T4-1287.forms: A. 더구나 B (= what's more); ≈ 게다가
T4-1287.m: moreover, besides, what's more, on top of that
T4-1287.x: The weather was cold, and on top of that it even rained.

T4-1288.ex: 그 말을 들으니까 더더욱 가고 싶어졌어요.
T4-1288.x: Hearing that made me want to go all the more.
T4-1288.e: 더 'more' stacked on 더욱 'more': an extra-strong 'even more'.

T4-1289.forms: 도리어 + opposite result; spoken ≈ 오히려, 되레
T4-1289.x: I tried to help but ended up ruining things instead.

T4-1290.ex: 이 문제는 도무지 이해할 수가 없어요.
T4-1290.x: I can't understand this problem at all.
T4-1290.t: Used with negatives and frustration: 도무지 모르겠어요 'I have no idea at all.'

T4-1291.forms: 되도록 + verb (되도록 빨리); 되도록이면 = if possible
T4-1291.x: Please contact me as soon as possible.
T4-1291.e: From 되다 'to become, be possible' + -도록 'so that'.

T4-1292.x: The person who was in the wrong was the one shouting instead.

T4-1293.m: widely, all around, extensively, to everyone
T4-1293.ex: 그는 여러 분야의 지식을 두루 갖추고 있어요.
T4-1293.x: He has broad knowledge across many fields.

T4-1294.x: I don't have anything in particular to do this weekend.
T4-1294.t: Pronounced [따키]; mostly with negatives, e.g. 딱히 없어요 'nothing in particular'.

T4-1295.m: just in time, right then, opportunely
T4-1295.ex: 비가 오기 시작했는데 때마침 버스가 왔어요.
T4-1295.x: It started raining, and just then the bus came.
T4-1295.e: 때 'time' + 마침 'just then': 'right at the right time'.

T4-1296.forms: 때로(는) + verb; 때로는 A, 때로는 B
T4-1296.x: Sometimes you need time alone, too.

T4-1297.forms: 마냥 + verb (마냥 기다리다); 마냥 좋다 = just happy
T4-1297.ex: 그 사람을 마냥 기다릴 수는 없어요.
T4-1297.x: I can't just wait for him forever.
T4-1297.t: With feelings it means 'just, purely': 아이처럼 마냥 신났어요 'excited like a kid'.

T4-1298.m: naturally, rightly, as one should, deservedly

T4-1299.forms: 마저 + verb (마저 먹다/하다) = finish the rest
T4-1299.m: (finishing) the rest, completely, all the way
T4-1299.x: I'll finish the rest of my rice and then go out.
T4-1299.t: As an adverb it means 'finish off the rest'; as a particle (너마저) it means 'even you'.

T4-1300.m: when it actually comes to it, actually (in reality)
T4-1300.ex: 막상 시험을 보려고 하니 너무 떨렸어요.
T4-1300.x: When it actually came time to take the test, I was so nervous.
T4-1300.t: Contrasts expectation with reality: 막상 해 보니 쉬웠어요 'once I actually tried, it was easy'.
rel: when it comes down to it

T4-1301.ex: 어릴 때는 막연히 의사가 되고 싶었어요.
T4-1301.x: When I was young, I vaguely wanted to become a doctor.
T4-1301.e: Literally 'desert-like': vast and hazy, with no clear outline.

T4-1302.x: He's late for our appointments every time.

T4-1303.m: soon, before long, in the near future
T4-1303.x: There will be good news before long.
T4-1303.e: 멀지 않아 'not being far' with ㄹ dropped: 'not far off'.
T4-1303.t: Written as one word for time ('soon'); 멀지 않아 is used for physical distance.

T4-1304.forms: 멋대로 + verb (멋대로 하다); 제멋대로 = as one pleases
T4-1304.m: as one pleases, at will, selfishly
T4-1304.ex: 남의 물건을 멋대로 쓰면 안 돼요.
T4-1304.x: You shouldn't use other people's things as you please.
T4-1304.e: 멋 'one's own taste' + 대로 'as, according to'.
T4-1304.t: Negative tone; 마음대로 is the neutral 'freely, as you like'.

T4-1305.x: My little sister ate snacks without Mom knowing.
T4-1305.e: Related to 모르다 'not to know': done so others won't know.
T4-1305.t: Put a person before it to mean 'behind their back': 선생님 몰래.

T4-1306.m: as many as, no less than, a whopping
T4-1306.ex: 이 영화는 무려 천만 명이 봤어요.
T4-1306.x: A whopping ten million people saw this movie.
T4-1306.t: Emphasizes a surprisingly large number; the opposite feeling is 고작 or 불과.

T4-1307.ex: 무심코 한 말이 친구에게 상처를 줬어요.
T4-1307.x: Something I said without thinking hurt my friend.

T4-1308.x: I came up to Seoul blindly, without any plan.

T4-1309.x: I was busy and didn't get a chance to contact you.
T4-1309.e: Related to 미치다 'to reach': not reaching that point in time.
T4-1309.t: 미처 몰랐어요 'I didn't realize' is a very common polite apology phrase.

T4-1310.m: every time, each and every time, invariably
T4-1310.x: He failed the exam every single time.
T4-1310.t: Usually for repeated bad outcomes, unlike neutral 매번.

T4-1311.forms: 별안간 + event (별안간 비가 쏟아지다); noun: 별안간에
T4-1311.x: All of a sudden the sky darkened, and rain poured down.
T4-1311.e: Literally 'in the space of a glance'.

T4-1312.forms: 보다 + adjective/adverb (보다 나은, 보다 많이); spoken ≈ 더
T4-1312.ex: 우리는 보다 나은 미래를 위해 노력합니다.
T4-1312.x: We work hard for a better future.
T4-1312.e: Same form as the particle -보다 'than'; here it stands alone before the word.
T4-1312.t: Formal, written style; in speech say 더: 더 나은 미래.

T4-1313.m: please, I sincerely hope, by all means
T4-1313.x: Please take good care of yourself and stay well.
T4-1313.t: Heartfelt and formal, used in wishes and farewells; 제발 sounds more pleading.

T4-1314.ex: 그 사람은 분명 내일 올 거예요.

T4-1315.forms: 불과 + number (불과 3일 만에); cf. N에 불과하다 'to be nothing more than N'
T4-1315.ex: 그는 불과 일 년 만에 한국어를 잘하게 되었어요.
T4-1315.x: He got good at Korean in just one year.

T4-1316.e: -적 = '-ic/-al', turning nouns into descriptors: 비교적, 경제적, 문화적.

T4-1317.m: without exception, without missing anything, all
T4-1317.x: Every employee attended the meeting without exception.
T4-1317.e: 빠짐 'omission' (from 빠지다 'to be left out') + 없이 'without'.

T4-1318.x: I unexpectedly ran into an old friend on the street.
T4-1318.e: 뜻 'intention, expectation' + 밖에 'outside': outside of what you expected.
T4-1318.t: Pronounced [뜯빠께]; 뜻밖의 + noun is common: 뜻밖의 소식 'unexpected news'.

T4-1319.ex: 아기가 깰까 봐 문을 살며시 닫았어요.
T4-1319.x: I closed the door gently so the baby wouldn't wake up.

T4-1320.m: anew, afresh; all over again, now (as if new)
T4-1320.ex: 외국에 살아 보니 가족의 소중함을 새삼 느꼈어요.
T4-1320.x: Living abroad, I felt anew how precious my family is.
T4-1320.e: Base of 새삼스럽다; related to 새 'new'.

T4-1321.m: to feel new again, to seem fresh; to be uncalled-for (bringing up old things)
T4-1321.ex: 오랜만에 고향에 오니 모든 것이 새삼스러워요.
T4-1321.x: Coming home after so long, everything feels new again.
T4-1321.t: 새삼스럽게 왜 그래요? means 'Why bring that up now, out of nowhere?'

T4-1322.x: He answered the question without hesitation.

T4-1323.x: My friend readily lent me money.
T4-1323.t: Also common negated: 선뜻 대답하지 못했어요 'I couldn't answer right away.'

T4-1324.x: Even if I fail, I won't give up.

T4-1325.m: surely not, no way, it can't be
T4-1325.x: Surely he didn't lie, did he?
T4-1325.t: Proverb 설마가 사람 잡는다: 'Saying "no way" gets people killed' — don't be careless.

T4-1326.ex: 설사 그 말이 사실이라고 해도 저는 믿지 않을 거예요.
T4-1326.x: Even if that's true, I won't believe it.
T4-1326.e: Literally 'suppose it were made so'. Homonym: 설사 also means 'diarrhea'.

T4-1327.forms: 섣불리 + verb (often with negative/caution): 섣불리 판단하지 마세요
T4-1327.ex: 상황을 잘 모르면 섣불리 판단하지 않는 게 좋아요.
T4-1327.x: If you don't know the situation well, it's better not to judge rashly.
T4-1327.t: Pronounced [섣뿔리]; usually appears in warnings like 섣불리 ~지 마세요 'don't rush to ~'.

T4-1328.forms: 수시로 + verb: 수시로 확인하다, 수시로 연락하다
T4-1328.m: frequently, at any time, whenever needed
T4-1328.x: It's safer to change your password frequently.
T4-1328.e: Literally 'following the time' — whenever the moment calls for it.
T4-1328.t: Also used in college admissions: 수시 (rolling/early admission) vs. 정시 (regular admission).

T4-1329.m: in an instant, in the blink of an eye
T4-1329.x: The cake was all gone in the blink of an eye.
T4-1329.e: Literally 'in the space of a blink and a breath'.
T4-1329.t: Pronounced [순식까네] — the ㄱ after ㄱ becomes tense.
rel: in the blink of an eye

T4-1330.forms: 스스럼없이 + verb: 스스럼없이 지내다, 스스럼없이 말하다
T4-1330.m: freely, without reserve, casually (as with close friends)
T4-1330.ex: 그 선배와는 스스럼없이 이야기할 수 있어요.
T4-1330.x: I can talk freely with that senior.
T4-1330.t: Pronounced [스스러멉씨]; 스스럼없이 지내다 means 'to be on easy, close terms'.

T4-1331.forms: 슬그머니 + movement verb: 슬그머니 나가다, 슬그머니 일어나다
T4-1331.ex: 회의 중에 그는 슬그머니 방을 나갔어요.
T4-1331.x: During the meeting, he quietly slipped out of the room.
T4-1331.e: A softer, more stealthy cousin of 슬며시.

T4-1332.forms: 슬며시 + verb: 슬며시 웃다, 슬며시 손을 잡다
T4-1332.x: The child quietly took her mom's hand.
T4-1332.t: Often softer than 몰래: it describes gentle, unnoticed action, not necessarily sneaky or wrong.

T4-1333.forms: 실컷 + verb: 실컷 먹다, 실컷 자다, 실컷 울다
T4-1333.m: to one's heart's content, as much as one wants
T4-1333.x: On the weekend I want to sleep at home as much as I like.
T4-1333.t: Can be ironic: 실컷 공부했는데 시험이 취소됐어요 'I studied so hard and then the exam was canceled.'

T4-1334.forms: 심지어 + clause: A도 하고, 심지어 B까지 해요
T4-1334.m: even, what's more, to make matters worse
T4-1334.ex: 그는 바빠서 심지어 밥 먹을 시간도 없어요.
T4-1334.x: He's so busy he doesn't even have time to eat.
T4-1334.e: Literally 'going as far as the extreme'.
T4-1334.t: Often paired with the particles 까지 or 조차/도 on the extreme item.

T4-1335.forms: 아예 + negative/verb: 아예 안 해요, 아예 그만두다
T4-1335.m: from the start, altogether, (not) at all
T4-1335.ex: 늦을 것 같으면 아예 오지 마세요.
T4-1335.x: If you're going to be late, just don't come at all.
T4-1335.t: Often signals giving up a half-measure: 아예 새로 사요 'I'll just buy a new one altogether.'

T4-1336.m: it seems like, I guess, after all; no matter how you look at it
T4-1336.ex: 아무래도 오늘은 비가 올 것 같아요.
T4-1336.x: It looks like it's going to rain today after all.
T4-1336.e: Contracted from 아무러하여도 'however it may be'.
T4-1336.t: Very common with ~것 같다 to soften a conclusion you've reluctantly reached.

T4-1337.m: in addition, at the same time, together with
T4-1337.ex: 참석해 주셔서 감사드리며, 아울러 건강을 기원합니다.
T4-1337.x: Thank you for attending, and I also wish you good health.
T4-1337.e: From the verb 아우르다 'to bring together'.

T4-1338.m: in the first place, from the very beginning
T4-1338.ex: 애초에 그 일을 맡지 말았어야 했어요.
T4-1338.x: I shouldn't have taken on that job in the first place.
T4-1338.e: 애초 'the very start' + -에; 초 means 'beginning', as in 초기 'early stage'.

T4-1339.m: before one knows it, already (time has passed)
T4-1339.x: Before I knew it, three years had passed since I came to Korea.

T4-1340.m: before one knows it, without noticing, already
T4-1340.x: While watching the movie, I fell asleep without realizing it.

T4-1341.forms: 어렴풋이 + perception verb: 어렴풋이 기억나다, 어렴풋이 보이다
T4-1341.ex: 어릴 때 살던 집이 어렴풋이 기억나요.
T4-1341.x: I vaguely remember the house I lived in as a child.
T4-1341.t: Pronounced [어렴푸시]; very often goes with 기억나다 or 보이다.

T4-1342.forms: 어쩌다(가) + verb: 어쩌다 만나다; 어쩌다 이렇게 됐어요?
T4-1342.m: by chance, accidentally; occasionally; how on earth
T4-1342.x: I ran into an old friend on the street by chance.

T4-1344.forms: 어찌 + question/exclamation: 어찌 된 일이에요? 어찌 알겠어요?
T4-1344.m: how, in what way; how could (rhetorical)
T4-1344.ex: 이게 어찌 된 일인지 설명해 주세요.
T4-1344.e: The root of 어찌하다 'to do how', which contracts to 어쩌다 and 어쩌면.
T4-1344.t: More formal or literary than 어떻게; 어찌 된 일이에요? means 'What happened here?'

T4-1345.forms: 어차피 + clause: 어차피 늦었으니까 천천히 가요
T4-1345.m: anyway, in any case, either way
T4-1345.x: We're late anyway, so let's take our time.
T4-1345.e: Literally 'whether this or that' — the outcome is the same.

T4-1346.forms: 억지로 + verb: 억지로 먹다, 억지로 웃다, 억지로 시키다
T4-1346.m: by force, against one's will, reluctantly
T4-1346.x: I was full, but I forced myself to eat it all.
T4-1346.t: Pronounced [억찌로]; 억지 부리다 means 'to be unreasonable, insist stubbornly'.

T4-1347.forms: 얼핏 + perception verb: 얼핏 보다, 얼핏 듣다, 얼핏 보기에
T4-1347.m: at a glance, briefly, in passing
T4-1347.ex: 얼핏 보면 두 사람이 쌍둥이 같아요.
T4-1347.x: At a glance, the two of them look like twins.

T4-1348.forms: 여태 + negative/past: 여태 안 왔어요? 여태 뭐 했어요?
T4-1348.x: You still haven't done your homework?
T4-1348.e: Means the same as 이제까지 'up to now'.
T4-1348.t: Often carries mild surprise or blame: 여태 자고 있었어요? 'You were sleeping until now?'

T4-1349.forms: 여태껏 + experience/negative: 여태껏 본 적이 없어요
T4-1349.ex: 이렇게 맛있는 음식은 여태껏 먹어 본 적이 없어요.
T4-1349.x: I've never eaten food this delicious until now.
T4-1349.e: 여태 'until now' + 껏 'all the way to', as in 힘껏.

T4-1350.forms: 연달아 + verb/count: 연달아 세 번 이기다
T4-1350.m: in a row, consecutively, one after another
T4-1350.ex: 우리 팀이 연달아 세 경기를 이겼어요.
T4-1350.x: Our team won three games in a row.
T4-1350.e: From 연달다 'to follow in succession'; 연 means connect.

T4-1351.forms: 연이어 + verb: 연이어 발생하다, 연이어 출시되다
T4-1351.x: New products are being released one after another.
T4-1351.e: From 연잇다 'to link in a chain' (연 'connect' + 잇다 'to join').
T4-1351.t: Frequent in news reports about incidents or releases: 사고가 연이어 발생했습니다.

T4-1352.ex: 그는 오로지 가족을 위해 열심히 일했어요.
T4-1352.x: He worked hard solely for his family.

T4-1353.x: You're the only person I can trust.

T4-1354.forms: 온통 + noun/state: 온통 하얗다, 머릿속이 온통 ~ 생각
T4-1354.x: When I woke up in the morning, the whole world was white.
T4-1354.e: Probably related to 온 'whole, entire', as in 온 세상.
T4-1354.t: 머릿속이 온통 ~ 생각뿐이에요 means 'I can think of nothing but ~'.

T4-1355.forms: 왠지 + feeling: 왠지 기분이 좋아요, 왠지 불안해요
T4-1355.ex: 오늘은 왠지 좋은 일이 생길 것 같아요.
T4-1355.x: Somehow I feel like something good will happen today.
T4-1355.e: Contraction of 왜인지 'why it is (I don't know)'.
T4-1355.t: Classic spelling trap: 왠지 (from 왜) vs. 웬 'what kind of', as in 웬일이에요?

T4-1356.m: in short, in a word, to sum up
T4-1356.x: In short, the problem is that there isn't enough time.
T4-1356.e: Contracted from 요하건대 'to state the essentials'.
T4-1356.t: Formal written style; in conversation people say 한마디로 or 결국.

T4-1357.forms: 웬만큼 + verb/adjective: 웬만큼 하다, 웬만큼 잘하다
T4-1357.m: to a fair degree, reasonably, moderately; enough
T4-1357.x: I speak Korean reasonably well, so traveling is no problem.

T4-1358.m: if possible, if it's not too much trouble, unless there's a good reason
T4-1358.x: If possible, please send it by tomorrow.

T4-1359.forms: 유난히 + adjective: 유난히 춥다, 유난히 조용하다
T4-1359.e: From 유난하다 'unusual'; 유난 떨다 means 'to make a fuss'.

T4-1360.forms: 으레 + habitual verb: 으레 ~곤 하다, 으레 ~는 법이다
T4-1360.m: as a matter of course, habitually, naturally
T4-1360.x: On weekends, my father would always go to the mountains.

T4-1361.forms: 의외로 + adjective/verb: 의외로 쉽다, 의외로 잘하다

T4-1362.forms: 이따금 + verb: 이따금 연락하다, 이따금 생각나다
T4-1362.x: I think of my hometown friends once in a while.
T4-1362.t: Don't confuse with 이따가 'a little later'; 이따금 means 'every now and then'.

T4-1363.x: These days many people do so-called 'honbap' (eating alone).
T4-1363.e: 이르다 'to call, say' + 바 'that which' — literally 'what is said'.

T4-1364.forms: 이리저리 + movement verb: 이리저리 다니다, 이리저리 찾다
T4-1364.m: here and there, this way and that
T4-1364.x: I ran here and there trying to find my lost key.

T4-1365.forms: 일일이 + verb: 일일이 확인하다, 일일이 설명하다
T4-1365.m: one by one, each and every, in detail
T4-1365.x: The teacher checked each student's homework one by one.
T4-1365.e: Literally 'one-one' — going through things one at a time.
T4-1365.t: Pronounced [이리리] — each ㄹ simply links to the next vowel (no ㄴ insertion).

T4-1366.x: He showed a talent for music early on.
T4-1366.e: From 일찍 'early'; the -이 form sounds more formal or literary.

T4-1367.forms: 잇따라 + verb: 잇따라 발생하다, 잇따라 터지다
T4-1367.x: This summer, typhoons came one after another.
T4-1367.e: From 잇따르다 'to follow in a row' (잇다 'to join' + 따르다 'to follow').
T4-1367.t: Pronounced [읻따라]; very common in news about accidents, complaints, or events.

T4-1368.forms: 자칫(하면/잘못하면) + bad result: 자칫하면 다칠 수 있어요
T4-1368.m: nearly, almost (something bad); if one isn't careful
T4-1368.x: The road was slippery, so I almost fell.

T4-1369.forms: 잠자코 + verb: 잠자코 듣다, 잠자코 있다
T4-1369.ex: 그는 아무 말 없이 잠자코 듣기만 했어요.
T4-1369.x: He just listened silently without saying a word.

T4-1370.forms: 저마다 + verb/noun: 저마다 다르다, 저마다의 이유
T4-1370.m: each, every one (in their own way)
T4-1370.ex: 사람들은 저마다 다른 꿈을 가지고 있어요.
T4-1370.x: Each person has a different dream.

T4-1371.forms: 제각기 + verb: 제각기 다르다, 제각기 흩어지다
T4-1371.m: each separately, individually, each in their own way
T4-1371.ex: 수업이 끝나자 학생들은 제각기 집으로 돌아갔어요.
T4-1371.x: When class ended, the students each went home separately.

T4-1372.forms: 제때(에) + verb: 제때 먹다, 제때 내다
T4-1372.m: on time, at the right time
T4-1372.ex: 건강을 위해 밥을 제때 먹어야 해요.
T4-1372.x: For your health, you should eat meals at the proper times.

T4-1373.t: Stronger and more emotional than a polite request; use 부디 for formal well-wishing.

T4-1374.forms: 조만간 + future: 조만간 만나요, 조만간 ~ㄹ 거예요
T4-1374.m: soon, before long, sooner or later
T4-1374.x: Let's grab a meal together sometime soon.
T4-1374.e: Literally 'between early and late' — sooner or later.

T4-1375.forms: 좀처럼 + negative: 좀처럼 ~지 않다, 좀처럼 ~ㄹ 수 없다
T4-1375.x: My cold just won't go away.

T4-1376.forms: 즉각 + action verb: 즉각 대응하다; noun use: 즉각적인
T4-1376.x: The government responded to the accident immediately.
T4-1376.t: Pronounced [즉깍]; formal and common in news, while everyday speech prefers 바로 or 당장.

T4-1377.forms: 지극히 + adjective: 지극히 정상적이다, 지극히 개인적인
T4-1377.x: That's just my very personal opinion.
T4-1377.t: Pronounced [지그키] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-1378.ex: 이럴 줄 알았으면 진작 말할걸 그랬어요.
T4-1378.x: If I'd known this would happen, I should have said something sooner.
T4-1378.t: Typically expresses regret: 진작 ~ㄹ걸 'I should have ~ sooner'.

T4-1379.forms: 차마 + negative: 차마 ~지 못하다, 차마 ~ㄹ 수 없다
T4-1379.m: (cannot) bear to, (not) have the heart to
T4-1379.ex: 친구의 슬픈 얼굴을 보니 차마 사실을 말할 수 없었어요.
T4-1379.x: Seeing my friend's sad face, I couldn't bring myself to tell the truth.
T4-1379.t: Only used with 못/없다 negatives and conveys emotional reluctance, not inability.

T4-1380.forms: 차츰 + change verb: 차츰 나아지다, 차츰 익숙해지다
T4-1380.ex: 새 회사 생활에 차츰 익숙해지고 있어요.
T4-1380.x: I'm gradually getting used to life at my new company.

T4-1381.forms: 철저히 + verb: 철저히 준비하다, 철저히 조사하다
T4-1381.x: I prepared thoroughly for the interview.
T4-1381.t: Pronounced [철쩌히] — tensing after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

T4-1382.forms: 최대한 + verb: 최대한 빨리, 최대한 노력하다; noun: 최대한으로
T4-1382.m: as much as possible, to the maximum
T4-1382.x: I'll get back to you as soon as possible.

T4-1383.forms: 충실히 + verb: 충실히 하다, 맡은 일을 충실히 하다
T4-1383.ex: 그는 맡은 일을 늘 충실히 해요.
T4-1383.x: He always does his assigned work faithfully.
T4-1383.t: A homophone 충실하다 (充實) means 'rich in content', as in 내용이 충실하다.

T4-1384.forms: 턱없이 + adjective: 턱없이 부족하다, 턱없이 비싸다
T4-1384.ex: 이 돈으로는 여행 경비가 턱없이 부족해요.
T4-1384.x: This money falls far short of what the trip costs.
T4-1384.e: 턱 here means 'grounds, reason' (not the chin): 'without reason'.
T4-1384.t: Pronounced [터겁씨]; 턱없이 부족하다 'woefully insufficient' is the top collocation.

T4-1385.forms: 통째로 + verb: 통째로 먹다, 통째로 외우다
T4-1385.ex: 그는 책 한 권을 통째로 외웠어요.
T4-1385.e: 통 'whole lump' + -째 'as it is', as in 껍질째 'peel and all'.

T4-1386.forms: 틈틈이 + verb: 틈틈이 공부하다, 틈틈이 운동하다
T4-1386.m: in one's spare moments, whenever one has time
T4-1386.x: I memorize English words in spare moments on my commute.
T4-1386.e: 틈 'gap, spare time' doubled + -이 — 'in every gap'.

T4-1387.t: Almost always paired with ~ㄹ 뻔했다 'nearly did (but didn't)'.

T4-1388.m: let alone, much less, all the more
T4-1388.x: It's hard even for adults, so imagine how it is for a child.
T4-1388.t: Usually ends in a rhetorical question: 하물며 ~는 어떻겠어요?

T4-1389.forms: 한결 + comparative adjective: 한결 낫다, 한결 편하다
T4-1389.x: After taking the medicine, I feel much better.

T4-1390.forms: 한껏 + verb: 한껏 멋을 내다, 한껏 기대하다
T4-1390.m: to the fullest, as much as possible, to one's heart's content
T4-1390.ex: 그녀는 파티에 가려고 한껏 멋을 냈어요.
T4-1390.x: She dressed up to the nines to go to the party.
T4-1390.e: 한 'the limit' + -껏 'to the extent of', as in 힘껏, 마음껏.
T4-1390.t: Pronounced [한껃]; 한껏 멋을 내다 'to dress up to the max' is a common chunk.

T4-1391.m: in full swing, at the peak, in the middle of
T4-1391.ex: 지금 한창 회의 중이니까 나중에 전화해 주세요.
T4-1391.x: We're right in the middle of a meeting, so please call back later.
T4-1391.t: Don't confuse 한창 'at the peak' with 한참 'for a long time'.

T4-1392.m: by any chance, possibly, in case
T4-1392.ex: 행여 늦을까 봐 일찍 집을 나섰어요.
T4-1392.x: I left home early in case I'd be late.
T4-1392.e: Built on 행 'luck, chance': 'if by chance'.
T4-1392.t: Often with ~ㄹ까 봐 'for fear that'; 혹시 is the everyday equivalent.

T4-1393.forms: 현저히 + change verb/adjective: 현저히 줄다, 현저히 낮다
T4-1393.x: The birth rate is decreasing markedly.

T4-1394.forms: 흔히 + verb: 흔히 보다, 흔히 ~라고 하다
T4-1394.x: Beginners commonly make this kind of mistake.

T4-1395.forms: 흔쾌히 + verb: 흔쾌히 승낙하다, 흔쾌히 도와주다
T4-1395.x: My friend gladly helped me move.

T4-1396.m: thus, and so, as a result
T4-1396.ex: 그는 꾸준히 노력했습니다. 그리하여 마침내 꿈을 이루었습니다.
T4-1396.x: He worked steadily. And so, he finally achieved his dream.
T4-1396.e: From 그리하다 'to do so' — 'having done so'.
T4-1396.t: Written or storytelling style; in conversation, use 그래서.

T4-1397.m: if so, in that case, then
T4-1397.x: In that case, let's look for another way.

T4-1398.forms: Sentence. 그럼에도 불구하고 + contrast; shorter: 그럼에도
T4-1398.ex: 비가 많이 왔습니다. 그럼에도 불구하고 많은 사람이 모였습니다.
T4-1398.x: It rained heavily. Nevertheless, many people gathered.
T4-1398.e: 불구하다 literally 'not be held back by'.
T4-1398.t: Formal; the same 불구하고 attaches to nouns too: 비에도 불구하고 'despite the rain'.

T4-1399.forms: A. 그뿐 아니라 B; also: 그뿐만 아니라
T4-1399.ex: 이 식당은 음식이 맛있어요. 그뿐 아니라 가격도 싸요.
T4-1399.x: This restaurant has delicious food. Not only that, it's cheap too.
T4-1399.t: The following clause usually takes 도: 그뿐 아니라 B도 ~.

T4-1400.x: A life lived together with your neighbors is important.
T4-1400.e: From 더불다 'to be together with', now used only in this form.

T4-1401.m: on the contrary, conversely, the other way around
T4-1401.ex: 형은 조용해요. 반대로 동생은 아주 활발해요.
T4-1401.x: The older brother is quiet. Conversely, the younger one is very outgoing.

T4-1402.forms: A. 이에 반해 B (formal); N에 반해
T4-1402.m: in contrast, on the other hand
T4-1402.ex: 도시는 인구가 늘고 있습니다. 이에 반해 농촌은 인구가 줄고 있습니다.
T4-1402.x: Cities are growing in population. In contrast, rural areas are shrinking.
T4-1402.e: Literally 'opposing this' — 이 'this' + 에 반하다 'to run contrary to'.
T4-1402.t: Common in TOPIK writing task 53 for comparing data.

T4-1403.m: like this, in this way, as shown
T4-1403.ex: 이처럼 운동은 건강에 많은 도움이 됩니다.
T4-1403.x: As shown, exercise is very good for your health.

T4-1404.m: like this, as such, in this way
T4-1404.x: In this way, language reflects culture.
T4-1404.e: Short for 이러하듯 'just as it is like this'.
T4-1404.t: Pronounced [이러튿] — ㅎ plus ㄷ becomes ㅌ.

T4-1405.forms: 이를테면 + example: 이를테면 사과나 배 같은 과일
T4-1405.m: for example, for instance, so to speak
T4-1405.ex: 저는 단 음식, 이를테면 케이크나 초콜릿을 좋아해요.
T4-1405.x: I like sweet foods, for example cake or chocolate.
T4-1405.e: Contracted from 이를 터이면 'if I am to say it'; 이르다 means 'to say'.
T4-1405.t: More conversational than 예컨대; in everyday speech 예를 들면 is the most common choice.

T4-1406.ex: 환경 문제, 예컨대 대기 오염은 심각한 사회 문제입니다.
T4-1406.x: Environmental problems, for example air pollution, are serious social issues.
T4-1406.e: Shortened from 예하건대, 'if I give an example'.
T4-1406.t: Pronounced [예컨대]; it sounds bookish, so use it in essays and presentations rather than chat.

T4-1407.forms: 다시 말해 · 다시 말해서 · 다시 말하면
T4-1407.m: in other words, that is to say
T4-1407.ex: 그는 회사를 그만뒀어요. 다시 말해 지금은 백수예요.
T4-1407.x: He quit his job. In other words, he's unemployed now.
T4-1407.e: Literally 'saying it again': 다시 'again' + 말하다 'to say'.

T4-1408.m: so to speak, in a way, as it were
T4-1408.ex: 그 사람은 말하자면 우리 팀의 엄마 같은 존재예요.
T4-1408.x: She's, so to speak, like the mom of our team.
T4-1408.e: From 말하다 'to say' + -자면 'if one is to': 'if I were to put it'.
T4-1408.t: Often softened with 굳이: 굳이 말하자면 'if I had to say'.

T4-1409.forms: 마지막으로 + final point: 마지막으로 한 가지만 말씀드릴게요
T4-1409.m: lastly, finally, for the last time
T4-1409.ex: 마지막으로 질문이 있으면 지금 해 주세요.
T4-1409.x: Lastly, if you have any questions, please ask them now.

T4-1410.ex: 끝으로 오늘 와 주신 모든 분께 감사드립니다.
T4-1410.x: In closing, I thank everyone who came today.
T4-1410.t: Pronounced [끄트로]; typical for closing speeches and formal emails.

T4-1411.m: anyway, in any case, whatever the case
T4-1411.x: Anyway, I'm really glad the exam is over.
T4-1411.e: Contraction of 어찌했거나, 'however it was done'.
T4-1411.t: Pronounced [어짿꺼나]; casual, and 어쨌든 is the everyday equivalent.

T4-1412.x: Anyway, let's talk again tomorrow morning.
T4-1412.e: From 하여 'how' plus -튼 (from 하든 'whether'): 'however it may be'; 여하튼 swaps the first two syllables.

T4-1413.m: anyhow, at any rate, in any case
T4-1413.ex: 여하튼 이번 일은 우리가 책임져야 합니다.
T4-1413.x: At any rate, we have to take responsibility for this matter.
T4-1413.e: Literally 'however it may be'; same meaning as 하여튼 with syllables swapped.

T4-1414.m: in a word, in short, simply put
T4-1414.x: In a word, that movie was the best.

T4-1415.x: With this game, the championship was virtually decided.
T4-1415.e: Literally 'in terms of fact'; -상 = 'in terms of': 역사상, 법률상.
T4-1415.t: Pronounced [사실쌍]; 사실상 means 'virtually', while 사실은 means 'actually, to tell the truth'.

T4-1416.m: actually, in fact, to tell the truth
T4-1416.ex: 실은 어제 너한테 할 말이 있었어.
T4-1416.x: Actually, I had something to tell you yesterday.
T4-1416.e: 실 'truth, reality' + topic particle -은: 'as for the truth'.

T4-1417.forms: 알고 보니 + past fact: 알고 보니 ~였어요
T4-1417.m: as it turned out, it turns out that
T4-1417.ex: 알고 보니 그 사람이 제 친구의 형이었어요.
T4-1417.x: As it turned out, that guy was my friend's older brother.
T4-1417.e: Literally 'having found out and looked': 알다 'to know' + 보다 'to see'.
T4-1417.t: Used for discoveries in the past; 알고 보면 'once you get to know' talks about general truths.

T4-1418.forms: 다름이 아니라 · 다름이 아니고 (casual) · 다른 게 아니라
T4-1418.m: the reason I'm contacting you is…, it's just that…
T4-1418.ex: 다름이 아니라 내일 회의 시간을 확인하고 싶어서 연락드렸어요.
T4-1418.x: The reason I contacted you is that I wanted to check tomorrow's meeting time.
T4-1418.e: Literally 'it is nothing other than': 다르다 'to be different' + 아니다.
T4-1418.t: A polite opener for calls, emails and requests, signaling you're getting to the point.

T4-1419.x: You studied hard, so naturally you'll pass.
T4-1419.e: Literally 'properly so': what ought to be.

T4-1420.forms: A 혹은 B (formal) · A 또는 B · A(이)나 B (casual)
T4-1420.ex: 신청서는 이메일 혹은 우편으로 보내 주세요.
T4-1420.x: Please send the application by email or by mail.
T4-1420.e: 혹 'perhaps, some' + -은; also seen in 혹시 'by any chance'.

T4-1421.forms: Number 내지 number (range) · A 내지 B (or)
T4-1421.ex: 수술 후 회복하는 데 일주일 내지 열흘이 걸립니다.
T4-1421.x: Recovery after surgery takes one week to ten days.
T4-1421.t: Formal; mostly used between two numbers to give a range, like '3 내지 4명'.

T4-1422.ex: 자세한 일정 및 장소는 홈페이지에서 확인하세요.
T4-1422.x: Check the homepage for the detailed schedule and location.
T4-1422.e: Probably from old 및다 'to reach', the root of today's 미치다 'to reach'.
T4-1422.t: Only links nouns in formal writing such as notices and reports; never say it in casual conversation.

T4-1423.forms: Noun 겸 noun · verb-(으)ㄹ 겸 verb-(으)ㄹ 겸
T4-1423.m: and also, cum (combining two roles or purposes)
T4-1423.ex: 운동도 할 겸 바람도 쐴 겸 공원에 갔어요.
T4-1423.x: I went to the park both to exercise and to get some fresh air.
T4-1423.e: Literally 'combining'; 거실 겸 서재 means 'living room cum study'.

T4-1424.forms: Mostly as connectors: N에 반해 · N에 반하여 · N에 반하는 (+noun)
T4-1424.m: to be contrary to, to go against; to contrast with
T4-1424.x: Contrary to expectations, the result wasn't good.
T4-1424.e: Literally 'to be opposite'; homonym warning: native 반하다 means 'to fall for someone'.
T4-1424.t: Don't confuse 기대에 반해 'contrary to expectations' with 그녀에게 반했어요 'I fell for her'.

T4-1425.forms: Mostly as connectors: N에 비해 · N에 비하여 · N에 비하면
T4-1425.m: to compare (to), to be in comparison with
T4-1425.ex: 올해는 작년에 비해 비가 많이 왔어요.
T4-1425.x: Compared to last year, it rained a lot this year.
T4-1425.t: N에 비해(서) means 'compared to N' and is one of the most common comparison patterns in TOPIK writing.

T4-1426.forms: N을/를 비롯해(서) · N을/를 비롯한 (+noun) · N에서 비롯되다
T4-1426.m: to begin with, including (and others), starting with
T4-1426.x: Large cities, including Seoul, have large populations.
T4-1426.e: Related to 비롯 'beginning'; 비롯되다 means 'to originate from'.
T4-1426.t: Pronounced [비로타다]; N을 비롯한 lists the main example first, like 'X and others'.

T4-1427.forms: Mostly as connectors: N(으)로 말미암아 · N(으)로 말미암은 (+noun)
T4-1427.m: to be caused by, to result from, to stem from
T4-1427.x: Many flights were canceled because of the typhoon.
T4-1427.e: Survives almost only in the fixed phrase (으)로 말미암아 'because of'.
T4-1427.t: Very formal and written; in speech say N 때문에 instead.

T4-1428.forms: Mostly as connectors: N(으)로 인해(서) · N(으)로 인하여 · N(으)로 인한 (+noun)
T4-1428.m: to be due to, to be caused by
T4-1428.x: The road was closed due to heavy snow.
T4-1428.t: N(으)로 인해 is the news-style way to say 'due to N'; 때문에 is the everyday version.

T4-1429.forms: Mostly as connectors: N에도 불구하고 · -(으)ㅁ에도 불구하고
T4-1429.m: despite, in spite of (lit. to disregard)
T4-1429.ex: 비가 오는데도 불구하고 많은 사람이 모였어요.
T4-1429.x: Despite the rain, many people gathered.
T4-1429.e: Literally 'not restrained by'; something doesn't stop the result.
T4-1429.t: Almost always appears as 에도 불구하고 'in spite of'; it rarely stands alone.

T4-1430.ex: 저도 마찬가지예요. 매운 음식을 잘 못 먹어요.
T4-1430.x: Same here. I can't really eat spicy food.
T4-1430.e: Probably from 마치 'just like' + 한가지 'the same kind'.

T4-1431.m: likewise, similarly, in the same way
T4-1431.x: Like his older brother, the younger one is also tall.

T4-1432.ex: 역시나 오늘도 지하철이 사람으로 꽉 찼어요.
T4-1432.x: As expected, the subway was packed with people again today.
