T4-1432.e: 역시 'also, as expected' + emphatic -나; stresses that it happened just as predicted.

T4-1433.ex: 하늘이 흐리더니 아니나 다를까 비가 오기 시작했어요.
T4-1433.x: The sky was cloudy, and sure enough, it started to rain.
T4-1433.e: Literally 'would it be otherwise, would it differ?'—a rhetorical 'of course not'.
T4-1433.t: Usually for things you predicted, often unwelcome ones.

T4-1434.ex: 불행히도 그 사고로 많은 사람이 다쳤습니다.
T4-1434.x: Unfortunately, many people were injured in that accident.

T4-1435.ex: 어릴 때 살던 집이 아직도 뚜렷이 기억나요.
T4-1435.x: I still clearly remember the house I lived in as a child.
T4-1435.t: Spelled 뚜렷이, not 뚜렷히; stems ending in ㅅ take -이.

T4-1436.x: This accident is clearly the company's responsibility.
T4-1436.e: Literally 'bright and white': plain as day.
T4-1436.t: Pronounced [명배키]; used for facts beyond doubt, like evidence or responsibility.

T4-1437.x: We clearly defined each person's role at the meeting.

T4-1438.ex: 최근 몇 년 사이에 출생률이 급격히 떨어졌습니다.
T4-1438.x: The birth rate has dropped sharply in recent years.
T4-1438.t: Pronounced [급껴키]; a TOPIK graph-writing favorite: 급격히 증가하다/감소하다.

T4-1439.ex: 그 소문은 인터넷을 통해 급속히 퍼졌어요.
T4-1439.x: The rumor spread rapidly through the internet.

T4-1440.x: Above all, health is the most important thing.

T4-1441.m: among them, of all of them, especially
T4-1441.ex: 한국 음식을 다 좋아하지만 그중에서도 김치찌개를 제일 좋아해요.
T4-1441.x: I like all Korean food, but among them I like kimchi stew the most.

T4-1442.m: to keep, to treasure, to cherish (a memory or keepsake)
T4-1442.ex: 할머니께 받은 편지를 지금도 소중히 간직하고 있어요.
T4-1442.x: I still treasure the letter I got from my grandmother.
T4-1442.e: Native Korean despite the 하다 ending; no hanja behind 간직.
T4-1442.t: Pronounced [간지카다]; used for things you keep close to your heart, unlike plain 보관하다 'to store'.

T4-1443.m: to handle, to cope with, to bear
T4-1443.ex: 혼자서 그 많은 일을 감당하기 어려워요.
T4-1443.x: It's hard to handle all that work alone.
T4-1443.t: Often negative: 감당할 수 없다 / 감당이 안 되다 'it's too much for me'.
rel: to be too much to handle

T4-1444.m: to accept (willingly), to put up with, to bear (a risk or loss)
T4-1444.ex: 성공하려면 어느 정도의 위험은 감수해야 해요.
T4-1444.x: To succeed, you have to accept a certain amount of risk.
T4-1444.e: Literally 'receive as if sweet': accept something bad without complaint.
T4-1444.t: Typical collocations: 위험을 감수하다, 손해를 감수하다, 불편을 감수하다.

T4-1445.m: to watch, to monitor, to keep under surveillance
T4-1445.x: The police are keeping the suspect under 24-hour surveillance.

T4-1446.m: to force, to coerce, to pressure into
T4-1446.ex: 부모님이 저에게 결혼을 강요하지 않으셨으면 좋겠어요.
T4-1446.x: I wish my parents wouldn't pressure me into getting married.

T4-1447.m: to intervene, to get involved, to interfere
T4-1447.ex: 다른 사람의 부부 싸움에 개입하지 않는 게 좋아요.
T4-1447.x: It's better not to get involved in other couples' fights.
T4-1447.t: Pronounced [개이파다]; common in news about governments: 정부가 시장에 개입하다.

T4-1448.m: to suggest, to propose, to make a recommendation (to a superior or organization)
T4-1448.ex: 직원들이 회사에 근무 시간 단축을 건의했어요.
T4-1448.x: The employees proposed shorter working hours to the company.
T4-1448.t: Used when suggesting something upward, to a boss, school or government; 제안하다 is more neutral.

T4-1449.m: to combine, to unite, to join together
T4-1449.ex: 이 제품은 전통과 현대 기술을 결합했어요.
T4-1449.x: This product combines tradition with modern technology.

T4-1450.x: Please share the meeting materials with your team members.

T4-1451.ex: 이 도시에는 전통과 현대가 공존하고 있어요.
T4-1451.x: Tradition and modernity coexist in this city.

T4-1452.m: to plan out, to conceive, to envision (an idea or project)
T4-1452.ex: 요즘 새 소설의 줄거리를 구상하고 있어요.
T4-1452.x: These days I'm working out the plot of a new novel.

T4-1453.m: to build, to establish, to set up (a system or network)
T4-1453.ex: 정부는 새로운 교통 시스템을 구축할 계획입니다.
T4-1453.x: The government plans to build a new transportation system.
T4-1453.t: Pronounced [구추카다]; used for abstract structures like systems, networks and relationships, not buildings.

T4-1454.m: to recommend, to invite, to urge (someone to do something)
T4-1454.x: My friend urged me to work out together.

T4-1455.m: to recommend, to encourage, to promote (officially)
T4-1455.ex: 의사들은 하루에 물을 여덟 잔 마시도록 권장합니다.
T4-1455.x: Doctors recommend drinking eight glasses of water a day.
T4-1455.t: Sounds official, like guidelines from doctors or governments; e.g. 권장 소비자 가격 'suggested retail price'.

T4-1456.m: to return home, to go home
T4-1456.ex: 늦게 귀가할 때는 가족에게 미리 연락하세요.
T4-1456.x: When you come home late, let your family know in advance.

T4-1457.m: to abuse, to misuse, to overuse
T4-1457.ex: 항생제를 남용하면 건강에 해로울 수 있어요.
T4-1457.x: Overusing antibiotics can be harmful to your health.
T4-1457.e: Literally 'overflowing use': using beyond the proper limit.

T4-1458.m: to understand and accept, to be convinced
T4-1458.ex: 그 설명은 도저히 납득할 수가 없어요.
T4-1458.x: I just can't accept that explanation.
T4-1458.t: Pronounced [납뜨카다]; often negative: 납득이 안 가요 'It doesn't make sense to me.'

T4-1459.m: to discuss, to talk over, to deliberate
T4-1459.x: We discussed next year's budget at the meeting.
T4-1459.t: Pronounced [노니하다]; more formal than 이야기하다, typical in meetings and news.

T4-1460.m: to shorten, to reduce, to cut (time or distance)
T4-1460.ex: 새 도로 덕분에 출근 시간을 30분 단축했어요.
T4-1460.x: Thanks to the new road, I cut my commute by 30 minutes.
T4-1460.t: Pronounced [단추카다]; 단축키 is a keyboard shortcut and 단축 번호 a speed-dial number.

T4-1461.m: to prepare for, to get ready for (a future event or risk)
T4-1461.ex: 겨울에 대비해서 따뜻한 옷을 미리 샀어요.
T4-1461.x: I bought warm clothes in advance to prepare for winter.
T4-1461.e: Literally 'prepare to face'; homonym warning: 대비 also means 'contrast'.
T4-1461.t: Pattern: N에 대비하다 'prepare for N', as in 시험에 대비하다 or 노후에 대비하다.

T4-1462.m: to deal with, to cope with, to handle (a situation)
T4-1462.x: You have to deal calmly with sudden situations.
T4-1462.t: Pattern: N에 대처하다; 대비하다 is before a problem, 대처하다 is when it happens.

T4-1463.m: to reach, to arrive at, to attain
T4-1463.ex: 오랜 회의 끝에 드디어 합의에 도달했어요.
T4-1463.x: After a long meeting, we finally reached an agreement.

T4-1464.m: to monopolize, to have all to oneself
T4-1464.ex: 동생이 텔레비전 리모컨을 하루 종일 독점했어요.
T4-1464.x: My little brother hogged the TV remote all day.

T4-1465.m: to mobilize, to bring in, to use all available (people or means)
T4-1465.x: Helicopters and soldiers were mobilized for the rescue.
T4-1465.t: Also figurative: 모든 방법을 동원하다 'use every possible means'.

T4-1466.m: to join in, to take part (in a shared cause)
T4-1466.ex: 많은 시민이 환경 보호 캠페인에 동참했어요.
T4-1466.x: Many citizens joined the environmental protection campaign.

T4-1467.m: to be paralyzed, to be numb; to be brought to a standstill
T4-1467.ex: 폭설 때문에 시내 교통이 완전히 마비됐어요.
T4-1467.x: Downtown traffic was completely paralyzed by the heavy snow.
T4-1467.t: Used for bodies and for systems: 교통이 마비되다, 기능이 마비되다.

T4-1468.m: to expire, to run out (a term or contract)
T4-1468.ex: 여권이 다음 달에 만료돼서 새로 만들어야 해요.
T4-1468.x: My passport expires next month, so I have to get a new one.
T4-1468.e: Literally 'full and finished': the term has run its course.
T4-1468.t: Pronounced [말료되다] — liquidization; used for contracts, visas and passports, not food (food uses 유통 기한이 지나다).

T4-1469.m: to be exempted, to be waived
T4-1469.x: Scholarship students are exempted from tuition.

T4-1470.m: to imitate, to copy, to mimic
T4-1470.x: Children learn by imitating their parents' behavior.

T4-1471.m: to seek, to look for, to explore (ways or solutions)
T4-1471.ex: 정부는 실업 문제의 해결 방안을 모색하고 있습니다.
T4-1471.x: The government is seeking solutions to the unemployment problem.
T4-1471.e: Literally 'grope and search', like feeling your way in the dark.
T4-1471.t: Pronounced [모새카다]; usually with 방법, 방안 or 대책 as the object.

T4-1472.m: to be absorbed in, to devote oneself to, to concentrate on
T4-1472.ex: 그는 연구에 몰두해서 밥 먹는 것도 잊었어요.
T4-1472.x: He was so absorbed in his research that he forgot to eat.
T4-1472.t: Pattern: N에 몰두하다, as in 일에 몰두하다 'bury oneself in work'.

T4-1473.m: to be immersed in, to get absorbed in
T4-1473.ex: 영화에 너무 몰입해서 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
T4-1473.x: I was so immersed in the movie that I lost track of time.
T4-1473.t: Pronounced [모리파다]; 몰입감 describes immersive games, dramas and films.

T4-1474.x: I have to return the library books by tomorrow.
T4-1474.t: Pronounced [반나파다]; standard for library books and rentals, while 반환하다 is more formal or legal.

T4-1475.m: to resist, to push back, to protest against
T4-1475.ex: 주민들이 새 공장 건설에 강하게 반발했습니다.
T4-1475.x: Residents strongly pushed back against building the new factory.

T4-1476.m: to return, to give back, to refund
T4-1476.x: When the contract ends, we'll return your deposit.

T4-1477.m: to excavate, to dig up; to discover (talent)
T4-1477.ex: 그 방송국은 새로운 인재를 발굴하는 데 힘쓰고 있어요.
T4-1477.x: That broadcaster is working hard to discover new talent.
T4-1477.t: Literal for archaeology (유물을 발굴하다) and figurative for talent (신인을 발굴하다).

T4-1478.m: to leave alone, to neglect, to leave unattended
T4-1478.ex: 고장 난 자전거가 몇 달째 길에 방치되어 있어요.
T4-1478.x: A broken bike has been left abandoned on the street for months.

T4-1479.m: to exclude, to rule out, to leave out
T4-1479.ex: 사고 가능성을 완전히 배제할 수는 없어요.
T4-1479.x: We can't completely rule out the possibility of an accident.
T4-1479.t: Common phrase: 가능성을 배제할 수 없다 'cannot rule out the possibility'.

T4-1480.m: to transform (oneself), to make over, to reinvent oneself
T4-1480.ex: 그 가수는 이번 드라마에서 배우로 변신했어요.
T4-1480.x: That singer transformed into an actor in this drama.
T4-1480.e: Literally 'change body'; used for superheroes and image makeovers alike.

T4-1481.ex: 전쟁으로 무너진 궁궐을 원래 모습으로 복원했어요.
T4-1481.x: They restored the palace destroyed in the war to its original form.

T4-1482.m: to impose, to levy (a tax, fine or duty)
T4-1482.x: The government imposed high taxes on imported goods.

T4-1483.m: to grant, to give, to assign (a right, meaning, role)
T4-1483.ex: 회사는 직원들에게 더 많은 권한을 부여했습니다.
T4-1483.x: The company gave its employees more authority.
T4-1483.e: Literally 'attach and give' — handing over something abstract like rights or meaning.
T4-1483.t: Used with abstract objects: 권한, 의미, 자격, 기회 — not for handing someone a physical item.

T4-1484.m: to separate, to divide, to split
T4-1484.x: You have to separate your trash by type before throwing it out.
T4-1484.t: Pronounced [불리하다] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T4-1485.m: to compare (figuratively), to liken, to use a metaphor
T4-1485.ex: 사람들은 인생을 긴 여행에 비유하곤 해요.
T4-1485.x: People often compare life to a long journey.
T4-1485.e: Literally 'compare to illustrate' — explaining one thing through another.
T4-1485.t: Pattern: A를 B에 비유하다 = to liken A to B.

T4-1486.x: Traffic accidents happen frequently on this road.
T4-1486.t: A formal word often used in news; in everyday speech people just say 자주.

T4-1487.m: to lose (something important), to be deprived of
T4-1487.x: He lost part of his memory in an accident.
T4-1487.e: Two 'lose' syllables stacked — a serious, permanent loss.
T4-1487.t: Used for abstract or serious losses like 기억, 자격, 의욕; for lost keys just say 잃어버리다.

T4-1488.x: The judges selected the best work of the year.
T4-1488.e: Literally 'choose and fix' — picking officially after review.

T4-1489.x: The students elected a new president by vote.
T4-1489.e: Literally 'choose and put forward' — choosing a person by vote.
T4-1489.t: 선출하다 is for people chosen by vote; use 선정하다 for things like books, sites or winners.

T4-1490.m: to take in, to consume (food, nutrients)
T4-1490.x: For your health, eat plenty of vegetables.
T4-1490.e: Literally 'take in and take' — absorbing food or nutrients.
T4-1490.t: A formal word from health articles; in daily speech say 먹다.

T4-1491.ex: 우리 회사는 지난 5년 동안 빠르게 성장했어요.
T4-1491.x: Our company has grown fast over the past five years.

T4-1492.m: to be damaged, to be harmed
T4-1492.x: Important documents got damaged because they got wet in the rain.

T4-1493.m: to establish, to set up (a plan, policy, government)
T4-1493.x: The government established a new economic policy.
T4-1493.e: Literally 'plant and make stand' — setting up a plan firmly.
T4-1493.t: Collocates with 계획, 정책, 대책, 전략; everyday equivalent is 계획을 세우다.

T4-1494.x: The company actively accepted its employees' opinions.
T4-1494.e: Literally 'receive and allow' — taking in ideas or opinions.
T4-1494.t: A homonym 수용하다 (with different hanja) means to house people, as in a stadium seating 5만 명.

T4-1495.m: to carry out, to perform (a task, duty)
T4-1495.x: He successfully carried out the mission he was given.

T4-1496.m: to suffer (from), to be troubled by, to be tormented
T4-1496.x: These days many office workers suffer from stress.
T4-1496.t: Pattern: N에 시달리다 — 불면증에, 소음에, 빚에 시달리다.

T4-1497.x: We will respond promptly to customers' inquiries.
T4-1497.t: Pronounced [신소카다]; common in formal service language as 신속하게 or 신속히.

T4-1498.m: to suppress, to restrain, to curb
T4-1498.ex: 정부는 물가 상승을 억제하기 위해 노력하고 있어요.
T4-1498.x: The government is working to curb rising prices.

T4-1499.m: to be extended, to be prolonged
T4-1499.x: The meeting was extended by another hour.

T4-1500.m: to direct (a film, play); to stage, to create (a scene or mood)
T4-1500.ex: 그 감독이 연출한 영화는 모두 인기가 많아요.
T4-1500.x: All the movies that director made are very popular.
T4-1500.t: Also used for creating a look or mood: 분위기를 연출하다.

T4-1501.x: My parents always worry about my health.
T4-1501.t: Pronounced [염녀하다]; more formal than 걱정하다, as in 염려하지 마세요.

T4-1502.ex: 모든 작업을 완료하면 저에게 알려 주세요.
T4-1502.x: Please let me know when you finish all the work.
T4-1502.t: Pronounced [왈료하다] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T4-1503.e: Literally 'move and go' — vehicles running on a route.

T4-1504.m: to cause, to trigger, to provoke
T4-1504.ex: 스트레스는 여러 가지 질병을 유발할 수 있어요.

T4-1505.m: to attract (investment, tourists, events), to bring in
T4-1505.ex: 우리 시는 올림픽을 유치하기 위해 노력하고 있어요.
T4-1505.x: Our city is working to host the Olympics.
T4-1505.e: Literally 'induce to come' — drawing in investment or events.
T4-1505.t: Don't confuse with the adjective 유치하다 (childish), which uses different hanja.

T4-1506.m: to foster, to nurture, to develop (talent, industry)
T4-1506.x: The government announced a policy to foster small businesses.

T4-1507.x: Thank you for responding to the survey.
T4-1507.t: Used for surveys, calls and requests; 대답하다 is the everyday word for answering a question.

T4-1508.m: to apply (knowledge, a technique), to put to practical use
T4-1508.ex: 배운 내용을 실제 생활에 응용해 보세요.
T4-1508.x: Try applying what you learned to real life.
T4-1508.e: Literally 'use in response' — adapting what you know to a new case.

T4-1509.m: to request, to commission, to ask (a professional to do something)
T4-1509.ex: 회사는 전문 변호사에게 이 사건을 의뢰했어요.
T4-1509.x: The company hired a specialist lawyer to handle this case.
T4-1509.e: Literally 'rely and depend' — entrusting a task to an expert.
T4-1509.t: Used when asking professionals: 변호사, 전문가, 업체에 의뢰하다.

T4-1510.ex: 그는 평생 한국 문화 발전에 이바지했어요.
T4-1510.x: He contributed to the development of Korean culture all his life.
T4-1510.e: Native Korean despite looking formal; a pure-Korean equivalent of 공헌하다.
T4-1510.t: Pattern: N에 이바지하다; mostly heard in speeches, writing and news.

T4-1511.m: to match, to agree, to coincide
T4-1511.x: What the two people said matches exactly.
T4-1511.e: Literally 'arrive at one' — becoming the same.

T4-1512.x: He proved his skill through results.
T4-1512.t: Pronounced [입쯩하다] — the ㅈ becomes tense after ㅂ.

T4-1513.ex: 많은 시민들이 부당한 권력에 끝까지 저항했습니다.
T4-1513.x: Many citizens resisted unjust power to the end.

T4-1514.m: to accumulate, to save up (points, funds)
T4-1514.ex: 이 카드로 결제하면 포인트를 적립할 수 있어요.
T4-1514.x: If you pay with this card, you can earn points.
T4-1514.t: Pronounced [정니파다]; you'll hear 포인트 적립해 드릴까요? at every Korean store checkout.

T4-1515.m: to devote oneself, to concentrate on
T4-1515.x: He quit his job and devoted himself to research.

T4-1516.ex: 새 기계 덕분에 비용을 크게 절감했어요.
T4-1516.x: Thanks to the new machine, we cut costs a lot.

T4-1517.x: It's dangerous, so don't approach this area.

T4-1518.ex: 그 가족은 십 년 전에 미국에 정착했어요.
T4-1518.x: That family settled in the U.S. ten years ago.
T4-1518.e: Literally 'fixed and attached' — staying put in one place.

T4-1519.m: to remove, to get rid of, to eliminate
T4-1519.ex: 이 세제는 얼룩을 깨끗하게 제거해 줘요.

T4-1520.m: to raise (a question, issue), to file (a lawsuit)
T4-1520.ex: 한 기자가 정부 발표에 의문을 제기했어요.
T4-1520.x: A reporter raised questions about the government's announcement.
T4-1520.t: Fixed collocations: 문제를 제기하다, 의문을 제기하다, 소송을 제기하다.

T4-1521.m: to present, to suggest, to show
T4-1521.x: He presented a good solution at the meeting.

T4-1522.m: to exclude, to leave out, to except
T4-1522.x: I work out every morning except on weekends.
T4-1522.t: N을 제외하고 (= except N) is the most common pattern.

T4-1523.e: Literally 'mainly hold' — the organizer of an event.

T4-1524.m: to observe, to comply with, to follow (rules)
T4-1524.ex: 모든 운전자는 교통 법규를 준수해야 합니다.
T4-1524.x: All drivers must obey traffic laws.
T4-1524.t: A formal word for rules and laws; in speech, 지키다 is far more common.

T4-1525.m: to promote, to improve, to enhance
T4-1525.ex: 규칙적인 운동은 건강을 증진하는 데 도움이 돼요.
T4-1525.x: Regular exercise helps improve your health.

T4-1526.m: to pay, to provide, to issue (money, supplies)
T4-1526.x: The company pays salaries on the 25th of each month.
T4-1526.t: 지급하다 is an organization giving money or items; 지불하다 is paying for something you bought.

T4-1527.m: to designate, to appoint, to specify
T4-1527.ex: 선생님이 학생들에게 각자 앉을 자리를 지정해 주셨어요.
T4-1527.x: The teacher assigned each student a seat.

T4-1528.m: to aim for, to pursue, to be oriented toward
T4-1528.ex: 우리 회사는 고객 중심의 서비스를 지향합니다.
T4-1528.x: Our company aims for customer-centered service.
T4-1528.t: Don't confuse with 지양하다 (to avoid), which sounds similar but means the opposite.

T4-1529.m: to be obsessed with, to cling to
T4-1529.ex: 너무 결과에만 집착하면 과정을 즐길 수 없어요.
T4-1529.x: If you're too obsessed with results, you can't enjoy the process.
T4-1529.e: Literally 'grasp and stick' — can't let go.

T4-1530.m: to block, to cut off, to shut out
T4-1530.t: Also for blocking someone online: 번호를 차단하다, 사이트를 차단하다.

T4-1531.ex: 공사장에서는 누구나 반드시 안전모를 착용해야 합니다.
T4-1531.x: Everyone must wear a hard hat at construction sites.
T4-1531.t: One formal verb covering 입다, 쓰다, 신다, 차다; common on signs and in announcements.

T4-1532.ex: 더 자세한 내용은 저희 홈페이지를 참조하세요.
T4-1532.x: For more details, please refer to our website.
T4-1532.t: 참조 also means 'cc' in emails; 참고하다 is the more common everyday word.

T4-1533.m: to adopt, to select (a proposal, method)
T4-1533.x: The company eventually adopted his proposal.

T4-1534.m: to be faced with, to be placed in (a situation)
T4-1534.ex: 그 회사는 지금 큰 위기에 처해 있어요.
T4-1534.x: That company is now facing a major crisis.
T4-1534.e: Literally 'to be placed' — being put in a situation.

T4-1535.ex: 가방 무게가 20킬로그램을 초과하면 추가 요금이 있어요.
T4-1535.x: If your bag weighs over 20 kilograms, there's an extra fee.

T4-1536.m: to urge, to call for, to press for
T4-1536.ex: 시민 단체는 정부에 빠른 대책을 촉구했습니다.
T4-1536.x: Civic groups urged the government to take quick measures.

T4-1537.m: to promote, to accelerate, to stimulate
T4-1537.ex: 물을 많이 마시면 소화를 촉진할 수 있어요.
T4-1537.x: Drinking lots of water can aid digestion.

T4-1538.x: Please add a little milk to my coffee.
T4-1538.t: Very common when ordering: 샷 추가해 주세요 = an extra shot, please.

T4-1539.m: to push forward, to carry out, to promote (a project, plan)
T4-1539.ex: 시는 새로운 공원 건설을 추진하고 있습니다.
T4-1539.x: The city is pushing ahead with building a new park.

T4-1540.m: to reduce, to scale down, to shrink
T4-1540.x: The economy was bad, so the company downsized.

T4-1541.ex: 그는 오랜 경험을 통해 많은 지식을 축적했어요.
T4-1541.x: He built up a lot of knowledge through long experience.
T4-1541.t: Pronounced [축쩌카다]; used with 지식, 경험, 자본, 데이터.

T4-1542.ex: 그 회사는 다음 달에 새 휴대폰을 출시해요.
T4-1542.x: That company is releasing a new phone next month.
T4-1542.t: Used for products; for movies or albums, 개봉하다 and 발매하다 are more common.

T4-1543.ex: 지원자는 다음 조건을 모두 충족해야 합니다.
T4-1543.x: Applicants must meet all of the following conditions.

T4-1544.ex: 다른 사람의 사생활을 침해하면 안 돼요.
T4-1544.x: You must not invade other people's privacy.

T4-1545.m: to compromise, to come to terms
T4-1545.ex: 두 사람은 결국 서로 조금씩 양보하며 타협했어요.
T4-1545.x: In the end, the two compromised by each giving in a little.
T4-1545.t: Pronounced [타혀파다]; 타협하지 않다 often praises someone who sticks to principles.

T4-1546.m: to explore, to investigate, to study in depth
T4-1546.x: Scientists are exploring the secrets of the universe.
T4-1546.t: 탐구 is exploring ideas or knowledge; 탐험 is exploring physical places.

T4-1547.m: to integrate, to unify, to merge
T4-1547.ex: 두 회사는 내년에 하나로 통합할 예정이에요.
T4-1547.x: The two companies plan to merge into one next year.

T4-1548.m: to put in, to invest, to deploy (resources, people)
T4-1548.ex: 정부는 이 사업에 많은 예산을 투입했어요.
T4-1548.x: The government put a big budget into this project.

T4-1549.x: On the weekend I edited and posted my travel video.
T4-1549.t: Pronounced [편지파다]; used for videos, books, photos and documents.

T4-1550.m: to explain (oneself), to clarify, to give an account
T4-1550.ex: 그 배우는 소문에 대해 직접 해명했어요.
T4-1550.x: The actor personally addressed the rumors.
T4-1550.t: Used when clearing up suspicion or criticism; 설명하다 is neutral explaining.

T4-1551.m: to lift, to cancel, to release (a restriction, alarm)
T4-1551.x: The typhoon passed, so the weather agency lifted the warning.
T4-1551.t: Everyday use: 잠금을 해제하다 (unlock a phone), 알람을 해제하다.

T4-1552.x: This restaurant allows you to bring pets.
T4-1552.t: 허용하다 is about rules and systems; 허락하다 is a person giving permission.

T4-1553.m: to appeal, to plead; to complain of (pain)
T4-1553.x: The patient had been complaining of a severe headache since yesterday.

T4-1554.ex: 공연을 보려고 일찍 가서 좋은 자리를 확보했어요.
T4-1554.x: I went early to the show and secured good seats.
T4-1554.t: Pronounced [확뽀하다]; common objects: 자리, 예산, 인력, 증거.

T4-1555.m: to expand, to extend, to enlarge
T4-1555.ex: 손님이 많이 늘어서 가게를 두 배로 확장했어요.
T4-1555.x: We got many more customers, so we doubled the size of the store.

T4-1556.m: to be confirmed, to be finalized
T4-1556.x: The date of the next meeting was confirmed for Friday.
T4-1556.t: Pronounced [확쩡되다] — the ㅈ becomes tense after ㄱ.

T4-1557.m: to obtain, to win, to acquire
T4-1557.x: A Korean athlete won a gold medal at the Olympics.

T4-1559.m: to block (the way), to obstruct, to stand in the way
T4-1559.x: A big truck is blocking the alley.
T4-1559.e: Built from 가로 (across, sideways) + 막다 (to block): blocking across the path.
T4-1559.t: Pronounced [가로막따]; also figurative: 꿈을 가로막다 = to stand in the way of a dream.

T4-1560.m: to cover, to hide, to block (from view); to be picky about, to tell apart
T4-1560.x: The child covered her face with her hands out of shyness.
T4-1560.e: Homonym warning: 'cover, hide' and 'pick, be choosy' are both 가리다.
T4-1560.t: Set phrases: 음식을 가리다 = to be picky with food; 낯을 가리다 = to be shy with strangers.

T4-1561.m: to sink, to settle; to calm down, to subside
T4-1561.x: After I took the medicine, the pain eased a little.
T4-1561.e: Contains 앉다 'to sit': something sinks and sits at the bottom.
T4-1561.t: Pronounced [가라안따] — ㄵ sounds like ㄴ before a consonant.

T4-1562.m: to intercept, to snatch; to steal (credit, an idea)
T4-1562.ex: 동료가 제 아이디어를 가로채서 정말 화가 났어요.
T4-1562.x: I was really angry because a coworker stole my idea.
T4-1562.e: 가로 'sideways' + 채다 'to snatch': grabbing something from the side.
T4-1562.t: 말을 가로채다 means to cut someone off mid-sentence.

T4-1563.forms: 갈아요 · 갈았어요 · 갈 거예요 · 가세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1563.m: to replace, to change; to grind, to sharpen
T4-1563.x: The fluorescent light burned out, so I replaced it with a new one.
T4-1563.e: Homonyms: 갈다 means 'replace', 'grind', and also 'plow' — context tells them apart.
T4-1563.t: 갈 거예요 and 가세요 look like forms of 가다 'to go', so rely on context.

T4-1564.m: to split, to crack; to break up, to be divided
T4-1564.x: The rice paddies cracked because of the drought.

T4-1565.m: to wrap, to cover; to protect, to stick up for
T4-1565.ex: 엄마는 항상 동생 편을 들고 감싸 줘요.
T4-1565.x: Mom always takes my little brother's side and sticks up for him.
T4-1565.e: Probably 감다 'to wind' + 싸다 'to wrap': wrapping all the way around.

T4-1566.m: to harvest, to gather; to achieve (results); to take back
T4-1566.ex: 우리 팀이 이번 경기에서 큰 승리를 거두었어요.
T4-1566.x: Our team won a big victory in this game.
T4-1566.e: Its short form 걷다 means 'to collect', as in 회비를 걷다.

T4-1567.forms: 거들어요 · 거들었어요 · 거들 거예요 · 거드세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1567.m: to help out, to lend a hand; to chime in
T4-1567.ex: 저녁 준비하는 것 좀 거들어 줄래요?
T4-1567.x: Could you help out a bit with getting dinner ready?
T4-1567.t: Also means backing up someone's argument: 옆에서 말을 거들다.

T4-1568.m: to take out (of liquid), to scoop up; to rescue; to salvage
T4-1568.x: I scooped the green onions out of the soup.
T4-1568.t: Casual: 사진 한 장 건졌다 means you got at least one good photo out of it.

T4-1569.m: to throw on (clothes), to drape; to span, to extend over
T4-1569.x: It was cold, so I draped a blanket over my shoulders.
T4-1569.e: Related to 걸다 'to hang': something hung loosely over something else.

T4-1570.m: to compete, to contend, to match skills
T4-1570.x: The two teams went head to head in the final.
T4-1570.t: Common pattern: 실력을 겨루다 'to test skills against each other'.

T4-1571.m: to serve with, to add on the side, to accompany
T4-1571.x: I had the steak with a salad on the side.
T4-1571.e: 곁 'side' + 들이다 'to bring in': bringing something in on the side.

T4-1572.m: to skip a meal, to go hungry, to starve
T4-1572.x: I was so busy that I skipped lunch today.
T4-1572.t: Pronounced [굼따] — in ㄻ only ㅁ is heard before a consonant.

T4-1573.m: to starve, to go hungry; to hunger for, to crave
T4-1573.ex: 전쟁 때문에 많은 아이들이 굶주리고 있습니다.
T4-1573.x: Many children are starving because of the war.
T4-1573.e: Built on 굶다 'to skip meals': this is the long-term, serious version.

T4-1574.m: to bend; to give in, to yield
T4-1574.ex: 그는 끝까지 자기 뜻을 굽히지 않았어요.
T4-1574.x: He never backed down from his position.
T4-1574.e: Causative of 굽다 'to be bent': literally 'make bent'.
T4-1574.t: Pronounced [구피다] — ㅂ + ㅎ merges into ㅍ.

T4-1575.m: to recommend, to suggest; to offer (food, drinks)
T4-1575.x: The doctor recommended that I exercise every day.
T4-1575.e: Literally 'do urging': 권 means to urge or encourage.
T4-1575.t: 술을 권하다 means offering someone a drink, a big part of Korean drinking etiquette.

T4-1576.m: to scratch; to scrape; (slang) to swipe (a card)
T4-1576.ex: 모기에 물린 데를 자꾸 긁지 마세요.
T4-1576.x: Don't keep scratching the mosquito bite.
T4-1576.t: Pronounced [극따]; before a vowel both sound: 긁어요 [글거요].

T4-1577.forms: 기울어요 · 기울었어요 · 기울 거예요 · 기운 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T4-1577.m: to lean, to tilt; to decline, to wane; to lean toward (an opinion)
T4-1577.x: The picture frame on the wall is tilted to one side.
T4-1577.e: Make it causative with -이-: 기울다 'lean' becomes 기울이다 'make lean'.

T4-1578.m: to tilt, to incline; to devote (effort, attention)
T4-1578.x: The students listened closely to the teacher.
T4-1578.e: Causative of 기울다 'to lean': literally 'make something lean'.
T4-1578.t: Key collocations: 귀를 기울이다 (listen closely), 노력을 기울이다 (put in effort).

T4-1579.forms: 깔아요 · 깔았어요 · 깔 거예요 · 까세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1579.m: to spread (out), to lay down; to install (an app)
T4-1579.x: We spread out a mat on the ground in the park and sat down.
T4-1579.e: Its passive 깔리다 means 'to be spread' or 'to be pinned under'.
T4-1579.t: Casual: 앱을 깔다 means to install an app.

T4-1580.m: to be spread, to be laid; to be crushed under; to be everywhere
T4-1580.x: The road is covered with fallen leaves.
T4-1580.e: Passive of 깔다 'to spread': literally 'get spread out' or 'get pinned under'.

T4-1581.m: to be reluctant, to avoid, to shy away from
T4-1581.ex: 그는 사람들 앞에서 말하는 것을 꺼려요.
T4-1581.x: He's reluctant to speak in front of people.
T4-1581.t: Usually -기를 꺼리다 or -는 것을 꺼리다: 대답하기를 꺼렸어요.

T4-1582.m: to hug, to embrace; to take on (a problem)
T4-1582.x: I gave my friend, whom I hadn't seen in ages, a tight hug.
T4-1582.e: 끼다 'to fit in' + 안다 'to hold': holding someone tightly.

T4-1583.m: to get twisted, to get tangled; to go wrong
T4-1583.x: Things went wrong from the start, so the plan got delayed.
T4-1583.e: Passive of 꼬다 'to twist', as in 다리를 꼬다 'to cross your legs'.
T4-1583.t: Homonym: 꼬이다 also means bugs swarming, as in 파리가 꼬이다.

T4-1584.x: The teacher scolded the student who came late.
T4-1584.t: 꾸짖다 sounds formal or literary; in everyday speech 혼내다 is more common.

T4-1585.x: He knelt down and begged for forgiveness.
T4-1585.t: Pronounced [꿀타]; the ㅎ goes silent before a vowel: 꿇어요 [꾸러요].

T4-1586.forms: 끌어요 · 끌었어요 · 끌 거예요 · 끄세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1586.m: to pull, to drag; to attract (attention); to drag out (time)
T4-1586.ex: 그 영화는 젊은 사람들의 관심을 끌었어요.
T4-1586.x: That movie attracted young people's attention.
T4-1586.t: Set phrases: 관심을 끌다 (attract interest), 시간을 끌다 (stall for time).

T4-1587.m: to be dragged; to be drawn to, to be attracted
T4-1587.ex: 이상하게 그 사람에게 자꾸 마음이 끌려요.
T4-1587.x: Strangely, I keep feeling drawn to that person.
T4-1587.e: Passive of 끌다 'to pull': literally 'get pulled' toward something.

T4-1588.m: to pull toward, to draw in; to attract
T4-1588.x: He pulled the chair toward the desk.
T4-1588.e: 끌다 'pull' + 당기다 'pull': doubled to stress drawing something closer.

T4-1589.m: to drag in, to draw in, to involve; to attract (investment)
T4-1589.x: Don't drag your friends into your own problems.
T4-1589.e: 끌다 'pull' + 들이다 'bring in': pulling someone into a situation.
T4-1589.t: Often negative, like dragging someone into trouble, but 투자를 끌어들이다 is neutral.

T4-1590.forms: 끼어들어요 · 끼어들었어요 · 끼어들 거예요 · 끼어드세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1590.m: to cut in, to butt in, to interrupt; to merge (into traffic)
T4-1590.x: Don't butt into other people's conversations.

T4-1591.m: to be divided, to be split
T4-1591.ex: 이 책은 세 부분으로 나누어져 있어요.
T4-1591.x: This book is divided into three parts.
T4-1591.e: 나누다 'to divide' + -어지다 'become'; often shortened to 나눠지다.

T4-1592.m: to be divided, to be split up
T4-1592.ex: 그 문제에 대해서 의견이 둘로 나뉘었어요.
T4-1592.x: Opinions were split in two on that issue.
T4-1592.e: Passive of 나누다 'to divide': a shorter way to say 나누어지다.
T4-1592.t: Don't confuse 나뉘어요 'it is divided' with 나눠요 'I divide it'.

T4-1593.m: to fly (a kite), to let fly; to blow away; to lose, to blow (money, a chance)
T4-1593.x: The kids are flying kites in the park.
T4-1593.e: Causative of 날다 'to fly': literally 'make fly'.
T4-1593.t: Casual: 돈을 날리다 = lose money; 기회를 날리다 = blow a chance.

T4-1594.m: to look out; to foresee, to look ahead
T4-1594.x: When I looked out the window, it was snowing.
T4-1594.e: 내다 'out' + 보다 'to look': looking outward, or forward into the future.

T4-1595.m: to put down, to set down; to let go of (a burden, a position)
T4-1595.x: Please set your heavy bags down here.
T4-1595.e: 내리다 'to lower' + 놓다 'to put': lower it and leave it.
T4-1595.t: Figurative: 마음을 내려놓다 means to let go of your worries.

T4-1596.forms: 내밀어요 · 내밀었어요 · 내밀 거예요 · 내미세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1596.m: to stick out, to hold out; to offer (a hand)
T4-1596.x: He smiled and held out his hand first.
T4-1596.e: 내다 'out' + 밀다 'to push': pushing something outward.

T4-1597.m: to spit out; to blurt out (words)
T4-1597.ex: 화가 나서 심한 말을 내뱉고 말았어요.
T4-1597.x: I got angry and ended up blurting out harsh words.

T4-1598.m: to put forward, to nominate; to emphasize, to insist on; to show off
T4-1598.ex: 그 회사는 저렴한 가격을 장점으로 내세워요.
T4-1598.x: That company promotes its low prices as its strong point.
T4-1598.e: 내다 'out' + 세우다 'to stand up': standing something at the front.
T4-1598.t: 내세울 게 없다 means 'I have nothing to brag about'.

T4-1599.m: to turn (a page); to hand over; to pass (a time, a deadline); to get through
T4-1599.x: I read slowly, turning the pages.
T4-1599.e: Causative of 넘다 'to go over': make something go over.

T4-1600.m: to overflow, to brim over; to be full of
T4-1600.ex: 그 가수의 무대는 언제나 에너지가 넘쳐요.
T4-1600.x: That singer's performances are always full of energy.
T4-1600.e: Related to 넘다 'to go over': liquid going over the edge.

T4-1601.m: to melt, to thaw; to warm up
T4-1601.x: Melt the butter over low heat.
T4-1601.e: Causative of 녹다 'to melt': make something melt.

T4-1602.m: to enjoy (a benefit, freedom, a good life)
T4-1602.ex: 할아버지는 은퇴 후에 여유로운 생활을 누리고 계세요.
T4-1602.x: My grandfather is enjoying a relaxed life after retiring.
T4-1602.t: Use 누리다 for privileges or rights like 자유 and 혜택; for food or fun, use 즐기다.

T4-1603.m: to spread out, to lay out; to leave scattered; to go on and on (talking)
T4-1603.x: My little brother left his toys scattered all over the floor.
T4-1603.e: Probably 늘다 'to extend' + 놓다 'to put': laying things out in a line.

T4-1604.m: to approach, to go up to
T4-1604.e: 다가 'closer' + 가다 'to go'; with 오다 it becomes 다가오다 'to come closer'.

T4-1605.m: to trim, to tidy; to polish, to refine; to clean (vegetables)
T4-1605.ex: 보고서를 내기 전에 문장을 다시 다듬었어요.
T4-1605.x: I polished the sentences again before turning in the report.
T4-1605.t: In cooking, 파를 다듬다 means cleaning and trimming green onions.

T4-1606.forms: 다물어요 · 다물었어요 · 다물 거예요 · 다무세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1606.ex: 그는 입을 꼭 다물고 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
T4-1606.x: He kept his mouth shut and didn't say a word.
T4-1606.t: Used only with 입 'mouth'; for doors use 닫다, and for eyes use 감다.

T4-1607.m: to mince, to chop finely; to firm up, to strengthen; to resolve firmly
T4-1607.x: Mince the garlic finely and add it.

T4-1608.m: to soothe, to calm, to comfort; to coax
T4-1608.x: Mom is soothing the crying baby.
T4-1608.e: Homonym warning: 달래요 can also be short for 달라고 해요 'they're asking for it'.

T4-1609.m: to run away, to flee, to escape
T4-1609.x: The thief saw the police and quickly ran away.

T4-1610.forms: 대들어요 · 대들었어요 · 대들 거예요 · 대드세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1610.m: to talk back, to defy, to stand up to (a superior)
T4-1610.x: The child talked back to his parents for the first time.
T4-1610.t: Used toward someone above you, like a parent, teacher or boss.

T4-1611.m: to grope, to feel for; to stammer; to search (one's memory)
T4-1611.x: It was dark, so I felt along the wall for the switch.
T4-1611.t: 말을 더듬다 means to stutter; 기억을 더듬다 means to search one's memory.

T4-1612.forms: 덜어요 · 덜었어요 · 덜 거예요 · 더세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1612.m: to take some off, to remove a portion; to lessen, to ease
T4-1612.x: There was too much rice, so I took some off.
T4-1612.t: Common pairs: 부담을 덜다 'ease a burden', 걱정을 덜다 'worry less'.

T4-1613.m: to add (on), to attach; to add (a remark)
T4-1613.ex: 발표 끝에 몇 가지 의견을 덧붙였어요.
T4-1613.x: At the end of the presentation, I added a few comments.
T4-1613.e: 덧- 'extra, on top' + 붙이다 'to attach'; 덧- also appears in 덧셈 'addition'.
T4-1613.t: Pronounced [덛뿌치다] — ㅌ before 이 becomes ㅊ.

T4-1614.m: to turn back, to reverse, to undo; to return
T4-1614.ex: 지나간 시간은 다시 되돌릴 수 없어요.
T4-1614.x: You can't turn back time once it's gone.

T4-1615.x: I left my wallet behind, so I went back home.
T4-1615.e: 되- 'back' + 돌아가다 'to go back': stresses turning back the way you came.

T4-1616.m: to look back (on), to reflect on
T4-1616.ex: 연말에 한 해를 되돌아보면서 일기를 썼어요.
T4-1616.x: At the end of the year, I wrote in my diary, looking back on the year.

T4-1617.m: to revive, to bring back to life; to restore
T4-1617.ex: 이 노래는 어린 시절의 추억을 되살려 줘요.
T4-1617.x: This song brings back childhood memories.
T4-1617.e: 되- 'again' + 살리다 'to keep alive', the causative of 살다.

T4-1618.m: to get back, to regain, to recover
T4-1618.x: I got my lost wallet back at the police station.
T4-1618.e: 되- 'back' + 찾다 'to find': finding what you once had.
T4-1618.t: Common with abstract nouns: 건강을 되찾다, 웃음을 되찾다, 자신감을 되찾다.

T4-1619.m: to knock, to tap, to beat
T4-1619.x: Someone knocked on the door, so I went to check.

T4-1620.forms: 뒤따라요 · 뒤따랐어요 · 뒤따를 거예요 · 뒤따르세요 (ㅡ drops)
T4-1620.m: to follow (behind); to come with, to accompany
T4-1620.x: The children followed the teacher into the classroom.

T4-1621.m: to fall behind, to lag behind; to be outdated
T4-1621.x: This phone's design is a bit outdated.
T4-1621.e: 뒤 'behind' + 떨어지다 'to drop away': dropping behind others.
T4-1621.t: 시대에 뒤떨어지다 'to be behind the times' is a common phrase.

T4-1622.m: to fall behind, to lag; to rummage, to search through
T4-1622.x: I rummaged through my whole bag looking for my keys.
T4-1622.e: Two homonyms: 'lag behind' and 'rummage' — context tells which.
T4-1622.t: Careful: in rude slang 뒤지다 also means 'to die', so watch your context.

T4-1623.m: to turn over, to flip; to turn inside out; to overturn (a decision)
T4-1623.ex: 고기가 익으면 한 번 뒤집어 주세요.
T4-1623.x: When the meat is cooked, flip it once.

T4-1624.forms: 드나들어요 · 드나들었어요 · 드나들 거예요 · 드나드세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1624.m: to come and go, to go in and out; to frequent
T4-1624.ex: 이 문으로는 직원만 드나들 수 있어요.
T4-1624.x: Only staff can go in and out through this door.
T4-1624.e: Built from 들다 'to go in' and 나다 'to go out': in and out.

T4-1625.m: to reveal, to show, to expose
T4-1625.ex: 그는 자기 감정을 잘 드러내지 않아요.
T4-1625.x: He doesn't show his feelings much.
T4-1625.e: Active partner of 드러나다 'to be revealed'.

T4-1626.forms: 들떠요 · 들떴어요 · 들뜰 거예요 · 들뜬 (+noun) (ㅡ drops)
T4-1626.m: to be excited, to be restless; (of wallpaper, skin) to lift, to peel
T4-1626.x: I'm all excited with the trip coming up.
T4-1626.e: Contains 뜨다 'to float': your heart floats up with excitement.

T4-1627.m: to fit, to match; to come true, to be right
T4-1627.x: Yesterday's weather forecast was exactly right.
T4-1627.e: 들다 'to go in' + 맞다 'to fit': fits right in.
T4-1627.t: Often about predictions: 예상이 들어맞다 'the prediction came true'.

T4-1628.m: to let in, to bring in; to spend (time, money, effort); to form (a habit)
T4-1628.ex: 좋은 습관을 들이는 데는 시간이 걸려요.
T4-1628.x: It takes time to form a good habit.
T4-1628.e: Causative of 들다 'to go in': make something go in.
T4-1628.t: Key pairs: 습관을 들이다 (form a habit), 공을 들이다 (put in effort), 돈을 들이다 (spend money).

T4-1629.x: I studied hard and caught up with my classmates.
T4-1629.e: 따라 'following' + 잡다 'to catch': follow and catch.

T4-1630.m: to leave out, to ostracize; to shake off, to get away from
T4-1630.x: Leaving a friend out is a bad thing to do.
T4-1630.e: The noun 따돌림 'ostracism' and slang 왕따 'outcast' come from this verb.

T4-1631.m: to take on, to be saddled with (a task)
T4-1631.ex: 동료가 휴가를 가서 제가 그 일을 떠맡았어요.
T4-1631.x: My coworker went on vacation, so I got stuck with the work.
T4-1631.e: Built on 맡다 'to take charge'; suggests a job pushed onto you.

T4-1632.m: to recall, to think of, to bring to mind
T4-1632.ex: 그 사진을 보면 항상 고향을 떠올려요.
T4-1632.x: Whenever I see that photo, I think of my hometown.
T4-1632.e: 뜨다 'to float' + 올리다 'to raise': floating a memory up to mind.
T4-1632.t: 떠오르다 = an idea pops up by itself; 떠올리다 = you call it up.

T4-1633.m: to drill, to pierce, to bore through; to break through; to unclog
T4-1633.x: I went to an accessory shop to get my ears pierced.
T4-1633.t: Pronounced [뚤타]; the ㅎ is silent before a vowel: 뚫어요 [뚜러요].

T4-1634.forms: 뛰어들어요 · 뛰어들었어요 · 뛰어들 거예요 · 뛰어드세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1634.m: to jump into, to dive in; to plunge into (a field)
T4-1634.x: He jumped into the river to save the child.

T4-1635.m: to jump over, to leap over; to overcome, to surpass; to skip
T4-1635.x: The cat leapt lightly over the wall.

T4-1636.m: to face, to sit facing; to confront
T4-1636.ex: 두 사람이 테이블을 사이에 두고 마주했어요.
T4-1636.x: The two of them faced each other across the table.

T4-1637.m: to stand up to, to confront, to face; to oppose
T4-1637.x: They fought against injustice to the very end.
T4-1637.e: 맞- 'facing, against' + 서다 'to stand': standing face to face.
T4-1637.t: Pronounced [맏써다] — the ㅅ tenses after the ㄷ sound.

T4-1638.m: to hang (from), to dangle; to cling to; to beg; to be devoted to
T4-1638.ex: 아이가 엄마 팔에 매달려서 떼를 썼어요.
T4-1638.x: The child hung on Mom's arm and threw a tantrum.
T4-1638.e: Passive of 매달다 'to hang', from 매다 'to tie' + 달다 'to hang'.
T4-1638.t: Figurative: 일에 매달리다 means to be glued to one's work.

T4-1639.m: to tie (a knot); to form (a relationship), to sign (a contract); to bear (fruit)
T4-1639.ex: 두 회사는 작년에 새로운 계약을 맺었어요.
T4-1639.x: The two companies signed a new contract last year.
T4-1639.e: Probably related to 매듭 'knot': tying things together, literally or socially.
T4-1639.t: Pronounced [맫따]; common pairs are 관계를 맺다, 계약을 맺다 and 열매를 맺다.

T4-1640.m: to fill (a hole, gap); to make up for (a shortfall)
T4-1640.x: We hired a new employee to fill the empty position.
T4-1640.e: Causative of 메다 'to be clogged', as in 목이 메다 'to choke up'.

T4-1641.forms: 몰아요 · 몰았어요 · 몰 거예요 · 모세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1641.m: to drive (a vehicle); to herd, drive (animals); to corner, accuse (someone of)
T4-1641.x: My father drove a taxi for 30 years.
T4-1641.t: 범인으로 몰다 means to treat someone as the culprit, often unfairly.

T4-1642.m: to crowd, flock; to be driven (into a corner); to be accused (of)
T4-1642.x: Since it was the weekend, lots of people flocked to the park.
T4-1642.e: Passive of 몰다 'to drive, herd': people get herded into one place.

T4-1643.x: The soldiers finally drove the enemy out of the village.

T4-1644.m: to step back, retreat; to resign, step down
T4-1644.x: The company president stepped down because of health problems.
T4-1644.t: Use 물러나다 for stepping down from a post; 물러서다 is more for physically backing up or backing down.

T4-1645.m: to step back; to back down, give in
T4-1645.x: It's dangerous, so please take a step back.

T4-1646.m: to defeat, repel; to turn down, reject
T4-1646.ex: 우리 팀이 강한 상대를 물리치고 결승에 올랐어요.
T4-1646.x: Our team beat a strong opponent and made it to the finals.
T4-1646.e: Probably 물리다 'to push back' + 치다 'to strike'.

T4-1647.m: to slip, slide; to fail (an exam)
T4-1647.x: The road was icy, so I slipped in front of my house.
T4-1647.t: Colloquially, 시험에 미끄러지다 means to fail an exam.

T4-1648.m: to be pushed out, be pushed aside
T4-1648.ex: 그 선수는 부상 때문에 주전에서 밀려났어요.
T4-1648.x: That player lost his starting spot because of an injury.

T4-1649.m: to push ahead (with), force through; to push (something) against
T4-1649.x: There was a lot of opposition, but the mayor pushed the plan through.
T4-1649.e: 밀다 'to push' + 붙이다 'to stick': pushing until it sticks.
T4-1649.t: Pronounced [미러부치다]: ㅌ before 이 becomes ㅊ (palatalization).

T4-1650.m: to accept, take in; to adopt (an idea)
T4-1650.x: He gladly accepted his friend's advice.

T4-1651.m: to support, prop up; to hold (an umbrella) over; to wear underneath
T4-1651.ex: 무거운 상자를 두 손으로 받쳐서 옮겼어요.
T4-1651.x: I carried the heavy box, supporting it with both hands.
T4-1651.t: Sounds just like 바치다 'to offer, dedicate'; spelling tells them apart.

T4-1652.m: to soak in, permeate (smell, sweat); to become ingrained
T4-1652.x: I grilled meat, and the smell soaked into my clothes.
T4-1652.e: Homonym warning: another 배다 means 'to be pregnant with', as in 아이를 배다.
T4-1652.t: 몸에 배다 means a habit has become second nature.

T4-1653.m: to spread (fire, disease, rumors); to run, smudge (ink, paint)
T4-1653.x: The fire quickly spread to the building next door.

T4-1654.m: to take off (someone's clothes, shoes); to peel, strip
T4-1654.x: I peeled the apple thinly with a knife.
T4-1654.e: Causative of 벗다 'to take off': making something come off.

T4-1655.m: to get out of, escape; to break free from; to deviate from
T4-1655.x: On weekends, I get out of the city and go to the countryside.
T4-1655.e: 벗다 'to take off' + 나다 'to come out': shedding a place or situation.
T4-1655.t: Takes 을/를: 위기를 벗어나다, 스트레스에서 벗어나다 (with 에서 is also common).

T4-1656.m: to cut (with a blade); to rest one's head on (a pillow)
T4-1656.x: Yesterday I cut my finger on a knife while cooking.
T4-1656.e: Homonym: 베개 'pillow' comes from the other 베다, 'to rest your head on'.
T4-1656.t: Don't confuse with 배다 (to soak in); 베다 cuts with a blade.

T4-1657.ex: 동생 학비에 제 월급을 조금 보탰어요.
T4-1657.x: I chipped in some of my salary for my younger sibling's tuition.
T4-1657.t: 힘을 보태다 means 'to lend a hand' or 'to pitch in'.

T4-1658.m: to bump into, collide with; to run into (a problem)
T4-1658.x: The bicycle collided with a car that suddenly pulled out.
T4-1658.e: Passive-style form of 부딪다 'to strike against'.
T4-1658.t: Pronounced [부디치다]; 부딪치다 stresses active hitting, 부딪히다 being bumped or running into something.

T4-1659.m: to egg on, incite, stir up
T4-1659.ex: 친구들이 옆에서 두 사람의 싸움을 부추겼어요.
T4-1659.x: Our friends egged on the fight between the two of them.
T4-1659.e: Unrelated to 부추 'garlic chives', despite the look-alike spelling.

T4-1660.m: to grab hold of; to catch; to hold (someone) back
T4-1660.ex: 떠나려는 친구를 붙잡고 조금 더 이야기했어요.
T4-1660.x: I held back my friend who was about to leave and talked a little longer.

T4-1661.m: to step aside, move out of the way
T4-1661.x: Excuse me, could you please step aside?
T4-1661.t: A bare 비켜! sounds rude; say 좀 비켜 주세요 or just 잠깐만요.

T4-1662.forms: 비틀어요 · 비틀었어요 · 비틀 거예요 · 비트세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1662.x: I wrung out the wet towel.

T4-1663.m: to miss (the target), go wide; to turn out wrong (a guess)
T4-1663.x: The last shot went just wide of the goal.

T4-1664.m: to drop (into); to leave out, omit; to lose (something)
T4-1664.x: I accidentally dropped my phone in the toilet.
T4-1664.e: 빠지다 'to fall in; to be missing' + -뜨리다, which makes it forceful.
T4-1664.t: 빠트리다 is also standard and means the same thing.
rel: to fall in; to be missing

T4-1665.x: My younger sibling snatched my snack and ate it.
T4-1665.t: In speech it is often shortened to 뺏다: 뺏어요, 뺏었어요.

T4-1666.m: to be robbed of, have (something) taken away
T4-1666.x: I was completely captivated by that movie.
T4-1666.t: 마음을 빼앗기다 literally 'to have your heart taken' means to be captivated.

T4-1667.m: to stretch out (arms, legs); to extend, spread (roads, branches)
T4-1667.x: I got up in the morning and stretched my arms out.
T4-1667.t: Casually, 뻗다 also means to conk out from exhaustion or drinking.

T4-1668.ex: 그는 대회에서 멋진 노래 실력을 뽐냈어요.
T4-1668.x: He showed off his great singing skills at the contest.

T4-1669.m: to refrain from, avoid; to be careful about
T4-1669.ex: 공연 중에는 사진 촬영을 삼가 주세요.
T4-1669.x: Please refrain from taking photos during the performance.
T4-1669.t: 삼가하다 is a common mistake; the correct forms are 삼가세요 and 삼가 주세요.

T4-1670.m: to carve, engrave; to keep in mind
T4-1670.x: I took my teacher's words deeply to heart.
T4-1670.t: 마음에 새기다 means to take something to heart.

T4-1671.m: to rise, soar; to gush out; to well up (strength)
T4-1671.ex: 아침 해가 산 위로 천천히 솟았어요.
T4-1671.x: The morning sun slowly rose above the mountain.

T4-1672.forms: 솟아올라요 · 솟아올랐어요 · 솟아오를 거예요 · 솟아오른 (+noun) (르 irregular)
T4-1672.m: to soar up, shoot up, spring up
T4-1672.ex: 축제 마지막 날 불꽃이 밤하늘로 높이 솟아올랐어요.
T4-1672.x: On the last day of the festival, fireworks shot high into the night sky.

T4-1673.m: to lean, tilt (to one side); to be drawn, be focused (attention)
T4-1673.x: Everyone's eyes were drawn to him.
T4-1673.t: Common with attention: 관심이 쏠리다, 시선이 쏠리다.

T4-1674.m: to fall down, collapse; to go under (a business)
T4-1674.ex: 어젯밤 강한 바람에 큰 나무가 쓰러졌어요.
T4-1674.x: A big tree fell over in the strong wind last night.
T4-1674.t: For people, 쓰러지다 often means collapsing from illness or exhaustion, not just tripping (넘어지다).

T4-1675.ex: 어린아이가 집 안에서 뛰다가 꽃병을 쓰러뜨렸어요.
T4-1675.x: The little kid was running around the house and knocked over the vase.
T4-1675.e: -뜨리다 makes a verb forceful or causative: 깨뜨리다, 넘어뜨리다.

T4-1676.forms: 아물어요 · 아물었어요 · 아물 거예요 · 아문 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T4-1676.ex: 다친 상처가 이제 거의 다 아물었어요.
T4-1676.x: My wound has almost completely healed now.

T4-1677.m: to go ahead, lead; to precede; to be ahead
T4-1677.x: In the second half, our team is ahead 2 to 1.
T4-1677.t: 앞서 as an adverb means 'earlier, previously': 앞서 말씀드린 것처럼.

T4-1678.m: to take the lead, lead the way; to spearhead
T4-1678.x: She led the way in the environmental protection movement.

T4-1679.m: to get tangled; to be entangled, be involved (in)
T4-1679.ex: 이어폰 줄이 가방 안에서 엉망으로 얽혔어요.
T4-1679.x: My earphone cord got all tangled up in my bag.
T4-1679.e: Passive of 얽다 'to bind, tie together'.

T4-1680.m: to lie face down; to bow down
T4-1680.x: The child is lying on his stomach on the bed, reading a book.
T4-1680.e: Related to 엎다 'to turn upside down': your front faces the floor.

T4-1681.forms: 엎질러요 · 엎질렀어요 · 엎지를 거예요 · 엎지르세요 (르 irregular)
T4-1681.x: I accidentally spilled coffee on my laptop.
T4-1681.t: 엎질러진 물 'spilled water' is the Korean way to say 'what's done is done'.

T4-1682.m: to come and go; to be exchanged (words, ideas)
T4-1682.x: Various opinions were exchanged at today's meeting.

T4-1683.ex: 그 사고는 우리에게 안전의 중요성을 일깨워 주었어요.
T4-1683.x: That accident made us realize the importance of safety.
T4-1683.e: Built on 깨우다 'to wake someone up': waking up someone's awareness.

T4-1684.forms: 저질러요 · 저질렀어요 · 저지를 거예요 · 저지르세요 (르 irregular)
T4-1684.m: to commit (a crime, mistake), do (something bad)
T4-1684.x: I'm really sorry for making such a big mistake.
T4-1684.t: Used only for bad things: 실수를 저지르다, 범죄를 저지르다, 일을 저지르다.

T4-1685.forms: 접어들어요 · 접어들었어요 · 접어들 거예요 · 접어드세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1685.m: to enter (a period, stage); to turn into (a road)
T4-1685.x: As it got colder, we entered the heart of winter.

T4-1686.forms: 졸라요 · 졸랐어요 · 조를 거예요 · 조르세요 (르 irregular)
T4-1686.m: to pester, beg, nag (for); to tighten, squeeze
T4-1686.ex: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 계속 졸랐어요.
T4-1686.x: The child kept begging me to buy him a toy.
T4-1686.t: Often used with -아/어 달라고 조르다: 'to beg someone to do something'.

T4-1687.ex: 첫인상이 면접 결과를 좌우할 수 있어요.
T4-1687.x: A first impression can decide the outcome of an interview.
T4-1687.e: Literally 'left and right': steering something either way.

T4-1688.m: to slump down, plop down; to give up; to cave in
T4-1688.ex: 나쁜 소식을 듣고 그녀는 바닥에 주저앉았어요.
T4-1688.x: Hearing the bad news, she sank to the floor.
T4-1688.e: Ends in 앉다 'to sit': sitting down because your legs give way.

T4-1689.m: to carry on one's back; to shoulder (a burden, responsibility)
T4-1689.x: He shouldered his family's livelihood all by himself.
T4-1689.e: Related to 지다 'to carry on one's back'.

T4-1690.m: to be kicked out, be thrown out, be expelled
T4-1690.x: I couldn't pay rent, so I got kicked out of my place.

T4-1691.m: to chase after, run after, follow
T4-1691.x: The police chased the fleeing thief all the way.
T4-1691.t: 쫓다 is physical chasing; 좇다 is for pursuing goals, like 꿈을 좇다.

T4-1692.forms: 찔러요 · 찔렀어요 · 찌를 거예요 · 찌르세요 (르 irregular)
T4-1692.m: to stab, prick, poke; to sting (a smell)
T4-1692.x: My friend poked me in the side with a finger.
T4-1692.t: 양심에 찔리다 means 'to feel a pang of conscience'.

T4-1693.m: to frown, grimace; to be overcast (sky)
T4-1693.ex: 그는 이상한 냄새 때문에 얼굴을 찌푸렸어요.
T4-1693.x: He frowned because of the strange smell.

T4-1694.m: to set (a table), prepare (a meal); to open (a business); to come to (one's senses)
T4-1694.x: My mom made us a delicious dinner.
T4-1694.t: 정신 차려! means 'Pull yourself together!' or 'Wake up!'.

T4-1695.m: to sag, droop; to fall behind; to feel down
T4-1695.x: As I got older, my eyelids drooped a little.
T4-1695.e: Homonym warning: the noun 처지 'situation, circumstances' is a different word.

T4-1696.m: to look at, stare at; to look up at
T4-1696.x: People stared at me as if I were strange.
T4-1696.t: Pronounced [처다보다]; it often suggests staring, which can feel rude.

T4-1697.m: to lean (to one side), be biased, be one-sided
T4-1697.ex: 그 기사는 한쪽 의견에 너무 치우쳐 있어요.
T4-1697.x: That article leans too heavily toward one side.

T4-1698.x: I opened up honestly to an old friend about my worries.
T4-1698.e: 털다 'to shake out' + 놓다 'to put down': emptying out your heart.

T4-1699.forms: 털어요 · 털었어요 · 털 거예요 · 터세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1699.m: to shake off, dust off; to rob (slang)
T4-1699.ex: 집에 들어가기 전에 신발의 눈을 털었어요.
T4-1699.x: I shook the snow off my shoes before going inside.
T4-1699.t: Slang: 가게를 털다 means to rob a store.

T4-1700.m: to jump out, pop out; to stick out
T4-1700.ex: 골목에서 고양이 한 마리가 갑자기 튀어나왔어요.
T4-1700.x: A cat suddenly jumped out of the alley.
T4-1700.e: 튀다 'to bounce, spring' + 나오다 'to come out'.

T4-1701.x: Who spread such a strange rumor?
T4-1701.e: 퍼지다 'to spread' + -뜨리다, which makes it active.

T4-1702.m: to unfold, open (a book), spread out; to carry out, unfold (an event)
T4-1702.x: Okay, everyone, open your textbooks to page 30.
T4-1702.t: 꿈을 펼치다 means to make your dreams come true.

T4-1703.m: to hold in one's arms, embrace; to harbor (a feeling, dream, doubt)
T4-1703.ex: 그는 어릴 때부터 가수의 꿈을 품었어요.
T4-1703.x: He has dreamed of being a singer since he was young.
T4-1703.e: From 품 'bosom, arms': holding something close to your chest.

T4-1704.m: to come undone; to be solved; to ease up (tiredness, weather, anger)
T4-1704.x: Taking a warm bath relieved my fatigue.
T4-1704.t: Very versatile: 날씨가 풀리다 (weather warms), 화가 풀리다 (anger fades), 일이 잘 풀리다 (things go well).

T4-1705.forms: 허물어요 · 허물었어요 · 허물 거예요 · 허무세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1705.m: to tear down, demolish; to break down (barriers)
T4-1705.x: They tore down the old building and made a park.
T4-1705.e: Homonym warning: the noun 허물 means 'fault' or 'shed skin'.

T4-1706.forms: 헐어요 · 헐었어요 · 헐 거예요 · 허세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1706.m: to demolish, pull down; to dip into (savings); to wear out; to get sores (skin)
T4-1706.x: Something urgent came up, so I broke into my savings.
T4-1706.t: 입안이 헐다 means to get mouth sores.

T4-1707.m: to count; to understand, consider (someone's feelings)
T4-1707.ex: 이제야 부모님의 마음을 헤아릴 수 있어요.
T4-1707.x: Only now can I understand how my parents feel.

T4-1708.x: I quickly skimmed the materials before the meeting.
T4-1708.e: 훑다 'to strip, run along' + 보다 'to look'.

T4-1709.forms: 휘둘러요 · 휘둘렀어요 · 휘두를 거예요 · 휘두르세요 (르 irregular)
T4-1709.m: to swing, wield; to push (people) around
T4-1709.x: He got angry and swung his fists.
T4-1709.t: The passive 휘둘리다 means 'to be swayed or pushed around' by someone.

T4-1710.forms: 휩쓸어요 · 휩쓸었어요 · 휩쓸 거예요 · 휩쓰세요 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1710.m: to sweep away; to sweep (awards, a region)
T4-1710.ex: 그 영화가 올해 큰 상을 모두 휩쓸었어요.
T4-1710.x: That movie swept all the major awards this year.
T4-1710.e: Built on 쓸다 'to sweep (with a broom)'.

T4-1711.m: to be swept away; to get caught up in (a crowd, mood)
T4-1711.x: Many houses were swept away by the flood.
T4-1711.t: 분위기에 휩쓸리다 means to get carried away by the mood.

T4-1712.m: to be scattered, be messed up; to lose focus
T4-1712.ex: 밖에 나가자마자 바람 때문에 머리가 흐트러졌어요.
T4-1712.x: As soon as I went outside, the wind messed up my hair.
T4-1712.t: Also figurative: 자세가 흐트러지다 (posture slips), 마음이 흐트러지다 (mind wanders).

T4-1713.x: The building shook hard because of the earthquake.

T4-1714.m: to flow (along); to pass (time); to go, turn out (a situation)
T4-1714.x: My four years of college went by really fast.

T4-1715.x: When class ended, the students scattered in all directions.

T4-1716.ex: 이 길은 너무 가팔라서 올라가기 힘들어요.
T4-1716.x: This road is so steep that it's hard to climb.
T4-1716.t: Also used for sharp rises: 가파른 상승 means 'a steep rise' in prices or numbers.

T4-1717.e: Literally 'sincere and urgent' — a wish you feel deep inside.
T4-1717.t: Very common as the adverb 간절히: 간절히 바라다, 간절히 원하다.

T4-1718.ex: 이 앱을 쓰면 결제가 아주 간편해요.
T4-1718.x: Paying is really easy with this app.

T4-1719.x: This failure was a valuable experience for me.
T4-1719.e: Built from 값 'price, value' + 지다 'to have' — something full of worth.
T4-1719.t: Pronounced [갑찌다]; usually for experiences or lessons, not prices — use 비싸다 for 'expensive'.

T4-1720.x: I saw a huge whale in the ocean.

T4-1721.ex: 거창한 계획보다 작은 실천이 더 중요해요.
T4-1721.x: Small actions matter more than grand plans.
T4-1721.e: Often slightly critical: big-sounding but maybe more than needed.
T4-1721.t: Often used modestly: 거창한 건 아니고… means 'It's nothing fancy, but…'.

T4-1722.x: He received treatment befitting his skills.
T4-1722.e: Pattern: N에 걸맞다 — 'matching N, fitting for N'.
T4-1722.t: It's an adjective, so the modifier is 걸맞은, not 걸맞는 — a very common mistake even among natives.

T4-1723.ex: 하루 종일 고된 일을 해서 너무 피곤해요.
T4-1723.x: I'm so tired from doing hard work all day.
T4-1723.e: Typically describes physical labor or a rough life: 고된 일, 고된 하루.

T4-1724.ex: 올해는 비가 고르게 와서 농사가 잘됐어요.
T4-1724.x: The rain fell evenly this year, so the harvest went well.
T4-1724.e: Homonym warning: 고르다 also means 'to choose'. Context tells which.
T4-1724.t: Most often seen as the adverb 고르게 (evenly), e.g. 고르게 섞다, 고르게 바르다.

T4-1725.ex: 한복에는 한국의 고유한 아름다움이 담겨 있어요.
T4-1725.x: Hanbok carries a beauty unique to Korea.
T4-1725.e: Literally 'firmly possessed' — something that belongs to it by nature.

T4-1726.ex: 이번 태풍으로 광범위한 지역이 피해를 입었습니다.
T4-1726.x: A wide area was damaged by this typhoon.

T4-1727.x: An extreme drought continued this summer.
T4-1727.t: Pronounced [극씸하다]; mostly for bad things like 극심한 고통, 극심한 교통 체증.

T4-1728.x: We had dinner at a fancy restaurant on our anniversary.
T4-1728.e: Literally 'close to resembling' — now mostly means 'impressively nice'.
T4-1728.t: In everyday speech it means stylish or fancy; 'approximate' (근삿값) is a math term.

T4-1729.e: Literally 'urgent and violent' — change that comes fast and hard.

T4-1730.ex: 이 식당 김치찌개는 맛이 정말 기막혀요.
T4-1730.x: The kimchi stew at this restaurant tastes amazing.
T4-1730.t: Works both ways: 기막힌 맛 (amazing taste) vs. 기가 막혀서 말이 안 나와요 (I'm speechless).

T4-1731.x: My friend came up with a really clever idea.
T4-1731.e: Literally 'strangely outstanding' — standing out by being unusual.

T4-1732.ex: 방이 깔끔하게 정리되어 있어서 기분이 좋아요.
T4-1732.x: It feels good because the room is neatly organized.
T4-1732.t: Also praises food: 국물 맛이 깔끔해요 means the broth tastes clean, not greasy.

T4-1733.x: I heard news of a terrible accident last night.
T4-1733.t: The adverb 끔찍이 can be positive: 아이를 끔찍이 아끼다 means 'to adore one's child'.

T4-1734.m: exceptional, special, out of the ordinary
T4-1734.ex: 그 선수는 어릴 때부터 실력이 남달랐어요.
T4-1734.x: That athlete's skills were exceptional from a young age.
T4-1734.e: Built from 남 'other people' + 다르다 'different' — different from everyone else.
T4-1734.t: A compliment, often in 남다른 재능 (exceptional talent) or 감회가 남다르다 (it feels special).

T4-1735.x: We have plenty of time, so get ready slowly.

T4-1736.x: He openly showed his dissatisfaction to me.

T4-1737.ex: 한국은 짧은 시간에 눈부신 발전을 이루었습니다.
T4-1737.x: Korea achieved remarkable development in a short time.
T4-1737.e: Built from 눈 'eye' + 부시다 'to be dazzled' — so bright it hurts your eyes.

T4-1738.x: My shoelaces were loose, so I tied them again.

T4-1740.x: He cried for help in an urgent voice.
T4-1740.t: Pronounced [다그파다]; often describes voices or situations: 다급한 목소리, 상황이 다급하다.

T4-1741.ex: 이 게임은 규칙이 단순해서 누구나 할 수 있어요.
T4-1741.x: This game has simple rules, so anyone can play.

T4-1742.ex: 갑자기 생긴 일이 별로 달갑지 않았어요.
T4-1742.x: The sudden task wasn't very welcome.
T4-1742.e: Probably linked to 달다 'sweet' — something sweet to accept.
T4-1742.t: Almost always negative: 달갑지 않다 or 달갑지 않은 손님 (an unwelcome guest).

T4-1743.x: The two teams played an evenly matched game.

T4-1744.x: I hurt my leg, so recovery is a bit slow.
T4-1744.t: More literary than 느리다; often for progress or time: 시간이 더디게 가다.

T4-1745.x: That company developed its own technology.
T4-1745.e: Literally 'alone by oneself' — doing it on your own.
T4-1745.t: Pronounced [독짜적]; common in news: 독자적으로 판단하다 (to judge independently).

T4-1746.x: The two products are identical in quality.

T4-1747.x: I realized my mistake late and apologized to my friend.
T4-1747.e: Built from 뒤 'behind' + 늦다 'late' — late, after the right moment.
T4-1747.t: Mostly used as 뒤늦게 (belatedly): 뒤늦게 알다, 뒤늦게 깨닫다.

T4-1748.x: Looking at the vast sea makes me feel at ease.
T4-1748.e: 드- is an intensifying prefix: 넓다 'wide' → 드넓다 'very wide'.

T4-1749.m: honorable, proud, having nothing to be ashamed of
T4-1749.x: I did nothing wrong, so I have nothing to be ashamed of.
T4-1749.t: Pronounced [떧떠타다]; the feeling of a clear conscience — 떳떳하게 말하다.

T4-1750.m: easy, easy to handle; a pushover
T4-1750.x: This exam isn't as easy as I thought.
T4-1750.e: Homonym warning: 자신감이 만만하다 'full of confidence' is a different word.
T4-1750.t: Very common in the negative: 만만치 않다 / 만만하지 않다 means 'tough, not to be taken lightly'.

T4-1751.x: The question is too vague to answer.

T4-1752.m: unrelated, irrelevant, having nothing to do with
T4-1752.x: This issue has nothing to do with age.

T4-1753.ex: 면접에는 무난한 색의 옷을 입는 게 좋아요.
T4-1753.x: It's best to wear safe-colored clothes to an interview.
T4-1753.t: It means 'fine, no problems' — neither great nor bad: 무난하게 합격하다 (to pass comfortably).

T4-1754.x: There was an accident, but the whole family is safe.

T4-1755.x: The bag is heavier than I expected.
T4-1755.e: Related to 무겁다 'heavy', with a solid, satisfying feel.
T4-1755.t: Pronounced [묵찌카다]; also figurative: 묵직한 목소리 (a deep voice), 묵직한 메시지.

T4-1756.x: There's a subtle difference between the two colors.

T4-1757.x: The effect of this policy is still minimal.

T4-1758.x: I'm still inexperienced at driving, so I'm being careful.

T4-1759.x: Health is closely related to eating habits.
T4-1759.t: Pronounced [밀쩌파다]; almost always 밀접한 관계 or 밀접하게 연결되다.

T4-1760.x: That student is polite and upright.
T4-1760.t: Pronounced [반드타다]; describes both things (반듯한 글씨) and well-behaved people.

T4-1761.ex: 서류를 다시 내야 해서 좀 번거로워요.
T4-1761.x: It's a bit of a hassle because I have to submit the documents again.
T4-1761.t: Polite apology phrase: 번거롭게 해 드려서 죄송합니다 'Sorry for the trouble.'

T4-1762.x: It's just a humble gift, but please accept it.
T4-1762.e: Built from 보다 'to see' + 것 + 없다 — 'nothing worth looking at'.
T4-1762.t: Often used modestly about your own things; pronounced [보잘꺼덥따].

T4-1763.x: I protested the company's unfair treatment.

T4-1764.x: That kind of joke is inappropriate in a meeting.

T4-1765.x: Information on the internet is often inaccurate.

T4-1766.x: Before the holidays, the market is bustling with people.

T4-1767.x: The room is so cramped it's hard to fit a bed.
T4-1767.e: Contains 좁다 'narrow' — so tight it's uncomfortable.

T4-1768.ex: 전쟁은 많은 사람에게 비참한 결과를 가져왔습니다.
T4-1768.x: The war brought miserable consequences to many people.

T4-1769.x: We often fight over trivial things.
T4-1769.e: Literally 'a little, small' — not worth worrying about.
T4-1769.t: Classic collocations: 사소한 실수 (a minor mistake), 사소한 일 (small stuff).

T4-1770.ex: 봄에는 산뜻한 색의 옷을 입고 싶어요.
T4-1770.x: In spring I want to wear fresh, bright-colored clothes.
T4-1770.t: Pronounced [산뜨타다]; great for colors, styles, moods and a fresh start: 산뜻한 출발.

T4-1771.ex: 처음에는 한국 음식이 생소했지만 지금은 좋아해요.
T4-1771.x: Korean food was unfamiliar at first, but now I love it.
T4-1771.e: Literally 'raw and distant' — not yet familiar to you.
T4-1771.t: 생소하다 is about things or ideas; for people and places 낯설다 is more common.

T4-1772.x: The new TV has a very sharp picture.

T4-1773.x: It's too early to draw a conclusion.
T4-1773.e: Literally 'urgent nature' — a temperament that rushes.
T4-1773.t: Pronounced [성그파다]; common in 성급한 결정 (a rash decision), 성급하게 판단하다.

T4-1774.x: The doctor examined the test results in detail.

T4-1775.ex: 우리는 작은 집에서 소박하게 살고 있어요.
T4-1775.x: We live simply in a small house.
T4-1775.e: Literally 'plain and natural, like uncut wood'.

T4-1776.ex: 요즘은 스마트폰으로 손쉽게 은행 일을 볼 수 있어요.
T4-1776.x: These days you can easily do your banking on a smartphone.
T4-1776.e: Built from 손 'hand' + 쉽다 'easy' — easy enough to do by hand.
T4-1776.t: Mostly used as the adverb 손쉽게 (easily, with little effort).

T4-1777.x: My friend helped, so the move went smoothly.
T4-1777.t: Often in comparisons: 생각보다 수월했다 (easier than expected), 훨씬 수월해지다.

T4-1778.x: Environmental problems must be solved urgently.
T4-1778.t: Pronounced [시그파다]; don't confuse with 시급 'hourly wage' — 최저 시급.

T4-1779.x: This bag looks nice and is practical too.

T4-1780.x: Our house is small, but it's cozy and pretty.
T4-1780.e: Literally 'elegant and plain' — small in a charming way.

T4-1781.x: This trip was short but full of good things.
T4-1781.e: Built from 알 'kernel, grain' + 차다 'to be full' — packed with substance.
T4-1781.t: Common with time and content: 알찬 하루, 알찬 정보, 방학을 알차게 보내다.

T4-1782.ex: 약속 시간이 애매해서 점심을 먹기가 어려워요.
T4-1782.x: The meeting time is awkward, so it's hard to fit in lunch.
T4-1782.e: Literally 'dim and dark' — not clear either way.
T4-1782.t: Everyday speech: 좀 애매해요 means 'it's hard to say' or 'it's neither here nor there'.

T4-1783.ex: 그 아이는 어리지만 일을 야무지게 해요.
T4-1783.x: That kid is young but does things very capably.
T4-1783.t: A warm compliment, often for children or young people who are smart and handle things well.

T4-1784.ex: 동생이 내 과자를 다 먹어서 너무 얄미워요.
T4-1784.x: My little brother ate all my snacks, so he's so annoying.
T4-1784.t: Lighter than 밉다; used for cheeky, sly behavior, often half-jokingly.

T4-1785.x: The atmosphere at the funeral hall was solemn.

T4-1786.x: The content of this report is a bit sloppy.

T4-1787.x: On weekends I spend relaxing time at a cafe.
T4-1787.e: From 여유 'surplus room' + -롭다 'having' — having time or space to spare.

T4-1788.x: That factory has poor working conditions.
T4-1788.t: Pronounced [여라카다]; almost always about conditions: 열악한 환경, 열악한 조건.

T4-1789.e: Opposite of 짙다 'dark, thick' — think light colors, thin fog, faint scents.
T4-1789.t: Pronounced [엳따]; don't mix it up with 얕다 (shallow water) — 옅다 is mostly for color and haze.

T4-1790.ex: 오래된 그릇이 깨지지 않고 온전하게 남아 있어요.
T4-1790.x: The old bowl remains intact without breaking.
T4-1790.e: Literally 'calm and whole' — nothing missing, nothing broken.
T4-1790.t: Also figurative: 온전히 나만의 시간 (time completely my own).

T4-1791.ex: 그 학생은 성적이 우수해서 장학금을 받았어요.
T4-1791.x: That student got a scholarship for excellent grades.

T4-1792.x: Traffic became smooth after the road work ended.
T4-1792.e: Literally 'round and slippery' — things roll along without friction.

T4-1793.x: That company's business situation is precarious.
T4-1793.e: Literally 'dangerous and perilous' plus -롭다 'having the quality'.

T4-1794.ex: 그 후보가 이번 선거에서 가장 유력합니다.
T4-1794.x: That candidate is the most likely to win this election.
T4-1794.t: Pronounced [유려카다]; common in news: 유력한 후보 (frontrunner), 유력 인사 (influential figure).

T4-1795.ex: 그는 우리 팀에서 유일하게 중국어를 할 수 있어요.
T4-1795.x: He's the only one on our team who can speak Chinese.
T4-1795.t: Very often used as the adverb 유일하게 ('the only one who...') or the modifier 유일한 ('the only').

T4-1796.x: This café's interior is really unusual.
T4-1796.e: Literally 'of a different color'; -적 = '-ic/-al': 이색적, 획기적, 과학적.
T4-1796.t: Common in ads and travel writing: 이색 체험 'unusual experience', 이색 카페 'quirky café'.

T4-1797.ex: 매일 일정한 시간에 자는 것이 건강에 좋아요.
T4-1797.x: Going to bed at a regular time every day is good for your health.
T4-1797.t: Pronounced [일쩡하다]. Don't mix it up with the noun 일정 'schedule', which is written the same.

T4-1798.x: There's no wind today, so the sea is calm.
T4-1798.e: The doubled syllable paints a soft, steady stillness, like 촘촘하다 or 팽팽하다.

T4-1799.ex: 이 일은 경험이 많은 사람에게 적합해요.
T4-1799.x: This job is suitable for someone with lots of experience.
T4-1799.t: Pattern: N에 적합하다 / N에게 적합하다 'suitable for N'. Pronounced [저카파다].

T4-1800.ex: 지금 우리에게는 여러분의 도움이 정말 절실해요.
T4-1800.x: Right now we desperately need your help.
T4-1800.e: Literally 'keenly real'—a need you feel in your bones.
T4-1800.t: Often as an adverb: 절실히 느끼다 'to feel keenly', 절실히 필요하다 'to be badly needed'.

T4-1801.x: This watch was made very intricately.

T4-1802.ex: 일한 만큼 정당한 대가를 받아야 해요.
T4-1802.x: You should get fair pay for the work you do.
T4-1802.t: Don't confuse with 정당 'political party' (政黨), a different word with the same sound.

T4-1803.ex: 어제부터 지독한 감기에 걸려서 너무 힘들어요.
T4-1803.x: I've had a terrible cold since yesterday, and it's really rough.
T4-1803.t: Can also describe a person who is relentlessly hardworking or stingy: 지독하게 공부하다 'to study like crazy'.

T4-1804.x: The fog was so thick this morning that it was hard to drive.
T4-1804.e: Close in meaning to 진하다, but 짙다 is more native and often used for fog, shadows and makeup.

T4-1805.ex: 그 학생은 착실해서 숙제를 한 번도 빠뜨리지 않아요.
T4-1805.x: That student is so diligent that she has never missed a homework assignment.
T4-1805.e: Literally 'firmly attached to what's real'—solid and dependable.
T4-1805.t: Not related to native 착하다 'kind'; 착실하다 means steady and dependable, not nice.

T4-1806.x: That ad's idea is really fresh.

T4-1807.ex: 친구들 앞에서 제 모습이 너무 초라하게 느껴졌어요.
T4-1807.x: I felt really shabby in front of my friends.

T4-1808.ex: 이 그물은 아주 촘촘해서 작은 물고기도 잡을 수 있어요.
T4-1808.x: This net is so fine that it can catch even small fish.
T4-1808.e: The doubled syllable suggests many small things packed closely together.

T4-1809.x: Competition for jobs is very fierce these days.
T4-1809.e: Literally 'blazing and fierce', like a raging fire.
T4-1809.t: Classic collocation: 경쟁이 치열하다 'competition is fierce'; also 치열한 전투 'fierce battle'.

T4-1810.ex: 우리 가족은 서로 아주 친밀한 관계예요.
T4-1810.x: Our family members have a very close relationship with each other.

T4-1811.ex: 그 의견은 충분히 타당한 것 같아요.
T4-1811.x: I think that opinion is perfectly reasonable.

T4-1812.x: This medicine works extremely well for colds.
T4-1812.t: Pronounced [타궐하다]. Often with 능력, 선택, 효과: 탁월한 선택 'an excellent choice'.

T4-1813.ex: 그 회사는 기술력이 탄탄해서 믿을 수 있어요.
T4-1813.x: That company has solid technology, so you can trust it.
T4-1813.e: Doubled syllable for firmness; used for muscles, stories and businesses alike.

T4-1814.ex: 이 컵은 유리처럼 투명하고 아주 가벼워요.
T4-1814.x: This cup is transparent like glass and very light.
T4-1814.t: Also used figuratively, as in English: 투명한 경영 'transparent management'.

T4-1815.x: The game between the two teams was neck and neck to the end.
T4-1815.e: Doubled syllable for something stretched tight; also used for smooth, firm skin.

T4-1816.ex: 시골에서 가족과 함께 평온한 주말을 보냈어요.
T4-1816.x: I spent a peaceful weekend with my family in the countryside.
T4-1816.e: Literally 'level and steady'—nothing disturbs the calm.

T4-1817.x: This restaurant serves generous side dishes.

T4-1818.ex: 어릴 때 집이 풍족하지 않았지만 행복했어요.
T4-1818.x: We weren't well-off when I was a kid, but I was happy.
T4-1818.t: Pronounced [풍조카다]. Often about money and living conditions; 풍부하다 suits resources and knowledge.

T4-1819.ex: 주말에는 사람이 적은 한적한 곳에 가고 싶어요.
T4-1819.x: On weekends I want to go somewhere quiet with few people.

T4-1820.m: to be limited, to be restricted
T4-1820.ex: 이 행사는 참가 인원이 백 명으로 한정돼요.
T4-1820.x: This event is limited to one hundred participants.
T4-1820.t: Pattern: N(으)로 한정되다 'to be limited to N'; 한정된 시간 'limited time'.

T4-1821.x: Security was so lax that personal information was leaked.
T4-1821.t: Often about systems and plans: 관리가 허술하다 'management is lax'. Compare 허름하다 'run-down'.

T4-1822.x: It was a run-down little restaurant, but the food was really delicious.

T4-1823.ex: 이 산은 길이 험해서 조심해야 해요.
T4-1823.x: The trails on this mountain are rough, so you need to be careful.
T4-1823.t: Also figurative: 험한 세상 'a harsh world', 말을 험하게 하다 'to talk nasty'.

T4-1824.ex: 저는 부모님 덕분에 화목한 가정에서 자랐어요.
T4-1824.x: Thanks to my parents, I grew up in a happy, close-knit family.
T4-1824.t: Pronounced [화모카다]. Almost always about families: 화목한 가정 'a harmonious family'.

T4-1825.x: He's firmly determined to become a doctor.

T4-1826.x: The morning market is bustling with people.

T4-1827.ex: 스마트폰은 우리 생활에 획기적인 변화를 가져왔어요.
T4-1827.x: Smartphones brought groundbreaking changes to our lives.
T4-1827.e: Literally 'dividing the periods'—so big it starts a new era.

T4-1828.x: Hearing that story warmed my heart.
T4-1828.e: Sino-Korean: a doubled syllable meaning 'warm, fragrant', for gentle, lingering warmth; now also slang for 'good-looking' (훈남).

T4-1829.ex: 안경을 안 써서 글씨가 흐릿하게 보여요.
T4-1829.x: I'm not wearing my glasses, so the letters look blurry.
T4-1829.e: Related to 흐리다 'cloudy, unclear'; -릿하다 adds a 'somewhat' feel.

T4-1830.ex: 이 새는 아주 희귀해서 보기 힘들어요.
T4-1830.x: This bird is very rare, so it's hard to spot.
T4-1830.t: Pronounced [히귀하다] — the vowel ㅢ after a consonant sounds like ㅣ.

T4-1831.x: My childhood memories are faint now.

T4-1832.ex: 할머니는 무거운 짐을 들고 힘겹게 계단을 올라가셨어요.
T4-1832.x: Grandma struggled up the stairs carrying a heavy bag.
T4-1832.e: Built from 힘 'strength' + 겹다 'too much to handle': more than your strength can bear.
T4-1832.t: Often as an adverb: 힘겹게 'with great effort', 힘겹게 버티다 'to barely hang on'.

T4-1833.ex: 새해에는 힘차게 새로운 일을 시작하고 싶어요.
T4-1833.x: In the new year, I want to start something new with energy.
T4-1833.e: Built from 힘 'strength' + 차다 'to be full': full of strength.

T4-1834.m: killing two birds with one stone
T4-1834.ex: 운동하면서 돈도 벌 수 있으니까 일석이조예요.
T4-1834.x: I can exercise and earn money too, so it's two birds with one stone.
T4-1834.e: Literally 'one stone, two birds'—exactly like the English idiom.
T4-1834.t: The native proverb 꿩 먹고 알 먹기 means the same thing and sounds more casual.
rel: eat the pheasant and its eggs

T4-1835.m: resolutions that don't last; giving up after three days
T4-1835.ex: 새해 다이어트 계획이 또 작심삼일로 끝났어요.
T4-1835.x: My New Year's diet plan fizzled out after a few days again.
T4-1835.e: Literally 'a made-up mind lasts three days'.
T4-1835.t: Usual pattern: 작심삼일로 끝나다 'to end as a three-day resolution'.

T4-1836.m: late bloomer; great talents mature late
T4-1836.ex: 그 배우는 마흔이 넘어서 유명해진 대기만성형이에요.
T4-1836.x: That actor is a late bloomer who became famous after forty.
T4-1836.e: Literally 'a big vessel is completed late'.

T4-1837.ex: 질문을 했는데 그 사람은 계속 동문서답만 했어요.
T4-1837.x: I asked a question, but he kept giving answers that had nothing to do with it.
T4-1837.e: Literally 'asked about east, answered about west'.

T4-1838.forms: 십중팔구가 · 십중팔구를 (mostly used as an adverb)
T4-1838.m: most likely, nine times out of ten
T4-1838.x: If traffic is this bad, we'll almost certainly be late.
T4-1838.e: Literally 'eight or nine out of ten'.

T4-1839.m: running around in confusion, not knowing what to do
T4-1839.ex: 불이 나자 건물 안의 사람들이 우왕좌왕했어요.
T4-1839.x: When the fire broke out, the people in the building ran around in confusion.

T4-1840.m: unspoken understanding; reading each other's minds
T4-1840.ex: 우리는 말하지 않아도 이심전심으로 알 수 있어요.
T4-1840.x: We can understand each other without saying a word.

T4-1841.m: you reap what you sow; getting what you deserve
T4-1841.ex: 공부를 안 했으니 시험에 떨어진 건 자업자득이에요.
T4-1841.x: You didn't study, so failing the test is your own doing.
T4-1841.e: Literally 'your own deeds, your own gain'—karma comes back to you.
T4-1841.t: Sounds blunt and judgmental; be careful saying it directly to someone.

T4-1842.m: a match made in heaven, soulmates
T4-1842.ex: 두 사람은 정말 천생연분인 것 같아요.
T4-1842.x: Those two really seem like a match made in heaven.

T4-1843.m: news to me; hearing something for the first time
T4-1843.x: He got married? That's news to me.
T4-1843.e: Literally 'only now hearing it for the first time'.

T4-1844.ex: 처음에는 친구가 말한 그 소문을 반신반의했어요.
T4-1844.x: At first I was half doubtful about the rumor my friend told me.

T4-1845.m: better safe than sorry; preparation prevents trouble
T4-1845.ex: 유비무환이라고, 비가 올 수도 있으니까 우산을 챙겨 가세요.
T4-1845.x: Better safe than sorry—it might rain, so take an umbrella.
rel: closing the barn door too late

T4-1846.m: after hardship comes joy; no pain, no gain
T4-1846.ex: 고진감래라고, 열심히 하면 좋은 날이 올 거예요.
T4-1846.x: As they say, after the bitter comes the sweet; if you work hard, good days will come.
T4-1846.e: Literally 'when the bitter is used up, the sweet arrives'.
T4-1846.t: Pronounced [고진감내] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅁ.

T4-1847.m: to make matters worse; one misfortune after another
T4-1847.x: I got lost, and to make matters worse, it started to rain.
T4-1847.e: Literally 'adding frost on top of snow'.

T4-1848.ex: 많은 시행착오를 겪은 후에 드디어 성공했어요.
T4-1848.x: After a lot of trial and error, I finally succeeded.
T4-1848.e: Literally 'trying it out and making mistakes'.

T4-1849.m: putting yourself in someone else's shoes
T4-1849.x: Before you fight, try putting yourself in their shoes.
T4-1849.e: Literally 'swap places and think about it'.

T4-1850.m: ups and downs, twists and turns
T4-1850.x: After many twists and turns, we ended up getting married.
T4-1850.e: Pictures a road that winds, bends and breaks before reaching the end.

T4-1851.ex: 그때 회사를 그만둔 것이 오히려 전화위복이 됐어요.
T4-1851.x: Quitting the company back then actually turned out to be a blessing in disguise.

T4-1852.ex: 민수는 저의 죽마고우라서 서로 모르는 게 없어요.
T4-1852.x: Minsu is my childhood friend, so we know everything about each other.
T4-1852.e: Literally 'an old friend from riding bamboo horses' together as kids.
T4-1852.t: Pronounced [중마고우] — nasalization of ㄱ before ㅁ.

T4-1853.m: a jack of all trades, an all-rounder
T4-1853.ex: 그 친구는 노래, 운동, 공부까지 다 잘하는 팔방미인이에요.
T4-1853.x: That friend is an all-rounder who's good at singing, sports and even studying.
T4-1853.e: Literally 'a person beautiful from all eight directions'.
T4-1853.t: In Korean it's praise, unlike the Japanese use of the same phrase for a people-pleaser.

T4-1854.ex: 축제에는 각양각색의 옷을 입은 사람들이 있었어요.
T4-1854.x: At the festival, there were people wearing all kinds of outfits.
T4-1854.e: Literally 'each a different shape, each a different color'.

T4-1855.m: people of all ages and genders, everyone
T4-1855.ex: 이 영화는 남녀노소 누구나 즐길 수 있어요.
T4-1855.x: Anyone, young or old, can enjoy this movie.
T4-1855.t: Notice 녀, not 여, because it isn't word-initial; 노 keeps its word-initial form because 노소 'old and young' counts as its own word.

T4-1856.x: In the final, the two players were evenly matched in skill.

T4-1857.x: Even for the same item, prices vary widely from store to store.
T4-1857.e: Literally 'a thousand differences, ten thousand distinctions'.

T4-1858.m: things keep getting worse; out of the frying pan into the fire
T4-1858.x: I solved one problem, and things just keep getting harder.
T4-1858.e: Literally 'the further you go, the bigger the mountain'.
T4-1858.t: 산 넘어 산 'mountain after mountain' expresses the same frustration.

T4-1859.forms: 누워서 떡 먹기예요 / N은/는 누워서 떡 먹기
T4-1859.m: a piece of cake, very easy
T4-1859.ex: 이 정도 문제는 저한테 누워서 떡 먹기예요.
T4-1859.x: A problem like this is a piece of cake for me.
T4-1859.e: Literally 'eating rice cake lying down'—that's how easy it is.

T4-1860.forms: 식은 죽 먹기예요 / N은/는 식은 죽 먹기
T4-1860.m: a piece of cake, a breeze
T4-1860.ex: 한국 요리는 저한테 식은 죽 먹기예요.
T4-1860.x: Cooking Korean food is a piece of cake for me.
T4-1860.e: Literally 'eating porridge that has cooled'—no burning, no waiting.

T4-1861.m: pie in the sky; something you want but can't have
T4-1861.ex: 그 비싼 차는 저한테 그림의 떡이에요.
T4-1861.x: That expensive car is just a dream for me.
T4-1861.e: Literally 'a rice cake in a picture'—you can see it but can't eat it.
T4-1861.t: 의 here is usually pronounced [에]: [그리메 떡].

T4-1862.forms: 하늘의 별 따기예요 / N이/가 하늘의 별 따기
T4-1862.m: next to impossible, extremely hard to get
T4-1862.ex: 요즘 서울에서 집을 사는 건 하늘의 별 따기예요.
T4-1862.x: Buying a home in Seoul these days is next to impossible.
T4-1862.e: Literally 'picking a star from the sky'.

T4-1863.forms: 티끌 모아 태산이에요 / 티끌 모아 태산이라고
T4-1863.m: every little bit counts; many a little makes a mickle
T4-1863.ex: 티끌 모아 태산이라고 매일 조금씩 저금하고 있어요.
T4-1863.x: Every little bit adds up, so I'm saving a little every day.
T4-1863.e: Literally 'gather specks of dust and you get a great mountain'.

T4-1864.de: 발 없는 말이 천 리 간다
T4-1864.pr: 발 엄는 마리 철 리 간다
T4-1864.forms: 발 없는 말이 천 리 간다고 / 발 없는 말이 천 리 가요
T4-1864.m: word spreads fast; rumors travel far
T4-1864.ex: 발 없는 말이 천 리 간다고 하니까 말조심하세요.
T4-1864.x: They say words travel fast, so be careful what you say.
T4-1864.e: Pun: 말 means both 'word' and 'horse'—a footless 'horse' still travels a thousand li.
T4-1864.t: 없는 is pronounced [엄는], and 천 리 is [철리].
rel: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다

T4-1865.m: eat first, then sightsee; nothing's fun on an empty stomach
T4-1865.x: Nothing's fun on an empty stomach, so let's eat first.
T4-1865.e: Literally 'even Mount Geumgang is a view for after the meal'.

T4-1866.forms: 소 잃고 외양간 고치다 / 소 잃고 외양간 고치는 격이에요
