T4-1866.m: closing the barn door after the horse has bolted; acting too late
T4-1866.ex: 사고가 난 후에 안전 교육을 하는 건 소 잃고 외양간 고치는 거예요.
T4-1866.x: Doing safety training after an accident is like closing the barn door after the horse has bolted.
T4-1866.e: Literally 'lose the cow, then fix the barn'—almost the same as the English saying.

T4-1867.forms: 눈코 뜰 새 없어요 · 눈코 뜰 새 없었어요 · 눈코 뜰 새 없이 바쁘다
T4-1867.m: to be extremely busy, to have no time to breathe
T4-1867.ex: 이번 주는 일이 많아서 눈코 뜰 새 없이 바빴어요.
T4-1867.x: I had so much work this week that I was crazy busy.
T4-1867.e: Literally 'no time to even open your eyes and nose'.

T4-1868.forms: 가슴이 뜨끔해요 · 가슴이 뜨끔했어요 · 가슴이 뜨끔한 (+noun)
T4-1868.m: to feel a pang of guilt, to be stung (by a remark)
T4-1868.ex: 거짓말을 한 게 생각나서 가슴이 뜨끔했어요.
T4-1868.x: I remembered the lie I'd told and felt a pang of guilt.
T4-1868.e: 뜨끔하다 describes a sudden prick or sting, like a needle; here it's a sting of conscience.

T4-1869.forms: 가슴이 벅차요 · 가슴이 벅찼어요 · 가슴이 벅찬 (+noun)
T4-1869.m: to be overwhelmed with emotion, to have your heart swell
T4-1869.ex: 졸업식 날 가족을 보니까 가슴이 벅찼어요.
T4-1869.x: Seeing my family on graduation day, my heart swelled with emotion.
T4-1869.e: 벅차다 means 'too much to handle', so the heart is too full to contain the feeling.
T4-1869.t: Usually positive (joy, pride); 벅차다 alone can also mean a task is too much for you.

T4-1870.forms: 가슴을 졸여요 · 가슴을 졸였어요 · 가슴을 졸일 거예요 · 가슴을 졸인 (+noun)
T4-1870.m: to be on edge, to be anxious, to hold your breath
T4-1870.x: I was on pins and needles waiting for my test results.
T4-1870.e: 졸이다 also means 'to boil down'—as if the heart is simmering with worry.
T4-1870.t: Same meaning as 마음을 졸이다; don't confuse 졸이다 with 줄이다 'to reduce'.

T4-1871.forms: 간이 커요 · 간이 컸어요 · 간이 큰 (+noun) (ㅡ drops)
T4-1871.ex: 혼자 밤에 산에 가다니 정말 간이 크네요.
T4-1871.x: Going to the mountain alone at night? You've really got guts.
T4-1871.e: Literally 'to have a big liver'—Koreans locate courage in the liver, not the heart.
T4-1871.t: Can be praise or a scolding for recklessness: 간이 부었다 'you've gotten too bold'.

T4-1872.forms: 간이 콩알만 해져요 · 간이 콩알만 해졌어요 · 간이 콩알만 해질 거예요
T4-1872.m: to be scared stiff, to have your heart in your mouth
T4-1872.ex: 갑자기 큰 소리가 나서 간이 콩알만 해졌어요.
T4-1872.x: There was a sudden loud noise, and I nearly jumped out of my skin.
T4-1872.e: Literally 'your liver shrinks to the size of a bean'—courage vanishes.
T4-1872.t: A similar way to say you got a big fright: 간 떨어질 뻔했어요 'my liver nearly fell out'.

T4-1873.forms: 고개를 끄덕여요 · 고개를 끄덕였어요 · 고개를 끄덕이며 (while nodding)
T4-1873.m: to nod (one's head); to agree, to show approval
T4-1873.ex: 선생님의 설명을 듣고 학생들이 고개를 끄덕였어요.
T4-1873.x: After hearing the teacher's explanation, the students nodded.
T4-1873.e: 고개 = the head; 끄덕 imitates the up-and-down nodding motion.

T4-1874.m: to bow one's head; to apologize humbly, to admit defeat
T4-1874.ex: 그는 실수를 인정하고 사람들 앞에서 고개를 숙였어요.
T4-1874.x: He admitted his mistake and bowed his head in front of everyone.
T4-1874.e: 숙이다 = to lower or bend; bowing the head shows apology, respect or defeat.

T4-1875.forms: 귀를 기울여요 · 귀를 기울였어요 · N에 귀를 기울이다
T4-1875.m: to listen carefully, to lend an ear, to pay attention to
T4-1875.ex: 정부는 시민들의 목소리에 귀를 기울여야 합니다.
T4-1875.x: The government must listen to the voices of its citizens.
T4-1875.e: Literally 'to tilt one's ear' toward a sound.

T4-1876.forms: 귀가 따가워요 · 귀가 따가웠어요 · 귀가 따갑도록 (ㅂ irregular)
T4-1876.m: to be sick of hearing something; (of a sound) to be ear-piercing
T4-1876.ex: 엄마의 잔소리를 매일 들어서 귀가 따가워요.
T4-1876.x: I hear Mom's nagging every day, and I'm sick of it.
T4-1876.e: 따갑다 = stinging, prickly; your ears 'sting' from hearing too much.
T4-1876.t: Often used as 귀가 따갑도록 듣다, 'to hear something until your ears sting.'

T4-1877.forms: 귀에 못이 박히도록 들어요 · 귀에 못이 박히도록 들었어요
T4-1877.m: to hear something over and over, to be told a million times
T4-1877.ex: 공부하라는 말은 귀에 못이 박히도록 들었어요.
T4-1877.x: I've been told to study a million times.
T4-1877.e: This 못 is a callus, not a nail: hearing something constantly gives your ears calluses.
T4-1877.t: Almost always used as 귀에 못이 박히도록 (or 박히게) + 듣다/말하다.

T4-1878.forms: 기가 죽어요 · 기가 죽었어요 · 기를 죽이다 (to discourage someone)
T4-1878.m: to lose heart, to feel discouraged, to be intimidated
T4-1878.ex: 동생이 시험을 망쳐서 기가 많이 죽었어요.
T4-1878.x: My younger sibling bombed the test and is really down.
rel: to cheer up, to feel free

T4-1879.forms: 기를 써요 · 기를 썼어요 · 기를 쓰고 + verb (ㅡ drops)
T4-1879.m: to try with all one's might, to go all out
T4-1879.x: He tried with all his might to come in first.

T4-1880.forms: 꼬리를 물어요 · 꼬리를 물었어요 · 꼬리에 꼬리를 물다 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1880.m: to follow one after another, to come in an endless chain
T4-1880.ex: 출근 시간이라 차들이 꼬리를 물고 이어졌어요.
T4-1880.x: It was rush hour, so the cars came one after another.
T4-1880.e: Literally 'to bite the tail' of the one in front, forming a long line.

T4-1881.forms: 낯을 가려요 · 낯을 가렸어요 · 낯을 많이 가리다
T4-1881.m: to be shy with strangers, to be wary of new people
T4-1881.ex: 우리 아이는 낯을 많이 가려서 처음에는 말을 안 해요.
T4-1881.x: My kid is really shy around strangers, so he doesn't talk at first.
T4-1881.e: 낯 = face; 가리다 here means 'to tell apart,' sorting familiar faces from unfamiliar ones.
T4-1881.t: A very common self-description: 저는 낯을 좀 가려요 means 'I'm a bit shy at first.'

T4-1882.forms: 눈길을 끌어요 · 눈길을 끌었어요 · 눈길을 끄는 (+noun) (ㄹ drops)
T4-1882.m: to catch the eye, to attract attention
T4-1882.ex: 그 가게의 독특한 간판이 사람들의 눈길을 끌었어요.
T4-1882.x: That store's unique sign caught people's eye.
T4-1882.e: 눈길 = line of sight (eye + road); literally 'to pull someone's gaze.'
T4-1882.t: Pronounced [눈낄]: the ㄱ is tensed in this compound.

T4-1883.m: to bring tears to one's eyes, to be moved to tears
T4-1883.ex: 그 영화의 마지막 장면이 관객들의 눈시울을 적셨어요.
T4-1883.x: The film's final scene brought the audience to tears.
T4-1883.e: 눈시울 = the rims of the eyelids; literally 'to wet the rims of the eyes.'

T4-1884.m: to feel hopeless, to be at a loss, to not know what to do
T4-1884.ex: 지갑과 여권을 모두 잃어버려서 눈앞이 캄캄했어요.
T4-1884.x: I lost both my wallet and my passport, and I had no idea what to do.
T4-1884.e: Literally 'everything in front of my eyes goes pitch-black.'
T4-1884.t: Pronounced [누나피 캄캄하다]: the ㅍ of 앞 links over to the next vowel.

T4-1885.forms: 눈에 띄어요 · 눈에 띄었어요 · 눈에 띄게 (noticeably)
T4-1885.m: to stand out, to be noticeable, to catch one's eye
T4-1885.ex: 빨간 코트를 입어서 사람들 사이에서 눈에 띄었어요.
T4-1885.x: She stood out in the crowd because she was wearing a red coat.
T4-1885.e: 띄다 is a contraction of 뜨이다, 'to come into view.'
T4-1885.t: A common spelling mistake: write 눈에 띄다, not 띠다; 띠다 means 'to have a tinge of.'

T4-1886.forms: 눈을 감아 줘요 · 눈을 감아 줬어요 · 눈감아 주세요
T4-1886.m: to turn a blind eye, to let something slide
T4-1886.ex: 이번 한 번만 눈을 감아 주세요.
T4-1886.x: Please let it slide just this once.
T4-1886.e: Literally 'to close one's eyes for someone,' pretending not to see.
T4-1886.t: The -아 주다 makes it a favor; 눈을 감다 alone means 'to close one's eyes' or even 'to pass away.'

T4-1887.forms: 눈이 빠지게 기다려요 · 눈이 빠지게 기다렸어요
T4-1887.m: to wait eagerly, to wait impatiently for a long time
T4-1887.ex: 아이들은 산타 할아버지를 눈이 빠지게 기다렸어요.
T4-1887.x: The kids waited impatiently for Santa.
T4-1887.e: Literally 'to wait until your eyes fall out' from staring at the door.
T4-1887.t: Means the same as 목이 빠지게 기다리다; both stress long, impatient waiting.

T4-1888.forms: 다리를 놓아요(놔요) · 다리를 놓았어요(놨어요) · 다리를 놓아 주다
T4-1888.m: to act as a go-between, to connect people, to set someone up
T4-1888.ex: 친구가 다리를 놓아 줘서 지금의 남편을 만났어요.
T4-1888.x: A friend set us up, and that's how I met my husband.
T4-1888.e: 다리 = bridge (homonym of 다리 'leg'); literally 'to build a bridge' between people.

T4-1889.forms: 등을 돌려요 · 등을 돌렸어요 · N에게 등을 돌리다
T4-1889.m: to turn one's back on, to abandon, to break with
T4-1889.ex: 가격이 너무 올라서 손님들이 그 가게에 등을 돌렸어요.
T4-1889.x: Prices went up too much, so customers turned their backs on that store.
T4-1889.e: Literally 'to turn one's back,' the same image as in English.
rel: to look away from, to ignore

T4-1890.m: to make up one's mind, to decide, to resolve
T4-1890.ex: 올해는 꼭 담배를 끊기로 마음을 먹었어요.
T4-1890.x: I've made up my mind to quit smoking this year.
T4-1890.e: 먹다 here means 'to take on' a feeling or resolve, as in 겁을 먹다 'to get scared.'
T4-1890.t: Usually V-기로 마음(을) 먹다, and it's often written as one word, 마음먹다.

T4-1891.forms: 마음을 놓아요(놔요) · 마음을 놓았어요 · 마음 놓고 (without worry)
T4-1891.m: to relax, to stop worrying, to feel at ease
T4-1891.ex: 아이가 무사히 도착했다는 전화를 받고 마음을 놓았어요.
T4-1891.x: I got a call that my child had arrived safely, and I could finally relax.
T4-1891.e: Literally 'to put down one's heart,' like setting down a heavy load.

T4-1892.m: to feel relieved, to be at ease
T4-1892.ex: 의사 선생님 말씀을 듣고 나니 마음이 놓였어요.
T4-1892.x: After hearing what the doctor said, I felt relieved.
T4-1892.e: 놓이다 is the passive of 놓다 'to put down.'
T4-1892.t: 마음을 놓다 is something you do; 마음이 놓이다 is a feeling that happens to you.

T4-1893.m: to weigh on one's mind, to bother someone
T4-1893.ex: 친구에게 화를 낸 것이 계속 마음에 걸려요.
T4-1893.x: Getting angry at my friend keeps weighing on my mind.
T4-1893.e: Literally 'to get caught on the heart,' like something snagging.
T4-1893.t: Don't mix it up with 마음에 들다 'to like': 마음에 걸리다 means something bothers you.

T4-1894.m: to let go of expectations or greed, to clear one's mind
T4-1894.x: I decided to let go and just wait for the results.
T4-1894.e: Literally 'to empty the heart' of desire and worry.

T4-1895.forms: 머리를 맞대요 · 머리를 맞댔어요 · 머리를 맞대고 + verb
T4-1895.m: to put heads together, to brainstorm together
T4-1895.x: The team members put their heads together and solved the problem.
T4-1895.e: 맞대다 = to put face to face; picture heads touching over a problem.
T4-1895.t: Pronounced [맏때다]: the batchim makes the following ㄷ tense.

T4-1896.forms: 머리를 식혀요 · 머리를 식혔어요 · 머리 좀 식히고 올게요
T4-1896.m: to clear one's head, to take a mental break
T4-1896.x: I took a short walk in the park to clear my head.
T4-1896.e: 식히다 = to cool down; literally 'to cool off the head.'
T4-1896.t: Pronounced [시키다]: ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-1897.m: to have a lot on one's mind, to feel mentally overwhelmed
T4-1897.x: I've got a lot on my mind these days with so much work.
T4-1897.e: Literally 'the head is complicated,' with thoughts tangled up.
T4-1897.t: Pronounced [복짜파다]: tensing, plus ㅂ and ㅎ merging into ㅍ.

T4-1898.forms: 목이 빠지게 기다려요 · 목이 빠지게 기다렸어요
T4-1898.m: to wait anxiously, to wait with bated breath
T4-1898.ex: 할머니는 손자가 오기를 목이 빠지게 기다리셨어요.
T4-1898.x: Grandma waited eagerly for her grandson to arrive.
T4-1898.e: Literally 'to wait until your neck comes loose' from craning it to look.

T4-1899.forms: 몸 둘 바를 몰라요 · 몸 둘 바를 몰랐어요 · 몸 둘 바를 모르겠어요 (르 irregular)
T4-1899.m: to not know what to do with oneself (from embarrassment or gratitude)
T4-1899.ex: 칭찬을 너무 많이 해 주셔서 몸 둘 바를 모르겠어요.
T4-1899.x: You're praising me so much that I don't know what to say.
T4-1899.e: Literally 'to not know where to put one's body.'
T4-1899.t: A humble, polite reply to big praise or kindness, usually as 몸 둘 바를 모르겠어요.

T4-1900.m: to kneel; to give in, to surrender, to lose
T4-1900.ex: 우리 팀은 결승전에서 강한 상대에게 무릎을 꿇었어요.
T4-1900.x: Our team fell to a strong opponent in the final.
T4-1900.e: Literally 'to bend the knees'; kneeling shows apology or defeat.
T4-1900.t: Pronounced [꿀타]: the ㅎ of ㅀ combines with ㄷ into aspirated ㅌ.

T4-1901.forms: 바가지를 써요 · 바가지를 썼어요 · 바가지를 씌우다 (to rip someone off) (ㅡ drops)
T4-1901.m: to get ripped off, to be overcharged
T4-1901.x: I took a taxi at a tourist spot and got ripped off.
T4-1901.e: 바가지 = a gourd dipper; how it came to mean 'rip-off' is uncertain.
T4-1901.t: The seller 'puts' it on you: 상인이 관광객에게 바가지를 씌웠어요.

T4-1902.m: to stop going (somewhere), to stop visiting, to cut ties
T4-1902.ex: 그 일 이후로 그는 술집에 발을 끊었어요.
T4-1902.x: Since that incident, he's stopped going to bars.
T4-1902.e: Literally 'to cut off one's feet' from a place.
T4-1902.t: Pronounced [끈타]: the ㅎ aspirates the following ㄷ.

T4-1903.m: to back out, to pull out (of an involvement)
T4-1903.ex: 문제가 생기자 그는 그 사업에서 발을 뺐어요.
T4-1903.x: When problems came up, he pulled out of that business.
T4-1903.e: Literally 'to pull one's foot out' of something.

T4-1904.forms: 발목을 잡아요 · 발목을 잡았어요 · 발목을 잡히다 (to be held back)
T4-1904.m: to hold someone back, to be a drag on, to hinder
T4-1904.ex: 이번에도 부상이 그 선수의 발목을 잡았어요.
T4-1904.x: Once again, an injury held that athlete back.
T4-1904.e: 발목 = ankle; literally 'to grab someone's ankle' so they can't move forward.

T4-1905.m: to be jealous, to be envious (of someone's good luck)
T4-1905.ex: 친구가 복권에 당첨됐다니 솔직히 배가 아파요.
T4-1905.x: Honestly, I'm jealous that my friend won the lottery.
T4-1905.e: From the proverb 사촌이 땅을 사면 배가 아프다: 'when your cousin buys land, your stomach hurts.'
T4-1905.t: It also literally means 'my stomach hurts,' so context tells you which one.

T4-1906.forms: 비위를 맞춰요 · 비위를 맞췄어요 · N의 비위를 맞추다
T4-1906.m: to humor someone, to cater to someone's moods, to please
T4-1906.ex: 그는 사장님의 비위를 맞추느라 늘 피곤해요.
T4-1906.x: He's always tired from catering to the boss's moods.
T4-1906.e: Literally 'to match someone's spleen and stomach,' meaning their tastes and moods.

T4-1907.forms: 속을 썩여요 · 속을 썩였어요 · 속(이) 썩다 (to be distressed)
T4-1907.m: to cause someone worry or grief, to give someone a hard time
T4-1907.ex: 어렸을 때 부모님 속을 많이 썩였어요.
T4-1907.x: I gave my parents a lot of grief when I was young.
T4-1907.e: 속 = one's insides; 썩이다 = to make rot, as if worry rots your insides.
T4-1907.t: Don't confuse 썩이다 (to distress) with 썩히다 (to let rot or go to waste), a common spelling mix-up.

T4-1908.forms: 속이 상해요 · 속이 상했어요 · 속상해요 (common one-word form)
T4-1908.m: to be upset, to feel hurt, to be distressed
T4-1908.ex: 열심히 준비했는데 시험에 떨어져서 속이 상해요.
T4-1908.x: I prepared so hard but failed the exam, so I'm really upset.
T4-1908.e: 속 = one's insides; literally 'one's insides get hurt.'
T4-1908.t: In speech it's usually one word, 속상하다: 정말 속상해 죽겠어요.

T4-1909.forms: 속이 타요 · 속이 탔어요 · 속을 태우다 (to make someone anxious)
T4-1909.m: to be anxious, to be worried sick, to be on pins and needles
T4-1909.ex: 아이와 연락이 안 돼서 속이 타요.
T4-1909.x: I can't reach my child, and I'm worried sick.
T4-1909.e: 타다 = to burn; literally 'one's insides burn' with worry.

T4-1910.forms: 손을 놓아요(놔요) · 손을 놓았어요 · 일손을 놓다
T4-1910.m: to stop working on, to give up on; to let go (of a hand)
T4-1910.ex: 그는 사업이 실패한 뒤 모든 일에서 손을 놓았어요.
T4-1910.x: After his business failed, he gave up on everything.
T4-1910.e: Literally 'to put down one's hands' and stop working.
T4-1910.t: Also literal: 제 손을 놓지 마세요, 'Don't let go of my hand.'

T4-1911.forms: 손을 떼요 · 손을 뗐어요 · N에서 손을 떼다
T4-1911.m: to wash one's hands of, to quit (a job or affair), to stay out of
T4-1911.x: He's completely out of politics now.
T4-1911.e: 떼다 = to detach; literally 'to take one's hands off.'
T4-1911.t: Usually with -에서: 이 일에서 손을 떼세요, 'Stay out of this.'

T4-1912.forms: 손을 봐요 · 손을 봤어요 · 손봐 줄게요
T4-1912.m: to fix, to touch up, to repair; (rough slang) to teach someone a lesson
T4-1912.ex: 고장 난 의자를 아버지가 손을 봐 주셨어요.
T4-1912.x: My dad fixed the broken chair for me.
T4-1912.e: Literally 'to see to something with one's hands.'

T4-1913.forms: 손을 써요 · 손을 썼어요 · 손을 쓸 수 없다 (ㅡ drops)
T4-1913.m: to take action, to do something about it, to take measures
T4-1913.ex: 병이 너무 심해져서 이제는 손을 쓸 수 없대요.
T4-1913.x: The illness has gotten too serious, and they say nothing can be done now.
T4-1913.e: Literally 'to use one's hands' to deal with a problem.
T4-1913.t: Very common as 손을 쓸 수 없다 or 손쓸 틈이 없다, 'too late to do anything.'

T4-1914.m: to look forward to, to count the days until
T4-1914.x: The kids are counting the days until vacation.
T4-1914.e: 손꼽다 = to count on one's fingers, so 'to wait counting the days on your fingers.'

T4-1915.forms: 손발이 맞아요 · 손발이 잘 맞았어요 · 손발이 안 맞다
T4-1915.m: to work well together, to be in sync
T4-1915.ex: 우리 팀은 손발이 잘 맞아서 일이 빨리 끝나요.
T4-1915.x: Our team works so well together that we finish quickly.
T4-1915.e: Literally 'the hands and feet match,' moving in sync.

T4-1916.forms: 숨을 돌려요 · 숨을 돌렸어요 · 한숨 돌리다
T4-1916.m: to catch one's breath, to take a breather
T4-1916.ex: 바쁜 일이 끝나서 이제 좀 숨을 돌릴 수 있어요.
T4-1916.x: The busy stretch is over, so now I can catch my breath.
T4-1916.e: Literally 'to get one's breath back' after rushing around.

T4-1917.forms: 신경을 써요 · 신경을 썼어요 · 신경 쓰지 마세요 (ㅡ drops)
T4-1917.m: to pay attention to, to care about; to worry about
T4-1917.ex: 외모에 너무 신경을 쓰지 않아도 돼요.
T4-1917.x: You don't have to worry so much about your looks.
T4-1917.e: 신경 = nerves; literally 'to use one's nerves' on something.
T4-1917.t: 신경 쓰지 마세요 means 'Don't worry about it'; casual 신경 꺼 is a rude 'Mind your own business.'

T4-1918.forms: 애를 써요 · 애를 썼어요 · 애쓰셨어요 (ㅡ drops)
T4-1918.m: to make a great effort, to try hard
T4-1918.x: I tried hard to forget, but it wasn't easy.
T4-1918.e: 애 here means 'anxious effort,' a homonym of 애 'kid.'
T4-1918.t: 애쓰셨어요 is a warm way to thank someone for their hard work.

T4-1919.forms: 애를 먹어요 · 애를 먹었어요 · V-느라 애를 먹다
T4-1919.m: to have a hard time, to struggle with
T4-1919.ex: 길을 몰라서 호텔을 찾느라 애를 먹었어요.
T4-1919.x: I didn't know the way, so I had a hard time finding the hotel.
T4-1919.e: 애 = anxious trouble; literally 'to swallow trouble.'
T4-1919.t: Don't confuse it with 애를 쓰다: 쓰다 is trying hard, 먹다 is going through trouble.

T4-1920.m: to feel a heavy responsibility, to feel the pressure
T4-1920.x: Now that I'm the new team leader, I feel the weight of responsibility.
T4-1920.e: Responsibility pictured as a load on your shoulders, much like in English.

T4-1921.m: to be shameless, to have a lot of nerve
T4-1921.ex: 그는 얼굴이 두꺼워서 매일 돈을 빌려 달라고 해요.
T4-1921.x: He's so shameless that he asks to borrow money every day.
T4-1921.e: Literally 'one's face is thick,' too thick to blush.
T4-1921.t: Unlike English 'thick-skinned,' this means shameless, not emotionally tough.

T4-1922.m: to get angry, to get worked up, to be ticked off
T4-1922.ex: 친구가 약속을 또 어겨서 열을 받았어요.
T4-1922.x: My friend broke our plans again, and I got really mad.
T4-1922.e: Literally 'to receive heat,' like a kettle coming to a boil.
T4-1922.t: Casual and a bit slangy; in formal situations say 화가 나다 instead.

T4-1923.forms: 입을 모아요 · 입을 모았어요 · 입을 모아 말하다
T4-1923.m: to say with one voice, to agree unanimously
T4-1923.ex: 전문가들은 입을 모아 운동의 중요성을 강조했습니다.
T4-1923.x: Experts unanimously stressed the importance of exercise.
T4-1923.e: Literally 'to gather mouths' so everyone says the same thing.

T4-1924.forms: 입에 침이 마르도록 칭찬해요 · 입에 침이 마르게 자랑했어요 (르 irregular)
T4-1924.m: to praise to the skies, to rave about
T4-1924.ex: 선생님은 그 학생을 입에 침이 마르도록 칭찬하셨어요.
T4-1924.x: The teacher praised that student to the skies.
T4-1924.e: Literally 'to talk until your mouth runs dry of saliva.'
T4-1924.t: Almost always 입에 침이 마르도록 (or 마르게) + 칭찬하다/자랑하다.

T4-1925.m: to be a picky eater, to eat very little
T4-1925.ex: 우리 아들은 입이 짧아서 밥을 조금만 먹어요.
T4-1925.x: My son is a picky eater, so he only eats a little.
T4-1925.e: Literally 'a short mouth'; it's about eating, not talking.
T4-1925.t: Pronounced [이비 짤따]: in 짧다 the ㄼ sounds like ㄹ.

T4-1926.forms: 코가 납작해져요 · 코가 납작해졌어요 · 코를 납작하게 만들다
T4-1926.m: to be humbled, to have one's pride crushed, to be taken down a peg
T4-1926.ex: 자랑만 하던 그는 시합에서 져서 코가 납작해졌어요.
T4-1926.x: He was always bragging, but losing the match took him down a peg.
T4-1926.e: In Korean idioms the nose stands for pride, so a flattened nose means crushed pride.

T4-1927.forms: 콧대가 높아요 · 콧대가 높았어요 · 콧대를 꺾다 (to humble)
T4-1927.m: to be stuck-up, to be arrogant, to be proud
T4-1927.ex: 그 배우는 인기가 많아서 콧대가 높아요.
T4-1927.x: That actor is so popular that he's stuck-up.
T4-1927.e: 콧대 = the bridge of the nose; a high nose bridge symbolizes pride.
T4-1927.t: Pronounced [코때]: the 사이시옷 makes the ㄷ tense.

T4-1928.m: to be dead tired, to be completely worn out
T4-1928.ex: 하루 종일 이사를 해서 파김치가 됐어요.
T4-1928.x: I spent the whole day moving and I'm completely wiped out.
T4-1928.e: 파김치 = green-onion kimchi; you're as limp as wilted, pickled scallions.

T4-1929.m: to feel firsthand, to experience directly
T4-1929.ex: 물가가 오른 것을 피부로 느낄 수 있어요.
T4-1929.x: You can really feel firsthand that prices have gone up.
T4-1929.e: Literally 'to feel it on your skin.'

T4-1930.forms: 한눈을 팔아요 · 한눈을 팔았어요 · 한눈파는 사이에 (ㄹ drops)
T4-1930.m: to look away, to get distracted, to not pay attention
T4-1930.x: It's dangerous to look away while driving.
T4-1930.e: 한눈 = a glance aside; 팔다 here means 'to let one's attention wander.'
T4-1930.t: Don't confuse 한눈을 팔다 with 한눈에 'at a glance.'

T4-1931.forms: 한숨을 쉬어요 · 한숨을 쉬었어요 · 깊은 한숨을 쉬다
T4-1931.ex: 시험 결과를 보고 그는 깊은 한숨을 쉬었어요.
T4-1931.x: He let out a deep sigh after seeing his test results.
T4-1931.t: 한숨(을) 돌리다 is different: it signals relief, 'to catch one's breath.'

T4-1932.m: to tighten one's belt, to cut back on spending
T4-1932.x: The economy is tough, so we have to tighten our belts.
T4-1932.e: Literally 'to tighten the belt,' just like the English idiom.

T4-1933.forms: 혀를 차요 · 혀를 찼어요 · 쯧쯧 (the sound)
T4-1933.m: to click one's tongue (in disapproval or pity)
T4-1933.x: Grandpa clicked his tongue as he watched the news.
T4-1933.e: The click itself is written 쯧쯧, Korean for 'tsk-tsk.'

T4-1934.forms: 활개를 쳐요 · 활개를 쳤어요 · 활개를 치고 다니다
T4-1934.m: to act freely and boldly; to run rampant
T4-1934.ex: 요즘 인터넷에서 가짜 뉴스가 활개를 치고 있어요.
T4-1934.x: Fake news is running rampant online these days.
T4-1934.e: 활개 = outspread arms or a bird's spread wings; picture flapping them freely.

T4-1935.forms: 힘을 써요 · 힘을 썼어요 · 힘써 주셔서 감사합니다 (ㅡ drops)
T4-1935.m: to use one's strength; to make an effort; to use one's influence
T4-1935.ex: 아버지가 힘을 써서 무거운 상자를 옮기셨어요.
T4-1935.x: Dad used all his strength to move the heavy box.
T4-1935.e: Literally 'to use strength'; it can also mean pulling strings for someone.

T4-1936.forms: 진땀을 빼요 · 진땀을 뺐어요 · 진땀(을) 흘리다
T4-1936.m: to sweat bullets, to have a really hard time
T4-1936.ex: 갑자기 질문을 받아서 대답하느라 진땀을 뺐어요.
T4-1936.x: I got a surprise question and sweated bullets trying to answer.
T4-1936.e: 진땀 = sticky sweat from stress or strain; literally 'to squeeze out sticky sweat.'

T4-1937.m: standstill, lack of progress; marking time, walking in place
T4-1937.ex: 협상이 몇 달째 제자리걸음을 하고 있습니다.
T4-1937.x: The negotiations have been at a standstill for months.
T4-1937.e: 제자리 (one's own spot) + 걸음 (step): walking without going anywhere.

T4-1938.x: That person made a really good first impression.
T4-1938.e: 첫 (first) + 인상: literally 'the image first stamped' on your mind.
T4-1938.t: Pronounced [처딘상]: the ㅅ of 첫 becomes a ㄷ sound before linking to 인.

T4-1939.ex: 사진은 찍는 각도에 따라 많이 달라 보여요.
T4-1939.x: Photos can look very different depending on the angle.

T4-1940.x: This bus comes to the stop every ten minutes.
T4-1940.t: N 간격으로 means 'every N' or 'at N intervals': 1미터 간격으로.

T4-1941.ex: 이 책은 너무 개념적이어서 이해하기 어려워요.
T4-1941.x: This book is so conceptual that it's hard to understand.
T4-1941.e: -적 turns nouns into '-ic/-al' words: 개념적, 과학적, 경제적.
T4-1941.t: -적 words link to nouns with 인: 개념적인 설명, 'a conceptual explanation.'

T4-1942.x: We plan to hold individual consultations with the students.

T4-1943.m: sense of distance; emotional distance, feeling of detachment
T4-1943.ex: 그 친구와 오랜만에 만나니 거리감이 느껴졌어요.
T4-1943.x: Meeting that friend after a long time, I felt some distance between us.
T4-1943.e: Literally 'feeling of distance'; -감 = feeling: 책임감, 안정감.

T4-1944.ex: 도시와 농촌의 소득 격차가 점점 커지고 있습니다.
T4-1944.x: The income gap between cities and rural areas keeps widening.
T4-1944.e: Literally 'a difference in rank or level.'

T4-1945.ex: 그 회사는 자동차 결함 때문에 리콜을 했습니다.
T4-1945.x: The company issued a recall because of car defects.
T4-1945.t: 결함 is for flaws in products or systems; for personal shortcomings, 단점 is more common.

T4-1946.ex: 비타민 결핍은 여러 가지 질병을 일으킬 수 있습니다.
T4-1946.x: Vitamin deficiency can cause various diseases.
T4-1946.e: Both syllables mean 'lacking,' doubling the idea.
T4-1946.t: 부족 is the everyday 'lack'; 결핍 sounds more serious, as in medical or psychological contexts.

T4-1947.ex: 내비게이션이 더 빠른 경로를 알려 줬어요.
T4-1947.x: The GPS showed me a faster route.
T4-1947.t: Pronounced [경노] — nasalization; don't confuse it with 경로 'respect for the elderly,' as in 경로석.

T4-1948.m: fixing, fixation; being fixed in place
T4-1948.x: I fixed the desk in place with screws so it wouldn't wobble.
T4-1948.t: 고정 관념 (fixed idea) means 'stereotype' and shows up a lot in reading passages.

T4-1949.m: blank, empty space; gap, hiatus (in time)
T4-1949.ex: 그 가수는 3년의 공백을 깨고 새 앨범을 냈어요.
T4-1949.x: The singer broke a three-year hiatus and released a new album.
T4-1949.e: Literally 'empty and white,' like a blank page.

T4-1950.x: Adolescence is the transition period from childhood to adulthood.
T4-1950.e: Literally 'a period of crossing over' from one stage to the next.

T4-1951.ex: 시간 관념이 없는 사람과 일하기는 힘들어요.
T4-1951.x: It's hard to work with someone who has no sense of time.
T4-1951.e: Literally 'viewing thought': how you picture something in your mind.
T4-1951.t: 시간 관념 means a sense of punctuality; 고정관념 means a stereotype.

T4-1952.ex: 회의 전에 인사를 나누는 것이 관례예요.
T4-1952.x: It's customary to exchange greetings before a meeting.
T4-1952.e: Literally 'habitual example': the way things are usually done.
T4-1952.t: Pronounced [괄례]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

T4-1953.x: Wrong practices must be corrected quickly.
T4-1953.e: Literally 'habitual doing': what people routinely do, often in business.

T4-1954.ex: 그는 감기를 구실로 회사에 가지 않았어요.
T4-1954.x: He used a cold as an excuse not to go to work.
T4-1954.e: Literally 'mouth fact': a reason that exists only in words.
T4-1954.t: A different native word 구실 means 'role': 제 구실을 하다 = to do one's part.

T4-1955.ex: 그 교수님은 이 분야에서 권위가 있어요.
T4-1955.x: That professor is an authority in this field.
T4-1955.t: 권위 is respected expertise, but 권위적 (authoritarian) is negative: bossy and controlling.

T4-1956.x: In the military, you have to follow the rules strictly.
T4-1956.e: Literally 'rule and law': the order a group must follow.
T4-1956.t: This suffix is read 율 after a vowel or ㄴ, but 률 after other batchim, as in 법률.

T4-1957.x: Extreme diets aren't good for your health.
T4-1957.e: Literally 'of the farthest end'. -적 = '-ic/-al': 경제적, 긍정적.
T4-1957.t: Pronounced [극딴적]; use 극단적인 before nouns and 극단적으로 as an adverb.

T4-1958.ex: 이 문제는 근본부터 다시 생각해 봐야 해요.
T4-1958.x: We need to rethink this problem from the ground up.

T4-1959.ex: 욕심은 모든 갈등의 근원이 될 수 있어요.
T4-1959.x: Greed can be the source of all conflict.
T4-1959.e: Literally 'root and spring': where something first flows from.

T4-1960.x: This company grew on the basis of its technology.
T4-1960.e: Literally 'base platform': the ground something is built on.
T4-1960.t: X을/를 기반으로 means 'based on X': 사실을 기반으로 한 영화.

T4-1961.ex: 이 음식의 기원은 조선 시대로 알려져 있어요.
T4-1961.x: This dish is known to date back to the Joseon era.
T4-1961.t: A homonym 기원 means 'prayer, wish', as in 평화를 기원합니다.

T4-1962.x: It's important to look at a person's inner self.
T4-1962.e: Literally 'inside face': the side of a person others can't see.

T4-1963.m: point at issue, point of argument
T4-1963.x: The main point of that presentation wasn't clear.
T4-1963.t: Pronounced [논쩜]: 점 is tensed in compounds like 장점 and 단점.

T4-1964.x: Consumer tastes are becoming more and more diverse.

T4-1965.x: The police found an important clue in the case.
T4-1965.e: Literally 'end of a thread': pull it and the story unravels.
T4-1965.t: Homonym: a different 단서 means 'proviso', as in 단서를 달다 'to attach a condition', common in formal writing.

T4-1966.x: I had to pay the price for my mistake.
T4-1966.t: Pronounced [대까]; without tensing, 대가 means 'great master', as in 음악의 대가.

T4-1967.x: Those eligible for the grant will be announced next week.

T4-1968.ex: 이 작품은 독창성이 뛰어나다는 평가를 받았어요.
T4-1968.x: This work was praised for its outstanding originality.
T4-1968.e: Literally 'the quality of creating alone'. -성 = '-ness/-ity': 가능성, 중요성.

T4-1969.ex: 칭찬은 학생들에게 큰 동기 부여가 됩니다.
T4-1969.x: Praise is a big motivator for students.
T4-1969.t: Say 동기 부여가 되다 for 'to get motivated' and 동기를 부여하다 for 'to motivate someone'.

T4-1970.x: Exports are an important driver of economic growth.
T4-1970.t: Pronounced [동녁]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

T4-1971.m: sense of kinship, feeling of sameness
T4-1971.ex: 같은 고향 사람을 만나면 동질감을 느껴요.
T4-1971.x: I feel a sense of kinship when I meet someone from my hometown.
T4-1971.e: Literally 'feeling of the same nature'. -감 = feeling: 책임감, 자신감.

T4-1972.x: We need data to back up that claim.
T4-1972.e: 뒤 'back' + 받치다 'to prop up': propping something up from behind.
T4-1972.t: Pronounced [뒤빧침]; 뒷받침하다 means 'to back up', often with claims and evidence.

T4-1973.x: The meaning of a word changes depending on the context.
T4-1973.e: Literally 'veins and links': how ideas connect like blood vessels.

T4-1974.x: That war had no justification from the start.
T4-1974.e: Literally 'name and role': a reason that looks right in public.

T4-1975.x: There's a contradiction between what he says and what he does.
T4-1975.e: From an old tale: a seller praising both an unstoppable spear and an unbreakable shield.

T4-1976.ex: 모르는 단어는 문맥을 보고 뜻을 추측해 보세요.
T4-1976.x: For unknown words, try guessing the meaning from the context.
T4-1976.t: 문맥 is context within a text; 맥락 is broader, including situations and history.

T4-1977.ex: 겸손은 한국 사회에서 큰 미덕으로 여겨져요.
T4-1977.x: Modesty is seen as a great virtue in Korean society.

T4-1978.ex: 그의 의견에 반론을 제기하는 사람은 없었어요.
T4-1978.x: No one raised an objection to his opinion.
T4-1978.t: Pronounced [발론]; often used with 제기하다: 반론을 제기하다 = to raise an objection.

T4-1979.ex: 발상을 바꾸면 문제가 쉽게 풀릴 수 있어요.
T4-1979.x: If you change your way of thinking, the problem may be easy to solve.
T4-1979.t: Pronounced [발쌍]; 발상의 전환 (a shift in thinking) is a common set phrase.

T4-1980.x: The company announced a new operating policy.
T4-1980.e: Literally 'direction needle', like a compass needle pointing the way.

T4-1981.ex: 배경지식이 있으면 글을 더 쉽게 이해할 수 있어요.
T4-1981.x: With background knowledge, you can understand a text more easily.
T4-1981.e: Literally 'backdrop knowledge': what you already know behind the text.

T4-1982.ex: 이 문제는 개인의 범주를 넘어선 사회 문제예요.
T4-1982.x: This is a social issue that goes beyond the individual.
T4-1982.e: Literally 'pattern and class': a box that ideas are sorted into.

T4-1983.ex: 날씨가 이번 경기의 가장 큰 변수예요.
T4-1983.x: The weather is the biggest wild card in this game.
T4-1983.e: Literally 'changing number', from math; now any unpredictable factor.
T4-1983.t: Pronounced [변쑤]; in news, 변수 often means a factor that could change the outcome.

T4-1984.ex: 이 박물관에서 한국 옷의 변천을 볼 수 있어요.
T4-1984.x: At this museum, you can see how Korean clothing changed over time.

T4-1985.x: A mother protecting her baby is instinct.
T4-1985.e: Literally 'original ability': what you can do without learning.

T4-1986.ex: 형은 동생들에게 좋은 본보기가 되어야 해요.
T4-1986.x: An older brother should be a good example to his younger siblings.
T4-1986.e: 본 'model' + native 보기 'something to look at': an example to follow.
T4-1986.t: Common patterns: 본보기가 되다 = to set an example; 본보기로 삼다 = to take as a model.

T4-1987.x: We need to grasp the essence of the problem accurately.
T4-1987.e: Literally 'original substance': what something really is underneath.

T4-1988.ex: 그 영화는 작품상 부문에서 상을 받았어요.
T4-1988.x: That film won in the Best Picture category.
T4-1988.e: Literally 'section gate': one branch of a larger field.
T4-1988.t: Don't confuse 부문 (sector, category) with 부분 (part, portion).

T4-1989.ex: 지역 간 경제적 불균형이 심해지고 있습니다.
T4-1989.x: The economic imbalance between regions is getting worse.
T4-1989.e: Literally 'not evenly balanced'. 불- = un-/in-: 불가능, 불편.
T4-1989.t: 불- becomes 부- before ㄷ and ㅈ: 부족, 부당.

T4-1990.x: What's your grandma's secret to staying healthy?
T4-1990.t: 비결 is a positive 'secret to success'; a hidden fact you keep is 비밀.

T4-1991.ex: 독서는 창의적 사고를 키우는 데 도움이 돼요.
T4-1991.t: Homonym: 사고 also means 'accident' (교통사고); context tells them apart.

T4-1992.m: sense of duty, sense of mission
T4-1992.ex: 그 의사는 강한 사명감을 가지고 일해요.
T4-1992.x: That doctor works with a strong sense of mission.

T4-1993.x: The two countries pledged mutual cooperation.
T4-1993.t: Homonym: 상호 also means 'business name', as on a store sign.

T4-1994.ex: 아이들은 친구와의 상호 작용을 통해 배워요.
T4-1994.x: Children learn through interaction with their friends.
T4-1994.t: Often written without a space: 상호작용.

T4-1995.ex: 이 식물은 생명력이 강해서 잘 죽지 않아요.
T4-1995.x: This plant is very hardy, so it rarely dies.
T4-1995.e: Literally 'life power'. -력 = power, ability: 노력, 능력.

T4-1996.ex: 한국 회사에서는 서열이 중요한 경우가 많아요.
T4-1996.x: In Korean companies, rank often matters a lot.
T4-1996.e: Literally 'ordered row': who stands where in line.

T4-1997.ex: 물은 높은 곳에서 낮은 곳으로 흐르는 속성이 있어요.
T4-1997.x: Water has the property of flowing from high places to low places.
T4-1997.e: Literally 'belonging nature': the qualities that come with a thing.
T4-1997.t: Pronounced [속썽]; a homonym 속성 means 'crash course', as in ads for 속성 과외.

T4-1998.x: Scammers' tricks are getting more and more sophisticated.
T4-1998.e: Literally 'hand method': the way someone does something.

T4-1999.x: My blood pressure numbers dropped a lot from last month.
T4-1999.t: Homonym: 수치 meaning 'shame' appears in 수치심, 'sense of shame'.

T4-2000.ex: 이 연구는 교육 정책에 중요한 시사점을 줍니다.
T4-2000.x: This study offers important implications for education policy.
T4-2000.e: Literally 'point that shows and hints': what a finding suggests.

T4-2001.x: It's hard to make a decision at this point.
T4-2001.t: Homonym: 시점 meaning 'point of view' is used for narration, as in 1인칭 시점.

T4-2002.x: The true nature of that company was finally revealed.
T4-2002.e: Literally 'real body': what actually exists behind appearances.

T4-2003.x: The government surveyed the actual state of youth unemployment.

T4-2004.ex: 경기는 시간이 갈수록 다른 양상으로 흘러갔어요.
T4-2004.x: As time went on, the game took a different turn.
T4-2004.e: Literally 'shape and appearance': how a situation looks as it unfolds.
T4-2004.t: 양상을 보이다 (to show a pattern) is a stock phrase in news reports.

T4-2005.ex: 인터넷은 편리함과 위험이라는 양면성을 가지고 있어요.
T4-2005.x: The internet has two sides: convenience and danger.
T4-2005.e: Literally 'the quality of having two sides'.

T4-2006.ex: 경제적 여건이 좋지 않아서 유학을 포기했어요.
T4-2006.x: I gave up studying abroad because my financial situation wasn't good.
T4-2006.e: Literally 'given items': the conditions you have to work with.
T4-2006.t: Pronounced [여껀]; 여건이 되다 means 'circumstances allow', often about money or time.

T4-2007.ex: 그 문제는 아직 논의할 여지가 있어요.
T4-2007.x: There's still room to discuss that issue.
T4-2007.e: Literally 'leftover ground': space still left over.
T4-2007.t: 의심의 여지가 없다 means 'there's no room for doubt.'

T4-2008.ex: 회사는 직원들의 역량을 키우기 위해 교육을 해요.
T4-2008.x: The company provides training to build its employees' skills.
T4-2008.e: Literally 'amount of strength': how much you can handle.

T4-2009.ex: 많이 가질수록 더 불행해지는 것은 역설이에요.
T4-2009.x: It's a paradox that the more you have, the unhappier you become.
T4-2009.t: Don't confuse it with the homonym 역설하다, 'to stress strongly', common in speeches.

T4-2010.x: That athlete won the championship three years in a row.
T4-2010.t: Number + 연속 means 'in a row': 3일 연속, 5경기 연속.

T4-2011.x: Artificial intelligence is being used in many fields.
T4-2011.e: Literally 'governed region': first a territory, then any field.

T4-2012.ex: 건강을 지키는 데 가장 중요한 요소는 수면이에요.
T4-2012.x: The most important factor in staying healthy is sleep.
T4-2012.t: 요소 is a component of something; 요인 is a cause behind a result.

T4-2013.ex: 우리 팀이 경기 초반부터 우위를 차지했어요.
T4-2013.x: Our team took the upper hand from the start of the game.

T4-2014.x: My family is the driving force behind my hard work.
T4-2014.e: Literally 'original moving power': what keeps you going.

T4-2015.ex: 저는 거짓말을 하지 않는 것을 원칙으로 해요.
T4-2015.x: I make it a rule never to lie.
T4-2015.t: 원칙적으로 means 'in principle', often before an exception: 원칙적으로는 안 되지만…

T4-2016.ex: 운동은 가족 간의 유대를 강화하는 데 좋아요.
T4-2016.x: Exercising together is good for strengthening family bonds.
T4-2016.e: Literally 'string and belt': what ties people together.
T4-2016.t: Homonym: 유대 also means 'Judea, Jewish', as in 유대인.

T4-2017.m: sense of bond, feeling of connection
T4-2017.x: Traveling together deepened my bond with my friends.

T4-2018.ex: 시험에 자주 나오는 문제 유형을 알아 두세요.
T4-2018.x: Get to know the question types that often appear on the test.
T4-2018.t: Homonym: 유형 meaning 'tangible' appears in 유형 문화재, 'tangible cultural property'.

T4-2019.ex: 이번 회의는 두 나라가 처음 만났다는 데 의의가 있어요.
T4-2019.x: This meeting is significant in that the two countries met for the first time.
T4-2019.t: Pronounced [의이]; X다는 데 의의가 있다 = 'it is meaningful in that X'.

T4-2020.ex: 두 정당은 정치 이념이 서로 달라요.
T4-2020.x: The two parties have different political ideologies.
T4-2020.e: Literally 'reasoned thought': a system of ideas.

T4-2021.ex: 온라인 수업은 시간을 아낄 수 있다는 이점이 있어요.
T4-2021.x: Online classes have the advantage of saving time.
T4-2021.t: Pronounced [이쩜]; 이점 is a benefit you gain, while 장점 is a good quality.

T4-2022.x: I think everything has a cause and effect.
T4-2022.e: Literally 'cause and fruit': the seed and what grows from it.
T4-2022.t: Pronounced [인꽈]; it usually appears in 인과 관계 rather than alone.

T4-2023.ex: 흡연과 폐암 사이에는 인과 관계가 있습니다.
T4-2023.x: There is a causal relationship between smoking and lung cancer.
T4-2023.t: Don't confuse 인과 관계 (causation) with 상관관계 (correlation) in reading passages.

T4-2024.x: Thanks to advertising, brand awareness went up.
T4-2024.e: Literally 'degree of being known'. -도 = degree: 만족도, 인기도.

T4-2025.ex: 부모는 아이에게 일관성 있는 태도를 보여야 해요.
T4-2025.x: Parents should show a consistent attitude toward their children.
T4-2025.e: Literally 'pierced through as one': staying the same from start to finish.
T4-2025.t: Pronounced [일관썽]; 일관성 있다/없다 works like an adjective.

T4-2026.x: He has the qualities of a leader.
T4-2026.e: Literally 'natural material': the qualities you bring to a role.
T4-2026.t: 자질 is about suitability for a role; 소질 is a natural talent for an activity.

T4-2027.ex: 이 학생은 성장할 잠재력이 매우 커요.
T4-2027.x: This student has great potential to grow.

T4-2028.ex: 언어의 장벽 때문에 처음에는 많이 힘들었어요.
T4-2028.x: At first it was really hard because of the language barrier.

T4-2029.ex: 우리 회사는 새로운 판매 전략을 세웠어요.
T4-2029.x: Our company came up with a new sales strategy.
T4-2029.t: Pronounced [절략]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

T4-2030.x: The company strategically expanded into overseas markets.
T4-2030.e: -적 turns a noun into '-ic/-al': 전략적, 정서적, 추상적.

T4-2031.ex: 두 사람은 결혼을 전제로 사귀고 있어요.
T4-2031.x: The two of them are dating with marriage in mind.
T4-2031.e: Literally 'put forward beforehand': what you lay down first.
T4-2031.t: Common pattern: N을/를 전제로 'on the premise of N, with N in mind'.

T4-2032.ex: 그 여행이 제 인생의 전환점이 되었어요.
T4-2032.x: That trip became a turning point in my life.
T4-2032.t: Usually with 되다: N이 전환점이 되다 'to become a turning point'.

T4-2033.x: We decided by finding a middle ground between their two opinions.
T4-2033.e: Literally 'break toward the middle': meeting halfway.
T4-2033.t: 절충 blends two ideas into one; 타협 stresses both sides giving something up.

T4-2034.ex: 음악은 아이들의 정서 발달에 도움이 돼요.
T4-2034.t: More formal than 감정; often means a shared sensibility, e.g. 한국인의 정서 'the Korean sensibility'.

T4-2035.x: Pets are a great emotional comfort.

T4-2036.ex: 해외에 살면서 제 정체성에 대해 많이 고민했어요.
T4-2036.x: Living abroad, I thought a lot about my identity.

T4-2037.ex: 시간의 제약 때문에 모든 곳을 볼 수 없었어요.
T4-2037.x: Because of time constraints, I couldn't see every place.
T4-2037.t: Homonym warning: 제약 also means 'drug manufacturing', as in 제약 회사 'pharmaceutical company'.

T4-2038.x: There are signs that the economy will recover.
T4-2038.e: Literally 'omen and sign': an early hint of what's coming.
T4-2038.t: Usual pattern: -(으)ㄹ 조짐이 보이다 'to show signs of ~'.

T4-2039.m: subject, main agent, the one in charge
T4-2039.x: Students should be the main agents of the class.
T4-2039.e: Literally 'main body': the one who acts.

T4-2040.x: I sorted my tasks in order of importance.

T4-2041.m: guideline, instructions; needle (of a compass or gauge)
T4-2041.ex: 회사의 안전 지침을 꼭 지켜 주세요.
T4-2041.x: Please be sure to follow the company's safety guidelines.
T4-2041.e: Literally 'pointing needle': like a compass needle showing the way.

T4-2042.ex: 실업률은 경제 상황을 보여 주는 중요한 지표입니다.
T4-2042.x: The unemployment rate is an important indicator of the economy.

T4-2043.ex: 이 문제는 국가 차원에서 해결해야 해요.
T4-2043.x: This problem has to be solved at the national level.
T4-2043.e: Used both for space (3차원 '3-D') and for the level at which something is handled.

T4-2044.ex: 이번 회의는 비용 절감에 초점을 맞췄어요.
T4-2044.x: This meeting focused on cutting costs.
T4-2044.e: Literally 'scorching point': where a lens gathers sunlight and burns.

T4-2045.ex: 그의 설명은 너무 추상적이라서 이해하기 어려웠어요.
T4-2045.x: His explanation was so abstract that it was hard to understand.
T4-2045.e: Literally 'drawing out the image': keeping the idea, dropping the details.

T4-2046.ex: 이 행사의 취지는 어려운 이웃을 돕는 것입니다.
T4-2046.x: The purpose of this event is to help neighbors in need.
T4-2046.e: Literally 'aim and meaning': the point behind something.

T4-2047.ex: 전문가들이 그 계획의 타당성을 검토하고 있어요.
T4-2047.x: Experts are reviewing the feasibility of that plan.

T4-2048.ex: 어릴 때의 경험이 지금 제 성격의 토대가 됐어요.
T4-2048.x: My childhood experiences became the foundation of my personality.
T4-2048.e: Literally 'earth platform': the base a building stands on.
T4-2048.t: Pattern: N을/를 토대로 'based on N', e.g. 조사 결과를 토대로 'based on the survey results'.

T4-2049.ex: 이 마을은 특색 있는 전통 음식으로 유명해요.
T4-2049.x: This village is famous for its distinctive traditional food.
T4-2049.e: Literally 'special color': what makes something stand out.
T4-2049.t: 특색 is about standing out from others; 특성 is an inherent property of something.

T4-2050.ex: 이 재료는 열에 강한 특성이 있어요.
T4-2050.x: This material has the property of being heat-resistant.

T4-2051.ex: 생각의 틀을 깨면 새로운 아이디어가 나와요.
T4-2051.x: When you break out of your usual frame of thinking, new ideas come.
T4-2051.e: Native word for any frame or mold, from window frames to frameworks of thought.
T4-2051.t: 틀에 박힌 means 'stereotyped, cookie-cutter', e.g. 틀에 박힌 생각 'clichéd thinking'.

T4-2052.ex: 그 정책은 사회 전체에 큰 파급을 미쳤어요.
T4-2052.x: That policy had ripple effects across the whole society.
T4-2052.e: Literally 'waves reaching': like ripples spreading across water.

T4-2053.ex: 올림픽은 지역 경제에 큰 파급 효과를 가져왔어요.
T4-2053.x: The Olympics had a big ripple effect on the local economy.
T4-2053.t: Pronounced [파그표과]: ㅂ and ㅎ merge into ㅍ.

T4-2054.ex: 이 카드는 한 달 사용 한도가 백만 원이에요.
T4-2054.x: This card has a monthly spending limit of one million won.
T4-2054.t: 한도 is a set amount, like a card limit; 한계 is the limit of what you can do.

T4-2055.m: item, category, entry (on a list or form)
T4-2055.ex: 신청서의 모든 항목을 빠짐없이 작성해 주세요.
T4-2055.x: Please fill in every item on the application without leaving any out.

T4-2056.ex: 그 계획에는 몇 가지 허점이 있어요.
T4-2056.x: That plan has a few weak spots.
T4-2056.e: Literally 'empty point': a gap someone can slip through.

T4-2057.ex: 정부는 오늘 경제 현안에 대해 논의했습니다.
T4-2057.x: The government discussed pressing economic issues today.
T4-2057.e: Literally 'hanging matter': an issue still up in the air.
T4-2057.t: Pronounced [혀난]; mostly a news and politics word.

T4-2058.ex: 매달 판매 현황을 팀장님께 보고하고 있어요.
T4-2058.x: I report the current sales status to my team leader every month.

T4-2059.x: These snacks are made in the shape of animals.

T4-2060.ex: 새 프로그램 덕분에 업무 효율성이 높아졌어요.
T4-2060.x: Thanks to the new program, work efficiency has gone up.

T4-2061.ex: 시대의 흐름에 따라 생활 방식도 바뀌어요.
T4-2061.x: Lifestyles change with the flow of the times.
T4-2061.e: Noun from 흐르다 'to flow': 흐르- plus -ㅁ.
T4-2061.t: Used for water, time and ideas: 시간의 흐름, 대화의 흐름 'flow of the conversation'.

T4-2062.ex: 그 도시에는 아직 전쟁의 흔적이 남아 있어요.
T4-2062.x: Traces of the war still remain in that city.
T4-2062.e: Literally 'scar and track': what's left behind.

T4-2063.ex: 도시의 주거 비용이 계속 오르고 있어요.
T4-2063.x: Housing costs in the city keep rising.
T4-2063.t: 주거 is housing as a need or category; 거주 is the act of living somewhere.

T4-2064.x: Do you currently reside in Seoul?
T4-2064.t: Formal: forms and news use 거주하다, but in conversation just say 살다.

T4-2065.x: If your place of residence changes, you have to report it to the community center.
T4-2065.e: Literally 'residing place'. -지 = place: 거주지, 관광지, 목적지.

T4-2066.x: Our house is in a quiet residential area.

T4-2067.ex: 저는 회사 근처 빌라에 살고 있어요.
T4-2067.x: I live in a low-rise apartment building near my office.
T4-2067.e: From English 'villa'. Konglish surprise: not a luxury house, but a small low-rise building of units.
T4-2067.t: A 빌라 is usually four or five floors without a large complex, cheaper than an 아파트.

T4-2068.ex: 요즘 우리 동네에 고층 아파트가 많이 생겼어요.
T4-2068.x: Lots of high-rise apartments have gone up in my neighborhood lately.

T4-2069.ex: 아이가 있어서 저층 집을 찾고 있어요.
T4-2069.x: We have a child, so we're looking for a place on a lower floor.
T4-2069.t: Families with kids often prefer 저층 units to avoid complaints about 층간 소음.

T4-2070.m: floor area (in pyeong), size of a home
T4-2070.e: Literally 'number of pyeong': a home's size.

T4-2071.m: pyeong (unit of area, about 3.3 m² or 35.6 sq ft)
T4-2071.e: Traditional unit of about 3.3 square meters, roughly two tatami mats.
T4-2071.t: Listings must officially use 제곱미터 (m²), but people still talk about homes in 평.

T4-2072.x: This park covers a very large area.

T4-2073.m: design, plan (of a building or system)
T4-2073.x: This house was designed by a famous architect.
T4-2073.t: Use 설계 for buildings, machines and systems; for clothes or logos say 디자인.

T4-2074.ex: 아파트 앞에서 도로 공사를 하고 있어요.
T4-2074.x: There's road construction going on in front of the apartment.
T4-2074.t: Homonym warning: 공사 also means 'public corporation', as in 한국전력공사.

T4-2075.x: Be careful near the construction site because it's dangerous.

T4-2076.ex: 오래된 부엌을 리모델링하는 데 한 달 걸렸어요.
T4-2076.x: It took a month to remodel our old kitchen.
T4-2076.e: From English 'remodeling'; used with 하다, also for whole buildings.

T4-2077.x: I did the interior design of our new home myself.
T4-2077.t: 인테리어 공사 means renovating the inside of a home or shop.

T4-2078.x: There was a leak from the upstairs unit, so our ceiling got wet.
T4-2078.t: In everyday speech people usually say 물이 새요 'water is leaking'.

T4-2079.x: Mold has grown on the bathroom wall.
T4-2079.e: In Korean, mold 'blooms' like a flower: 곰팡이가 피다.

T4-2080.x: During the rainy season, it's very damp inside the house.

T4-2081.x: Our heating bill was high this winter.
T4-2081.e: Literally 'warm-room cost'. -비 = cost: 난방비, 교통비, 관리비.
T4-2081.t: Bills 'come out' in Korean: 난방비가 많이 나왔어요 'the heating bill came out high'.

T4-2082.m: noise between floors (from upstairs or downstairs neighbors)
T4-2082.ex: 층간 소음 때문에 이웃과 자주 다퉈요.
T4-2082.x: We often argue with our neighbors because of noise between floors.
T4-2082.e: Literally 'between-floor noise': a top apartment complaint in Korea.
T4-2082.t: A big social issue in Korea; many people wear slippers or lay mats indoors to reduce it.

T4-2083.m: security office, guard booth (in an apartment complex)
T4-2083.x: Please leave the package at the security office.
T4-2083.e: Literally 'guard room'. -실 = room: 경비실, 화장실, 사무실.
T4-2083.t: In Korean apartment complexes, the 경비실 often holds parcels for residents who are out.

T4-2084.x: The security guard received the package for me.

T4-2085.x: There's a maintenance fee bill in the mailbox.

T4-2086.ex: 나갈 때 현관문을 꼭 잠가 주세요.
T4-2086.x: Please make sure to lock the front door when you leave.
T4-2086.e: 현관 'entryway', where Koreans take off their shoes, plus 문 'door'.
T4-2086.t: Most Korean front doors have a 도어락, a keypad lock, so people rarely carry house keys.

T4-2087.ex: 누가 초인종을 눌러서 문을 열어 봤어요.
T4-2087.x: Someone rang the doorbell, so I opened the door.

T4-2088.x: The weather was nice, so I dried the laundry on the balcony.
T4-2088.e: From English 'balcony'. In Korean apartments it is usually enclosed with windows.

T4-2089.x: We keep old things in the basement.
T4-2089.t: 반지하 'half-basement' apartments are cheap housing, made famous abroad by the film Parasite.

T4-2090.m: housekeeping, running a household; household finances, livelihood
T4-2090.x: After getting married, I started keeping house for the first time.
T4-2090.e: Probably from 살리다 'to keep alive': the work that keeps a household going.
T4-2090.t: 살림을 차리다 means 'to set up house', often as a new couple.

T4-2091.x: My husband usually does the weekend grocery shopping.
T4-2091.e: From 장을 보다, literally 'to see the market': to go food shopping.
T4-2091.t: As a verb, say 장을 보다 (장 보러 가요), not 장보기를 하다, in everyday speech.

T4-2092.ex: 집 근처 식료품점에서 우유와 빵을 샀어요.
T4-2092.x: I bought milk and bread at a grocery store near my house.
T4-2092.t: Pronounced [싱뇨품점] by nasalization; in speech, 마트 is far more common.

T4-2093.ex: 재래시장에 가면 채소를 싸게 살 수 있어요.
T4-2093.x: If you go to a traditional market, you can buy vegetables cheaply.
T4-2093.t: The official term is now 전통 시장, but many people still say 재래시장.

T4-2094.ex: 명절 전에는 전통 시장이 사람들로 붐벼요.
T4-2094.x: Before the holidays, traditional markets are packed with people.

T4-2095.x: I bought household goods all at once at a discount store.
T4-2095.t: Pronounced [하린점]: the ㄹ carries over to the next syllable.

T4-2096.e: Literally 'sell all together': selling in bulk.

T4-2097.ex: 이 회사는 도매와 소매를 모두 하고 있어요.
T4-2097.x: This company does both wholesale and retail.
T4-2097.e: Literally 'sell small': selling in small quantities.
T4-2097.t: Homonym warning: the native word 소매 means 'sleeve'.

T4-2098.m: direct trade (without a middleman); in-person deal
T4-2098.x: I bought apples directly from the farmer.
T4-2098.e: 직 'direct' plus 거래 'trade', literally 'going and coming'.
T4-2098.t: Pronounced [직꺼래]. On secondhand apps it means meeting in person rather than shipping.

T4-2099.x: There's a flea market in the park every weekend.
T4-2099.e: Native 벼룩 'flea' plus 시장 'market': a direct translation of the English phrase.

T4-2100.x: I haggled over the price with the lady at the market.
T4-2100.e: Used with 하다; a classic traditional-market skill, together with asking for 덤.
T4-2100.t: To ask for a lower price, say 좀 깎아 주세요 'please give me a discount'.

T4-2101.m: a little extra thrown in for free, bonus
T4-2101.ex: 사과를 샀더니 할머니가 하나를 덤으로 주셨어요.
T4-2101.x: When I bought apples, the grandma gave me one extra for free.
T4-2101.e: A real market custom: sellers add a little extra to keep customers coming back.
T4-2101.t: Markets give 덤; restaurants call a free extra 서비스.

T4-2102.ex: 에누리 좀 해 주시면 두 개 살게요.
T4-2102.x: If you give me a little off, I'll buy two.
T4-2102.e: Two senses: knocking down a price, or padding the truth.
T4-2102.t: 에누리 없다 means 'no haggling, fixed price' or 'no exaggeration, exactly as stated'.

T4-2103.x: I got ripped off on the taxi fare at a tourist spot.
T4-2103.e: Originally a gourd bowl; why 'wearing the bowl' means getting ripped off is uncertain.
T4-2103.t: The victim 쓰다 'wears' the 바가지; the seller 씌우다 'puts it on' them.

T4-2104.x: Those shoes are already sold out.
T4-2104.t: 품절 is for goods; for tickets and seats, 매진 is more common.

T4-2105.ex: 죄송하지만 그 사이즈는 지금 재고가 없어요.
T4-2105.x: Sorry, but we don't have that size in stock right now.
T4-2105.t: Homonym warning: 재고 also means 'reconsideration', as in 재고해 주세요 'please reconsider'.

T4-2106.ex: 새로 나온 상품을 가게 앞에 진열했어요.
T4-2106.x: We displayed the new products at the front of the store.
T4-2106.t: Pronounced [지녈]: the ㄴ carries over to the next syllable.

T4-2107.m: reward points (cash value), store credit; accumulated savings
T4-2107.ex: 이번 주문에서 적립금 오천 원을 사용했어요.
T4-2107.x: I used 5,000 won of store credit on this order.
T4-2107.e: Literally 'money set aside and piled up.'

T4-2108.x: If you pay with this card, you earn points.

T4-2109.ex: 생일 쿠폰을 받아서 커피를 무료로 마셨어요.
T4-2109.x: I got a birthday coupon, so I had coffee for free.

T4-2110.ex: 화장품을 사면 사은품으로 작은 가방을 줘요.
T4-2110.x: If you buy cosmetics, they give you a small bag as a free gift.
T4-2110.e: Literally 'an item to thank you for your favor' — a thank-you gift to customers.
T4-2110.t: Used for store giveaways; for a personal present, say 선물 instead.

T4-2111.ex: 짐이 많아서 포장 이사를 하기로 했어요.
T4-2111.x: I have a lot of stuff, so I decided to use a full-service mover.
T4-2111.e: Literally 'packing move' — the company does all the packing for you.
T4-2111.t: Very common in Korea; the cheaper option where you pack yourself is 일반 이사.

T4-2112.ex: 이사한 후에 주민센터에서 전입 신고를 했어요.
T4-2112.x: After moving, I registered my new address at the community center.
T4-2112.t: Legally required within 14 days of moving in Korea, and important for protecting your rental deposit.

T4-2113.ex: 마트에서 휴지와 비누 같은 생필품을 샀어요.
T4-2113.x: I bought daily necessities like toilet paper and soap at the supermarket.
T4-2113.e: Short for 생활필수품, 'goods necessary for living.'

T4-2114.ex: 세탁기에 세제를 너무 많이 넣지 마세요.
T4-2114.x: Don't put too much detergent in the washing machine.

T4-2115.m: laundry (items to be washed or cleaned)
T4-2115.x: Please come pick up your laundry tomorrow afternoon.
T4-2115.t: Pronounced [세탕물] — nasalization; it's a more formal word than everyday 빨래.

T4-2116.ex: 어제 산 셔츠에 커피 얼룩이 생겼어요.
T4-2116.x: I got a coffee stain on the shirt I bought yesterday.
T4-2116.e: Native word; it also appears in 얼룩말 'zebra,' literally a 'striped horse.'
T4-2116.t: Stains 'appear' (얼룩이 생기다) and you 'remove' them (얼룩을 지우다/빼다).

T4-2117.m: to get stained, to become blotchy
T4-2117.x: My white pants got stained because of kimchi juice.

T4-2118.x: I iron my shirts every weekend.
T4-2118.e: From 다리다 'to iron' + -질, a suffix for repeated handwork.
T4-2118.t: Don't confuse 다리다 'to iron' with 달이다 'to boil down (medicine)'; both sound like [다리다].

T4-2119.x: My grandmother is very good at sewing.
T4-2119.e: From 바늘 'needle' + -질 'handwork'; the ㄹ drops before ㅈ.

T4-2120.x: The pants were too long, so I took them in for alteration.
T4-2120.t: 수선 is mainly for clothes, shoes and bags; for machines and buildings, use 수리.

T4-2121.x: In winter, I knit scarves myself.

T4-2122.ex: 청소할 때 걸레로 바닥을 깨끗하게 닦았어요.
T4-2122.x: When I cleaned, I wiped the floor with a rag.
T4-2122.t: 걸레 is for floors; a cloth for dishes or tables is 행주, so don't mix them up.

T4-2123.x: In the morning, I swept the fallen leaves in the yard with a broom.
T4-2123.e: 비 'broom' + 자루 'handle' — a broom on a handle.
T4-2123.t: Pronounced [비짜루]; the verb that goes with it is 쓸다 'to sweep.'

T4-2124.m: phone and internet bill, telecom charges
T4-2124.ex: 이번 달 통신비가 생각보다 많이 나왔어요.
T4-2124.x: My phone bill this month was higher than I expected.

T4-2125.x: Semi-basement units have cheap rent, but they're very damp.

T4-2126.x: Rooftop rooms are hot in summer and cold in winter.
T4-2126.e: Literally 'room in the rooftop structure' — a small unit built on a building's roof.

T4-2127.ex: 서울에 처음 왔을 때 고시원에서 살았어요.
T4-2127.x: When I first came to Seoul, I lived in a gosiwon.
T4-2127.e: Literally 'exam house' — originally tiny rooms for people studying for state exams.

T4-2128.m: living on your own (away from family, cooking for yourself)
T4-2128.ex: 대학교 때부터 혼자 자취를 하고 있어요.
T4-2128.x: I've been living on my own since college.
T4-2128.t: Don't confuse with homonym 자취 'trace, track' (발자취 'footprints').

T4-2129.ex: 자취생은 보통 간단한 음식을 자주 해 먹어요.
T4-2129.x: Students living alone usually cook simple meals.

T4-2130.m: passage, traffic (people or cars going through)
T4-2130.ex: 공사 때문에 이 길은 차량 통행이 금지됐어요.
T4-2130.x: Because of construction, vehicles are banned from this road.

T4-2131.x: I usually pay highway tolls with Hi-pass.
T4-2131.e: Literally 'fee for passing through.' -료 = fee: 입장료, 수수료.

T4-2132.ex: 이 비행기는 도쿄를 경유해서 뉴욕에 가요.
T4-2132.x: This flight goes to New York via Tokyo.
T4-2132.t: Use as 'A를 경유해서' = 'via A'; at gas stations, 경유 means diesel.

T4-2133.x: A direct flight from Incheon to Chicago takes about 13 hours.
T4-2133.t: Pronounced [지캉] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

T4-2134.m: late arrival, delay (of a train, plane, etc.)
T4-2134.x: It snowed a lot, so the train arrived 30 minutes late.
T4-2134.t: Usually used as 연착되다; for a late departure, 지연되다 is more common.

T4-2135.ex: 태풍 때문에 제주행 비행기가 모두 결항됐어요.
T4-2135.x: Because of the typhoon, all flights to Jeju were cancelled.
T4-2135.e: Literally 'missing voyage' — the flight or ferry doesn't run.

T4-2136.x: Sir/Ma'am, please show your boarding pass and passport.
T4-2136.t: Pronounced [탑씅꿘] — tensing after ㅂ and in -권.

T4-2137.ex: 공항에 일찍 가서 출국 수속을 했어요.
T4-2137.x: I went to the airport early and went through departure procedures.
T4-2137.e: The parts read 'hand + continue,' which doesn't help; just learn it as 'official steps.'
T4-2137.t: Common collocations: 출국 수속, 탑승 수속, 입원 수속 — all with 수속을 밟다/하다.

T4-2138.x: In peak season, lodging costs double.
T4-2138.t: Nights are counted with 박: 2박 3일 means 'three days, two nights.'

T4-2139.ex: 여름 성수기에는 비행기 표를 구하기 어려워요.
T4-2139.x: It's hard to get plane tickets in the summer peak season.

T4-2140.ex: 비수기에 여행하면 돈을 많이 아낄 수 있어요.
T4-2140.x: If you travel in the off-season, you can save a lot of money.

T4-2141.x: When I was in college, I went backpacking in Europe.
T4-2141.t: Pronounced [배낭녀행] — an ㄴ sound is inserted before 여.

T4-2142.x: Myeongdong is always crowded with foreign tourists.

T4-2143.x: Before the trip, I made a detailed itinerary.
T4-2143.t: Pronounced [일쩡표] — ㅈ tenses after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

T4-2144.x: On Jeju Island, we rented a car and traveled all over.
T4-2144.t: Say 렌터카를 빌리다 'rent a car'; 렌트하다 is also common in speech.

T4-2145.x: You can rent bikes at this park.

T4-2146.x: Starting next month, bus fares will go up.

T4-2147.x: It's rush hour, so traffic is really backed up.
T4-2147.e: Literally 'stopping and stagnating.' Homonym warning: 정체 also means 'true identity.'
T4-2147.t: Common in traffic reports: 정체가 심하다 'heavy congestion'; in speech, 길이 막혀요 is more natural.

T4-2148.m: to take a detour, to go around; to bypass
T4-2148.x: There was an accident, so we took a detour.
T4-2148.t: Also used figuratively: 우회적으로 말하다 'to say something indirectly.'

T4-2149.x: I paid a fine for speeding yesterday.

T4-2150.ex: 건물 앞에 불법 주차한 차가 견인됐어요.
T4-2150.x: The car illegally parked in front of the building was towed.

T4-2151.x: On the highway, driving safely is the most important thing.
T4-2151.t: 운전 is what a person does; 주행 describes the vehicle's movement, as in 자율 주행 자동차.

T4-2152.x: Our team's performance has improved a lot.

T4-2153.x: The Korean team has finally advanced to the final.
T4-2153.e: Literally 'the battle that decides the winner.'

T4-2154.ex: 우리 팀은 아쉽게도 준결승에서 지고 말았어요.
T4-2154.x: Unfortunately, our team lost in the semifinal.
T4-2154.t: Rounds are counted by teams left: 16강, 8강, 4강 (= 준결승).

T4-2155.x: Our school's team made it through the qualifying round.

T4-2156.ex: 한국은 월드컵 본선에 열 번 넘게 진출했어요.
T4-2156.x: Korea has qualified for the World Cup finals more than ten times.
T4-2156.e: Literally 'main selection' — the stage after the prelims.

T4-2157.ex: 아쉽게 우승은 못 했지만 준우승을 했어요.
T4-2157.x: Sadly we didn't win, but we took second place.

T4-2158.x: That athlete set a new world record.

T4-2159.x: That athlete won a gold medal at the Olympics.

T4-2160.ex: 제 꿈은 축구 국가대표가 되는 거예요.
T4-2160.x: My dream is to play for the national soccer team.
T4-2160.t: Pronounced [국까대표]; often shortened to 국대 in casual speech.

T4-2161.x: Fifty thousand spectators gathered at the stadium.
T4-2161.t: 관중 is for sports events; for movies and concerts, use 관객.

T4-2162.x: At the end of the game, the referee called a foul.

T4-2163.x: That player committed a foul and was sent off.
T4-2163.t: Used outside sports too: 반칙이야! means 'That's not fair!' or 'No cheating!'

T4-2164.x: They scored in the second half and tied the game.

T4-2165.m: comeback, reversal (taking the lead from behind)
T4-2165.x: They made a dramatic comeback in the last minute.
T4-2165.t: Pronounced [역쩐]; 역전승 is a comeback win and 역전패 a loss after leading.

T4-2166.x: The two teams ended the game in a 1-1 draw.

T4-2167.x: Our team is on a five-game winning streak.
T4-2167.e: Literally 'wins in a row.' 연- = consecutive: 연휴, 연속.

T4-2168.x: That team finally won after ten straight losses.
T4-2168.e: Literally 'defeats in a row.' Homonym warning: another 연패 means consecutive championships.
T4-2168.t: Context decides: '3연패 달성' (achieved) means three straight titles, while '연패에 빠지다' means a losing streak.

T4-2169.x: Every morning I do some light exercises in the park.

T4-2170.x: My younger sibling came in first at the school track meet.
T4-2170.e: Literally 'on land' — sports on land, as opposed to swimming.

T4-2171.ex: 이번 주말에 친구들과 설악산 등반을 해요.
T4-2171.x: This weekend I'm climbing Seoraksan with friends.
T4-2171.t: 등산 is everyday hiking; 등반 suggests a serious climb, like Everest or rock walls.

T4-2172.ex: 요즘은 수상 레저를 즐기는 사람이 많아요.
T4-2172.x: These days, a lot of people enjoy water sports.
T4-2172.e: From English 'leisure'; in Korean it usually means active outdoor sports.

T4-2173.x: Every weekend I play tennis with other tennis enthusiasts.
T4-2173.e: Literally 'people who like the same thing.'

T4-2174.ex: 명절에는 친지들이 모두 할머니 댁에 모여요.
T4-2174.x: On holidays, all our relatives gather at Grandma's house.

T4-2175.ex: 결혼식 날짜는 양가 부모님과 상의해서 정했어요.
T4-2175.x: We set the wedding date after talking it over with both sets of parents.

T4-2176.m: formal meeting between the families of an engaged couple
T4-2176.x: Next month our families are meeting formally.
T4-2176.t: Pronounced [상견녜] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㄴ.

T4-2177.x: I went to the funeral hall to pay my respects.
T4-2177.t: At a Korean funeral hall, wear dark clothes and bring condolence money in a white envelope.

T4-2178.x: Grandfather's funeral will be held over three days.
T4-2178.t: Pronounced [장녜]; you 'hold' a funeral with 장례를 치르다.

T4-2179.m: arranged blind date (with marriage in mind)
T4-2179.x: I went on a marriage-minded blind date set up by my mom's friend.
T4-2179.e: 맞- 'facing each other' + 선, as in 선을 보다 'to size someone up for marriage.'
T4-2179.t: Use with 보다: 맞선을 보다. 소개팅 is the casual, no-pressure version.

T4-2180.x: My parents met through a matchmaker and got married.

T4-2181.m: compatibility (of a couple, by fortune-telling); good match
T4-2181.x: I had a fortune-teller check my compatibility with my boyfriend.
T4-2181.e: Traditionally read from a couple's birth dates; now also used jokingly for any good combination.

T4-2182.x: We sent a gift to our child's in-laws for the holiday.
T4-2182.e: English has no one word for this: the two sets of parents of a married couple.
T4-2182.t: The idiom 사돈 남 말 하네 means 'look who's talking.'

T4-2183.m: husband's family, in-laws' home (from the wife's view)
T4-2183.ex: 이번 추석에는 시댁에 먼저 가기로 했어요.
T4-2183.x: This Chuseok, we decided to visit my husband's family first.
T4-2183.e: 시- marks the husband's side: 시어머니, 시아버지; -댁 is the polite word for 'house.'
T4-2183.t: Only a wife says 시댁; a husband calls his wife's family 처가.

T4-2184.m: wife's family, in-laws' home (from the husband's view)
T4-2184.x: I visited my wife's family with her over the weekend.
T4-2184.e: Literally 'wife's house.' 처- marks the wife's side: 처남, 처제.
T4-2184.t: The polite form is 처가댁; 처갓집 is a common everyday variant.

T4-2185.m: a married woman's parents' home; her birth family
T4-2185.x: I visited my parents' home with my husband for the holiday.
T4-2185.e: Literally 'parents' courtyard' — the home a married woman grew up in.
T4-2185.t: Used only from a married woman's point of view; her husband's family home is 시댁.

T4-2186.x: I go to see my parents-in-law every weekend.
T4-2186.e: 시- marks the husband's side: 시아버지, 시어머니, 시댁.
T4-2186.t: In polite speech, almost always add 님: 시부모님.

T4-2187.e: Literally 'elder person'. Homonym warning: another 장인 means 'craftsman'.
T4-2187.t: When talking to or about him politely, say 장인어른.

T4-2188.ex: 장모님이 해 주신 김치가 정말 맛있어요.
T4-2188.x: The kimchi my mother-in-law made is really delicious.
T4-2188.t: Say 장모님 when speaking to her or about her politely.

T4-2189.m: to support, to provide for (a family)
T4-2189.ex: 그는 혼자서 가족 다섯 명을 부양해요.
T4-2189.x: He supports a family of five on his own.
T4-2189.t: Usually appears as 가족을 부양하다; 부양가족 (dependents) shows up on tax and job forms.

T4-2190.ex: 요즘은 아빠들도 아이 양육에 많이 참여해요.
T4-2190.x: These days, dads also take a big part in raising their kids.
T4-2190.t: 육아 is the everyday word for childcare; 양육 is more formal and legal, as in 양육권 (custody).

T4-2191.x: That couple adopted a daughter last year.
T4-2191.e: Literally 'enter to be raised' — a child entering a new family.
T4-2191.t: Pronounced [이뱡]: the ㅂ carries over into the next syllable.

T4-2192.m: a devoted son, a dutiful son
T4-2192.x: Minsu is a devoted son who calls his parents every day.
T4-2192.t: Also used for products: 효자 상품 means a best-selling item that brings in lots of money.

T4-2193.m: lack of filial piety, being an undutiful child
T4-2193.x: Lying to your parents is unfilial.

T4-2194.x: My grandfather was a very patriarchal man.
T4-2194.e: 가부장 'patriarch' + -적 '-ic/-al'; -적 is hugely productive: 사회적, 경제적.

T4-2195.x: Jisu and I have been best friends since elementary school.
T4-2195.e: Built on 짝 'partner, one of a pair', as in 짝꿍 (seatmate).
T4-2195.t: Often used as 단짝 친구, 'best friend'.

T4-2196.ex: 고등학교 때는 이성 친구가 한 명도 없었어요.
T4-2196.x: In high school, I didn't have a single boyfriend or girlfriend.
T4-2196.e: Literally 'different sex'. Homonym warning: another 이성 means 'reason, rationality'.
T4-2196.t: 이성 친구 can mean a friend of the opposite sex, but often implies a boyfriend or girlfriend.

T4-2197.ex: 저는 고등학교 때 한 선배를 오래 짝사랑했어요.
T4-2197.x: In high school, I had a crush on an older student for a long time.
T4-2197.e: 짝 'one of a pair' + 사랑 'love': love coming from just one side.
T4-2197.t: Use 짝사랑하다 as a verb: 누구를 짝사랑하다 means to secretly love someone who doesn't love you back.

T4-2198.ex: 제 이상형은 잘 웃고 친절한 사람이에요.
T4-2198.x: My ideal type is someone who smiles a lot and is kind.
T4-2198.e: 이상 'ideal' + 형 'type': the kind of person you'd love to date.
T4-2198.t: A classic question on dates and TV shows: 이상형이 어떻게 되세요? 'What's your ideal type?'

T4-2199.x: My mother remarried after my father passed away.

T4-9001.m: vibrating pager, buzzer (given at cafés and food courts)
T4-9001.x: When the buzzer goes off, please come to the counter.
T4-9001.t: At most cafés and food courts you order, take a 진동벨, and pick up your order when it buzzes.

T4-9002.ex: 호텔에 세면도구가 없어서 챙겨 가야 해요.
T4-9002.x: The hotel doesn't provide toiletries, so I have to bring my own.
T4-9002.e: Literally 'wash-face tools': toothbrush, toothpaste, soap and so on.
T4-9002.t: Since 2024, larger Korean hotels may no longer give out free single-use toiletries, so it's wise to pack your own.

T4-9003.x: Breakfast is included at this hotel.
T4-9003.t: A formal word seen on hotel and menu signs (조식 뷔페, 조식 포함). In everyday talk people say 아침 or 아침밥.

T4-9004.x: She's been my best friend since high school.
T4-9004.e: Short for 절친한 친구 'very close friend'.
T4-9004.t: Casual. Similar words: 베프 (from 'best friend') and the slang 찐친 'real friend'.

T4-9005.ex: 회식 때 부장님이 소맥을 말아 주셨어요.
T4-9005.x: At the company dinner, the manager mixed somaek for us.
T4-9005.t: Casual. You 'roll' it: 소맥을 말다 'to mix somaek'.

T4-9006.ex: 술 마신 다음 날 아침에는 해장국을 먹어요.
T4-9006.x: The morning after drinking, I have hangover soup.
T4-9006.e: 해장 'easing a hangover' (from older 해정 解酲) + 국 'soup'.
T4-9006.t: Pronounced [해장꾹]. 해장하다 means 'to cure a hangover', usually with a hot soup.

T4-9007.ex: 김장할 때 젓갈을 넣으면 더 맛있어요.
T4-9007.x: When you make kimchi, adding jeotgal makes it tastier.
T4-9007.e: From 젓, salted and fermented fish, shrimp or shellfish.
T4-9007.t: Pronounced [젇깔]. 새우젓 (salted shrimp) and 멸치젓 (salted anchovy) are used in kimchi.

T4-9008.ex: 주말에 친구랑 카페 투어를 가기로 했어요.
T4-9008.x: My friend and I decided to go café hopping this weekend.
T4-9008.e: From English 'café' + 'tour'; English speakers say 'café hopping'.
T4-9008.t: Pretty interiors and desserts get photographed and shared on social media.

T4-9009.m: words of blessing, good wishes (esp. at New Year)
T4-9009.x: On Lunar New Year's Day, my grandfather gave us his good wishes.
T4-9009.t: Pronounced [덕땀]. Elders give 덕담 after the New Year's bow (세배), e.g. 올해도 건강해라.

T4-9010.x: Have a happy Chuseok with your family.
T4-9010.e: Native word: 한 'great' + 가위, an old word for the 15th day of the eighth lunar month.
T4-9010.t: Common in greetings and in the saying 더도 말고 덜도 말고 한가위만 같아라 'no more, no less — may every day be like Hangawi'.

T4-9011.x: Gyeongbokgung is a palace built in the Joseon era.
T4-9011.e: Literally 'morning freshness', the source of the phrase 'Land of the Morning Calm'.
T4-9011.t: 조선 시대 = the Joseon era, the setting of most historical dramas. It was renamed the Korean Empire (대한제국) in 1897.

T4-9012.x: On Lunar New Year I flew kites with the kids in the park.
T4-9012.t: A classic Lunar New Year folk game. The traditional rectangular kite (방패연) has a round hole in the middle.

T4-9013.ex: 어렸을 때 친구들이랑 공기놀이를 자주 했어요.
T4-9013.x: When I was little, I often played gonggi with my friends.
T4-9013.t: Played with five small pebbles or plastic pieces: you toss one up and pick up the others before catching it.

T4-9014.x: On Chuseok I watched a ssireum tournament with my family.
T4-9014.e: Native word. The top champion of a big tournament is called 천하장사 'strongest under heaven'.
T4-9014.t: Wrestlers grip each other's cloth thigh band (샅바) and win by making the opponent touch the sand with any body part above the knee.

T4-9015.x: Our class won the tug-of-war at the school sports day.
T4-9015.e: 줄 'rope' + 다리기, from an old verb meaning 'to pull' (now 당기다).
T4-9015.t: A staple of school sports days (운동회). Also used figuratively for a tug-of-war between two sides, as in negotiations.

T4-9016.x: My nephew grabbed a pencil at his doljabi.
T4-9016.t: At a 돌잔치 the baby picks one item from a table: thread means long life, money means wealth, and a pencil means studiousness.

T4-9017.ex: 시험 날 수험표와 신분증을 꼭 챙기세요.
T4-9017.x: On exam day, be sure to bring your admission ticket and ID.
T4-9017.e: Literally 'take-exam ticket', the slip given to each 수험생 (exam taker).
T4-9017.t: After the 수능, many shops, restaurants and cinemas give students discounts if they show their 수험표.

T4-9018.m: yeot (sticky taffy, given for luck before exams)
T4-9018.ex: 수능 보는 친구한테 합격하라고 엿을 선물했어요.
T4-9018.x: I gave yeot to a friend taking the CSAT so they'd pass.
T4-9018.e: Native word for a chewy candy made from grain and malt.
T4-9018.t: Given before exams because 붙다 'to stick' also means 'to pass (an exam)'. Careful: 엿 먹어 is a rude insult.

T4-9019.m: visit (to a soldier, patient or inmate)
T4-9019.ex: 주말에 군대에 있는 동생 면회를 갔어요.
T4-9019.x: On the weekend I went to visit my younger brother in the army.
T4-9019.t: Used for visits to the army, a hospital or a prison. 면회 시간 = visiting hours.

T4-9020.x: The agency announced news of a new album.
T4-9020.e: 소속 'belonging to' + 사 'company': the company an artist belongs to.
T4-9020.t: Pronounced [소속싸]. News reports often quote 소속사 측 'the agency side'.

T4-9021.ex: 그 그룹의 팬덤은 전 세계에 있어요.
T4-9021.x: That group has a fandom all over the world.
T4-9021.t: Most K-pop groups have an official name for their fandom.

T4-9022.ex: 콘서트에 갈 때 응원봉을 꼭 챙겨 가요.
T4-9022.x: I always bring my light stick when I go to a concert.
T4-9022.t: Each group has its own official design. At concerts the sticks can be synced to light up in patterns.

T4-9023.x: My favorite in this group is the youngest member.
T4-9023.t: Casual fan slang. Your second favorite is 차애 (次愛 'next love').

T4-9024.x: I stood in line at the concert venue to buy merch.
T4-9024.e: From English 'goods'; in Korean it means fan merchandise.
T4-9024.t: Typical items are photo cards (포토카드), slogan towels and light sticks. 공식 굿즈 = official merch.

T4-9025.ex: 팬 사인회에서 좋아하는 멤버와 눈을 마주쳤어요.
T4-9025.x: At the fan signing, I made eye contact with my favorite member.
T4-9025.t: Spots are often given by lottery based on album purchases, so fans buy many copies.

T4-9026.ex: 티켓팅에 성공해서 콘서트에 갈 수 있게 됐어요.
T4-9026.x: I succeeded in getting tickets, so now I can go to the concert.
T4-9026.e: From English 'ticketing'. Konglish: the race to grab tickets the moment online sales open.
T4-9026.t: A brutal one is jokingly called 피켓팅 (피 'blood' + 티켓팅), 'bloody ticketing'.

T4-9027.ex: 콘서트에서 팬들이 떼창을 해서 정말 감동했어요.
T4-9027.x: I was really moved when the fans sang along together at the concert.
T4-9027.t: Korean audiences are known for singing along to whole songs, even in English, at concerts by foreign artists.

T4-9028.ex: 이번 주 음방에서 신곡 무대를 처음 공개해요.
T4-9028.x: They're revealing the new song's stage for the first time on a music show this week.
T4-9028.e: Short for 음악 방송 'music broadcast', taking the first syllable of each word.
T4-9028.t: Casual fan word. Weekly music shows feature live K-pop stages and give a weekly 1위 (No. 1) trophy.

T4-9029.m: fancam, focused video of one performer
T4-9029.ex: 무대 직캠 조회수가 벌써 백만이 넘었어요.
T4-9029.x: The fancam of the stage already has over a million views.
T4-9029.e: 직(접) 'directly, in person' + 캠 from English 'cam(corder)'.
T4-9029.t: Originally footage shot by fans; music shows now also upload official 개인 직캠 that follow each member.

T4-9030.m: chart reversal, an old song climbing the charts again later; driving the wrong way
T4-9030.ex: 몇 년 전 노래가 갑자기 역주행해서 1위를 했어요.
T4-9030.x: A song from a few years ago suddenly climbed back up the charts and hit No. 1.
T4-9030.e: Literally 'running in reverse'; originally driving against traffic.
T4-9030.t: Pronounced [역쭈행]. It often happens after a fan video goes viral; the verb is 역주행하다.

T4-9031.ex: 이번 노래는 포인트 안무가 쉬워서 다들 따라 해요.
T4-9031.x: The signature move of this song is easy, so everyone copies it.
T4-9031.t: Usually the catchy move in the chorus (후렴) that fans copy.

T4-9032.ex: 주말마다 친구들이랑 커버 댄스 영상을 찍어요.
T4-9032.x: Every weekend I film cover dance videos with my friends.
T4-9032.e: From English 'cover' + 'dance': copying an existing song's choreography, like a cover song.
T4-9032.t: Popular with K-pop fans worldwide; dance studios run classes for it, and people film 커버 댄스 in public places.

T4-9033.ex: 신곡 챌린지 영상이 SNS에서 유행하고 있어요.
T4-9033.x: Challenge videos for the new song are trending on social media.
T4-9033.t: In K-pop, singers post a short clip of a new song's 포인트 안무, often with other stars, and fans join in. 챌린지에 참여하다 = to take part in a challenge.

T4-9034.ex: 그 가수는 오 년 동안 연습생으로 지냈어요.
T4-9034.x: That singer spent five years as a trainee.
T4-9034.t: Pronounced [연습쌩]. K-pop trainees often train for years in singing, dancing and languages before they debut.

T4-9035.x: He started out as a trainee at a big agency.
T4-9035.t: Pronounced [기획싸]. For the agency a particular star belongs to, 소속사 is more common.

T4-9036.x: Many groups debuted through survival shows.
T4-9036.e: From English 'survival' + 'program'; English usually says 'competition show'.
T4-9036.t: Contestants are eliminated round by round, often by viewer votes (투표), and the finalists debut together as a group.

T4-9037.m: to be eliminated, to drop out
T4-9037.x: Sadly, the trainee I was rooting for was eliminated.
T4-9037.t: Pronounced [탈라카다]. Takes 에서: 예선에서 탈락하다 'to be eliminated in the preliminaries'.

T4-9038.ex: 예고편만 봐도 정말 재미있을 것 같아요.
T4-9038.x: Just from the trailer, it looks really fun.
T4-9038.t: On TV, the 예고편 for the next episode plays right after the credits.

T4-9039.ex: 스포일러를 볼까 봐 댓글을 안 읽어요.
T4-9039.x: I don't read the comments in case I see spoilers.
T4-9039.e: From English 'spoiler'; usually shortened to 스포.
T4-9039.t: Casual: 스포하지 마! 'Don't spoil it!' 스포 주의 'spoiler alert' appears at the top of posts.

T4-9040.x: A love triangle has started in the drama, and it's so frustrating.
T4-9040.t: Pronounced [삼각꽌계]. A staple plot device of romantic K-dramas.

T4-9041.x: She resolved to take revenge for her family.
T4-9041.t: Homonym: 복수 (複數) also means 'plural'. A revenge drama is called a 복수극.

T4-9042.ex: 주말에 가볍게 볼 로코 좀 추천해 주세요.
T4-9042.x: Please recommend a light rom-com to watch on the weekend.
T4-9042.e: Clipped from 로맨틱 코미디 'romantic comedy', like English 'rom-com'.
T4-9042.t: Casual. 로코 장인 'rom-com master' is praise for an actor known for the genre.

T4-9043.x: In historical dramas, the actors appear in hanbok.
T4-9043.t: Most 사극 are set in the Joseon dynasty (조선), with palace scenes and old-style speech.

T4-9044.ex: 밤에 혼자 스릴러를 보니까 좀 무서웠어요.
T4-9044.x: Watching a thriller alone at night was a bit scary.
T4-9044.t: Crime thrillers are a strong Korean genre. For horror, Koreans say 공포 영화.

T4-9045.m: weekend drama (family drama aired on weekends)
T4-9045.ex: 우리 부모님은 주말 드라마를 꼭 챙겨 보세요.
T4-9045.x: My parents never miss the weekend drama.
T4-9045.t: Long-running family dramas, often 50 episodes or more, aired on weekend evenings. They draw many older viewers and high ratings.

T4-9046.ex: 요즘은 연애 리얼리티 프로그램이 인기가 많아요.
T4-9046.x: Dating reality shows are very popular these days.
T4-9046.t: Usually followed by 프로그램 or 쇼. 관찰 예능 'observational variety' is a related genre that follows celebrities' daily lives. On its own it often means 'realism': 리얼리티가 떨어지다 = to feel unrealistic.

T4-9047.ex: 생일에 친구들이 몰래카메라를 해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
T4-9047.x: My friends pulled a hidden camera prank on my birthday, and I was really surprised.
T4-9047.t: Often shortened to 몰카. Careful: 몰카 also means an illegal spy camera used to film people without consent, a serious crime in Korea.

T4-9048.ex: 요즘은 영화를 극장보다 오티티로 더 많이 봐요.
T4-9048.x: These days I watch movies on streaming services more than at the theater.
T4-9048.e: The English letters OTT ('over-the-top') read in Korean.
T4-9048.t: Usually written OTT. 구독하다 = to subscribe to a service.

T4-9049.m: binge-watching (a series from start to finish)
T4-9049.ex: 주말 동안 드라마 한 시즌을 정주행했어요.
T4-9049.x: I binge-watched a whole season of a drama over the weekend.
T4-9049.e: Literally 'driving in the right direction': watching straight through from episode 1, the opposite of 역주행.
T4-9049.t: The verb is 정주행하다; also used for reading a whole webtoon from the start.

T4-9050.m: to binge-watch, to watch many episodes at once
T4-9050.x: I binge-watched all the drama episodes I'd missed over the weekend.
T4-9050.e: 몰다 'to herd, gather together' + 보다 'to watch'.
T4-9050.t: Also written 몰아 보다. Same pattern: 몰아서 하다 'to do it all at once'.

T4-9051.x: I saw a play at a small theater in Daehangno.
T4-9051.t: Pronounced [소극짱]. Seoul's 대학로 is packed with 소극장 showing plays and small musicals.

T4-9052.ex: 주말에 대학로에서 연극을 한 편 봤어요.
T4-9052.x: I saw a play in Daehangno on the weekend.
T4-9052.e: Literally 'university road'; Seoul National University's campus was here until 1975.
T4-9052.t: Pronounced [대항노]. The streets around Hyehwa Station are packed with small theaters, so it's the place to see plays.

T4-9053.ex: 공연이 끝나자 관객들이 기립 박수를 보냈어요.
T4-9053.x: When the show ended, the audience gave a standing ovation.
T4-9053.t: Pronounced [기립빡쑤]. Give one is 기립 박수를 치다/보내다; get one is 기립 박수를 받다.

T4-9054.ex: 장구 소리에 맞춰서 다 같이 춤을 췄어요.
T4-9054.x: We all danced together to the sound of the janggu.
T4-9054.e: From 장고 (杖鼓 'stick drum'), the older name still used by musicians.
T4-9054.t: Played with a thin stick on one head and a mallet or bare hand on the other; play it is 장구를 치다.

T4-9055.x: I saw a singer busking in front of Hongdae.
T4-9055.t: 버스킹하다 = to busk; the performer is a 버스커. Buskers often need a permit for popular spots.

T4-9056.x: If you have any song requests, please let me know.
T4-9056.t: Radio DJs and buskers often ask 신청곡 있으세요? 'Any requests?'

T4-9057.x: That webtoon comes out every Tuesday.
T4-9057.t: 연재하다 = to serialize; 연재되다 = to be serialized; 연재 중 = currently running.

T4-9058.x: The webtoon I was reading has finally ended.
T4-9058.t: 완결되다 or 완결이 나다 = (a series) ends; 완결작 = a finished series, perfect for reading in one go.
