T4-9059.x: This artist's drawing style is really pretty.
T4-9059.e: Native 그림 'picture, drawing' + 체 'style' (as in 글씨체 'handwriting').
T4-9059.t: The everyday word for comics and webtoons; 화풍 is the formal term for a painter's style.

T4-9060.ex: 다음 화가 궁금해서 미리 보기를 결제했어요.
T4-9060.x: I wanted to know what happens next, so I paid for early access.
T4-9060.t: On webtoon platforms you pay a small fee to read episodes before their free release; it also means a file or image preview.

T4-9061.ex: 사진을 올릴 때 해시태그를 꼭 달아요.
T4-9061.x: I always add hashtags when I post photos.
T4-9061.t: Add one is 해시태그를 달다/붙이다; Koreans read the # sign as 샵 ('sharp').

T4-9062.ex: 오늘 밤 아홉 시에 라이브 방송을 할게요.
T4-9062.x: I'll do a livestream tonight at nine.
T4-9062.t: Casually shortened to 라방; 라방을 켜다 = to go live.

T4-9063.m: proof shot, photo to prove you were there or did something
T4-9063.x: Whenever I go to a famous restaurant, I always take a photo to prove it.
T4-9063.t: Casual. On election day many people post a 투표 인증샷 'I voted' photo.

T4-9064.ex: 자취생을 위한 요리 꿀팁 좀 알려 주세요.
T4-9064.x: Please share some cooking tips for people living alone.
T4-9064.e: 꿀 'honey' + English 'tip'; slang 꿀- means 'sweet, great'.
T4-9064.t: Casual. The same 꿀- appears in 꿀잼 'super fun' and 꿀잠 'sweet sleep'.

T4-9065.x: Watching mukbang at night makes me hungry.
T4-9065.e: 먹(다) 'to eat' + 방(송) 'broadcast'; now borrowed into English as 'mukbang'.
T4-9065.t: Pronounced [먹빵]. Jokingly, 먹방 찍었어요 means 'I really pigged out.'

T4-9066.x: My old classmates and I made a new group chat.
T4-9066.t: Pronounced [단톡빵]. Casual, often just 단톡. Leaving one is 단톡방을 나가다.

T4-9067.ex: 요즘 줄임말이 너무 많아서 무슨 뜻인지 모르겠어요.
T4-9067.x: There are so many abbreviations these days that I don't know what they mean.
T4-9067.t: Korean often keeps the first syllable of each part: 프로필 사진 → 프사, 단체 톡방 → 단톡방.

T4-9068.x: I was writing in a hurry, so I made a lot of typos.
T4-9068.t: A typo happens is 오타가 나다; fix one is 오타를 고치다/수정하다.

T4-9069.ex: 저는 요즘 취준생이라서 매일 도서관에 가요.
T4-9069.x: I'm job hunting these days, so I go to the library every day.
T4-9069.e: Short for 취(업) 준(비)생 'person preparing for employment'.
T4-9069.t: Informal but widely used, even in news; many build up 스펙 'qualifications' like test scores and certificates.

T4-9070.ex: 쓰레기는 꼭 종량제 봉투에 담아서 버려야 해요.
T4-9070.x: You have to put your trash in an official pay-per-bag trash bag before throwing it out.
T4-9070.e: 종량제 'volume-based fee system' (literally 'system following the amount') + 봉투 'bag'.
T4-9070.t: Pronounced [종냥제 봉투]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ. General waste must go out in these bags, sold at convenience stores and supermarkets; each city or district has its own design, so bags from another area may not be accepted.

T4-9071.ex: 일 년에 한 번은 치과에서 스케일링을 받아요.
T4-9071.x: I get my teeth cleaned at the dentist once a year.
T4-9071.e: From English 'scaling' (removing tartar); in Korean it is the everyday word for a dental cleaning.
T4-9071.t: Use 스케일링을 받다 'to get a cleaning'. National health insurance covers one scaling a year for adults, so it is cheap.

T4-9072.m: reading room, study room (in a library)
T4-9072.ex: 시험 기간이라서 도서관 열람실에 자리가 없어요.
T4-9072.x: It's exam period, so there are no seats in the library reading room.
T4-9072.t: In Korean libraries it is mainly where students study with their own books; seats are often booked at a kiosk, and silence is strictly kept.

T4-9073.x: I attached the report file to the email.
T4-9073.t: Common email line: 첨부 파일을 확인해 주세요 'Please see the attached file.'

T4-9074.m: reply, response (formal, e.g. to an email)
T4-9074.t: A formal word for business emails and official letters; with friends use 답장.

T4-9075.x: I sent the email with the team leader cc'd too.
T4-9075.t: In Korean email apps the cc field is labelled 참조, and bcc is 숨은 참조 'hidden cc'. In documents it means 'see': 3쪽 참조 'see page 3'.

T4-9076.x: I put the baby in the stroller and took a walk in the park.
T4-9076.t: 'Push a stroller' is 유모차를 밀다; 'put a baby in' is 태우다, the same verb as giving someone a ride.

T4-9077.ex: 졸업식 날 학사모를 쓰고 가족과 사진을 찍었어요.
T4-9077.x: On graduation day I wore my cap and took photos with my family.
T4-9077.t: Pronounced [학싸모]: ㅅ becomes tense after ㄱ. Like other hats it takes 쓰다 'to wear'; graduates often throw their caps in the air (학사모를 던지다).

T4-9078.ex: 지진 때문에 휴대폰에 재난 문자가 왔어요.
T4-9078.x: I got an emergency alert text on my phone because of an earthquake.
T4-9078.t: Pronounced [재난 문짜]: the ㅈ in 문자 is said tense. Phones in Korea receive these government alerts automatically, often with a loud alarm, for earthquakes, heavy rain, heat waves or missing persons.

T4-9079.ex: 텐트를 칠 필요가 없어서 글램핑이 편해요.
T4-9079.x: Glamping is convenient because you don't have to pitch a tent.
T4-9079.t: Korean glamping sites usually provide a ready-made tent with beds, heating and a barbecue grill, so you just bring food.

T4-9080.ex: 밤에 추워서 침낭 안에 들어가서 잤어요.
T4-9080.x: It was cold at night, so I slept inside my sleeping bag.

T4-9081.ex: 모닥불 앞에 앉아서 고구마를 구워 먹었어요.
T4-9081.x: We sat by the campfire and roasted sweet potatoes.
T4-9081.e: Native word for a fire of gathered twigs and wood; 불 = fire.
T4-9081.t: Pronounced [모닥뿔]: ㅂ becomes tense after ㄱ. 'Make a campfire' is 모닥불을 피우다.

T4-9082.x: We bought firewood at the campsite and made a fire.
T4-9082.e: Literally 'long chopped (wood)': logs cut into lengths and split.
T4-9082.t: 'Burn firewood' is 장작을 때다, and a wood fire is 장작불.

T4-9083.ex: 이 노래는 고음이 어려워서 노래방에서 못 불러요.
T4-9083.x: The high notes in this song are hard, so I can't sing it at karaoke.
T4-9083.e: Literally 'high sound'; the opposite is 저음 'low sound'.
T4-9083.t: 'Hit a high note' is 고음을 내다; 고음이 안 올라가요 means 'I can't reach the high notes.'

T4-9084.ex: 노래방에 가면 제 애창곡을 꼭 불러요.
T4-9084.x: Whenever I go to karaoke, I always sing my go-to song.
T4-9084.e: Literally 'loved singing tune': 애 'love' + 창 'sing' + 곡 'tune'.
T4-9084.t: Casually people say 18번 (십팔번) 'my number 18' for the same idea.

T4-9085.m: tone-deaf person, someone who can't sing in tune
T4-9085.x: I'm tone-deaf, so I get embarrassed when we go to karaoke.
T4-9085.e: Literally 'sound fool'; -치 'fool' also gives 몸치 'bad dancer' and 길치 'someone with no sense of direction'.
T4-9085.t: Usually said jokingly about oneself. Someone with no sense of rhythm is a 박치.

T4-9086.ex: 야구장에서 팬들이 다 같이 응원가를 불러요.
T4-9086.x: At the ballpark, the fans all sing the cheering songs together.
T4-9086.t: At Korean baseball games each player has his own 응원가, sung by the whole stand and led by the cheering squad.

T4-9087.ex: 자유이용권이 있으면 놀이기구를 마음껏 탈 수 있어요.
T4-9087.x: With an all-day pass you can go on as many rides as you like.
T4-9087.t: Pronounced [자유이용꿘]: 권 is said tense, as in 입장권 [입짱꿘]. A cheaper 입장권 only gets you in, and rides cost extra.

T4-9088.m: best photo ever (of oneself), photo of a lifetime
T4-9088.ex: 바다 앞에서 친구가 제 인생샷을 찍어 줬어요.
T4-9088.x: My friend took the best photo of my life in front of the sea.
T4-9088.e: 인생 'life' + 샷 from English 'shot': the best shot of your life.
T4-9088.t: Casual. A spot with a great backdrop is an 인생샷 명소, and finally getting that photo is 인생샷을 건지다.

T4-9089.ex: 사진을 너무 많이 보정해서 제 얼굴 같지 않아요.
T4-9089.x: I edited the photo so much that it doesn't look like my face.
T4-9089.t: 보정 앱 is a photo-editing app. Outside photos, 보정 속옷 means shapewear.

T4-9090.x: Could you change the grill plate, please?
T4-9090.t: At Korean BBQ places staff replace a charred plate for free when you ask; 불판을 갈다 is the set phrase.

T4-9091.x: Rice cakes made with glutinous rice are really chewy.
T4-9091.e: 찰- 'sticky' + 쌀 'rice'; the ㅂ is a trace of the old form of 쌀 (ᄡᆞᆯ).
T4-9091.t: The prefix 찰- marks sticky varieties of other foods too: 찰옥수수 'waxy corn', 찰보리 'sticky barley'.

T4-9092.m: injeolmi (sticky rice cake coated in bean powder)
T4-9092.ex: 할머니가 직접 만든 인절미를 보내 주셨어요.
T4-9092.x: Grandma sent us injeolmi she made herself.
T4-9092.e: Origin uncertain; a popular legend says King Injo named it after a Mr. Im (임) who offered it to him.
T4-9092.t: Its roasted soybean powder flavor is also used in modern desserts like 인절미 빙수 and 인절미 토스트.

T4-9093.x: I got a box of traditional Korean sweets as a Lunar New Year gift.
T4-9093.e: Literally 'Korean confection'; a general name for traditional sweets such as 약과 and 유과.
T4-9093.t: Most 한과 are fried, pressed or candied with honey or grain syrup rather than baked.

T4-9094.ex: 약과는 달아서 차랑 같이 먹으면 좋아요.
T4-9094.x: Yakgwa is sweet, so it goes well with tea.
T4-9094.e: Literally 'medicine confection': honey was regarded as medicinal (약), as in 약식 'sweet rice with honey'.
T4-9094.t: Pronounced [약꽈]: ㄱ after ㄱ becomes tense. It had a big retro boom among young Koreans around 2022–2023.

T4-9095.ex: 식사 후에 시원한 수정과 한 잔 어때요?
T4-9095.x: How about a glass of cold sujeonggwa after the meal?
T4-9095.e: Sino-Korean 水正果: 수 'water' + 정 'proper' + 과 'fruit, confection'.
T4-9095.t: A sweet drink of cinnamon and ginger, served cold with dried persimmon and pine nuts; like 식혜, it is a classic after-meal drink.

T4-9096.ex: 저는 비건이라서 고기랑 우유를 안 먹어요.
T4-9096.x: I'm vegan, so I don't eat meat or drink milk.
T4-9096.t: Often used before nouns: 비건 식당 'vegan restaurant', 비건 화장품 'vegan cosmetics'. The general word for a vegetarian is 채식주의자.

T4-9097.ex: 부처님 오신 날에 절에 가서 연등을 달았어요.
T4-9097.x: On Buddha's Birthday, I went to a temple and hung a lantern.
T4-9097.e: Literally 'burning lamp'. The 연 is 'burn', not 연꽃 'lotus', even though many lanterns are lotus-shaped.
T4-9097.t: Every spring Seoul holds 연등회, a lantern festival and parade, ahead of Buddha's Birthday.

T4-9098.x: On Buddha's Birthday, I went to a temple with my family.
T4-9098.t: Pronounced [석까탄시닐]: ㄱ after ㄱ becomes tense. A public holiday on the 8th day of the 4th lunar month; since 2017 its official name is 부처님 오신 날.

T4-9099.m: wooden floor; open wooden-floored hall (in a hanok)
T4-9099.ex: 더운 날에는 마루에 누워서 낮잠을 자요.
T4-9099.x: On hot days, I lie on the wooden floor and take a nap.
T4-9099.e: Native word for a raised wooden floor; 대청마루 is the big central hall of a hanok.
T4-9099.t: In a hanok, the 마루 stays cool in summer while 온돌 rooms keep you warm in winter. In modern homes 마루 also means wood flooring.

T4-9100.x: Buddhism flourished greatly in the Goryeo period.
T4-9100.e: Its characters mean 'high' and 'beautiful', but the name is a shortened form of 고구려, whose successor Goryeo claimed to be.
T4-9100.t: The English name 'Korea' comes from 고려, via the name used by foreign traders.

T4-9101.ex: 삼국 시대에는 고구려, 백제, 신라가 있었어요.
T4-9101.x: In the Three Kingdoms period, there were Goguryeo, Baekje and Silla.
T4-9101.e: Literally 'three countries era': 고구려, 백제 and 신라, traditionally dated 57 BC–AD 668.
T4-9101.t: Pronounced [삼국씨대]: ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense. Silla's victory in 668 began the Unified Silla (통일 신라) period.

T4-9102.x: The instructor taught me kicks in detail.
T4-9102.t: Students call the instructor 사범님 directly; the head of the gym is 관장님.

T4-9103.x: I put on my uniform and tied my belt tightly.
T4-9103.t: Taekwondo 도복 are white; the color of the belt (띠) shows your rank.

T4-9104.ex: 삼 년 만에 드디어 검은띠를 땄어요.
T4-9104.x: After three years, I finally earned my black belt.
T4-9104.t: You 'earn' one with 따다: 검은띠를 따다. Black-belt ranks are counted in 단 (1단, 2단…); children under 15 get a half red, half black 품띠 instead.

T4-9105.x: I sparred with a friend in class today.
T4-9105.t: Taekwondo training has two main parts, 겨루기 (sparring) and 품새 (forms); Olympic taekwondo is 겨루기.

T4-9106.m: saju, fortune read from one's birth date and hour
T4-9106.x: At New Year, I went with a friend to get my fortune read.
T4-9106.e: Literally 'four pillars': the year, month, day and hour of birth.
T4-9106.t: Each pillar is written with two characters, eight in all, hence the set phrase 사주팔자 'one's destiny'. 'To have it read' is 사주를 보다.

T4-9107.ex: 점쟁이가 올해 좋은 일이 생긴다고 했어요.
T4-9107.x: The fortune-teller said something good will happen this year.
T4-9107.e: 점 'fortune-telling' + -쟁이, a suffix for a person known for a trade or habit.
T4-9107.t: Pronounced [점쨍이]: ㅈ becomes tense in this compound. The word can sound slightly belittling; the place you go for a reading is a 점집.

T4-9108.x: Every morning I check my horoscope for the day on my phone.
T4-9108.e: Literally 'luck trend': the way one's fortune is going.
T4-9108.t: 신년 운세 'fortune for the new year' is popular in January; newspapers and apps often list daily fortunes by Chinese zodiac animal (띠).

T4-9109.e: 손 'hand' + 금 'line, crease' (as in 금이 가다 'to crack').
T4-9109.t: Pronounced [손끔]: ㄱ becomes tense in this compound. 'To read palms' is 손금을 보다.

T4-9110.ex: 어렸을 때 할머니가 전래 동화를 자주 읽어 주셨어요.
T4-9110.x: When I was little, my grandmother often read me traditional folk tales.
T4-9110.t: Pronounced [절래 동화]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ. Most open with 옛날 옛적에 'once upon a time'.

T4-9111.x: A fairy came down from the sky and bathed.
T4-9111.e: Literally 'immortal woman': a heavenly maiden of Taoist-flavored folklore.
T4-9111.t: Best known from the tale 선녀와 나무꾼 'The Fairy and the Woodcutter'. 선녀 같다 praises a woman as graceful and beautiful.

T4-9112.x: The lanterns made of hanji are really pretty.
T4-9112.e: Literally 'Korean paper'; made from the bark of the paper mulberry (닥나무).
T4-9112.t: Strong and breathable, it is used for crafts, lamps and doors; 한지 공예 workshops are popular with visitors.

T4-9113.x: I made a key ring with traditional knotwork.
T4-9113.e: Native word. The traditional craft of decorative cord knotting is protected as a national intangible cultural heritage (매듭장).
T4-9113.t: 매듭을 짓다 is 'to tie a knot' and also 'to wrap up (a matter)'; 매듭을 풀다 is 'to untie a knot'. Traditional 매듭 decorates 노리개 (hanbok pendants).

T4-9114.x: It's easy to catch a cold when the seasons change.
T4-9114.t: 환절기 감기 조심하세요 'watch out for colds at the change of season' is a common caring remark; the big gap between day and night temperatures gets the blame.

T4-9115.ex: 이 웹소설은 30회차까지 무료로 볼 수 있어요.
T4-9115.x: You can read this web novel for free up to episode 30.
T4-9115.t: On webtoon and web-novel platforms each numbered episode is a 회차, as in 무료 회차 'free episodes' and 유료 회차 'paid episodes'; 화 is also used, as in 1화, 2화.

T4-9116.e: Sound word (의성어) for laughter you try to hold in.
T4-9116.t: 킥킥거리다 and 킥킥대다 are common: 수업 시간에 킥킥거리다.

T4-9117.m: beaming, grinning from ear to ear
T4-9117.ex: 합격 소식에 동생이 하루 종일 싱글벙글 웃어요.
T4-9117.x: After hearing they passed, my younger sibling has been beaming all day.
T4-9117.e: Manner word (의태어) for a happy face that keeps smiling; 싱글 and 벙글 rhyme for emphasis.
T4-9117.t: Often as 싱글벙글하다: 요즘 왜 이렇게 싱글벙글해요? 'Why are you so smiley lately?'

T4-9118.m: with a sweet little smile (esp. a baby)
T4-9118.x: The baby looks at its mom and smiles sweetly.
T4-9118.e: Manner word (의태어) for a soft smile with the mouth slightly open. Dark-vowel 벙긋 is a bigger, wider smile.
T4-9118.t: Pronounced [방귿]: a final ㅅ sounds like ㄷ. 방긋방긋 means smiling again and again; 방긋거리다 also exists.

T4-9119.ex: 슬픈 영화를 보면서 동생이 훌쩍훌쩍 울었어요.
T4-9119.x: My younger sibling sniffled through the sad movie.
T4-9119.e: Sound and manner word (의성어·의태어) for sniffing and quiet sobbing. Bright-vowel 홀짝홀짝 is mostly used for sipping a drink.
T4-9119.t: Pronounced [훌쩌쿨쩍]: ㄱ + ㅎ becomes ㅋ. Verbs: 훌쩍이다, 훌쩍거리다.

T4-9120.x: When the movie ended, people all over the theater were sniffling.
T4-9120.t: Pronounced [훌쩌기다]: the final ㄱ links to the next vowel. Also for a runny nose with a cold: 코를 훌쩍이다. Same meaning: 훌쩍거리다.

T4-9121.m: (of eyes) to brim with tears, to well up
T4-9121.x: At my graduation, Mom's eyes welled up with tears.
T4-9121.e: Mimetic 글썽 'tears filling the eyes' + verb suffix -이다.
T4-9121.t: Usually 눈물을 글썽이다 or 눈에 눈물이 글썽이다. Same meaning: 글썽거리다.

T4-9122.x: The ducks are quacking in the pond.
T4-9122.e: Sound word (의성어) for a duck's quack or a shrill shout.
T4-9122.t: 꽥 alone is a sudden shriek: 소리를 꽥 지르다 'to let out a yell'.

T4-9123.x: Bees are buzzing around the flowers.
T4-9123.e: Sound word (의성어) for insects' wings, strong wind or a running machine.
T4-9123.t: 윙윙거리다 is common: 모기가 귀에서 윙윙거려요 'A mosquito is buzzing in my ear.'

T4-9124.forms: 탕 + 하고 울리다 / 소리가 나다; 탕탕 (repeated)
T4-9124.ex: 밖에서 갑자기 탕 하고 총소리가 났어요.
T4-9124.x: Suddenly there was a bang of a gunshot outside.
T4-9124.e: 의성어 (sound word) for a sharp bang, like a gunshot or a door slammed shut.
T4-9124.t: Repeat it for several shots: 탕탕. Also used for slamming: 문을 탕 닫았어요.

T4-9125.ex: 조용한 방에 시계 소리만 째깍째깍 들려요.
T4-9125.x: In the quiet room, all you can hear is the clock going tick-tock.
T4-9125.e: 의성어 (sound word) for the small, crisp tick of a clock's second hand.
T4-9125.t: The verb 째깍거리다 is common: 시계가 째깍거려요. 똑딱똑딱 is another way to say tick-tock.

T4-9126.x: The glass fell on the floor and broke with a crash.
T4-9126.e: 의성어 (sound word) for glass or thin metal hitting something hard and ringing or shattering.
T4-9126.t: Often with 하고 or 소리: 쨍그랑 하는 소리가 났어요. For a big, messy smash, Koreans say 와장창.

T4-9127.x: A fine spring rain has been drizzling since morning.
T4-9127.e: 의태어 (manner word) for fine, soft rain. The dark-vowel pair 부슬부슬 sounds a little heavier and gloomier.
T4-9127.t: A light drizzle like this is called 보슬비. The opposite feel is 주룩주룩 for heavy rain.

T4-9128.ex: 창문을 여니까 시원한 바람이 솔솔 불어요.
T4-9128.x: When I opened the window, a cool breeze came gently blowing in.
T4-9128.e: 의태어 (manner word) for something light flowing out softly and steadily. Its dark-vowel pair 술술 now mostly means 'smoothly, fluently'.
T4-9128.t: Also for smells and sleepiness: 고소한 냄새가 솔솔 나요 'a nutty smell wafts'; 잠이 솔솔 와요 'I'm getting drowsy'.

T4-9129.forms: 우르릉 + 울리다 / 소리가 나다; 우르릉 쾅쾅
T4-9129.x: Dark clouds gathered, and then thunder rumbled.
T4-9129.e: 의성어 (sound word) for a deep, rolling rumble, like thunder or a heavy machine.
T4-9129.t: Thunder in Korean picture books goes 우르릉 쾅쾅: the rumble, then the crack.

T4-9130.x: A spring breeze is blowing softly, so I feel good.
T4-9130.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a light, cool breeze or a gentle swaying motion. The dark-vowel pair 설렁설렁 is a bigger, looser movement, and also means 'half-heartedly'.
T4-9130.t: Also used for a wagging tail: 강아지가 꼬리를 살랑살랑 흔들어요. The verb is 살랑거리다.

T4-9131.m: splash, crash (waves on a shore); smack
T4-9131.x: The waves crashed against the rocks with a splash.
T4-9131.e: 의성어 (sound word) for a big wave hitting something, or a hard slap. Its bright-vowel pair 찰싹 is a smaller, sharper slap or splash.
T4-9131.t: Waves that keep crashing are 철썩철썩, or the verb 철썩이다: 파도가 철썩이는 소리.

T4-9132.ex: 키 큰 형이 앞에서 성큼성큼 걸어가요.
T4-9132.x: My tall older brother is striding ahead with long steps.
T4-9132.e: 의태어 (manner word) for walking with long, confident steps.
T4-9132.t: Single 성큼 also means 'all of a sudden, by a big step': 봄이 성큼 다가왔어요 'Spring has suddenly arrived.'

T4-9133.x: The penguins are waddling across the ice.
T4-9133.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a heavy body rocking from side to side as it walks.
T4-9133.t: The verb 뒤뚱거리다 is common: 오리가 뒤뚱거리며 걸어요. Classic for ducks, penguins and toddlers.

T4-9134.x: The turtle is crawling slowly across the sand.
T4-9134.e: 의태어 (manner word) for crawling slowly on hands and knees or on four legs.
T4-9134.t: Pronounced [엉그멍금]: the ㅁ batchim links to the next vowel. Almost always paired with 기다 'to crawl'.

T4-9135.x: A drunk man is staggering along.
T4-9135.e: 의태어 (manner word) for walking unsteadily, swaying as if about to fall.
T4-9135.t: Typical causes are drinking, dizziness or exhaustion. The verb is 비틀거리다.

T4-9136.x: The baby is toddling over to Mom.
T4-9136.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a small child taking short, careful steps.
T4-9136.t: It sounds cute and affectionate, so it isn't used for adults; for an unsteady adult, 비틀비틀 fits better.

T4-9137.m: to stagger, to totter, to reel
T4-9137.x: I was so tired that I staggered on the stairs.
T4-9137.t: Also figurative in the news: 경제가 비틀거리다 'the economy is faltering'.

T4-9138.x: The baby is munching on rice in little bites.
T4-9138.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a small mouth chewing with lips closed. Its dark-vowel pair 우물우물 is bigger, slower chewing, or mumbling.
T4-9138.t: Pronounced [오무로물]: the ㄹ batchim links to the next vowel. The verb 오물거리다 is common, usually about children.

T4-9139.x: I was thirsty, so I gulped the water down.
T4-9139.e: Both 의성어 and 의태어: the glugging sound and the manner of drinking a lot in big gulps.
T4-9139.t: Pronounced [벌컥뻘컥]: the ㄱ batchim makes the next ㅂ tense. Single 벌컥 also means 'abruptly': 화를 벌컥 내다 'to flare up'.

T4-9140.ex: 밥 먹을 때 쩝쩝 소리 내지 마세요.
T4-9140.x: Please don't smack your lips when you eat.
T4-9140.e: 의성어 (sound word) for loud chewing with an open mouth.
T4-9140.t: Loud chewing is considered rude in Korea, so 쩝쩝거리다 is usually a complaint. Single 쩝 also shows mild disappointment.

T4-9141.ex: 좋아하는 사람을 보니까 가슴이 콩닥콩닥 뛰어요.
T4-9141.x: Seeing the person I like makes my heart go thump-thump.
T4-9141.e: Also the sound of grain being pounded in a mortar; today it's mostly used for a heart beating fast.
T4-9141.t: The verb is 콩닥거리다. It sounds lighter and cuter than 두근두근, often for a crush.

T4-9142.ex: 공포 영화를 보는데 소름이 오싹오싹 돋았어요.
T4-9142.x: I got chills all over while watching the horror movie.
T4-9142.e: 의태어 (manner word) for the body shrinking and shivering from cold or fear.
T4-9142.t: Pronounced [오싸고싹]: the ㄱ batchim links to the next vowel. Single 오싹하다 is common: 오싹한 이야기 'a chilling story'.

T4-9143.ex: 잠을 못 자서 머리가 지끈지끈 아파요.
T4-9143.x: I couldn't sleep, so my head is throbbing.
T4-9143.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a pounding, splitting pain, almost always in the head.
T4-9143.t: The verb 지끈거리다 is common: 머리가 지끈거려요 'I have a pounding headache'.

T4-9144.ex: 점심을 먹고 수업 시간에 꾸벅꾸벅 졸았어요.
T4-9144.x: After lunch, I kept nodding off in class.
T4-9144.e: 의태어 (manner word) for the head dropping forward and coming back up, as when dozing off or bowing.
T4-9144.t: Single 꾸벅 is one quick bow: 꾸벅 인사했어요.

T4-9145.x: This sofa is soft and cushiony, so it's comfortable to sit on.
T4-9145.e: 의태어 (manner word) for something soft that gently sinks when pressed. Its dark-vowel pair 푹신푹신 feels deeper and softer.
T4-9145.t: Pronounced [폭씬폭씬]: the ㄱ batchim makes the next ㅅ tense. Also used for fluffy food like pancakes: 폭신폭신한 팬케이크.

T4-9146.x: The country road is bumpy, so the car shakes a lot.
T4-9146.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a surface full of bumps and dips; the rhyme 울퉁 + 불퉁 echoes the up-and-down.
T4-9146.t: Mostly used as 울퉁불퉁하다. Also for bulging muscles: 근육이 울퉁불퉁해요.

T4-9147.x: The stones on the beach are worn smooth by the waves.
T4-9147.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a surface with nothing rough on it. Its dark-vowel pair 미끈미끈 feels slipperier.
T4-9147.t: Common in skincare ads: 피부가 매끈매끈해져요. The shorter 매끈하다 also means 'sleek', as in a design.

T4-9148.x: Grandma rolled the rice cakes into little round balls.
T4-9148.e: 의태어 (manner word) built on 동글다 'round'. Its dark-vowel pair 둥글둥글 is bigger, and also describes an easygoing person.
T4-9148.t: 동글동글하다 is a cute way to describe a round face or eyes: 얼굴이 동글동글해요.

T4-9149.x: Now that it's autumn, the mountains are dyed in many colors.
T4-9149.e: 의태어 (manner word) for spots and stripes of different colors. Its dark-vowel pair 얼룩덜룩 often suggests stains or blotches.
T4-9149.t: Pronounced [알록딸록]: the ㄱ batchim makes the next ㄷ tense. Usually positive and cheerful: 알록달록한 옷.

T4-9150.x: My grandmother was hospitalized due to illness.
T4-9150.t: Honorific of 병, used for the illness of grandparents, parents or other elders, never your own. Often with 편찮으시다.

T4-9151.m: alcohol, a drink (honorific, of an elder)
T4-9151.x: Dad, did you have a lot to drink today?
T4-9151.e: Literally 'medicine liquor'; also the name of a clear, filtered rice wine.
T4-9151.t: Pronounced [약쭈]: the ㄱ batchim makes the next ㅈ tense. Honorific of 술, used for a father, grandfather or other elder's drinking.

T4-9152.forms: 눈 좀 붙여요 · 잠깐 눈을 붙였어요 · 눈을 붙이세요
T4-9152.m: to get some sleep, to grab a nap (lit. to stick the eyes together)
T4-9152.ex: 피곤하면 이동하는 동안 잠깐 눈을 붙이세요.
T4-9152.x: If you're tired, get some sleep for a bit on the way.
T4-9152.e: The eyelids are 'stuck together' (붙이다 'to attach') — closing your eyes for a short sleep.
T4-9152.t: Usually a short sleep: 잠깐, 좀 or 한숨 눈을 붙이다. 붙이다 is pronounced [부치다].

T4-9153.m: to be just around the corner, to be imminent (lit. to come right up in front of one's nose)
T4-9153.ex: 시험이 코앞에 닥쳤는데 아직 공부를 못 했어요.
T4-9153.x: The exam is right around the corner, and I still haven't studied.
T4-9153.e: 코앞 'in front of the nose' means very close in space or time; 닥치다 means 'to come upon, to draw near'.
T4-9153.t: Used for exams, deadlines and events that are worryingly close. 코앞이에요 alone also works: 시험이 코앞이에요.

T4-9154.forms: 입이 귀에 걸렸어요 · 입이 귀에 걸려서 (…)
T4-9154.m: to grin from ear to ear, to be all smiles (lit. the mouth is hooked on the ears)
T4-9154.ex: 합격 소식을 듣고 동생 입이 귀에 걸렸어요.
T4-9154.x: When my younger brother heard he'd passed, he grinned from ear to ear.
T4-9154.e: The smile is so wide that the corners of the mouth seem to hang on (걸리다) the ears.
T4-9154.t: Casual and humorous; usually in the past form 걸렸어요 to describe someone visibly delighted.

T4-9155.forms: 손이 많이 가요 · 손이 많이 가는 (+noun)
T4-9155.m: to take a lot of work or care, to be labor-intensive (lit. the hand goes to it a lot)
T4-9155.ex: 김밥은 맛있지만 손이 많이 가는 음식이에요.
T4-9155.x: Gimbap is delicious, but it's a lot of work to make.
T4-9155.e: 손 'hand' stands for work: something that needs your hands again and again.
T4-9155.t: Common for cooking, housework and crafts; also for people who need looking after: 손이 많이 가는 아이. Opposite: 손이 덜 가다.

T4-9156.m: to be short-handed, to not have enough help
T4-9156.x: On weekends we have lots of customers, so we're short-handed.
T4-9156.e: 손 here means 'working hands, labor': there aren't enough hands for the work.
T4-9156.t: Used at shops, restaurants, events and family gatherings; 일손이 모자라다 and 손이 부족하다 mean the same.

T4-9157.m: to be stranded, to be stuck and unable to leave (lit. one's feet are tied)
T4-9157.ex: 폭설로 비행기가 결항돼서 공항에 발이 묶였어요.
T4-9157.x: My flight was canceled because of heavy snow, so I was stranded at the airport.
T4-9157.e: With tied feet you can't move: weather, strikes or rules keep you from going anywhere.
T4-9157.t: Pronounced [바리 무끼다]. Very common in news about weather and transport: 폭설로 귀성객 발이 묶였다.

T4-9158.m: to laugh one's head off, to split one's sides laughing (lit. to hold one's belly button)
T4-9158.ex: 그 영화가 너무 웃겨서 배꼽을 잡고 웃었어요.
T4-9158.x: That movie was so funny that I laughed my head off.
T4-9158.e: Laughing so hard that you clutch your stomach, as if your belly button might fall off.
T4-9158.t: Usually in 배꼽을 잡고 웃다. A similar phrase is 배꼽이 빠지게 웃다 'to laugh till one's belly button falls out'.

T4-9159.m: to fail (an exam), to be rejected (lit. to eat seaweed soup)
T4-9159.x: I prepared hard, but I flunked the interview.
T4-9159.e: Seaweed is slippery, and 미끄러지다 'to slip' also means to fail an exam. A popular story also links it to 해산, meaning both 'disbanding' and 'giving birth' (after which mothers eat seaweed soup).
T4-9159.t: Casual and humorous. This is why many Koreans avoid seaweed soup before exams and give sticky 엿 or 찹쌀떡 instead.

T4-9160.forms: 언제 국수 먹여 줄 거예요? · 국수를 먹게 되다
T4-9160.m: to get married, to hold a wedding; to attend someone's wedding (lit. to eat noodles)
T4-9160.ex: 두 분 사귄 지 오래됐는데 언제 국수 먹여 줄 거예요?
T4-9160.x: You two have been dating for a long time. When are you getting married?
T4-9160.e: Noodle soup (잔치국수) was traditionally served to wedding guests, and long noodles stand for a long life together.
T4-9160.t: Mostly in the teasing question 언제 국수 먹여 줄 거예요? 'When are you treating us to noodles?', asked to someone single or in a long relationship.

T4-9161.m: one's heart races, to be thrilled (with joy or anticipation)
T4-9161.ex: 내일 첫 해외여행을 간다고 생각하니 가슴이 뛰어요.
T4-9161.x: Just thinking about my first trip abroad tomorrow makes my heart race.
T4-9161.e: 뛰다 'to jump, to run': the heart beats fast with excitement.
T4-9161.t: Mostly positive excitement; 가슴이 두근거리다 is similar. For sudden fear, use 가슴이 철렁하다.

T4-9162.m: to be a headache, to be troublesome and hard to deal with
T4-9162.ex: 이사 준비 때문에 요즘 골치가 아파요.
T4-9162.x: Getting ready to move has been giving me a headache lately.
T4-9162.e: 골치 is a colloquial word for the head or brain (골 'brain'), so literally 'the head hurts'.
T4-9162.t: For annoying problems, not real headaches (use 머리가 아프다 for those): 골치 아픈 문제 'a thorny problem'. Related: 골칫거리 'a nuisance'.

T4-9163.forms: 속이 시원해요 · 속이 다 시원하네요 · 속 시원한 (+noun)
T4-9163.m: to feel relieved, to feel a weight off one's chest (lit. the inside feels cool)
T4-9163.ex: 하고 싶던 말을 다 하니까 속이 시원해요.
T4-9163.x: Now that I've said everything I wanted to say, I feel so relieved.
T4-9163.e: 속 'inside, gut' is where frustration is felt; when it clears, the inside feels cool and fresh.
T4-9163.t: Also for satisfying news or a well-deserved outcome: 속 시원한 결말 'a satisfying ending'. Opposite feeling: 속이 답답하다.

T4-9164.m: to have a heavy heart, to feel burdened
T4-9164.ex: 친구 부탁을 거절하고 나니 마음이 무거워요.
T4-9164.x: I turned down my friend's request, and now I have a heavy heart.
T4-9164.e: Worry, guilt or responsibility felt as a weight on the heart.
T4-9164.t: Opposite: 마음이 가볍다 'to feel at ease'. 무겁다 is ㅂ-irregular: 무거워요, 무거웠어요.

T4-9165.m: to feel frustrated and stifled; to have a tight chest (lit. the chest feels stuffy)
T4-9165.ex: 아무리 설명해도 이해를 못 하니까 가슴이 답답해요.
T4-9165.x: No matter how much I explain, they don't get it, and it's so frustrating.
T4-9165.e: 답답하다 is the closed-in feeling of a stuffy room: worry or frustration seems to block the chest.
T4-9165.t: Pronounced [가스미 답따파다]. Also a physical symptom: tell a doctor 가슴이 답답해요 for chest tightness.

T4-9166.m: a great stroke of luck, a huge relief; thank goodness
T4-9166.ex: 큰 사고였는데 아무도 안 다쳐서 천만다행이에요.
T4-9166.x: It was a big accident, but thank goodness nobody got hurt.
T4-9166.e: 千萬 'ten million' + 多幸 'good fortune' — lucky ten million times over.
T4-9166.t: A stronger 다행이다; said after a near miss. 불행 중 다행 means 'a blessing in disguise / it could have been worse'.

T4-9167.m: to treat (people) to a meal or drinks, to buy a round
T4-9167.x: I got promoted, so dinner tonight is my treat.
T4-9167.e: Native compound: 한턱 'a treat (for others)' + 내다 'to pay, to put out'.
T4-9167.t: Pronounced [한텅내다]. Usually to celebrate good news (a promotion, first salary). Casual equivalent: 쏘다, as in 오늘은 내가 쏠게!

T4-9168.forms: 발등에 불이 떨어졌어요 · 발등에 불이 떨어져서 · 발등에 불 떨어진 사람
T4-9168.m: to be under pressing pressure, to have a deadline looming (lit. fire falls on the top of one's foot)
T4-9168.x: The exam is tomorrow, so I'm in a real rush now.
T4-9168.e: A burning ember lands right on your foot: the trouble is on you and can't be ignored any longer.
T4-9168.t: Pronounced [발뜽에 부리 떠러지다]. Everyday and casual; typical for deadlines, exams and last-minute panic.
rel: to be right around the corner

T4-9169.forms: 손에 익었어요 · 손에 익으면 · 손에 익은 일
T4-9169.m: to get the hang of something, to become practiced at it (lit. it ripens in the hand)
T4-9169.ex: 처음엔 어려웠는데 이제 일이 좀 손에 익었어요.
T4-9169.x: It was hard at first, but now I've got the hang of the work.
T4-9169.e: 익다 means 'to ripen' and also 'to become familiar'; the task becomes familiar to your hands.
T4-9169.t: Pronounced [소네 익따]. The task is the subject: 일이 손에 익다, not 제가 손에 익다.

T4-9170.forms: 땡땡이를 쳤어요 · 땡땡이를 치지 마세요 · 땡땡이치다
T4-9170.m: to skip class or work, to play hooky
T4-9170.ex: 날씨가 좋아서 친구랑 수업 땡땡이를 쳤어요.
T4-9170.x: The weather was nice, so I skipped class with a friend.
T4-9170.e: 땡땡이 means slacking off or sneaking away from one's duties; 치다 is the verb it pairs with. The origin of 땡땡이 is unclear.
T4-9170.t: Casual. For skipping without permission; neutral alternatives: 수업을 빼먹다, 수업에 빠지다.

T4-9171.ex: 확진자랑 밥을 먹어서 일주일 동안 자가격리를 했어요.
T4-9171.x: I ate with a confirmed case, so I self-quarantined for a week.
T4-9171.e: 自家 'one's own home' + 隔離 'separation, isolation' — isolation at home.
T4-9171.t: Pronounced [자가경니]. Also spelled 자가 격리; used with 하다 or 들어가다 (자가격리에 들어가다).

T4-9172.ex: 거리 두기 때문에 식당이 밤 아홉 시에 문을 닫았어요.
T4-9172.x: Because of social distancing, restaurants closed at 9 p.m.
T4-9172.e: 거리 'distance' (距離) + 두기 'keeping' (from 두다 'to keep, to leave'). Short for 사회적 거리 두기.
T4-9172.t: A COVID-era term: 거리 두기 단계 'distancing level', 거리 두기가 해제되다 'distancing is lifted'. Not to be confused with native 거리 'street'.

T4-9173.x: With the wind, they say it feels like minus ten.
T4-9173.e: 體感 'felt by the body' + 溫度 'temperature'.
T4-9173.t: Common in weather reports: 체감 온도가 영하 15도까지 떨어지다. 체감 also appears in 체감 물가 'how expensive prices feel'.

T4-9174.m: air-conditioning sickness (headache, chills, cold-like symptoms from too much AC)
T4-9174.ex: 사무실 에어컨이 너무 세서 냉방병에 걸렸어요.
T4-9174.x: The office AC is too strong, so I came down with air-conditioning sickness.
T4-9174.t: Pronounced [냉방뼝]. Use 냉방병에 걸리다. An everyday term rather than a formal diagnosis.

T4-9175.ex: 친구 상태 메시지를 보니까 요즘 많이 바쁜가 봐요.
T4-9175.x: Judging from my friend's status message, they must be really busy these days.
T4-9175.t: The short line shown under your name and profile picture. Casually shortened to 상메; people change it to hint at their mood or news.

T4-9176.m: host/owner of a chat room; head of a room (e.g. in a dormitory)
T4-9176.x: The host invited me to the classmates' group chat.
T4-9176.t: Online, 방장 is whoever created or manages a chat room or game room and can invite or remove members. Offline it means the person in charge of a shared room, e.g. in a dorm.

T4-9177.m: silent mode, mute (phone, notifications); no sound
T4-9177.ex: 회의 중이라서 휴대폰을 무음으로 해 놨어요.
T4-9177.x: I'm in a meeting, so I've put my phone on silent.
T4-9177.t: A phone can be on 소리 'ring', 진동 'vibrate' or 무음 'silent'. Muting a noisy group chat: 알림을 끄다 or 채팅방을 무음으로 하다.

T4-9178.x: These days many people work as independent creators.
T4-9178.t: Sounds more professional than 유튜버 and covers any platform. 1인 크리에이터 'one-person creator' is someone who plans, films and edits alone.

T4-9179.m: to subscribe (to a channel, service, magazine)
T4-9179.ex: 영상이 마음에 드시면 채널을 구독해 주세요.
T4-9179.x: If you like the video, please subscribe to the channel.
T4-9179.e: Literally 'buy to read' + 하다; first used for newspapers and magazines.
T4-9179.t: Pronounced [구도카다]. Creators often end videos with 구독과 좋아요 부탁드려요 'please subscribe and like'. Also for paid services: 음악 앱을 구독하다. Cancel: 구독을 취소하다.

T4-9180.ex: 어제 올린 영상 조회수가 벌써 만 회를 넘었어요.
T4-9180.x: The video I posted yesterday already has over ten thousand views.
T4-9180.t: Pronounced [조회쑤]. Views are counted with 회: 조회수 100만 회. Used for videos, posts and news articles; 조회수가 오르다/나오다 = to get views.

T4-9181.ex: 제 일상을 담은 브이로그를 찍어서 올리고 있어요.
T4-9181.x: I film and upload vlogs about my daily life.
T4-9181.e: From English 'vlog' (video + blog); the v is spelled out as 브이.
T4-9181.t: Popular kinds: 일상 브이로그 (daily life), 여행 브이로그 (travel), 직장인 브이로그 (office worker's day). Make one: 브이로그를 찍다.

T4-9182.ex: 간편 결제를 등록해 두면 비밀번호만 누르면 돼요.
T4-9182.x: If you register for simple payment, you just enter your PIN.
T4-9182.e: 간편 'simple and convenient' + 결제 'payment' (literally 'decide and settle').
T4-9182.t: Your card or account is saved in an app, so you pay online or in shops with a PIN, fingerprint or face scan instead of typing card details. In everyday speech these services are called 페이.

T4-9183.m: (digital) certificate, e-certificate (for online banking and government sites)
T4-9183.x: I forgot my certificate password, so I had it reissued.
T4-9183.t: Korean banking and government websites use a digital certificate to confirm who you are. The old 공인 인증서 was renamed 공동 인증서 in 2020, and certificates issued inside apps are now common too. Get one issued: 인증서를 발급받다.

T4-9184.m: mobile pay, digital wallet (paying by phone)
T4-9184.ex: 지갑을 안 가져와서 휴대폰 페이로 계산했어요.
T4-9184.x: I didn't bring my wallet, so I paid with mobile pay on my phone.
T4-9184.e: From English 'pay'. Korean payment services are named '…페이', so 페이 alone came to mean paying by phone.
T4-9184.t: Casual. Ask 페이 돼요? 'Can I pay by phone?'. 페이 is also slang for wages: 페이가 세다 'the pay is good'.

T4-9185.m: room/flat where you live on your own
T4-9185.ex: 제 자취방은 좁지만 학교에서 가까워서 좋아요.
T4-9185.x: My place is small, but it's close to school, so I like it.
T4-9185.e: 자취 'living on your own' (literally 'cooking for yourself') + 방 'room'.
T4-9185.t: Pronounced [자취빵]. Usually a small 원룸 rented with 월세; 자취방 구하기 'finding a place of your own' is a familiar task for university students.

T4-9186.x: I had lunch alone at a restaurant near the office.
T4-9186.t: Casual. Korean meals were traditionally shared, so eating alone used to feel awkward; now it's common, and many places have counter seats or one-person menus for 혼밥족 'solo diners'.

T4-9187.ex: 퇴근하고 집에서 맥주 한 캔으로 혼술했어요.
T4-9187.x: After work I had a can of beer by myself at home.
T4-9187.t: Casual. Usually means a relaxed drink at home rather than heavy drinking.

T4-9188.x: With a meal kit, dinner is ready in thirty minutes.
T4-9188.t: A box with pre-cut ingredients and sauce: you still cook it yourself, unlike 간편식, which is already cooked and just needs heating.

T4-9189.ex: 바쁠 때는 전자레인지에 데우는 간편식을 자주 먹어요.
T4-9189.x: When I'm busy, I often eat ready meals that I heat in the microwave.
T4-9189.t: Common on packaging and in news as 가정 간편식 'home ready meals', also called HMR (home meal replacement).

T4-9190.x: I have plans today, so I'm leaving work right on time.
T4-9190.e: Short for 칼퇴근: 칼 'knife' + 퇴근 'leaving work' — leaving as sharply and precisely as a knife cuts.
T4-9190.t: Casual. Seen as a mark of good 워라밸, the opposite of 야근. Verb: 칼퇴하다.

T4-9191.ex: 다음 주에 팀장님하고 연봉 협상이 있어요.
T4-9191.x: I have my salary negotiation with my team leader next week.
T4-9191.t: Usually held once a year. Office workers often joke that it's really 연봉 통보 'salary notification', since the company simply announces the number.

T4-9192.m: condescending know-it-all; preachy older person or boss (slang)
T4-9192.ex: 우리 부장님은 좋은 분인데 가끔 꼰대 같아요.
T4-9192.x: My department head is a good person, but sometimes acts like a preachy know-it-all.
T4-9192.e: Old slang for one's father or teacher; its origin is uncertain. Now it means anyone who lectures others and insists 'my way is right'.
T4-9192.t: Casual and critical — never say it to someone's face. The joke phrase 라떼는 말이야 (a pun on 나 때는 말이야 'back in my day') mocks typical 꼰대 talk. Young people can be 꼰대 too (젊은 꼰대).

T4-9193.m: side job, side business, side hustle
T4-9193.x: My salary alone isn't enough, so I started a side job.
T4-9193.t: 투잡 'two jobs' is a casual equivalent, and N잡러 is slang for someone juggling several jobs.

T4-9194.ex: 이 식당은 양도 많고 가성비가 좋아요.
T4-9194.x: This restaurant gives big portions and is good value for money.
T4-9194.e: Short for 가격 대비 성능 'performance relative to price': 가 'price' + 성 'performance' + 비 'ratio'.
T4-9194.t: Very common: 가성비가 좋다 'good value'; 가성비 갑 is slang for 'best value'.

T4-9195.ex: 요즘 이 동네가 핫플이라서 주말엔 사람이 많아요.
T4-9195.x: This neighborhood is a hot spot these days, so it's crowded on weekends.
T4-9195.e: Clipped from 핫플레이스, from English 'hot place'; English speakers would say 'hot spot'.
T4-9195.t: Casual. People visit 핫플 to try the food and take 인증샷 for social media.

T4-9196.m: Millennials and Gen Z, the MZ generation
T4-9196.ex: MZ세대는 회식보다 개인 시간을 더 중요하게 생각해요.
T4-9196.x: The MZ generation values personal time more than company dinners.
T4-9196.e: M for Millennials + Z for Generation Z + 세대 'generation' (世代).
T4-9196.t: Read 엠지 세대. A Korean-made label used heavily in media and marketing for people born roughly from the early 1980s to the early 2010s; many young people dislike being lumped together this way.

T4-9197.ex: 밤에 주문하면 새벽 배송으로 아침에 받아요.
T4-9197.x: If I order at night, it comes by early-morning delivery and I get it in the morning.
T4-9197.t: Orders placed by late evening arrive at your door by about 7 a.m.; especially popular for groceries.

T4-9198.ex: 안 쓰는 구독 서비스는 해지하는 게 좋아요.
T4-9198.x: It's best to cancel subscription services you don't use.
T4-9198.e: 구독 'subscription' (literally 'buy to read') + 서비스 from English 'service'.
T4-9198.t: Covers streaming, music, meal kits and regular deliveries. Cancel a subscription: 해지하다.

T4-9199.ex: 출근할 때 공유 자전거를 타고 역까지 가요.
T4-9199.x: When I go to work, I ride a shared bike to the station.
T4-9199.t: You rent one through an app and return it at a docking station or designated spot; many cities run public bike-share systems.

T4-9200.ex: 전동 킥보드를 탈 때는 꼭 헬멧을 쓰세요.
T4-9200.x: Always wear a helmet when you ride an electric scooter.
T4-9200.e: 전동 'electric-powered' (literally 'electric motion') + 킥보드, Konglish from 'kickboard' for a kick scooter.
T4-9200.t: By Korean law riders need at least a moped license and a helmet, and riding two on one scooter is banned.

T4-9201.ex: 집 앞 무인 매장에서 아이스크림을 샀어요.
T4-9201.x: I bought ice cream at the unstaffed store in front of my place.
T4-9201.t: Common types are ice-cream shops, laundromats and study cafés: you pay at a kiosk while CCTV keeps watch.

T4-9202.forms: Same form after any noun: 이름조차 · 물조차 · (+ usually a negative)
T4-9202.x: I was so busy I couldn't even eat lunch.
T4-9202.e: Native particle that points to the most basic thing you'd expect — and says even that didn't happen.
T4-9202.t: Mostly with negatives or bad situations: 이름조차 몰라요 'I don't even know the name.' For a positive 'even', use 도 or 까지.

T4-9203.forms: 은커녕 after a consonant (밥은커녕) · 는커녕 after a vowel (커피는커녕) · + 도/조차 + negative
T4-9203.m: let alone, far from (… not even)
T4-9203.x: I was so busy I couldn't even drink water, let alone eat.
T4-9203.e: 은/는 (topic) + 커녕 'far from it': 'as for X — forget it'.
T4-9203.t: The second half usually has 도/조차 + a negative, or 만 for an unwanted result: 칭찬은커녕 잔소리만 들었어요 'Far from being praised, I just got nagged.'

T4-9204.forms: 이야 after a consonant (주말이야) · 야 after a vowel (저야) · 저야 좋죠 · 그거야 당연하죠
T4-9204.m: (emphatic) as for …, of course …; … sure, but (contrast)
T4-9204.x: The weekend is fine, of course, but I'm a bit busy on weekdays.
T4-9204.e: A stronger, more emotional version of the topic marker 은/는: 'X — that goes without saying'.
T4-9204.t: Common replies: 저야 좋죠 'That's fine by me', 그거야 당연하죠 'That goes without saying.' Not the same as the calling 야 after names (민수야!).

T4-9205.forms: Same form after any noun: 겨울치고(는) · 외국인치고(는) · N치고 … 없다 (every N)
T4-9205.m: for a …, considering it's …; (with a negative) every … without exception
T4-9205.e: From the verb 치다 'to count as, regard as' + -고: 'counting it as a …'.
T4-9205.t: Two uses: 겨울치고(는) 따뜻해요 'warm for winter'; with a negative it means 'every': 부모치고 자식 걱정 안 하는 사람은 없어요 'There's no parent who doesn't worry about their kids.'

T4-9206.forms: 이야말로 after a consonant (건강이야말로) · 야말로 after a vowel (저야말로) · 저야말로 감사하죠
T4-9206.m: truly, precisely, (it is) none other than
T4-9206.x: Health is truly the most precious wealth.
T4-9206.e: An extra-strong form of the emphatic particle (이)야: 'X, if anything, is the one'.
T4-9206.t: 저야말로 'It's me who should (thank you / apologize)' is a very common polite reply: A: 감사합니다. B: 저야말로 감사하죠.

T4-9207.forms: 으로서 after a consonant (학생으로서) · 로서 after a vowel or ㄹ (엄마로서) · ≠ (으)로써 (by means of)
T4-9207.m: as (in the role or capacity of)
T4-9207.ex: 엄마로서 할 수 있는 건 다 했어요.
T4-9207.x: I did everything I could as a mother.
T4-9207.e: (으)로 'as' + -서, marking a role, status or qualification.
T4-9207.t: Don't confuse it with (으)로써 'by means of, through': 대화로써 해결해요 'We solve it through dialogue.' Koreans mix up the spelling too.

T4-9208.forms: 이라든지 after a consonant (빵이라든지) · 라든지 after a vowel (과자라든지) · A(이)라든지 B(이)라든지
T4-9208.ex: 과일이라든지 채소라든지 몸에 좋은 걸 드세요.
T4-9208.x: Eat things that are good for you, like fruit or vegetables.
T4-9208.e: From 이다 'to be' + -라든지, a quoting form of -든지: 'whether it's X or …'.
T4-9208.t: Lists a few examples without being complete. In casual speech 같은 거 is similar: 과일 같은 거.

T4-9209.forms: A. 그 결과 B. · N의 결과 · -(으)ㄴ 결과
T4-9209.ex: 매일 운동했어요. 그 결과 오 킬로가 빠졌어요.
T4-9209.x: I exercised every day. As a result, I lost five kilos.
T4-9209.t: Common in writing, reports and presentations; in conversation people often say 그래서 or 결국.

T4-9210.forms: A. 그러다 보니 B. · after verbs: -다 보니
T4-9210.m: and so (over time), as a result of that
T4-9210.ex: 매일 야근했어요. 그러다 보니 건강이 나빠졌어요.
T4-9210.x: I worked late every day. And over time, my health got worse.
T4-9210.e: 그러다 'to do so' + -다 보니 'as one keeps doing (one finds that)'.
T4-9210.t: Shows a result that came gradually, often unplanned, from repeating something: 자주 만났어요. 그러다 보니 친해졌어요.

T4-9211.forms: 하필 + time/thing: 하필 오늘 · emphatic: 하필이면 (왜 저예요?)
T4-9211.ex: 소풍 가는 날 하필 비가 왔어요.
T4-9211.x: Of all days, it rained on the day of the picnic.
T4-9211.t: Complains about bad luck or timing. 하필이면 is more emphatic: 하필이면 왜 저예요? 'Why me, of all people?'

T4-9212.forms: 어쩐지 + reason: 어쩐지 …더라고요 · 어쩐지 기분이 이상해요 (somehow)
T4-9212.x: Was today a holiday? No wonder the streets were so quiet.
T4-9212.e: From 어찌하다 'how' + -ㄴ지 'whether': 'I didn't know how, but …'.
T4-9212.t: Two uses: after you learn the reason, 어쩐지! means 'No wonder!'; for an unexplained feeling it means 'somehow', like 왠지.

T4-9213.forms: Short for 하기는 · 하긴 그렇네요 · 하긴 그래 (casual)
T4-9213.m: well, true (admitting a point), come to think of it
T4-9213.x: Well, it's the weekend, so it makes sense that it's crowded.
T4-9213.e: Short for 하기는 'as for doing (it)': admitting the other side has a point.
T4-9213.t: Used when you think again and agree: A: 오늘 춥네요. B: 하긴, 벌써 12월이니까요. Spoken style.

T4-9214.forms: 정작 + key person/moment: 정작 필요할 때 · 정작 본인은
T4-9214.m: actually, when it really matters, the very (one)
T4-9214.ex: 할 말이 많았는데 정작 만나니까 아무 말도 못 했어요.
T4-9214.x: I had so much to say, but when we actually met, I couldn't say a thing.
T4-9214.e: Native adverb that points to the person, moment or thing that really matters, often against expectations.
T4-9214.t: Close to 막상 'when it comes to it'. It also marks 'the very person': 정작 본인은 괜찮대요 'The person himself says he's fine.'
rel: when it actually comes to it

T4-9215.x: This apartment is 84 square meters, so it's good for a family.
T4-9215.t: Home sizes are officially given in 제곱미터, but many people still talk in 평 (1평 ≈ 3.3 m²).

T4-9216.x: I'm on my period, so my stomach hurts a bit.
T4-9216.e: Literally 'life principle', i.e. a body function; it also means 'physiology' (생리학).
T4-9216.t: Pronounced [생니]. The normal, neutral word, fine with a pharmacist or doctor. Period pain is 생리통.

T4-9217.x: You can buy sanitary pads at convenience stores too.
T4-9217.t: Pronounced [생니대]. Sold at convenience stores, supermarkets and drugstores. A tampon is 탐폰.

T4-9218.ex: 어제 술을 많이 마셔서 숙취가 심해요.
T4-9218.x: I drank a lot last night, so my hangover is bad.
T4-9218.t: Koreans fight a hangover with 해장국 'hangover soup', and convenience stores sell 숙취 해소제 (hangover drinks).

T4-9219.x: Lately I've started losing hair because of stress.
T4-9219.t: Anti-hair-loss shampoo (탈모 샴푸) is a big product category in Korea.

T4-9220.forms: 체해요 · 체했어요 · 체할 거예요 · 체한 것 같아요
T4-9220.ex: 점심을 급하게 먹었더니 체한 것 같아요.
T4-9220.x: I ate lunch too fast, and I think it's given me indigestion.
T4-9220.e: 滯 'stuck, blocked' + 하다: food that won't go down.
T4-9220.t: A very common Korean complaint: the heavy feeling of food 'stuck' after eating too fast. People take 소화제, and some still use the folk remedy of pricking a fingertip (손을 따다).

T4-9221.x: I get carsick if I'm on a bus for a long time.
T4-9221.t: Use 멀미가 나다 or 멀미하다. 차멀미 = carsickness, 뱃멀미 = seasickness, 멀미약 = motion-sickness medicine.
